Goal (rev. 20): under which conditions does the TLP admit a self-consistent formal system,
given by a minimal spanning set of axioms (A) and derivations (D)?
- Choices between non-congruent witnesses or readings are made by LI, then LI+
  (PRINCIPLE), and logged in DECISIONS (X0-X53).
- A HIGH ALERT is either of two cases. Both are recorded and adjudicated at the end.
  - (1) An LI+ tie that leaves two incongruent minimal systems (both are recorded).
  - (2) An unresolvable incongruence between an axiom and a derivation (the axiom holds).
Answer (rev. 58, X53): yes. The system and its conditions are below. TLP is
self-consistent: Phi is a model, every axiom proved (A11 for the series grammar G*, X50-X52;
A16-A18 and A6a, A6s, A7, X53; the rest by construction). Open: A17's independence (E33),
and A11 in the other countermodels.
- Final adjudication so far (rev. 45-46): X40 reads 3.332 as containment, so A6d lost its
  limit source. X41 re-decided X29 Q2: the self-settling general signs (s, p v s) have
  sense, and the bipolarity texts 2.173 and 2.224 are restricted. A6d gives way to A6s
  (3.13), D10 holds, and HIGH ALERT #2 is dissolved. X42 (rev. 47) verified the result,
  with A6s read hereditarily (no picture or part of a picture depicts itself).
- Candidate model: Phi (X26; X42 and X44 under X41, with machine checks on finite cuts; A17
  for all four invariant families), with its notation (names a, b, h, h', o_i, R_i, f_{i,j},
  indices in decimal; X49). A11 in Phi: PROVED at kinds 1-3 for G* (X50, X52). A16-A18,
  A6a, A6s, A7: PROVED (X53). Phi is a model of TLP.
- Each axiom was given a countermodel satisfying all the others (rev. 38-42; revised in
  X41-X44: A6s new, A7 replaced, A4's and A17's descriptions repaired; A11 in A7's and

Signature
- O: objects. A: states of affairs, each a slot map kappa(a): P -> O (partial on slots).
  Lambda = {0,1}^A: worlds. chi*: the actual world.
- Picture or proposition: a sign with a projection (rho on names, tau on forms) inducing
  r from the sign's states to A.
- Medium (M+, X29; X41): the whole sign, every signifying token included. A sign is
  possible iff its letter pattern fits the frame (X31):
  - one state per distinct atomic formula;
  - object letters to objects injectively, renaming allowed;
  - form symbols to forms injectively;
  - logical signs are not atoms;
  - defined signs take no tokens of their own: a sign with defined signs is possible,
    and has sense, iff its translation fits (X47);
  - series signs (X51): one state per propositional letter of a bracket (7b); each hole
    writes its interface image, whose letters and names are words (H1).
- Sense: [[phi]] ⊆ Lambda. Propositions are what N (joint negation of the values of a
  variable given by enumeration, a function, or a formal series) builds from elementary
  propositions.
- Quantifiers are weakly exclusive. A quantifier excludes the values of the variables
  free in its scope and of the names occurring in it (5.53; X35). This holds for object
  and form variables alike.
- Values (C-nv, X24). In Phi(x), x ranges over the o (not named in the scope) for which
  Phi(o) is a proposition. Details:
  - an atom has sense only if its tuple is a state of the frame;
  - a truth-function has sense only if all its components do;
  - a general proposition has sense iff its whole sign fits the frame (X41; under X29-X40:
    fits outside its support);
  - N over no values is the tautology;
  - a formal series' values at an instance are its terms T_k[a-bar] with sense (X51); N
    over a series with no term with sense is true;
  - a vacuous binder is transparent: its letter takes a token; otherwise (Ez)B has B's
    sense and truth (X51, 3.328; X50's range rule for vacuous binders superseded).
- Convention (X44): "p has a state off {s, t}" := (Eu, v)(St(p, u, v) . St(p, s, t)); s and t
  must occur in the scope, or weak exclusion does not keep u, v apart from them.
- Commitments:
  - S1: one fixed O and A across worlds;
  - (S2, constraints finitary: dropped in rev. 50; A4 gives Lambda = {0,1}^A, X45);
  - S3: every projection admissible unless A6s forbids it (r has a cycle);
  - S4: states are partial slot maps (typing only).
Axioms (A) and derivations (D), in numerical order. A: adopted and independent (a
countermodel satisfies all the others). D: follows from the premises listed; no claim to
independence. Tractatus sources in brackets.
  D1   O is nonempty.  <- A19                                                 [2.026]
  D2   Distinct states of affairs have distinct slot maps.  <- A7, 2.15 (S3: r
       well-defined)                                                         [2.01, 2.03]
  D3   Every object occurs in some state of affairs.  <- A13                  [2.011]
  A4   States of affairs are independent: Lambda = {0,1}^A.          [2.061, 4.27, 6.37]
  A5   There is an actual world chi*.                                         [2.04, 2.06]
  A6a  A picture's medium (the whole sign, M+) is a fact of the world it depicts:
       its states are in A (M = A).                                         [2.141, 3.14]
  A6s  No picture's sense is its own sign-fact, nor any part's (J-sub): for every
       picture P = (D, rho, tau), no nonempty D' ⊆ D has r(D') = D'; for finite D,
       r has no cycle.                                   [3.13; 4.024, 4.061, 2.161]
  A7   Every nonempty finite situation is the sense of some picture.          [2.19, 4.5]
  A8   Definitions are well-founded, uniform, one per sign; syntax is settled
       without meaning.                                                       [3.23, 3.33]
  D9   Every object has a name.  <- D3, A7                                    [3.203, 3.314]
  D10  Every possible sign expresses a sense under some admissible projection.
       <- A7, A6s, S3, A6a, A4, A8                                          [4.5, 5.473]
  A11  There is an adequate notation, an injective naming of all objects and forms by
       finite strings (J-N), in which it is decidable from the sign and the definitions
       of its defined signs (X47) whether a proposition is a tautology (J-FS). A promise
       problem over the possible signs.                              [5.551, 6.126]
  D12  If chi* is the actual world, every world with the same completely general
       truths is isomorphic to it.  <- A17                                   [5.526]
  A13  Every object occurs in some state of affairs together with a different
       object.                                                                [2.0121]
  A14  Every state of affairs combines at least two distinct objects.
                                                       [2.03, 2.031, 2.032, 2.14, 2.15, 4.0311]
  D15  If chi* is the actual world, every object fixed by all automorphisms of the
       frame and chi* is singled out by one completely general description.  <- A16
                                                                             [2.02331]
  A16  If chi* is the actual world, every object is singled out by one completely
       general description.                                                   [5.526]
  A17  Any two worlds with the same completely general truths are isomorphic.
                                                                     [5.5262, 2nd sentence]
  A18  If chi* is the actual world, then for every proposition p, every minimal
       alteration of chi* that changes p's truth value changes the completely
       general truths (MC-all).                                  [5.5262, 1st sentence]
  A19  Some world has two distinct objects o, o' such that every name-free
       formula Psi(x) has sense at o iff at o', and where it does has the same
       truth value.                                                           [5.5302]
  D-S4 Every state of affairs is finite.  <- A11 (J-FS), A7, S3          [4.2211, 4.04]

Model: Phi (X26).
- Frame: O = {h, h', a, b} ∪ {o_i}.
  - Forms R_i, each with the states R_i(a, b), R_i(b, a) and R_i(h, o_i).
  - Marker forms f_{i,j} (j <= i), each with the one state f_{i,j}(h', o_i).
- chi*: R_i(a, b) iff i in S, R_i(b, a) iff i in T, all else true. (S, T) is Cohen-generic.
- The frame has the automorphism (a b), so A19 holds. chi* is rigid, so A16 holds.
- A11 at all kinds (X32, X33: a live-interface automaton for formal series); under X41
  the empty-support case of X33. Rev. 55 (X49): OPEN. That case is not compositional
  under X43 (R1, R2); under J-N's old input A11 fails in Phi (In, G_n); in Phi's notation
  the indices decide those separators. Obligations: E31, E32. Rev. 56 (X50): kinds 1-2
  PROVED; kind 3 open (the fit state needs occurrence sets and reserved name slots).
  Rev. 57 (X51, X52): E31 closed (G*); kind 3 PROVED for G*.
- Under X41 (X42): A6s and A7 by state-disjoint copies on fresh units; A16 by
  descriptions of a, h, h' and o_i whose 5.5321 sentences have sense; A17 (two invariant
  families checked); A18 (genericity over all finite signs); A11 by X32's procedure with
  X41's sense colours (X33's fit automaton): refuted as a proof in rev. 55 (X49).
Countermodels (CORE AXIOMS, CURRENT COUNTERMODELS; rev. 38-42, revised in X41):
  - A4: Phi with an invariant constraint.
  - A5: the Phi frame with no chi*.
  - A6a: an external medium.
  - A6s: unrestricted Pi over Phi.
  - A7: Phi plus two ternary states Q(h, h', z), Q2(h', h, z2), each the other's token
    (X42; A11 a sketch).
  - A8: a circular definition.

  - A16: Phi with S = T.
  - A17: Phi ⊔ eta_0 (aleph_1 one-state forms); fails A11 under J-N (rev. 55, X49; E33).
  - A18: Phi with S = N, T = {}.

  Checked under X41 in X42 (A4's and A17's descriptions repaired; zeta's h described by

Main consequences
- A is infinite (THEOREM: A7 with A6s; every multiplicity class is infinite). D9: every
  object has a name. Under X41 a state with no second state of its pattern is invisible
  to every proposition, so A17 implies A7 for singleton situations (X42).
- Under A16, chi* is rigid on objects, every object can be named apart (3.263), and
  |O| <= aleph_0. A19 keeps the frame non-rigid: indiscernibles are possible, never
  actual ("nie richtig").
- A17 implies D12. Rev. 55 (X49): that it is strictly stronger relative to all the other
  axioms rested on Phi ⊔ eta_0, which fails A11 under J-N; open (E33). A11's correct
  notation makes O and the forms countable, so |A| = aleph_0. aleph_0 effects fall under J6.
- A18 gives MC-fin: no finite alteration of chi* is an isomorph of chi*.
- A11 restricts the frame (THEOREM 3; X42): (a_k*) and (b_k) are necessary, without a
  named block; (d) the X41 truth of the fitting frame sentences is decidable; not
  sufficient (S(K_omega)).
- Full frames: infinite O fails A11; finite O with finitely many arities admits no chi*
  (A16 + A18); infinitely many arities: open.
- Frame facts are tautologies under C-nv and show themselves (6.12, 6.124). Whatever is
  invariant across Lambda shows and cannot be said.

FINAL FORM (rev. 48; the user's decisions of 2026-10-23, recorded for the paper)
- Name: the axiomatic system is TLP, the system that spans the Tractatus. In the paper
  the book is cited as the Tractatus [Witt1922d, Witt1922e] and the system is set as
  *TLP*. (In this ledger "TLP" still means the book.)
- Title: "TLP as axiomatic system".
- Abstract: "The *Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus* [Witt1922d, Witt1922e] admits a
  self-consistent axiomatic system, *TLP*, under the *Least Inconsistent* (LI)
  criterion."
- Main part, introductory paragraph (draft, rev. 48; numbers unchanged at the freeze,
  rev. 53):
  "The following system *TLP* of 13 independent axioms (A) and 9 dependent derivations
  (D) spans the 526 propositions of the *Tractatus* under the least inconsistent
  criterion (LI).[1] It violates none of them, reads 13 narrowly, and adds one commitment
  without a textual source. No tie between inequivalent systems survives LI+. *TLP* has
  a model, so it is
  self-consistent. There are infinitely many states of affairs, and the decidability of
  logic restricts which states of affairs there are."
  Rev. 55 (X49): "TLP has a model, so it is self-consistent" and "13 independent axioms"
  are unsupported until E32 and E33 close; so is the abstract's "self-consistent". They
  are the user's to restate; the paper's notes carry the evidence. Rev. 57 (X51): "reads
  13 narrowly" becomes 14 (5.24), also the user's to restate.
  Rev. 58 (the user's decision, 2026-10-31): "a spanning set of 13 axioms (A) and 9
  derivations (D)"; "reads 14 narrowly"; self-consistency stated (X53); minimality and
  independence qualified in notes [2] and [10] (E33; A11 in the other countermodels).
- Main part, body: signature; commitments (S1-S4, K3); axioms and derivations; the
  restricted propositions with their readings. Extremely terse.
- Footnote 1: the LI criterion (kind first: definition, limit, assertion, presentation,
  with the criteria for definitions and limits and the unit rule for mixed propositions;
  then decimal level; violations before restrictions; LI+ for ties).
- Other footnotes (copious): per axiom, its textual sources and LI costing; per
  derivation, its proof; per restriction, the reading kept and why the plain one fails;
  per logged judgment, its ground.
- Appendix: the model (Phi) and the countermodels.
- Bibliography, short:
  - witnesses the system depends on: the 1922 German and Ogden [Witt1922d, Witt1922e];
    the 1933 reprint (5.152, X39); Pears-McGuinness (1961; 1963 impression); Lewy 1967;
    Letters to Ogden (1973; 4.023);
  - the text base: Project Gutenberg 5740 (a transcription, not a witness);
  - about ten works for priority and borrowed results (e.g. Wehmeier 2004, Rogers and
    Wehmeier 2012, Hintikka 1956, Weiss 2017, Lokhorst 1988, Button 2017, Carnap 1945;
    Cohen forcing, Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse, Feferman-Vaught, Trakhtenbrot-Vaught).
- Out of scope: ZFC (a future project). Note for it (rev. 47 analysis, not a ledger
  result): A11 rules out a theorem-preserving computable translation of ZFC into TLP
  tautologies, and THEOREM 3's (a_k*) rules out any world carrying a ZFC model's
  membership in its atomic facts.

- Thawed (rev. 55, X49): four triggers; J-N re-decided (an adequate notation; provisional).
  Phi is a candidate model (A11 open, E32); A17's countermodel fails A11 (E33). The freeze
  resumes when E31-E33 close. E32 is an open mathematical problem; until it closes, the
  paper cannot state self-consistency. Rev. 56 (X50): A11 in Phi proved at kinds 1-2.
  Rev. 57 (X51, X52): E31 closed (G*); A11 in Phi proved at kinds 1-3 for G*. Rev. 58
  (X53): E32 closed; Phi is a model of TLP; the paper may state self-consistency. E33
  (A17's independence) remains.

Key: DONE = prior work covers it. PARTIAL = prior work covers part of it.
THIN = ours, but minor. OPEN = searched, not found. UNCHECKED = not yet searched.
Math status (independent of search status): [ok] = checked; [rev] = revised after check.
Evidence for citations (rev. 16): [F] read in full; [P] partly read; [A] abstract only;
[S] reported by another source; [W2] checked by two model-mediated fetches (blind first,
then targeted) that agree, which is not a direct reading; [unverified] could not be checked
(the reader stopped before the passage).
Branch marks: [A7] / [A7c] = holds under that reading of adequacy only; [A6d] = holds only
if candidate A6d is adopted; [finite A] / [infinite A] likewise. The branches are kept as
a record; LI RESOLUTION says which ones the principle selects.

PRINCIPLE: LEAST INCONSISTENT (LI), adopted 2026-10-07. Replaces case-by-case decisions.
(Rev. 48: the name is "least inconsistent", the user's term; "least inconsistency" before.)
- Goal (rev. 20): find the conditions under which the TLP admits a self-consistent formal
  system with a minimal spanning set of A and D. Every criterion below is read against
  this goal. The complement of what LI keeps (violations, restrictions, weight-0
  commitments, witness selections) is exactly that set of conditions.
- Discretion is accepted where witnesses or readings are non-congruent. Harsher criteria
  would stall the enterprise. Every such decision is logged (DECISIONS).
- T := the formal contents of the 526 propositions under admissible readings, plus this
  ledger's non-textual commitments. T is inconsistent.
- A formalization is a consistent subset of T. Its violations are the propositions it leaves
  out.
- Weight has two keys: the kind of statement first, then its decimal level.
- Kind (from the tag; for a mixed proposition, the kind of the unit narrowed: rev. 51,
  below), highest weight first:
  1. Definitions (DEF). They fix the terms everything else uses. An assertion that
     contradicts the definition of its own terms has no consistent content to keep.
  2. Limits (UNS). These are W's own priority: what can be shown cannot be said (4.1212;
     for formal concepts, 4.1272). An assertion that conflicts with a limit tries to say
     what only shows, so it yields. (Until rev. 19 this cited 6.54, which speaks only of
     W's own propositions.) Criterion (rev. 31, E11, made explicit): a sentence is a
     limit if it states that something cannot be said, expressed, asserted, thought or
     asked, or is nonsense. That something shows itself is not, by itself, a limit; it
     is an assertion about expression.
     Definitions (rev. 51, X46, made explicit): a unit is a definition if it fixes what
     a term or sign means. Markers: a meaning or naming verb that states what a term or
     sign means ("heisst", "nenne ich", "Def."); a gloss ("das heisst", "das ist" +
     phrase, or "also" in a verbless apposition restating a preceding phrase; elsewhere
     "also" marks a consequence); "besteht darin, dass", also for a term already named;
     "X ist (waere) das, was ..." or "Was ..., ist X" only if X is not fixed before.
     Without a marker, a unit that says what an already fixed term applies to, states a
     condition on it or draws a consequence is an assertion; so is a requirement.
     Units (rev. 51, X46): a sentence; a gloss or a parenthesis is a unit of its own. A
     mark weighs by the kind of the unit whose content the reading narrows (a
     definition's definiens is part of its content); if a reading narrows several units
     of one proposition, the mark counts once, at the heaviest of their kinds. The level
     stays the proposition's. This states the practice of X7 (4.463) and X40 (5.473).
  3. Assertions (AX, SIG, THM). These are merged because the axiom/theorem split is this
     ledger's reconstruction, not the text's. Dependency counts in the tag graph rank AX/SIG
     highest, but that only reflects which assertions were chosen as axioms.
  4. Presentation (NOT, REM). These add no content, so they never outweigh content.
  Weight follows the kind, not the current derivation status: 2.224 is an assertion
  whether it is an axiom (rev. 2-5) or a theorem (rev. 6).
- Level: the footnote to 1 says the decimal figures "indicate the logical importance of the
  propositions". Level k = k digits after the point (1-7 are level 0). An axiom or
  commitment takes the shallowest level among its textual sources.
- Order: compare violation counts key by key: kind 1 at level 0, kind 1 at level 1, ...,
  then kind 2, and so on. At the first key where they differ, fewer violations wins.
- Readings and formal choices are optimized like axioms. A reading must be admitted by the
  proposition's own wording; a reading its wording argues against counts as a violation.
  The plain reading is what the wording says. Strengthening a proposition beyond its
  wording is not a reading.
- Restriction before violation (rev. 11).
  - Suppose a proposition's strong or general reading collapses the system: the kept set
    becomes inconsistent, or something of higher rank has to be dropped.
  - If a weak reading, or a special clause that its wording admits, keeps the system
    consistent, that restricted form is adopted.
  - A restricted proposition is retained, not violated.
  - Order: violations are minimized first, then restrictions, by the same kind/level order.
  - Every restriction is marked RESTRICTED at the proposition and listed under
    RESTRICTIONS, with the reading adopted and the reason the stronger one fails.
  - (Rev. 28 added a "minimal weakening" rule here as an explicitation. The rev. 28
    referee showed it is a new rule: it adds a maximality condition that decides between
    restrictions of equal cost. Withdrawn in rev. 29. Rejected by the user in rev. 30 on
    parsimony: a rule with no use is not kept.)
- Versions (rev. 19). The wording a reading must be admitted by belongs to a witness.
  - Witnesses are printed texts in the canonical languages:
    - German: the 1921 Annalen text, the 1922 printing, later editions;
    - English: Ogden 1922 and later impressions, Pears-McGuinness.
    Copies and transcriptions are not witnesses; they are checked against one. On hand: the
    1922 printing, German and Ogden.
  - No witness has priority a priori. Version choice is optimized under LI like any
    reading, in two stages, proposition by proposition:
    1. Selection: among the readings the witnesses admit, take the one least inconsistent
       with the system (violations, then restrictions, in the usual order). Ties keep all.
    2. Alignment: grade every other witness against the selected reading.
       - V0: the same wording.
       - V1: admits the reading plainly (translation variance).
       - V2: admits it only as a weak reading or under a special clause.
       - V3: contradicts it.
       The grade measures how much work it takes to align the versions.
  - Variants within one language (editions, impressions, translations) go through the same
    two stages.
  - Earmark rule:
    - V3 goes to research (text history, translation) before the reading is relied on.
    - V2 is noted at the proposition.
    - V0 and V1 need nothing.
    - A selection that rests on a witness not yet checked is provisional.
- Non-textual commitments have weight 0: they stay only while they cause no violation.
- LI+ (rev. 20; replaces "keep all tied branches"). LI is the primary criterion. If LI
  leaves a tie, subsidiary criteria apply in this order, each read against the goal:
  1. Fewer weight-0 commitments: the TLP then admits the system under weaker conditions.
  2. Fewer axioms (A) for the same coverage, since the goal asks for a minimal spanning
     set.
  3. Lower alignment cost across witnesses (fewer V2, no V3), so the result depends less
     on which witness is read.
  4. In the absence of countervailing evidence, the 1922 printing is canonical. This is
     used only if 1-3 leave a tie (rev. 21).
  If a tie survives:
  - Congruent options have the same deductive closure, i.e., the same models (rev. 24;
    before, "the same minimal spanning set"). They may differ in restriction marks, in
    wording, or in which of two interderivable statements is the axiom. The choice is
    recorded, and any one is taken.
  - Incongruent options yield two different minimal spanning sets. That is a HIGH ALERT:
    both systems are recorded in full and adjudicated at the end of the exercise.
  The order of the subsidiary criteria is itself a discretionary decision (DECISIONS,
  X0).
- Axioms and derivations (rev. 21). An axiom (A) is independent. A derivation (D) claims
  only to follow from its premises. If a derivation turns out incongruent with an axiom
  and the incongruence cannot be resolved (its derivation fails, or it contradicts an
  axiom), the axiom holds and the derivation is suspended. That is a HIGH ALERT.
- Robustness: kind-first, level-first and a plain count all give the same resolutions
  below. The kind-first choice matters only for a future conflict between a deep
  definition or limit and a shallow assertion. Re-verified in rev. 31 for X1-X23 (E11).
  So no current outcome depends on how a proposition's kind is tagged. Rev. 37: except
  X29. There the conflict arose: under a level-first order, alternatives (i) and (iii)
  would win (no marks at levels 0-1). X29 depends on the kind-first order. Rev. 45:
  X29 Q2 is reopened (X40, E23); alternative (i) would win under every order. Rev. 46:
  decided (X41). (i) wins kind-first, level-first and on a plain count, given J-apriori
  and 6.113's type reading; on a plain count without them, K would win. Rev. 48: X43
  (the token rule) also depends on the kind-first order: a plain count picks the loose
  rule (1 mark against 2). The kind-first order is PRINCIPLE's; until rev. 50 the ledger
  mislabeled it "X0's", but X0 orders LI+'s subsidiary criteria. Rev. 51 (X46): the
  robustness claim is replaced by a check per decision. X41 and X43 hold kind-first and
  level-first; a plain count picks K (without J-apriori and 6.113's type reading) and the
  loose rule. X43 rests on 3.325 s2 being DEF or on both of its own marks lying below
  kind 2 (X45's tag dependence assumed 4.1272's mark at kind 2). Rev. 57: X51 holds
  kind-first and on a plain count; level-first picks identity maps (V0); kind-first it
  rests on 5.2522's third member being DEF.

- A8e: rejected. With infinite A it fixes |A| = aleph_0 (COROLLARY), violating 4.128 and
  5.453 (assertions, 3). 3.33 says syntax "must admit of being established without mention
  being thereby made of the meaning of a sign". That is the plain reading of A8; the
  effective reading strengthens it beyond its wording, so it is not a reading. (Until
  rev. 15 this was a restriction of a word, "decidable", that 3.33 does not contain.)
- "Sense" includes the two limiting senses (null sense). "Without sense" in 4.461 is the null
  sense, which says nothing (RESTRICTED); 4.4611's analogy with 0 admits this reading. Then 4.5(iii)
  holds for every symbol, and D10 needs no exception. The alternative leaves out 4.5(iii)
  (assertion, 1).
- A11 (calculability: 5.551, 6.126, 6.127) and A12 (complete general description: 5.526)
  are adopted. They are consistent with everything kept, and leaving them out costs four
  assertions at level 3.
  A12 follows the wording of 5.526: "the world", i.e., the actual world. The every-world
  strengthening is not a reading of 5.526. It would also collapse against 4.128 and 5.453:
  for full frames it forces |A| = aleph_0 (THEOREM 3). So it is not adopted, and A11 stays
  independent. (Rev. 33: A12 is D12. The every-world version is A17, read plainly from
  5.5262's second sentence (X25). Its aleph_0 effect is a J6 mark, and A11 stays
  independent (B4).)
- Infinite vs. finite A: infinite. Finite A leaves out 4.5 (assertion, 1) and 4.463
  (assertion, 3: "unendlichen" sits in an assertion, though the proposition is tagged
  DEF). Infinite A only restricts 5.5262 (RESTRICTED). (Rev. 34: withdrawn, X26.)
- Forms: THEOREM 3 (rev. 14), a condition on frames. For full frames: O finite (infinitely
  many forms), or O infinite with finitely many forms, all 1-place. A13 (rev. 19) excludes
  the second branch.
- Pi: natural (S3, from 5.473). A gappy Pi is a non-textual commitment. Consequence:
  D10 <-> A7.
- Exclusive quantifiers (5.53): weak (free-variable) exclusion (RESTRICTED). The strong
  reading makes closed propositions context-dependent, against 5.54 (assertion, 2), and
  makes A11 fail.
- Operations (5.2522, 6.01): the substitution reading (6.01 with 5.501 kind 2 and 3.315).
  Under weak exclusion it keeps A11 (Lemma U), so 4.1273 is not violated.
- 2.0121 (rev. 19): read plainly, every object can combine with other objects ("seiner
  Verbindung mit anderen" / "its connexion with other things"). Its REM tag had dropped
  that content. The system stays consistent with it (B1', B3), so LI adopts it as A13. A3
  follows from it and becomes D3. Cost of the alternative: 2.0121 left out (assertion, 4).
- Versions (rev. 19): see EARMARKS, D1 and E6, for the selections and grades.
- E12 (rev. 23): how many objects a state of affairs combines. Three options, all without
  violations, compared by their restrictions (kind first, then level):
  - Grounding (corrected in rev. 24 by the referee). A bare generic plural is
    number-neutral (X13). So the case rests on the reciprocal and collective predicates,
    which need two distinct objects:
    - 2.031 "verhalten sich ... zueinander" (relate to one another; DEF, 3);
    - 2.03 "ineinander, wie die Glieder einer Kette" (hang one in another, like the
      members of a chain);
    - 2.032 "zusammenhaengen" (hang together; DEF, 3);
    - 2.14 and 2.15 (DEF, 2): a picture's elements "zu einander verhalten" (relate to one
      another), and by 2.13 each stands for one object (rho injective);
    - 4.0311 (DEF, 4): "ein Name ... fuer ein Ding, ein anderer fuer ein anderes Ding und
      untereinander sind sie verbunden" (one name for one thing, another for another, and
      they are connected).
    2.01 and 2.0272 are compatible but do not carry it on the plural alone.
  - (alpha) 1-place forms allowed. Each of the definitions above must be read as a
    degenerate one-object case: DEF-level restrictions on 2.031, 2.032, 2.0272, 4.22,
    2.14, 2.15 and 4.0311, plus 2.01, 2.03, and arguably 3.14.
  - (beta) At least two places, one object repeated allowed (R(a, a)). The diagonal states
    need the same DEF-level restrictions, 4.22 included. The sign of R(a, a) has one name
    (rho acts on sign types, 3.203; identity of object is identity of sign, 5.53). 4.24
    and 5.47 are restricted too.
  - (gamma) At least two distinct objects. No DEF-level restriction. Restricted:
    - 4.24 (NOT, 2): "fx" is schematic. Which forms occur is not given a priori
      (5.554-5.557). Under A6a and 5.5542, a sign set up as the form "fx" would itself be
      a one-object state.
    - 5.47 (assertion, 2; added rev. 24): "'fa' sagt dasselbe wie ..." reads fa as an
      elementary proposition with one name. It is read schematically (fa = R(a, b) taken
      as a function of a, 3.318), and the argument of 5.47 survives.
    5.531-5.532's "f(a, a)" needs nothing, because f need not be elementary. For an
    elementary f, f(a, a) is outside the frame: no proposition (C-nv, rev. 32; it was
    "false by the convention" under C-false).
  (gamma) wins kind-first, level-first (at level 2 it has 2 restrictions against at least
  5), and on a plain count. LI adopts (gamma) as A14. It is a clear decision, not a tie
  (DECISIONS, X18).
  - 4.1274 (UNS, 4): "Man kann also z. B. nicht fragen: 'Gibt es unanalysierbare
    Subjekt-Praedikatsaetze?'" (one cannot ask whether there are unanalysable
    subject-predicate propositions). This is the question A14 settles. It is not
    violated: its content is that no proposition answers the question, and A14 is a frame
    axiom, not a proposition. A1 and 4.1272 are read the same way. It is the only text
    that could flip E12.
  - 2.0131 does not count against A14. 6.3751 makes colour ascriptions non-elementary, and
    "Der Raumpunkt ist eine Argumentstelle" puts location in a relational form.
  - A14 restricts no special form: it comes from the general concept of the elementary
    proposition (5.555: "einen Begriff, abgesehen von seiner besonderen logischen
    Form"), so 5.554-5.557 are kept.
- E13 (rev. 24): 2.02331. Three options:
  - (A) The plain reading, adopted as A15. "Eigenschaften" unqualified; "eine
    Beschreibung" one finite sign; "ueberhaupt unmoeglich ... zu zeigen" is pointing by
    any means, naming included; the either/or exhaustive. No restriction; one axiom added.
  - (B) "Eigenschaften" narrowed to name-free definable (external) properties and
    "zeigen" to "single out by description": a restriction on 2.02331 (5), no axiom
    added.
  - (C) 2.02331 left out: a violation (5).
  Restrictions are counted before LI+ counts axioms, so (A) wins. No tie (X20). The old
  tag's "(finite O)" qualified a biconditional that fails even for finite O (alpha, beta;
  FORMAL NOTES), so it was an unmarked restriction that did not even rescue its claim.
- Violations: none. The two former residual violations (5.5262, 5.152) are retained under
  special clauses (rev. 34: 5.5262's clause withdrawn, X26). (Rev. 13 wrongly took 5.152's general clause to be absent from the text;
  rev. 15 restores it from the 1922 scans.)

RESTRICTIONS (each also marked at the proposition)
  (3.33: withdrawn in rev. 15. Its wording, "established without mention being thereby
          made of the meaning of a sign", is already the reading A8 uses; see LI
          RESOLUTION, A8e.)
  4.128,  (rev. 29; J6, X22) "Darum gibt es in der Logik keine ausgezeichneten Zahlen" / "Es
  5.453   gibt keine ausgezeichneten Zahlen". Read as: no number is pre-eminent among
          logical forms, and no number of objects or forms is fixed. The countability of
          completely general signs still singles out aleph_0 for what they can fix or name:
          - A12: on a B3 frame, a world with infinitely many true and infinitely many false
            pairs satisfies A12 only if |O| = aleph_0 (A12's CM is the aleph_1 case);
          - D15: at most aleph_0 objects are fixed (gamma_omega1);
          - A16: |O| <= aleph_0.
          The plain reading would leave out A12 (four assertions at level 3, X5). Until
          rev. 29 this was unmarked (the THEOREM's "no finite number" gloss).
          Rev. 50 (X45): current grounds. A16 caps |O| at aleph_0, and A17 excludes Phi ⊔
          eta_0 (aleph_1 one-state forms), which satisfies every other axiom (X36). Every
          option keeps A17, so the marks are incurred in every option. The plain reading
          would leave out A16 (5.526, level 3) and A17 (5.5262, level 4).
          Rev. 55 (X49): Phi ⊔ eta_0 fails A11 under J-N's adequate notation, so A17's
          ground lapses. A11 makes O and the forms countable (|A| = aleph_0), and A16 caps
          |O|; the marks are incurred in every option. The plain reading would leave out
          A16 (5.526, level 3) and A11 (5.551, 6.126, level 3).
  (5.526: restricted in rev. 28 to the objects that can be named apart; withdrawn in rev.
          29. The plain reading, A16, is adopted (X22).)
  5.47    (rev. 24) "Denn 'fa' sagt dasselbe wie '(Ex).fx.x = a'". The "fa" of the
          elementary proposition is read schematically: R(a, b) as a function of a
          (3.318). The plain one-name reading would need DEF-level restrictions (E12).
  4.24    (rev. 23) "Den Elementarsatz schreibe ich als Funktion der Namen in der Form:
          'fx', 'phi(x,y)', etc." The list of forms is notation; with A14 no elementary
          proposition has a single object, so "fx" stands schematically. The plain
          existential reading (monadic elementary propositions exist) would put DEF-level
          restrictions on 2.031, 2.032, 2.0272, 4.22, 2.14, 2.15 and 4.0311 (rev. 24 list),
          and would specify a form a priori against 5.554. Rev. 24: the restriction is
          necessary, not cautious: under A6a and 5.5542 a sign set up as the form "fx" is
          itself a one-object state.
  4.461   "without sense" = the null sense (says nothing). "No sense at all" would contradict
          4.5(iii) ("every symbol ... can express a sense"). 4.4611's 0 analogy supports the
          null sense. Rev. 19: the same reading applies to every "sinnlos" in the text:
          5.132, 5.1362, 5.5351. German and English agree (V1).
  5.152   (LIFTED in rev. 44 by version selection; final in rev. 45, R3b; X39. Record
          follows.)
          "Independent propositions (e.g. any two elementary propositions) give to one
          another the probability 1/2" (1922, German and Ogden alike: "Von einander
          unabhaengige Saetze (z. B. irgend zwei Elementarsaetze) ..."): holds for
          propositions of prior 1/2, as in W's example. The general clause contradicts 5.15:
          P(r v s | p) = 3/4.
  5.53   exclusive quantifiers in the weak sense (only the values of variables free in the
          scope; rev. 40, X35: and of names in the scope). Level 2 (rev. 40 correction). Strong exclusion makes closed propositions context-dependent (against
          5.54) and logic undecidable (against A11; Lemma U).
  5.5262  (WITHDRAWN in rev. 34; record follows) special clause: a change in a proposition's
          truth alters the general structure
          whenever some count it changes is finite. This is the sense of W's parenthesis
          ("one more elementary proposition true"). The general minimal-change reading fails
          for infinite A, where a flip can yield an isomorphic world.
          Rev. 33 (X25): first sentence only, and provisional. The premise above has lapsed:
          under C-nv the strong reading holds in zeta. The plain reading is MC-all. It is
          kept restricted unless E19 finds a model where MC-all costs nothing. The second
          sentence is not restricted: it is A17.
          WITHDRAWN in rev. 34 (X26): Phi is a non-rigid model of everything with MC-all, so
          MC-all costs nothing. 5.5262 is read plainly (S1: A18; S2: A17).
  2.173   (rev. 46; X41) "Das Bild stellt sein Objekt von ausserhalb dar ..., darum stellt das
          Bild sein Objekt richtig oder falsch dar". Kept: no picture is its own object
          (A6s). The material reading (A6d) and the bipolar "darum" fail for s and p v s,
          which have sense and are true wherever their sign exists.
  2.224   (rev. 46; X41) "Aus dem Bild allein ist nicht zu erkennen, ob es wahr oder falsch
          ist". Read for the picture as a token (J-tok: 2.223, 2.141). Kept: the type
          reading, that no picture's sense fixes its truth value (contingency). s and p v s
          are self-settling. (An exception clause for signs self-settling under every
          projection has the same frame models under A6s and A7; LI+2 drops it.)
  5.5321  (rev. 47; X42) "Und der Satz nur Ein x befriedigt f( ) lautet: (Ex).fx :
          ~(Ex, y).fx.fy". Kept: it says "only one" where the doubled instances have
          sense. Under X31's token rule (no binder shares a name's token) the sign is a
          tautology for f = Cyc ("x is in a 2-cycle") in Phi, though a and b both satisfy
          f. A cost of the token model, shared by every option (E25: a looser rule).
          Rev. 48 (X43): the mark covers both formulas; "statt (x): fx ⊃ x = a" has no
          sense for a and h in Phi under the strict rule. The loose rule would lift it but
          restricts 3.325 (DEF, 3), so the strict rule stays. Rev. 51 (X46): weighed
          (assertion, 4): the mark narrows the claim that the formulas say what the words
          say, an assertion about expression, not the notation.
  4.1272  (rev. 48; X43) "Zum Beispiel in dem Satz 'es gibt 2 Gegenstaende, welche ...'
          durch '(Ex, y) ...'". Kept: "there are n objects which phi" is sayable where the
          n-fold instances fit. Under X31's strict token rule, (Ex, y)(Cyc x . Cyc y) is
          false in Phi though a and b both satisfy Cyc. The same cost as 5.5321's. Rev. 51
          (X46): weighed (assertion, 4): the mark narrows the sentence on expression ("Wo
          immer das Wort Gegenstand ... richtig gebraucht wird ...", with its example), not
          a limit sentence.
  5.24    (rev. 57; X51) "(Und das Gemeinsame zwischen den Basen und dem Resultat der
          Operation sind eben die Basen.)" Kept: for operations that keep their bases
          (truth-operations, 5.234). Under variabilization (3.315), which 4.1273's series
          needs (aRb to (Ex)(aRx . xRb)), base and result share the base's form. The plain
          reading forbids name variabilization (V0): it narrows 5.2522's third member (DEF,
          4), 4.1273 (assertion, 4) and 5.501's kind-3 unit (assertion, 3). Weighed
          (assertion, 2), kind-first; level-first would pick (V0). Ground J-5.24 (R).
  (4.5(iii), (rev. 37; X29, HIGH ALERT #2; LIFTED in rev. 46, X41: D10 holds) "jedes Symbol,
          worauf die Beschreibung passt, einen
  5.473   Sinn ausdruecken kann, wenn die Bedeutungen der Namen entsprechend gewaehlt werden";
          "Ein moegliches Zeichen muss auch bezeichnen koennen". Read as: a symbol can
          express a sense if some admissible choice of meanings exists. p v s (s :=
          (E phi)(Ex, y) phi xy, p of s's arity) has none under A6d, since s's support
          contains p's medium under every projection.)
  (5.5261 (rev. 37; X29, M+; LIFTED in rev. 46, X41: s has sense) "(Ex, phi).phi x": the
          composition claim holds. The example
          holds schematically: its binary instance (E phi)(Ex, y) phi xy has no sense,
          because it is true wherever its own sign exists (A6d with the whole sign as
          medium).)
  (5.5262: see the entry above; withdrawn in rev. 34. The entry is a dated record.)
  (5.557: withdrawn in rev. 19. The German reads "welche Elementarsaetze es gibt" (which
          elementary propositions there are), so "which ones" is the plain reading, and

X20 A15 (E13, rev. 24): 2.02331 read plainly. Options:
    - (A) Adopt the plain reading as A15: no restriction, one added axiom.
    - (B) Narrow "Eigenschaften" to definable properties and "zeigen" (point) to "single
      out by description": a restriction on 2.02331, plus an axiom unless A15'' ("unique
      type => describable") is derivable. It is derivable for finite O with countably many
      forms per arity and in bounded-orbit frames, open in A11 frames (rev. 25; rev. 24
      said "no added axiom").
    - (C) Leave 2.02331 out: a violation (assertion or limit, 5).
    - (B1) (rev. 25, from the referee) "Eigenschaften" = external properties (the facts)
      only, "zeigen" plain. Under S3 names see the frame (a sign whose projection leaves
      the frame has no sense), so in alpha a and c are named apart although they share
      all external properties. Horn 2 is then not a theorem: (B1) needs two axioms, A15'
      ("fixed by Aut(M+) => describable"; beta fails it) and H2' ("objects with the same
      external properties are Aut(H, C, chi*)-conjugate"; alpha fails it). Together they
      imply A15; A15 does not imply H2'. If (B1) were as plain as (A), LI+2 picks (A).
    LI counts restrictions before LI+ counts axioms, so (A) wins over (B) and (C). No tie.
    Provisional (rev. 25): the de re reading (E16) is not costed. Admissibility
    judgments, logged (J2, J4, J5 added in rev. 25; see A15):
    - Horn 1 works through external properties. A description describes an object by
      its external properties (4.023), and internal ones cannot be ascribed (4.1241, UNS).
    - "Entweder ... oder aber" is exhaustive.
    - "ueberhaupt unmoeglich ... zu zeigen" and "durch nichts hervorgehoben" mean by any
      means at all, naming included, not only by description.
    Together these exclude a thing that is internally distinct but externally
    indiscernible, which is A15. Near-alert and candidate: see HIGH ALERT. Provisional
    status lifted by X21 (rev. 26).
X21 E16 (rev. 26; corrected rev. 27 by the referee): the de re readings of 2.02331,
    costed against (A) = A15.
    - (M+) internal properties qualitative (form = Aut(H, C)-orbit); external properties
      de re, from positive facts only: the functions phi(., y) obtained from facts
      phi(o, y) by replacing o (3.318). Twins := same form, same such properties.
      - Horn 1 gives A15m (an object whose profile no other has is fixed and singled out
        by one description, names allowed); B3 (all true) fails it.
      - Horn 2 gives H2m (twins are conjugate). It is not a theorem: epsilon satisfies
        A1-A14 and A15m but not H2m. So (M+) needs two axioms and loses at LI+2.
      - (M+) is an artifact of 2.01231's DEF, which took "obtaining states" only.
    - (M±) (rev. 27, from the referee) the same, but with facts as in 2.06 ("positive"
      and "negative Tatsache"): the profile of o is pi(o) = {(s[o := x], chi*(s)) : s a
      state containing o}. A property is had only where its ascription has sense (S3).
      - Horn 2 is a theorem (Lemma T, FORMAL NOTES): twins share no state, and swapping
        them is in Aut(H, C, chi*), so they cannot be named apart.
      - Horn 1 gives A15dr: if chi* is actual, an object whose profile pi no other object
        shares is fixed by Aut(H, C, chi*) and singled out by one description, which may
        contain names.
      - Independent: B3 fails A15dr (each 2n is the only object with
        (R(., 2n+1), true); none is fixed). Consistent: B1'' with chi* = {R_0(a, b)}.
      - Textual cost: none found (2.0233, 2.01231, 2.0231, 2.06, 3.318, 4.023, 4.122,
        5.02 "Der Caesar aus dem Geschlechte der Julier", 5.5301, 5.5302). Both are V1.
    - (F) fully de re (internal properties tied to objects too). Corrected reason
      (rev. 27; rev. 26 said "vacuous", which is false: r_1 and s_1 in epsilon would
      share all internal properties):
      - with form = orbit (2.0233's DEF), same-form objects with different possible
        partners (p_1, p_2) differ internally, so 2.0233 is false: a violation (DEF, 4);
      - with form de re (2.0141 literally), the cost moves to the orbit DEF and to 2.0251
        (forms many objects share): at least one restriction.
      Either way LI drops (F). (Formally, (F) with de re form has the same twins as (M±).)
    - Outcome on 2.02331 alone:
      - (A) and (M±) are both admissible (4.123: "schwankenden Gebrauch"). Each has no
        violation, no restriction, and one axiom (the horn-1 axiom; horn 2 is a theorem).
      - LI ties. LI+1 ties (same commitments), LI+2 ties (1 against 1), LI+3 ties (V1
        both), LI+4 ties (same printing).
      - The two are incongruent. B3 satisfies A15 (vacuously) and fails A15dr. beta
        satisfies A15dr (a is "the x with (E phi) phi(x, b)", and b is fixed, so it can
        be named) and fails A15.
      - HIGH ALERT #1. Both systems are recorded (HIGH ALERT).
    - Counting convention, discretionary and logged: for LI+2 an option's axioms are
      counted per horn of the text, each horn being a theorem or an axiom. Splitting one
      statement into independent parts is not unique (phi = (phi v psi).(phi v ~psi)), so
      it is not counted. It was first used for (B1) in rev. 25. A count by conjuncts
      would favor (A) (A15dr splits into "unique => fixed", which B3 fails, and "fixed =>
      describable", which alpha fails), but it is the ill-defined count.
    - Uncounted: 5.526's second sentence (E15). It bears on the alert:
      - read universally ("every object is reached this way"), it is an axiom A16 that
        implies both A15 and A15dr, and the two systems become congruent. But A16 bounds
        |O| <= aleph_0 (completely general descriptions are countably many), which is
        the kind of cost the ledger charged A8e with (4.128, 5.453);
      - restricted to the objects that can be named apart, it is A15 itself: a theorem in
        System I, an extra axiom in System II;
      - restricted to "where such an expression exists", it costs neither system.
      So E15 can decide the alert or leave it. It is LI on further text, not the final
      adjudication.

    - Readings:

      So 4.128 and 5.453 are restricted in every option, and A16's cap |O| <= aleph_0 adds
      no new mark. Without J6 nothing is marked. The two policies give the same axioms and

        28 also misstated the A8e precedent, whose charge was "fixes |A| = aleph_0".
      - Rev. 28's further possible cost ("A16 with A11 forces O finite") is withdrawn.
        zeta is a model of A1-A14 and A16 with |O| = aleph_0 (A11 there is a sketch).
        Bounded orbits do force O finite, but A11 does not need them.

        Glieder Saetze sind"), and under S3 an instance outside the frame is no

        - Quantifier shifts such as (Ex)(phi x v psi x) = (Ex)phi x v (Ex)psi x fail when
          frames differ; no proposition states them.

          not saying (6.12, 6.124: "es etwas ueber die Welt anzeigen muss, dass gewisse

      - S3: "(Wenn ein Elementarsatz wahr ist, so ist damit doch jedenfalls Ein
        Elementarsatz mehr wahr.)"
    - S2 (judgment, logged): a claim about logical space.
      - "Spielraum" is a range of possibilities (4.463).
      - "Gesamtheit der Elementarsaetze" has no "wahren"; W adds it when he means truth
        values (4.26). Inserting it would be a strengthening.
      - "ihrem Bau" refers back to S1's general structure.
      - So the range of possible general structures is the range that completely general
        propositions delimit: A17, every-world A12, up to two-sorted isomorphism. V1.
      - The weak reading ("same space") makes S2 a theorem, which drops its content
        (X13, X22-(W)).
      - The draft's actual-world exact reading is refuted: even with truth values, "Bau"
        gives only the isomorphism class.
      - A17: consistent (zeta, alpha, B1''); independent (CM eta). Strictly stronger than
        D12 given A1-A16 (beta_A, uncountable A; countable A open). No new mark (J6).
        A12 becomes D12.
    - S1 (judgment, logged; close call): MC-all, the plain reading. For every
      proposition p, every minimal alteration of chi* that changes p changes the general
      truths. "veraendert ... jedes Satzes" is a ceteris-paribus comparison, and S3
      performs one (cf. 1.21).
      - Exact determination of chi* (the draft's R2-AW) also lets other propositions
        change, so it is a strengthening. In any case, with A16 it costs a restriction of
        5.5302 (it makes every model rigid on objects).
      - Narrower readings (single flips, finite alterations) narrow "jedes Satzes":
        restrictions.
      - Order: exact => MC-all => finite alterations => single flips. B1'' with one fact,
        and B1'' "polar", separate them.
    - Costs:
      - Vacuity caused by axioms is no mark (2.0233, 2.02331 horn 2; as under A16).
      - 5.5302 ("hat doch Sinn": indiscernibles possible) is restricted if every model is
        rigid on objects.
      - 5.135/2.062: chi* constant on state orbits is a condition on chi*, not an
        inference within Lambda (the A15 precedent). No mark; judgment logged.
    - LI (axioms counted per textual unit):
      - O1: R0 + A17. One restriction (5.5262 S1); no axiom added beyond A17.
      - O4: MC-all + A17. No mark if some non-rigid model satisfies everything, else one
        restriction (5.5302); one axiom more.
      - O5: exact + A17. One restriction (5.5302); one axiom more; a strengthening anyway.
      If a non-rigid model exists, O4 wins outright. Otherwise O1, O4 and O5 tie at one
      level-4 restriction, and LI+2 picks O1. No HIGH ALERT either way.
      - The candidate non-rigid model is Phi (the referee's): a Cohen-generic colouring
        on a frame with marker forms. A11 there is unchecked: E19.
      - Until E19 is settled, O1 stands: 5.5262 S1 stays restricted (R0), and A17 is
        adopted.
    - Near-alert, logged: if S2's weak or truth-valued reading were judged plain, exact
      determination co-plain, and MC-all forced rigidity, then R0 [5.5262 R; A12] and
      exact [5.5302 R; exact] would tie through LI+4. They are incongruent (B1'' with one
      fact separates them): trigger (1). Rev. 34: void, since MC-all does not force
      rigidity (Phi).
    - Ledger corrections:
      - 5.5302's tag was not a valid derivation (zeta and alpha are rigid models). It is

        A17 fail. Proposed: B1'' with C = {~(R_i(a, b) . R_i(b, a)) : i in N} and chi* =
        {R_0(a, b)} (own; checked in E19).

X26 E19 (rev. 34; refereed): 5.5262 S1 (MC-all) costs nothing, so it is adopted as A18.
    - MC-all: if chi* is actual, then for every proposition p, every minimal alteration of
      chi* that changes p changes the completely general truths. It implies MC-fin (no
      finite alteration of chi* is an isomorph), via p := ~(the alteration's literals on
      the difference) and A7. The converse fails (B1'' "polar").
    - Consistent: zeta (all true), alpha (all false), Phi. Independent: B1'' with chi* =
      {R_0(a, b)}. No axiom becomes derivable; no derivation is incongruent.
    - Phi, a non-rigid model:
      - Frame and chi*: O = {h, h', a, b} plus {o_i : i >= 1}. Forms R_i, each with the
        states R_i(a, b), R_i(b, a) and R_i(h, o_i). Marker forms f_{i,j} (j <= i), each
        with the one state f_{i,j}(h', o_i). chi*: R_i(a, b) true iff i in S, R_i(b, a)
        true iff i in T, the rest true. (S, T) is Cohen-generic over a countable model
        containing the codes of all propositions.
      - Aut(H, C) = {id, (a b)} x the products of Sym(i) on the markers. Aut(H, C, chi*)
        consists of the marker permutations only.
      - A1-A17 hold at all kinds; A11 by profiles and Lemma U_v. Kind-3 series cannot
        compare marker counts across units, so no arithmetic is interpreted.
      - MC-all holds. The only isomorph other than chi* is (a b).chi*, and its difference
        is infinite. Decide p at (a b).chi* (which is generic too) on a finite support. A
        finite change of chi* matching it there is a proper sub-alteration that already
        changes p.
      - Corrections to the draft: the decision is taken at (a b).chi*, not at chi*. All
        markers must be true. Genericity is needed: S = N, T empty fails MC-all.
      - The frame keeps (a b), so 5.5302 keeps its possibility.
    - LI: O4 (MC-all + A17) has no mark; O1 (R0) has one restriction. LI decides before
      LI+2 counts the added axiom. 5.5262 is read plainly and leaves RESTRICTIONS.
      X25's near-alert premise ("MC-all forces rigidity") is false.
    - CMs rebuilt (CORE AXIOMS, current list):
      - the B1''-based CMs move to alpha with chi* all false, since B1'' with one fact
        fails A18;
      - A17's CM is eta_0; zeta_omega fails A18 by a two-atom form transposition;
      - eta_0 also replaces beta_A as the uncountable-A witness.
      - The smallest model is O = {a, b} with single-state forms R_i(a, b) and chi* all
        false.
    - Rests on X25's S1 judgment and on the compositional semantics of series (as zeta's
      A11).
    [own draft; refereed, rev. 34]

X27 E2, closed as scoped (rev. 35; refereed). Scope (user, rev. 35): what the goal needs,
    not a classification of the frames that satisfy A11. The system has models, and
    THEOREM 3 states the conditions on frames. (Two drafts, one from a turn cut off by the
    usage limit, are folded in here.)
    - (a_k*) The projection condition, for forms of any arity and sparse frames.
      - Statement: for each arity k, slot pair (i, j) and equality pattern pi of the other
        slots, the union over all k-place forms of their pattern-pi projections to (i, j)
        contains K_{n,n} with disjoint sides for only finitely many n.
      - Proof: E''(x, y) := (E phi)(Ez1)... phi(..). Weak exclusion makes the z's distinct
        from x, y and from each other. Every subgraph G of the union projection is E'' in
        some world: make true one witness state per pair of G and nothing else. Read back
        with Vert(x) := (Ey)Adj(x, y), guarding the empty case. Then THEOREM 3 (a)'s
        incidence encoding and Trakhtenbrot-Vaught inseparability apply. Fullness is not
        used.
      - The union is needed: forms f_{m,n} with the one state f_{m,n}(m, n) each have a
        one-pair projection, but their union is the complete digraph, so A11 fails at
        kind 2. Merging finitely many patterns or arities is equivalent (disjunction plus
        bipartite Ramsey).
      - Under C-nv: Adj's two-atom matrix has sense exactly at common frame-neighbours,
        and Adj is false (E1) where there are none, which is the right "no edge". C-nv
        agrees with C-false for atoms and conjunctions, but not for disjunctive matrices
        ((Ex)(Rxc v Sxc) is false under C-nv when S(1, c) is outside the frame).
      - The names: the encoding sentences contain none, so "given the names" supplies no
        input.
    - (b_k) The incidence condition (new; the referee's). For each arity and pattern, the
      incidence between forms and frame tuples contains K_{n,n} for only finitely many n.
      - Proof: forms as vertices, tuples as edges. Vert(phi) := (Ex)phi x and
        Adj(phi, psi) := (Ex)(phi x . psi x). Every finite graph is realizable, then
        Trakhtenbrot-Vaught.
      - Witness, B3-forms: matching pairs (2n, 2n+1), forms R_i (i in N) each on every
        pair. It meets (a_k*) and (d), and fails A11 at kind 2.
      - So THEOREM 3's remark that (b) "does not arise in the adopted system" (A14) was
        wrong in substance: the mechanism carries over to k-place forms.
    - (d) The frame's own theory (kinds 1-3) is decidable. Necessary under C-nv.
      - St(phi; t) := (Ez)((phi t v ~phi t) . (Gamma z v ~Gamma z)), where Gamma is any
        general proposition in z with sense at every z. It holds iff t is a phi-state and
        some object lies outside t; that needs O infinite or larger than the arity.
      - Negations and quantifiers stay unrelativized, and kind 3 is compositional. A
        translated frame sentence is the same in every world (S1), so it is a tautology or
        a contradiction. The translation is computable; which of the two it is is exactly
        the undecidable part. So A11 implies (d).
      - Finite O: (d) still holds through form counts ("at least m k-place forms" is
        kind 2).
      - (d) already bites at kind 2: O = N, one binary form, frame = disjoint finite paths
        whose lengths form a non-recursive set L. "There is a maximal frame path of
        exactly n edges" is a tautology iff n is in L. That frame meets (a_k*) and (b_k).
      - (c) is an instance, not a separate condition: B4's frame is (N, S), which at kind
        3 interprets arithmetic, so it fails (d) at kind 3. At kinds 1-2 it is
        decidable.
    - Not sufficient: S(K_omega), the subdivided complete graph.
      - O = M plus {e_ij}; one binary form with the states R(m_i, e_ij) and R(m_j, e_ij).
        Adj(u, v) := (Ee)(Rue . Rve) is an arbitrary graph on M across worlds, so A11
        fails at kind 2.
      - Its frame has no K_{2,2} and one form, and Sym(M) is oligomorphic, so (a_k*),
        (b_k) and (d) hold at all kinds.
      - It also refutes the inference in FORMAL NOTES for gamma ("no two objects share two
        partners, so THEOREM 3 (a) does not bite") as a ground for A11.
      - General form: A11 fails whenever a fixed kind-2 interpretation realizes, across
        worlds, a class with an undecidable or Trakhtenbrot-Vaught-inseparable theory.
        That is A11 restated, so no simple test is expected.
    - The grid (my draft): refuted as written. With a fixed number m of colour forms only
      finitely many tile sets fit. Repaired by block coding with H and V alone (the corner
      is definable), it fails A11 at kinds 1-2. At kind 3 it fails (d) (the x-axis is a
      copy of (N, S)), so it separates nothing for the adopted A11.
    - Sufficient side: the Lemma U_v class plus a per-frame check at kinds 1-2. This is a
      reduction, not a test.
    - Consistency and independence are unaffected. In alpha, eta_0 and the smallest model
      O is finite. In zeta each form has one state. In Phi only (a, b) and (b, a) are shared
      (at most K_{2, infinity}), with no pair-specific connectors. The countermodels are
      unchanged.
    - E8 leftover (C-false vs C-nv): the path-forest frame is a candidate separator. My
      draft claimed that under C-false tautologyhood does not depend on L. That is too
      quick: "every object is in a fact" constraints make realizability depend on L
      (for example, whether L meets [1, n-1]). A separation would need an L for which all
      such tests are uniform. Unchecked; nothing depends on it.

X28 E3 math (rev. 36; refereed): inclusive formal series into weakly exclusive ones.
    - Setting. Under weak exclusion every subformula is evaluated at an assignment that
      gives its free variables distinct values. Values on the diagonal come from
      substitution instances. Substitution lemma: phi[x := y] at s equals phi at
      s(x := s(y)). So "phi represents the inclusive chi" means agreement at all
      assignments, covering every equality pattern of the free variables.
    - Translation Tr (Hintikka; Rogers & Wehmeier, C16):
      - Tr((Ex) chi(x, y-bar)) := (Ex) Tr(chi) v the disjunction over i of
        Tr(chi)[x := y_i];
      - the same clause for form variables, with disjuncts [phi := psi_j];
      - if quantifiers also exclude named objects (the ledger was silent; rev. 40, X35:
        they do, N+), disjuncts
        [x := a] for the names in scope.
      Tr commutes with truth-functions and substitution, and preserves free variables.
    - Claim 1 (two-valued semantics: proved, and machine-checked on random formulas incl.
      nested series). Every inclusive formula without "=", of kinds 1-3, has a weakly
      exclusive equivalent in every structure, computably.
      - Series: for [a, xi, O'xi] with O' a fixed context (hole under substitutions,
        X10), Tr(O'(T)) and O'_Tr(Tr(T)) are syntactically identical, up to duplicate
        disjuncts and renaming. Syntactic identity is needed: under weak exclusion an
        equivalent filler can change what outer quantifiers exclude. O'_Tr takes its
        disjuncts over all variables declared in the hole.
      - Kind-2 brackets with parameters, infinite ones included: N over the exclusive
        bracket plus a finite enumeration of the instances.
    - Under C-nv (adopted), Claim 1 as first drafted is false. Substitution disjuncts
      such as Rxx have no sense under A14, and a truth-function with a senseless
      component has none, so the reachability translation collapsed to R (192 of 200
      frames). Repair: guard each disjunct, G(D) := (Ez)(D . (Gamma z v ~Gamma z)) with z
      fresh. It works when some object lies outside the free values, so whenever O is
      infinite (checked: 2431 formulas, 0 mismatches). For finite O the guard can fail,
      but there identity is countable (below).
    - Claim 2, corrected. "=" is no obstacle at kinds 1-2: there it is eliminable
      instance by instance. In series it is no obstacle either outside argument
      positions or in a base outside the recursion (R* = (x = y) v R+). The residue is
      "=" between argument variables of a series' function, under single series. There
      a weakly exclusive psi(x, y), false at distinct pairs with psi(x, x) true, is
      exactly what packing the patterns into one series needs. Sufficient conditions for
      psi:
      - O finite (counting; O is the same in every world, S1);
      - a definable relation with private partners: every x has a partner w ≠ x and no w
        partners two objects; then Id(u, v) := (Ew)(Fuw . Fvw). B4 all true is this;
        checked under C-nv;
      - "=" definable by an "="-free inclusive formula (Claim 1 then gives psi).
      "Any definable function" is not enough (a constant function).
      - psi fails to exist in an infinite pure set: every weakly exclusive formula is
        constant there, since the excluded set is finite. But every series there is
        eventually periodic, so no untranslatable sentence arises.
      - Whether some structure has an inclusive kind-3 sentence with no weakly
        exclusive equivalent: open.
    - Weiss (hedged; his text not on hand, quote [W2]). The equality obstacle as quoted
      does not arise for LF formulas that:
      - are "="-free, or
      - keep "=" out of series argument positions, or
      - are evaluated where psi exists.
      Whether this covers his Lemma 3.4 needs his text (research tier), as does whether
      "Wehmeier's 2004 semantics" is the ledger's weak exclusion. Hardness results
      transfer under these shapes; upper bounds transfer the other way only if LF has "=".
    - Ledger effects:
      - THEOREM 3 (c) stands; its translation step now cites Claim 1 with Id and the
        C-nv guards (O = N);
      - C11's proviso becomes a disjunction;
      - Lemma U's proof: the next term depends on the term set and the current term's
        free-variable set. The latter is fixed by syntax and eventually periodic, so the
        period bounds become B * 2^m (Lemma U) and 2^B(v) * 2^v (Lemma U_v). The
        conclusions are unchanged.
      - No effect on consistency, independence, the models or the countermodels.

X29 F1 (rev. 37; final math referee, then a referee of the draft): generality, the

          RESTRICTED (limit, 3). Containment does not rescue it: A6d already goes beyond
          containment (X2).
        - J-P: s's picture is the configuration of its tokens (2.14), and their obtaining
          settles s. So either 2.224, 2.225 (diagonal) and 6.113 (second sentence) are
          restricted (assertions, 3), or DEF 2.14 is marked.
        - M- also had a hole: "(Ey) R a y" with rho(a) = a's own token and tau(R) = the
          token's own form has medium {} yet is true wherever written.

        (self-settling), so its example holds only schematically.
      - Costs shared by both: 4.5(iii) and 5.473 (Q2).
      - LI: M+ (one assertion restriction at level 4) over M- (a limit restriction, plus
        assertions at level 3). Not a tie. My draft's "M+ has no model" was refuted:
        under M+ zeta (all true) still satisfies A1-A18, and Phi does in a sketch.
      - What M+ changes (the referee's; verified in E20):
        - A completely general sign has sense iff A6d holds of its whole sign. C-nv's "a
          general proposition always has sense" becomes "has sense iff its support
          misses its own tokens". Placing tokens elsewhere often restores sense; in zeta
          the count sentences for o_n can be written at o_m.

          that no meaning can be re-chosen.
        - Single-form classes fail even with constant relation signs (sketch: zeta plus

      - D10 as stated ("every well-formed sign expresses a sense under some admissible

X30 5.5302 (rev. 37; the audit and the X29 referee): A19 adopted.
    - Text: "Selbst wenn dieser Satz nie richtig ist, hat er doch Sinn." Plain reading:

X31 E20 (rev. 38; refereed): the system under M+ (X29) and A19 (X30).
    - Tokens (X29's M+ made precise; corrected by the referee). A sign fits a frame iff
      its letter pattern embeds into the frame minus the sentence's support:
      - one state per distinct atomic formula (repeated atoms share a token, D2);
      - object letters go injectively to objects, and the same letter gets the same
        object. Bound letters may be renamed, since the choice of letters is accidental
        (3.34);
      - form symbols (relation constants and form variables) go injectively to token
        forms: one tau per sign (S3), distinct symbols to distinct forms (3.325);
      - logical signs are not further atoms (4.0312; 5.4611 "Interpunktionen").
      Fitting is an embedding problem, not a count. Sparse frames constrain signs by
      shape as well as by support.
    - Orbit lemma (confirmed).
      - A completely general sentence's support is a union of Aut(H, C)-orbits of atoms.
        With names, the orbits are those of the group fixing the named objects. With C
        nonempty, dependence is on finite sets of atoms.
      - Under M+ it has sense iff its pattern embeds outside that union.
      - Ranges (C-nv) now also depend on whether tokens fit. They stay Aut-invariant.
      - Consequences:
        - M+ favors frames whose atoms fall into many small orbits.
        - Where one orbit fills all states of an arity, no contingent completely general
          sentence of that arity has sense. This is why B1'', alpha and the smallest
          model fail.
    - A19, guarded form (corrected). There are a world w and distinct objects o, o' such
      that, for every name-free formula Psi(x), Psi(o) has sense iff Psi(o') has sense,
      and where both do they have the same truth value in w.
      - Names are excluded: (E phi)(phi xb v ~phi xb) would tell a from b.
      - Sufficient: some sigma in Aut(H, C) moves an object and fixes some world (with
        A4, the all-false world). Not necessary: objects of the same L_T-type need not
        be automorphic (gamma's two centres).
      - With A5 and A16 the proposition is false at chi* ("nie richtig").
      - Whether one sentence of L_T expresses it: open. The naive form is a tautology
        under C-nv.

X32 E21a (rev. 39; refereed): Phi's A11 under M+. Proved at kinds 1-2; kind 3 open (X33).
    Rev. 55 (X49): under X41-X47 an outline (the local counts proved, R1, R2). Its use of
    the small named units exceeded J-N's input (an unlogged judgment).
    Setting. Phi (X26). Under M+, A11 is a promise problem: decide tautologyhood for the
    signs that have sense. Two new elements beyond rev. 34:
    - (S) whether a sign has sense (X31: some fitting sign exists, over alphabetic
      variants and token placements; not the sub-sign as placed inside a larger sign,
      so p v ~p has sense);
    - (R) ranges restricted by sense (C-nv: x ranges over the o for which Phi(o) has
      sense).
    Both are world-independent (supports are computed over Lambda; fitting is a frame
    property; A4 lets any finite token set be true together) and invariant under the
    stabilizer of the names. Names include relation constants.
    - Recursion: well-founded. At kinds 1-2 by formula size; at kind 3 by (series
      nesting, term index k, size), which is infinitary.
    - P1 (orbits): Stab(N)-orbits of atoms are finite and per unit. With form constants
      among the names, a named marker splits its unit's marker orbit.
    - P2 (uniformity), as corrected:
      - Realizable unit types (min(c, q), min(i - c, q)) are the same for all i >= 2q;
        single-flip transitions are the same for all i >= 2q + 1. (Not every type is
        realizable at every large i: a type with both counts < q occurs only at
        i = c + d. Machine-checked for q <= 6, i <= 200.)
      - Colours are k-ary (sense and range predicates of formulas with parameters). P2
        is stated for parameter tuples: tuples in large units with the same equality
        and incidence pattern get the same colours, with supports matched under index
        transport. n0 depends on q, on the letters (object and form) of the variants
        considered, and on the small named units, not on the names' indices.
      - With that, the induction closes. Fitting is uniform because large units have
        more markers than a pattern has form letters.
    - (S) and (R) decidable at kinds 1-2. The search runs over alphabetic variants
      (finitely many up to isomorphism; renaming can help or hurt). The large slots
      number object letters plus form letters. Ranges are finite exceptions plus a
      uniform tail, in every arity.
    - Kinds 1-2: tautologyhood is decidable. Truth is a first-order formula with
      quantifiers restricted to colour predicates and inequality guards. Ehrenfeucht-
      Fraisse runs with the hubs fixed, up to the a/b swap. Realizability is a finite
      matching problem. Every non-constant first-order sentence has nonempty flip-support.
    - Kind 3: gap (referee).
      - (i) Which series terms have sense is not decided. Example: a := p, O'(xi) := xi
        v s, with s's support all atoms. Then T_1, T_2, ... have no sense and
        N(series) = ~p.
      - (ii) Lemma U_v's per-world step T_{k+1} = F_w(T_k) fails under M+: ranges inside
        O'(T_k) depend on supports (computed over all worlds) and on fitting. The
        recursion must run on a global state.
      - (iii) n0 was given in rank q, which grows along a series. It must be restated
        in v.
      Repair route: X33.

X33 E21b (rev. 39; refereed): Phi's A11 at kind 3 under M+. Holds: tautologyhood and "has
    sense" are decidable for signs with formal series. Steps as corrected:
    - K1 (rank-free v-pebble uniformity). Each term of a v-letter series is a v-variable
      formula, and N over the series is a countable conjunction of them, so the game is
      the unbounded v-pebble game. Units meet only at h, h', a and b, so Duplicator
      answers a large unit with an unused unit of the same capped type.
      - Correction: when parameters or names pin p markers of a unit, capped types and
        their single-flip transitions are uniform only from i = 2v + p + 1 on
        (machine-checked for v <= 7, p <= v; exact). So n0(v) := 3v + 2. It depends on
        v only, not on k.
    - K2 (sense colours uniform from n0 on). Sense is world-independent, so a colour
      depends only on the tuple's frame pattern (which elements of which units;
      equality; incidence), not on world-dependent counts. Each T_k is a finite sign,
      so for a fixed term, fitting given the support summary is a finite search.
    - K3 (fitting): the embedding facts hold. Additional constraints:
      - one state per source per form, so phi xy . phi xz with y ≠ z never fits one form;
      - a letter in both slots goes to a or b;
      - at most one h-sourced form letter per target letter;
      - unit i holds at most i markers;
      - whether letters may be identified depends on liveness (where binders sit), not
        on shapes.
    - K4: my justification ("targets and forms in large units can be chosen fresh") was
      refuted.
      - Counterexample: sigma := "some unit has a true h-state, at least v true markers
        and at least v false markers" (names for h and h'). Its support is the units
        i >= 2v, so its tokens must sit in a unit with v <= i < 2v. It fits there,
        since its two blocks can share letters.
      - The series a := sigma, O'(xi) := sigma . xi makes every T_k equivalent to sigma.
        Its repeated atoms share tokens (D2), so every T_k fits. Fresh letters would
        need k distinct such units and would wrongly report "no sense" for k > v.
      - Letters must be shared across the context and the term where they do not
        conflict. The 4-source bound forces this.
    - Repair: a live-interface automaton.
      - Renaming lemma: a renaming of bound letters avoids capture iff no letter class
        contains a binder together with a variable free in its scope (machine-checked:
        1,701 formulas, 243,305 renamings, 0 mismatches).
      - Hence, given an availability set S, Fit(T; S) holds iff there is a map g from
        binders, free letters and names to frame elements such that:
        - every atom goes to an available state;
        - each binder's image differs from the images of the variables free in its
          scope;
        - names are mapped injectively and no binder shares a name's image.
        Every constraint involves live letters only, and at most v are live.
      - Acc_S(psi) := the images of psi's interface letters (free letters and names)
        that extend to such a g inside psi. Hubs and small-unit elements are exact;
        large-unit elements count only up to an equality pattern. This is finite and
        sound: there are infinitely many large units, S is uniform on them, and each has
        more than v markers.
      - Acc_S(O'[T]) is computed from Acc_S(T), O' and the substitution, as a bottom-up
        tree automaton.
      - state_k := (truth types of T_k; T_k's sense colours; the map S -> Acc_S(T_k)
        over the finitely many support summaries; T_k's free-variable set; rev. 40: and
        T_k's set of names, X35). The space is
        finite and computable, and state_{k+1} = F_{O'}(state_k) is computable.
      - So the states are eventually periodic, with preperiod + period <= |space|.
        N(series) = N over the terms with sense among the first preperiod + period
        terms. Nested series reduce from the inside. The series sign's own fit is a
        finite check.
      - A bare bound on distinct (truth, sense, fit) triples would not suffice; the
        deterministic step F_{O'} is what fixes when no new triple can appear.
    - Tautologyhood then falls to X32's kinds 1-2 procedure in the expanded signature.
    - Successor on indices stays undefinable: colours are uniform from n0(v) on.
    - Outcome: A11 holds in Phi under M+ at all three kinds. With X31 (the other
      axioms), Phi is a model of the whole system.
      Rev. 55 (X49): specialized to empty support (X41), the state is not compositional
      under X43's (St): closed P, Q with equal states differ in a named context (R1, R2).
      The rev. 39 proof is untouched (C had no sense then).

X35 Near-alert 2 (rev. 40; refereed): quantifiers skip named objects (N+). Near-alert void.
    - (N+) a quantifier excludes the values of every term free in its scope, variables
      and names alike. (N-) variables only.
    - Text:
      - 5.53 is stated for signs, and a name and a bound variable are different signs.
        5.531 applies it to names, 5.532 to variables.
      - Neutral: 5.5321 and 6.1201 (a outside the scope); 5.47, 5.441, 5.5301 (Russell's
        notation with "="); 4.1252 and 4.1273 (the union "Nachfolger" is the same).
    - My draft's ground (N- would be a further restriction of 5.53, DEF, 3) does not
      decide.
      - 5.53 is level 2 (my error), and it is already RESTRICTED.
      - The ledger counts marks per proposition (X22, J6), so N- adds no mark there.
      - Choosing the less-narrowed reading on that ground alone is the minimal-weakening
        rule, rejected in rev. 30.
    - Deciding ground (referee): under nested weak exclusion, N- contradicts the
      substitution reading of values (the 5.501 tag, C-nv, X10, 5.52).
      - f(x) := (Ey)((Ew)R(x, w) . (Ev)S(y, v)) in the world {R(o, p), S(o, q)}. Weak
        exclusion makes (Ex)f(x) false, because y must differ from x.
      - Under N-, the instance f(o) lets y be o, so 5.52 over the instances makes it
        true.
      - Under N+ the instance excludes o, and the two agree.
      - Machine check (classical, 4 objects, 2 binary forms, names injective, random
        formulas): N+ 7,152 cases, 0 mismatches; N- 59 mismatches.
      So N- costs at least one mark: 5.52 (THM, level 2) or 5.501's reading (DEF,
      level 3). N+ costs none.
      - Corroboration: 5.526's "Und dies x ist a" preserves sense only under N+.
    - Judgments (logged):
      - Under N+, swapping a closed constituent for an equivalent one with other names
        can change an enclosing quantifier's range: (Ex)(Fx . R(a, b)) against (Ex)(Fx .
        R(a, b) . (Sc v ~Sc)). This bears on 5.141 and 5.2341 and is judged no mark: the
        range is fixed by the sign (3.317, 5.501). M+ already makes ranges sign-dependent
        (X31) without a mark.
      - The joint-prefix alternative (exclusion only inside a joint "(Ex, y)" prefix,
        never costed in X9) loses. Read as Russell's iteration (5.532: "statt des
        Russell'schen"), it breaks 5.532 for complex f.
    - Effects:
      - Wording: the signature's quantifier bullet (variables and names free in the
        scope); the C-nv range clause and the 5.501 tag ("o not named in the scope");
        RESTRICTIONS 5.53; X28's "(the ledger is silent)".
      - THEOREM 3 under M+: its proviso was N+ all along.
      - X32: names are parameters, and N+ adds guards x ≠ c.
      - X33 (correction): state_k must also record T_k's set of names (finite;
        periodicity stands). Lemma U's step likewise.
      - Models and countermodels unchanged. A18's witness p' excludes only diagonal
        states, which have no sense under A14.
