    - Rev. 44 (R3): Wehmeier 2004 [F] corroborates N+ for first-order logic. His free
      variables play the role of names, and a bound variable excludes the values of the

    - A14's CM (Phi plus U_k(o_k)).

        class is fixed by:
        - which object entries are e or f;
        - the equality pattern of the form entries relative to the named Q's;
        - the truth values of the entries and of the named Q's;
        - (min(t_u, v), min(f_u, v)) for the unnamed Q's.

X40 E22 (rev. 45; refereed: my J-3332 refuted): contrary interpretive inputs from R3. Final
    adjudication, part 1. Result: 3.332 is read as containment; A6d loses its limit
    source; X29 Q2 is reopened (E23).
    - Rule (E22): secondary readings are not witnesses. They count only through readings
      of the text, which LI then costs.
    - 3.332 (Niedermair 1987 [P], pp. 14-16). Text: "Kein Satz kann etwas ueber sich selbst
      aussagen, weil das Satzzeichen nicht in sich selbst enthalten sein kann, (das ist
      die ganze Theory of types)." Readings of the main clause:
      - (S) support: no proposition's sense depends on a state of its own sign. This is
        A6d.
      - (C) containment: no proposition says anything about the complex that is its own
        sign. It could do so only by describing it (3.24), and its sign would then contain
        itself. This follows from well-founded finite signs (A8) and 3.144; it is not an
        axiom.
      - (N) formal: no proposition says anything about its own sense, truth or symbol
        (cf. 4.442). It holds in the signature (3.144; 2.1513).
    - Decided (refereed): (C) is plain. (S) is at best co-plain and possibly a
      strengthening. (N) is co-plain on its core and narrower than (C).
      - Aboutness of complexes: "Der Satz, welcher vom Komplex handelt, steht in interner
        Beziehung zum Satze, der von dessen Bestandteil handelt. Der Komplex kann nur durch
        seine Beschreibung gegeben sein" (3.24; also 2.0201). The sign is a complex fact
        (3.14). So a sense that depends on one state of its sign is about that state, not
        about the sign. (S) needs that part-to-whole step, and it counts name-free
        dependence as aboutness. The wording gives neither.
      - "A, weil B" asserts that B grounds A. Under (C) it does; under (S) it does not
        (X29 Q1: "A6d already goes beyond containment"). Co-text fixes plainness (X34,
        X38), and the reason clause is the nearest co-text.
      - 3.333 has the same shape: Funktion and Funktionszeichen, "das Urbild seines
        Arguments enthaelt und es sich nicht selbst enthalten kann". On either attachment
        of "das", the parenthesis ties 3.332 to the theory of types, i.e. to
        self-application (3.331, 3.333).
      - "etwas" is what is said; the topic, "sich selbst", is fixed. (C) does not narrow
        it. My draft's charge confused the two.
      - 3.34 makes the features of the whole sign (accidental) features of the Satz. That
        defeats (N)'s exclusion of material self-description of the whole sign. It
        supports (C), not (S).
      - The ledger's own first reading was (C) (FORMAL NOTES C30: "3.332 blocks
        self-containment, not self-reference by description"; rev. 5: "Full A6d (literal
        3.332) is still open"). Rev. 6 took (S) as "literal 3.332" without costing (C).
      - My draft's other grounds fail. 6.124 and 5.44 show that aboutness is semantic for
        named objects, not that it passes from a part to the whole. 3.12-3.14 show the sign
        belongs to the proposition, not that it is the proposition. The reply to
        Niedermair ("Tatsachenbezug" and self-reference are not exclusive) holds only for
        the whole sign, i.e. for (C).
    - LI: 3.332 is read as (C), at no cost. It sources no axiom.
      - Kind: 3.332 is a limit by the rev. 31 criterion. X2 and X29 weighed it so, but the
        tag said AX6d, and E11b's list missed it. Retagged UNS.
      - X2's ground ("without it, 3.332 is violated") fails. A6d's remaining source is
        2.173 on its material reading (assertion, 3), which is co-plain with a standpoint
        reading that does not give A6d (below).
      - 4.442 is not a source of A6d (CORE AXIOMS A6 listed it); it supports (N) and (C).
    - Effect on X29 Q2 (the referee's recomputation, checked here). A6d no longer carries
      a limit, so alternative (i) (admit p v s and s; restrict the bipolarity texts) is no
      longer beaten kind-first.

X41 E23 (rev. 46; refereed: my choice of form refuted): X29 Q2 re-decided under X40. Result:
    alternative (i) in the form (i-s), with a new axiom A6s from 3.13. A6d, D6b and D10s

    - Setting. Under X40, 3.332 is read as containment and costs nothing in any option.
      s := (E phi)(Ex, y) phi xy and p v s are self-settling under every admissible
      projection (K3, A6a, A4; X29). Either they have no sense, and D10's sources are
      restricted (K, X29's chosen option), or they have sense, and the bipolarity texts are
      restricted ((i)).
    - Judgments (logged):
      - J-2.18. 2.18 and 2.17: "um sie ueberhaupt---richtig oder falsch---abbilden zu
        koennen". The scope reading (the condition for depicting at all, rightly or
        wrongly) is at least co-plain, from "ueberhaupt", the dashes, the purpose clause
        and "jedes Bild, welcher Form immer". A free-choice reading ("able to depict
        rightly, and able to depict falsely") is also admitted. LI selects scope; no mark.
        (My draft's "'oder', not 'und'" argument fails: under "koennen" a disjunction
        normally reads as free choice.)
      - J-3.13. Three readings:
        - (Tag) the sign fixes form, not content (content = rho). Weak: 3.13's first
          clause puts everything belonging to the projection, rho included, in the Satz
          ("Zum Satz gehoert alles, was zur Projektion gehoert").
        - (Sit) the projected situation, the sense, is not part of the Satz; only its
          possibility is ("die Moeglichkeit des Projizierten, aber nicht dieses selbst";
          2.203). Plain.
        - (Act) the Satz does not contain the obtaining of what it projects. Co-plain at
          most.
        s and p v s satisfy (Sit): their senses are not situations, and the sign is one
        instance. A self-depicting picture does not: for P = (T, id, id), DEF 2 and DEF
        2.11 make the sign-fact chi*|T the sense.
      - J-apriori. 3.04 defines "a priori richtig" by the thought's possibility; s's
        possibility does not condition its truth. 3.05 is an "only if" and claims nothing
        about which thoughts meet it ("none is" was the tag's addition). 2.225's "a priori
        wahr" is truth known without experience; knowing that s is true requires
        perceiving its sign (5.634). So 3.04, 3.05 and 2.225 are unmarked on their plain
        readings; their "diagonal" readings are not readings.
      - J-tok. "Bild" and "Satz" are read as tokens where the co-text says so: 2.224
        follows 2.223 ("mit der Wirklichkeit vergleichen") and 2.141 ("Das Bild ist eine
        Tatsache"), so 2.224 is marked. 6.113's "am Satz allein" follows "am Symbol allein"
        in its first sentence, so its type reading is co-plain, and LI selects it; no mark.
      - 2.173 is bipolar on both readings: "darum stellt das Bild sein Objekt richtig oder
        falsch dar" states a consequence, which a scope reading would empty.

      - K: 4.5(iii) (assertion, 1), 5.473 (3), 5.5261 (4); 5.4733 (4) if its unmarking
        fails without A6d.

        every assertion at levels 0-1 found no other mark for s and p v s.

      - (i-b) type reading, no diagonal content (my draft). It admits self-depicting

    - A6s (3.13; also 4.024, 4.061, 2.161): no picture's sense is its own sign-fact. For
      every picture P = (D, rho, tau) and every chi, sigma_{P,chi} ≠ chi|D. Equivalently,
      r(D) ≠ D (if r(D) = D, take chi with D all true). Senses that are not situations

    - Consequences:

        not barred, and general signs are never barred. HIGH ALERT #2 dissolves. D10s is

      - The THEOREM stands, on A6s in place of D6b:
        - route 1: for finite A, A7 for the total situation needs r(D) = D = A, which A6s
          bars;
        - route 2: for a finite multiplicity class K, A7 for "all of K true" needs D ⊆ K
          (r preserves multiplicity) with |D| = |K|, so D = K and r(D) = D. So every
          nonempty multiplicity class is infinite <- A7, A6s, A6a, S3, D2.
        Its textual source is now 3.13 (DEF, 2), shallower than 2.224 (3).
      - D20, a second route: A is infinite <- A16, A18, A19, A4, A7, D2, D3, D-S4.
        - Lemma F. If A is finite, A19 gives a frame automorphism that moves an object.
          Theta'(x) lists every state of the frame as "phi(...) v ~phi(...)", with x in
          o's place and distinct variables elsewhere. Theta'(o) is a frame fact (null
          sense; it fits, since its pattern is the frame), so by A19 Theta'(o') holds too.
          Weak exclusion (5.53; X35) makes the witnesses distinct. Under C-nv each atom
          must go to a state. So the witnessing g is injective on objects, forms and states
          (D2); A is finite (and O, by D3 and D-S4), so g is a frame automorphism with
          g(o) = o'.
        - A16 makes chi* rigid on objects, so g.chi* ≠ chi*. It is an isomorph of chi*,
          differing on a finite set Delta.
        - X26's MC-fin step: p := ~(g.chi*'s literals on Delta) has sense (A7) and is true
          at chi*. Only flipping all of Delta changes p, so Delta is a minimal alteration
          changing p. A18 says it changes the completely general truths. g.chi* is an
          isomorph (sense and truth are Aut-equivariant), so it does not. Contradiction.
        - With Theta' the argument also holds in the rev. 44 system. (The draft's Theta,
          with w's truth values, has support all of A there, so it had no sense.)
        - So infinite A follows from 5.526, 5.5262 and 5.5302 as well as from the picture

X43 E25a (rev. 48; refereed: verdict confirmed, grounds and costs corrected): the
    name/binder token rule. X31's strict rule stays. 5.5321 stays RESTRICTED, and 4.1272
    joins it. No cascade.
    - The question (X42). X31/X33's fit rule: names are mapped injectively, and no binder
      shares a name's token object. Binders may share tokens with each other where no
      capture arises (the renaming lemma, X33). The rule covers form names and form
      variables as well as object names and variables.
    - Options:
      - (St) strict (X31): a name's token is never a binder's.
      - (Lo) loose: a name may share a token with a binder whose scope does not contain
        it. A rule tied to scopes or to N+ is (Lo) itself. Changing C-nv's range clause
        instead costs 5.501 and 3.315-3.317 (DEF) and undoes C-nv's basis (X24). Typed
        token classes and a fully strict rule cost more. So the choice is (St) or (Lo).
    - Text: 3.325 (DEF, 3), "eine Zeichensprache ..., welche ... nicht das gleiche Zeichen
      in verschiedenen Symbolen ... verwendet".
      - Judgment J-3.325 (logged): within a propositional sign, the Zeichen is the element
        of the sign-fact (3.14 "seine Elemente, die Woerter"; 3.32 "das sinnlich
        Wahrnehmbare"; 3.1431). Reuse of an object across sign-facts is token reuse
        (3.322: "das Zeichen ist ja willkuerlich"). The alternative, the abstract letter,
        is a sign that is not the perceptible element, against 3.32 and 3.14.
      - Under (Lo), one element of a single sign-fact sits at name positions and at
        variable positions, told apart only by the binding scaffolding. A name means its
        object (3.203); a variable signifies the formal concept (4.1272). They signify in
        different ways, so they are different symbols (3.321). That is 3.323's "Gruen ist
        gruen" pattern, which 3.325 is introduced to exclude.
      - Two binders sharing a token signify the same way (the variable name, 4.1272), so
        they are one symbol. 3.325 names Frege's and Russell's notation, which reuses
        bound letters across scopes.
      - (Lo) keeps 3.325 read scope-relatively (no element in two symbols within one
        scope), as 5.53 is kept scope-relatively (weak exclusion). So (Lo) costs a
        restriction of 3.325 (DEF, 3), not a violation.
      - 5.53 does not separate the options: (St)'s binder-binder sharing already lets one
        sign range independently in disjoint scopes. (My draft's 5.53 paragraph is
        withdrawn.)
    - Costs of (St) (machine checks on Phi's 4-unit cut, hereditary A6s):
      - 5.5321 (NOT, 4), as marked in X42, now for both formulas. "Nur Ein x befriedigt
        f( )" is vacuous for Cyc. "Statt (x): fx ⊃ x = a" has no sense under (St) for a and
        h in Phi with every description tried (the name's token and the binders x, y all
        need the two-place regions {a, b} or {h, h'}); it has sense for o_2.
      - 4.1272 (UNS, 4), new: "es gibt 2 Gegenstaende, welche ... durch '(Ex, y) ...'".
        For Cyc in Phi, (Ex, y)(Cyc x . Cyc y) is false under (St) though two objects
        satisfy Cyc. No sign says it. Same failure as 5.5321's; consistency requires the
        mark.
      - Not marked: 5.532 (both notations range over instances with sense, so they
        agree), 5.5301 (its example uses "="), 5.5302 (it claims only sense), A16, A19,
        D15. 5.526: not marked under X42's Both reading. If "Und dies x ist a" were read as
        one sentence with the uniqueness clause (5.5321's first formula), (St) would
        restrict 5.526 too (assertion, 3). Both is logged as plain, so this is a note.
    - LI:
      - (St): 4.1272 (UNS, 4) and 5.5321 (NOT, 4). (Lo): 3.325 (DEF, 3); it would lift
        both marks and restore Lemma R's (c) for names.
      - Kind-first (PRINCIPLE): at kind 1, (Lo) 1 and (St) 0, so (St) wins. Level-first:
        at level 3, (Lo) has a DEF mark and (St) none, so (St) wins. A plain count (1
        against 2) picks (Lo): X43 depends on the kind-first order, as X29 did, and the
        robustness note (C25) does not cover it.
      - No tie, no alert. If J-3.325 failed, (Lo) would win outright: a reversal, not a
        tie, so not a trigger-(1) near-alert.
    - Effects: 4.1272 joins RESTRICTIONS; 5.5321's entry names both formulas; J-3.325 is
      logged; 3.325's tag is reworded for the token model; Lemma R's (c) stays false under
      (St).

X46 E27 (rev. 51; refereed: all four parts confirmed with corrections): kind review of the
    pivotal tags. Two criteria are made explicit (definitions; units of mixed
    propositions). Three marks change weight; no decision changes. HIGH ALERT #2 now

    - Criteria (in PRINCIPLE, as rev. 31 did for limits):
      - DEF. A unit is a definition if it fixes what a term or sign means. Markers:
        - a meaning or naming verb that states what a term or sign means ("heisst",
          "heisse", "nenne ich", "bedeutet", "Def."), not "heisst nichts" (5.473);
        - a gloss: "das heisst", "das ist" + phrase, or "also" in a verbless apposition
          that restates a preceding phrase (3.325, Ogden "that is to say"); elsewhere
          "also" marks a consequence;
        - "besteht darin, dass", also for a term already named (2.14, 2.222, 3.14 s1);
        - "X ist (waere) das, was (ein solcher, dessen) ..." or "Was ..., ist X" only if X
          is not fixed before (2.18, 3.04; not 2.17, 3.341).
        Without a marker, a unit that says what an already fixed term applies to, states
        a condition on it or draws a consequence is an assertion; so is a requirement
        ("muessen wir ... verwenden").
      - Units of mixed propositions. E11 adopted no rule ("no decision needs one"); X41's
        T2 analysis (4.5), X43 and E29 need one. Units: a sentence; a gloss or a
        parenthesis is a unit of its own. A mark weighs by the kind of the unit whose
        content the reading narrows; a definition's definiens is part of its content. If
        a reading narrows several units of one proposition, the mark counts once, at the
        heaviest of their kinds. The level stays the proposition's.
        - Ground: PRINCIPLE weighs "the kind of statement", and its reasons (a definition
          fixes the terms; an assertion that conflicts with a limit yields) concern the
          content narrowed. The number already carries the level. The rule states the
          practice of X7 (4.463: "unendlichen" weighed as an assertion under a DEF tag)
          and X40 and X45 (5.473's limit-form parenthesis). The kind field, one kind per
          proposition (AX, SIG and THM record a source or derivation role), misweighs
          marks on mixed propositions.
        - Not the minimal-weakening rule (rejected in rev. 30): it adds no choice between
          restrictions; it fixes an input PRINCIPLE already uses, and it has a use.
        - W2 (the proposition's highest kind) gives the same decisions, given 4.5's DEF
          gloss, but differs in dependences: X41 would rest on 4.5's DEF unit and X43 on
          3.325's, and narrow J6's second branch would not tie (5.526's "das heisst also"
          would make (N)'s mark DEF). W1 is kept on PRINCIPLE's ground, not on outcomes.

X47 E28 (rev. 52; refereed: confirmed with corrections; the central gap, how a written
    abbreviation is a fact, is the referee's): fit of defined signs. Decided: (D-f). A
    defined sign takes no tokens of its own; a sign with defined signs is possible, and
    has sense, iff its translation fits. No new mark; 4.1272 and 5.5321 stay restricted.
    Not a tie.
    - Question (E25, X42; X45). Under M+ a sign is possible, and a general sign has sense,
      iff it fits the frame (X31, X41). A sign may contain defined signs (A8). Options:
      - (D-f) a defined sign takes no tokens of its own. The sign-fact of a sign with
        defined signs is a tokening of its translation (each defined sign replaced by its
        definiens, bound letters renamed apart); writing the abbreviation is a way of
        producing it (3.34 s2), as logical signs are not atoms (4.0312, 5.4611);
      - (D-w) written defined signs take tokens of their own, and the sign has sense iff
        its translation fits;
      - (W) written defined signs take tokens of their own, and the written sign's fit
        decides;
      - (V) a symbol fits iff some sign of it fits, abbreviations with their own tokens
        included;
      - (H2) the definiens's binders are exempt from the name/binder rule.
      (W) or (V) could lift 4.1272 and 5.5321: "(Ex, y)(Cx . Cy)" with C := Cyc writes
      none of Cyc's binders.
    - Text (kinds per X46):
      - 3.261 (assertions, 3): "Jedes definierte Zeichen bezeichnet ueber jene Zeichen,
        durch welche es definiert wurde; und die Definitionen weisen den Weg."
      - 4.241 (s2 DEF, 3): "'a = b' heisst also: das Zeichen a ist durch das Zeichen b
        ersetzbar"; a definition introduces a sign that "solle ein bereits bekanntes
        Zeichen a ersetzen"; "Die Definition ist eine Zeichenregel." 6.23 s1 ("so heisst
        das, sie sind durch einander ersetzbar"; DEF, 2) and 6.24 likewise.
      - 3.343: s1 (DEF, 3), "Definitionen sind Regeln der Uebersetzung von einer Sprache
        in eine andere"; s2 (assertion, 3), every correct sign-language must be
        translatable into every other by them. 4.025: translation goes by constituents.
      - 3.344 (DEF, 3): what signifies in a symbol is common to all symbols that may
        replace it by the rules of logical syntax. 3.3442: the sign of a complex is not
        resolved arbitrarily in analysis.
      - 3.34 (s2-s3 DEF, 2): features due to "der besonderen Art der Hervorbringung des
        Satzzeichens" are accidental; essential are those "welche allein den Satz
        befaehigen, seinen Sinn auszudruecken". 3.341 (assertion, 3).
      - 3.24 (last sentence): the symbol of a complex is contracted "in ein einfaches
        Symbol" by a definition; by 3.261 the simple symbol signifies through the
        complex's.
      - 3.2 (assertion, 1) and 3.25 (assertion, 2): the thought can be expressed with
        elements of the Satzzeichen corresponding to its objects; there is one complete
        analysis. Under M+ an expression is a possible sign (judgment J-anal, logged).

X50 E32a (rev. 56; refereed, two referees: kinds 1-2 confirmed with corrections; kind 3
    refuted as stated, a repaired state tested): Phi's A11 under J-N (X49). PROVED at kinds
    1-2: the kind <= 2 part of A11's promise problem, and sense, are decidable in Phi's
    decimal notation. Kind 3 OPEN: the route holds, the fit state needs the repair below,
    and the grammar waits on E31. E32 stays open (kind 3; A16-A18 at proof level).
    - Setting. Phi (X26) with its decimal notation (X49): names a, b, h, h', o_i, R_i,
      f_{i,j}, one name per object and form (5.53; X49's injective naming). The result is
      relative to J-N's adequate notation, provisional per X49; under J-N's old input (Q) or
      (L), Phi fails A11 (In, W_n). Signs are expanded by X47 first; the kind <= 2 fragment
      is R2 sec. 6.1's (atoms, finite N, N over the values of one variable), vacuous binders
      and empty N included. For a closed sign phi:
      - S(phi): every component has sense; every fully named atom not under a binder denotes
        a state (C-nv's atom clause, read literally: a general proposition has sense iff its
        whole sign fits); the whole sign fits: a sort-respecting token map g on its letters
        with every atom on a state, a binder's token unlike the tokens of the variables free
        in its scope, names injective, no binder on any name's token (X43, (St)), hereditary
        A6s on the fully named atoms (X42). The result also holds with the clause on every
        fully named atom (both readings below are quantifier-free).
      - V(phi, w): atoms by w; N(list) true iff all false; N over z in B true iff every
        admitted d gives a false B[z := d]. d is admitted iff it has z's sort, differs from
        the values of B's names and of the outer variables free in B (N+), and S(B[z := d]):
        the instance's own sign (C-nv: "for which Phi(o) is a proposition"; Lemma R', X42).
        An empty range gives true. The in-context reading (the instance inside the whole
        sign) gives other values (C . C' becomes a contradiction), and the proof survives it
        too.
      - Tautology: S(phi) and V(phi, w) for every w in {0,1}^A, on the promise S(phi).
    - Lemma 1. S(phi) iff AC(phi) and Fit*(phi): AC is the atom clause, Fit* is fit without
      hereditary A6s.
      - Components: a component's fit is a restriction of g (fewer names, fewer (St) pairs),
        and its fully named atoms are among phi's.
      - A6s: move each unit g uses to a fresh unit of larger index (o_i -> o_m, R_i -> R_m,
        f_{i,j} -> f_{m,s(j)}, s injective; hubs fixed), distinct per unit and above every
        index phi names. States and inequalities are preserved. Afterwards every token state
        has a fresh form and every denoted state a named one, so token -> denotation has no
        chain of length 2 and no cycle. Hereditary A6s never binds in Phi, at any kind. (It
        does bind on 1- and 2-unit cuts.)
    - Lemma 2 (fit as a finite tree problem). A type is a hub (a, b, h, h') or (role o / R /
      marker, unit label, marker label). For the letters L live at a node (its free
      variables and all names of the sign), Acc(node) is the set of type maps on L that
      extend to the letters bound below it: an atom's letters go to a state; at N(list), the
      type map restricted to each child's live letters is in the child's Acc; at a binder z
      with body B, z gets a type unlike the free variables of B other than z and every name
      of z's sort, and the extended map is in Acc(B). Names are injective at the root. Every
      constraint between a letter bound below a node and one outside it passes through a
      letter live at the node; siblings may share tokens; unit capacity is only a lower
      bound, so units can be taken large and every type map is realizable. Fit* is decidable
      and reads no denotation: it depends only on the shape (which letters are names).
    - Lemma 3 (ranges, translation). For N over z in B, the range is theta_B(z, x-bar): z's
      sort; z unlike each same-sort name of B and each other free variable of B (N+); E(t)
      for each atom t of B with all letters among the free variables, z and the names (AC);
      and one Boolean constant, Fit*(B with its free letters named). The constant is the
      same for every admitted d, since N+ makes all names of the instance distinct.
      Translate: atom -> W(atom); N(list) -> conjunction of negations; N over z in B -> not
      (Ez)(theta_B and B*). By induction on the instances, V(phi, w) = ((Phi, w) |= phi*),
      and phi* has q variables, q the number of phi's variables.
    - Lemma 4 (R2 Thm 6; checked). The q-profile of a world: for each named unit, its exact
      data (R-bits; the named markers' values; the residual true and false marker counts,
      capped at q); for each other unit, its type (R-bits; true and false marker counts
      capped at q); for each type, its number of units capped at q. Worlds of one profile
      agree on every formula with at most q variables, infinitary conjunctions included:
      Duplicator matches the touched units injectively (named units to themselves); a move
      inside a matched unit finds a mate (equal counts, or both >= q, with at most q-1
      pebbles left); a move to a fresh unit finds a fresh unit of the same type (supply
      capped at q). Realizable profiles are finitely many and decidable (R2 sec. 10.4: a
      type with both counts below q occurs only at i = c + d; the infinite tail needs a
      saturated tail type; named units use their exact capacity). For each realizable P a
      finite M_P (q units per saturated type, q markers per saturated colour, named units
      with their named markers) is q-equivalent to every Phi-world of profile P. It need not
      be a cut of Phi; the a/b swap is not used. The number of candidate profiles is finite
      but astronomically large.
    - Theorem (kinds 1-2). For closed phi of kind <= 2: S(phi) is decided by AC (parsing the
      decimal names; f_{i,j} needs j <= i) and Fit* (Lemma 2); on the promise, phi is a
      tautology iff M_P |= phi* for every realizable P (Lemmas 3-4). At kind 1 it is
      propositional validity (X49). Vacuous binders: theta_B has no z-atoms, and the range
      is infinite iff S(B). (Rev. 57, X51: superseded; vacuous binders are transparent,
      the atom clause applies to atoms not under a non-vacuous binder, and the theorem
      holds with vacuous binders removed, X52.) Empty N: true. This discharges X49's
      kind-2 obligation (R2 sec. 10.5).

          third member being DEF (X46: "das dritte [ist] die Form ...", the bracket newly
          introduced). Were that unit an assertion, (V0)'s marks (assertion, 3-4) would beat
          (Vn)'s (assertion, 2) kind-first too. Both dependences are recorded.
        - Under N+, G*'s terms from T_2 on differ from 4.1273's printed terms (the inner
          variable may take b; the printed prefix excludes it): they disagree in 600 of
          4,096 irreflexive worlds on four objects (ref57/scripts/wex.py). Only the union,
          "Nachfolger", agrees. Ground: X35's logged note (4.1252 and 4.1273 are judged by
          the union). Prefix-merging (C's binders join the filler's prefix) yields the
          printed terms but inspects the filler: item 6.
      - (2) Hole occurrences. (M) any number, each with its own map; (S) one. The doubling
        series T_{k+1}(u, v) := (Ew)(T_k[v := w] . T_k[u := w]) and x |-> (x == p) need (M)
        (term size doubles; non-monotone in x). (S) narrows 5.2522's third member (DEF, 4)
        and 5.501's kind-3 unit (assertion, 3). (M): no mark, under every order.
      - (3) Interface. The bracket's members are propositions (5.501 s1), so at every
        instance a term's free letters are the series' outer parameters: a fixed interface
        V; FV(B) and FV(C) within V; maps into V, the letters bound above the hole, and
        N_br. Terms may lose letters of V. Growth is impossible (finitely many parameters).
        Forced.
      - (4) No name generation: the names of every term are in N_br, the names written in
        the bracket. Ground: item 6 with X49's ruling (3.3411 s2, 5.02, 3.26; a name's
        spelling is accidental, 3.34). Forced.
      - (5) Nesting. (Nh) series signs may occur in B and C, and a hole of C may lie in an
        inner series sign's base or operation (O'x := N([x, y, O''y])). (Nf) not around a
        hole: narrows 5.2522's third member (DEF, 4) and 5.501's kind-3 unit (assertion, 3).
        (Nh): no mark, under every order.
      - (6) Fixed contexts. (F) a map acts on the declared interface only; the context never
        inspects the filler, except for the normal form (D1, J-norm), which deletes idle
        units only. (Iu) unrestricted inspection: any finite rule on the filler's syntax
        (5.231 admits form-dependent operations). (Ir) G* plus a fixed finite inspecting
        repertoire, e.g. prefix-merging.
        - (Iu) makes A11 fail in every model. Fix an elementary p with sense. Code a Turing
          machine's configuration in the shape of a term equivalent to p (runs of double
          negations); a finite rule, acting on N-structure only, steps the code and, on
          halting, adds one N, after which the terms stay equivalent to ~p. The terms share
          p's atom, so each has sense where p has. N over the series (the joint negation of
          all terms) is equivalent to ~p if the machine never halts and is a contradiction
          if it halts (p is contingent, A4). So N(N over the series) is a tautology iff the
          machine halts: undecidable, a violation of A11's sources (X5), which comes before
          every restriction.
        - (Ir) narrows 5.2521's parenthesis (assertion, 4), given J-subst (logged; class N):
          a declaration substitutes for constituents (3.315) and does not restructure. So
          the result of applying "O' xi" to a is "O' xi" with a at xi through xi's
          declaration (item 7) under G*, and not under an inspecting operation. (Ir) has
          G*'s marks and one more. Backup if J-subst fails: a fixed repertoire is a clause
          the text does not give (weight 0, as (T+)), so LI+1 takes (F).
        - 5.24 s1 does not separate: G* already marks 5.24 (item 1), one mark per
          proposition.
        - (F), under every order.
      - (7) Tokens of the written series sign. (7a) the propositional variable x has no
        token: by X48's ground a variable is a word of the Satzzeichen (4.1271), so 3.14 s1
        (DEF, 2) is marked. (7b) each distinct propositional letter of a bracket (x,
        wherever it stands) takes one state, distinct from the sign's other token states
        (the analogue of X31's rule for form letters). No mark found. (7b), under every
        order. The terms' tokens (infinite) are no sign (J-FS).
        - (D1) What a hole writes. A hole stands for its fillers; X28 declares its
          variables. Rule (A), for items 7 and 8 alike: 5.47321 applies to the units of
          every sign, terms included.
          - Words: what a hole writes is words of the sign, with tokens (3.14 s1 as X48
            reads it). (D1b), not words, narrows it (DEF, 2). A letter takes that letter's
            token; a name counts for (St), injectivity and N+. Sources, where a format
            writes them, are scope-inert: not free at the hole and not counted for N+ (each
            source is in the closure, so its token and (St) are present anyway).
          - The bracket's closure: the least set that contains the free letters and names of
            B and C outside the holes (and, for a hole of an enclosing series inside the
            bracket, the images of that series' closure under its map), closed under the
            maps' images. V := its free letters, less every bnd(xi_j); N_br := its names.
            Every element reaches some filler: B's in T_0, C's in every T_{k+1}, and the
            image of a reached element in the next term (at some outer level, for inner
            signs).
          - What xi_j writes:
            - (H1) its interface image mu_j(V u N_br), in any format (all entries,
              identities included, or the targets in a canonical order of the closure).
              Sources, where a format writes them, are not free at the hole: the copy does
              not contain them (3.315). Every written unit reaches the copy: no unnecessary
              unit.
            - (H2) the image of a declared interface larger than the closure. Its extra
              units are unnecessary, and as words they shift ranges (N+) and fit: 5.47321
              (assertion, 5).
            - (H3) sources counted free at the hole. Binders above it then avoid letters the
              copy never contains, and fit varies with the format: 3.34 (DEF, 2; "Zufaellig
              sind die Zuege, die ...").
            - (H6) moved entries only, identities unwritten. Identity letters reach the copy
              but are not written at the hole, so binders above need not avoid them: the
              third member does not show the form of the next term, 5.2522 (DEF, 4).
            - (H4) nothing written: the sign does not fix its next term, against 5.2522's
              third member (DEF, 4).
            - (H1), under every order. It adds no clause: it is X28's declaration read under
              3.14 s1 and 5.47321. The format is notation (J-Nn, X49): every format writes
              the same words with the same scopes, so the formats are congruent.
          - Terms. A term the operation produces (T_{k+1}) is written in normal form,
            without the units that idle in it. First each inner hole writes the image of the
            term's own inner closure ((H1) at the term). Then binders made vacuous are
            deleted; deleting a hole unit can make a binder vacuous, not the reverse. Under
            (Et) (item 8), deleting a vacuous binder changes nothing where its token can be
            placed, which is always in Phi. Options:
            - (Ht1) the substituted image kept: idle hole units mean something (their names
              shift N+, their letters bind fit): 5.47321 (assertion, 5).
            - (Ht2) normal form: no mark, given J-norm (logged; R), a reading of 5.2521's
              parenthesis and 5.47321: the result of applying "O' xi" is the sign without
              its unnecessary units, and 3.34 makes the choice of sign accidental. It
              deletes idle units only, moves or adds none, and leaves every retained unit's
              scope unchanged. Prefix-merging moves binders and so changes the scopes of
              used units: still inspection (item 6). If J-norm failed, (Ht2) would narrow
              5.2521's parenthesis (assertion, 4), and (Ht1) would win: 5.47321 restricted.
            - (Ht3) idle units in terms are not words: 3.14 s1 (DEF, 2).
            - (Ht4) terms with idle units drop out of the values: 5.47321, and a clause.
            - (Ht5) series whose terms can hold idle units are barred: 5.2522's third member
              (DEF, 4).
            - (Ht2), under every order, while 5.47321 is unmarked elsewhere in TLP (one mark
              per proposition). It is in every branch of item 8: (Et) where a token can be
              placed, (E-) where it cannot.
          - Merges: an outer map that identifies two elements of an inner closure with
            different images leaves the inner map undefined, so the series has no next term.
            Such a sign is no series sign (5.2522: O' applies to every term); a resolution
            convention would be a clause the text does not give (LI+1). Decidable from the
            finite state (X52).
          - A binder of C whose letter occurs only at holes is atom-free at the written
            sign; its token is as under (Et).
      - (8) Empty enumerations and vacuous binders. N() as a component is true (E1); N()
        alone is no sign (A6a). A binder is vacuous where its letter does not occur in its

      - (9) Values at an instance: the terms with the outer parameters named, T_k[a-bar],

        written vacuous binders are transparent (item 8).

X52 E32b (rev. 57; refereed, six rounds: PROVED for G*): Phi's A11 under J-N at kind 3, for
    X51's grammar G* (single series, nested; no tuples, X51 item 10). PROVED, with round 1's

    - Setting: X50 (S, V, Lemmas 1-4; the literal atom clause; the instance's own sign). A
      kind-3 sign contains N over series signs [B, x, C] of G* (X51), possibly nested. N* :=
      the names of the closed sign under test (the brackets' and the holes' interface images
      included, X51 item 7, (H1)). Mov := the names that some map of the sign, inner series'
      maps included, sends to a variable. Lemmas 5-7 are uniform in which words a hole
      writes; (H1) fixes them as mu_j(V u N_br), sources not free at the hole, and excludes
      merges. Terms are in normal form (X51 D1, (Ht2)): each inner hole writes the image of
      the term's own inner closure; idle hole units never arise beyond (H1) (below; "reach"
      read syntactically: the source occurs free in some inner term). Vacuous binders are
      transparent (X51 item 8, (Et)): the letter takes a token, which in Phi always goes to
      a fresh unit, and otherwise (Ez)B has B's sense and truth; for the atom clause and the
      theta filters a vacuous binder is absent. Whether a binder of C is vacuous in C[T] is
      decided by T's free letters and names, which sigma(T) carries; a binder of T keeps its
      vacuity in every copy (bound letters are renamed bijectively, and maps never target a
      copy's binders), so J(copy) = mu_j(J(T)). So each step runs Lemmas 5-7 on a variant of
      C (vacuous binders marked transparent), chosen from sigma(T_k); the lemmas are uniform
      in the template. X51's normal form deletes vacuous binders from terms; in Phi this
      equals keeping them transparent (their tokens are fresh), so the proof covers both. At
      kinds 1-2 (X50) transparency is syntactic: decide the sign with its vacuous binders
      removed, plus their tokens (placeable in Phi). X50's range rule for vacuous binders is
      superseded (X51). X50's Lemma 3 theta reads "not under a non-vacuous binder" (its
      wording selects atoms by their letters, the every-atom reading; flagged in ref56).
      Values at an instance with parameters a-bar: the T_k[a-bar] with sense (X51 item 9).
    - Lemma 5 (width; corrected, C1). Count each hole occurrence as an atom over mu_j(V) and
      over the images of the names mu_j moves. From level to level the letters of a node
      change by a function (renaming apart is a bijection on bound letters; mu_j acts
      letterwise; names outside its moves stay), so the number of variables plus moved names
      at a node never grows; at its creation it is at most |FV(t)| + |Mov|, t its template
      node. Hence width(T_k) <= v + |Mov|, v the largest template width (outer and inner
      series). q := v + |Mov|. (q = v is false under name variabilization: B := (Ek)(k(H, c)
      . p1(H, c) . p2(H, c)), C := (Eq1)(Eq2)(xi[p1 := q1, p2 := q2] . K) gives width 4 at
      T_2, and with q = 2 the procedure misdecides p1(H, c) v p2(H, c) v N([B, x, C]);
      ref57, lemma5.py.)
    - Lemma 6 (finite fit state; corrected, C2). L(T) := FV(T) u names(T). sigma(T) has:
      - FV(T) within V, names(T) within N*;
      - J(T): the atoms of T over L(T) not under a non-vacuous binder of T (the atom
        clause);
      - for each role partition rho of L(T) (blocks of letters sharing one token; each block
        a variable, a promoted name, or identified with a name of N*), each presence flag on
        the names of N* outside T, and each count of anonymous reserved promoted names, with
        the promoted blocks plus the anonymous names at most v + |Mov| per sort (C2d):
        Acc_T^{rho,R}, the type maps on the blocks, the present names and the anonymous
        names that extend to a placement of T's bound letters with every atom on a state,
        every binder unlike the letters free in its scope, no binder on the token of a name
        of the checked sign (C2c: a moved name constrains only the binders with its image in
        scope), names pairwise distinct.
      - Exactness (re-derived): for phi = D[copies of T], every atom constraint lies in D or
        in one copy; a copy's binder constrains only the copy's binders and the copy's free
        letters, all of mu_j(L(T)) (C2b; for a binder z of D above the hole, an image bound
        strictly between z and the hole is not free in z's body); D's binders constrain no
        bound letter of a copy; (St) and injectivity involve names only. With D's letters
        and all names fixed, the copies are independent, each Fit(T) under the induced role
        partition (the outer role of each letter's image, uniformly: C2a) and the
        reservation of the checked sign's other names. No frame property is used.
      - Type abstraction on Phi: a fit witness moves injectively, unit by unit and marker by
        marker, into units of larger index, preserving states and inequalities; so fit on
        Phi is fit with all units large, and there Acc depends only on type maps (hubs
        exact, unit and marker labels up to relabeling). Finite: boundedly many blocks and
        names, finitely many types.
      - Compositional: sigma(C[T]) is the constraint problem over C's own letters with one
        table constraint per hole occurrence, read from Acc_T at the induced partition and
        reservation. A letter sent to a binder of C above the hole is a variable unless that
        binder is promoted in the current check (binder filters). A hole's interface image
        is a set of template words of C at the hole. For an inner series sign of C in
        T_{k+1} it is the image of that term's inner closure, whose base is the template
        letters outside the holes plus the copy's letters mu_j(L(T_k)): a function of
        sigma(T_k) and the templates, computed in the sigma transition (it enters fit and
        the N+ filters). Inner signs deeper in a copy change letterwise: for a map merging
        nothing, Cl(mu(S)) = mu(Cl(S)), so their hole words are the images of the old ones.
      - Merges (X51 D1) are decided from the state extended by Pi(T): per inner-sign
        occurrence, its inner map on the closure elements free in T. Pi(T_{k+1}) is C's

X53 E32c (rev. 58; refereed: not proved as drafted, PROVED with the referee's three edits,
    applied): A16-A18 and A6a, A6s, A7 in Phi at proof level. With A6a, A6s and A7 (Lemma C,
    from X42's argument), X50-X52 (A11) and the axioms Phi meets by construction, Phi is a
    certified model of TLP: TLP is self-consistent (E32 closed). A17's independence stays
    open (E33).
    - Setting. Phi (X26): O = {h, h', a, b} u {o_i : i >= 1}; forms R_i with the states
      R_i(a, b), R_i(b, a), R_i(h, o_i); markers f_{i,j} (j <= i) with the one state
      f_{i,j}(h', o_i). chi*: R_i(a, b) iff i in S, R_i(b, a) iff i in T, every other state
      true; (S, T) Cohen-generic over a countable transitive model M that codes every sign.
      Semantics: sense S = AC and Fit* (X50 Lemma 1); Fit: atoms on states, every binder
      unlike the same-sort letters free in its body, binders off names, names distinct;
      values by C-nv: N over z in B ranges over d unlike the names of B with S(B[z := d]);
      vacuous binders transparent (X51). Aut(frame) = {id, (a b)} x Prod_i Sym(f_{i,1..i}).
    - Abbreviations (all name-free; p, q form letters; others object letters):
      - St(p, u, v) := p(u, v) v ~p(u, v) ("(p, u, v) is a state": its innermost instance
        has sense iff it is one);
      - Off(p, u, v) := (Es, t)(St(p, s, t) . St(p, u, v)) ("p has a state off {u, v}": u, v
        stand in the scope of s, t, so weak exclusion keeps s, t unlike them; X44's
        convention. The draft's (Es, t)St(p, s, t) only says "p has a state": it made Rf
        hold of markers and falsified HT, MC and the h, h' descriptions, referee);
      - M_k(x) := (Ey)(Ep_1 .. p_k) AND_j St(p_j, y, x) ("k forms reach x from one source");
        U_i(x) := M_i(x) . ~M_{i+1}(x);
      - Rf(p, w) := (Eu)(St(p, u, w) . Off(p, u, w)) ("p reaches w and has an off-state");
      - Unit_i(w, p) := U_i(w) . Rf(p, w).
    - Lemma S (sense). Every sentence below has sense, and so do the instances at the values
      claimed in Lemma V and below (an instance can lack fit where a name occupies a token a
      binder needs: the draft's D_a with Rf did, referee). AC: a name-free sentence has no
      top atom; in an instance, an atom becomes top only at its innermost binder, where the
      range keeps exactly the d that make it a state. Fit: blocks under different binders
      share no disequality, so each block is placed on its own: object letters on h, h', a,
      b and o_m, form letters on R_m and f_{m,j}, for one unit m larger than every index in
      the sentence (for U_i: m >= i + 1; markers give m distinct forms from h' to o_m; R_m
      gives (h, o_m) with off-states (a, b), (b, a)). Doubled 5.5321 instances take a second
      unit m' != m. No vacuous binder occurs.
    - Lemma V (values). By Lemma S, each quantifier ranges over the values unlike the other
      letters of its body (N+) for which the innermost atoms are states. Hence, at every
      world w and every i (frame facts first, world-independent):
      - M_k(o) iff k forms reach o from one source: M_k(o_i) iff k <= i (h' sends i markers,
        h one form); M_k(a), M_k(b) for all k (R_n(b, a), R_n(a, b) for all n); not M_1(h),
        not M_1(h'). So U_i holds of o_i only.
      - Rf(p, o_i) iff p = R_i (markers have one state; R_i reaches o_i from h and has the
        off-states (a, b), (b, a)).
    - Invariant families (completely general; true or false at a world w):
      - HT_i := (Ew)(Ep)(Unit_i(w, p) . (Eu)(St(p, u, w) . p(u, w))): R_i(h, o_i) is true.
      - MC_{i,k} := (Ew)(U_i(w) . (Eu)(Ep_1 .. p_k) AND_j (St(p_j, u, w) . ~Off(p_j, u, w) .
        p_j(u, w))): at least k markers of unit i are true.
      - TT_i := (Ew)(Ep)(Unit_i(w, p) . (Ex, y)(p(x, y) . p(y, x))); FF_i likewise with
        ~p(x, y) . ~p(y, x); MIX_i with p(x, y) . ~p(y, x). The only state pairs of R_i in
        both directions are (a, b), (b, a), so these read the unit's type.
      - OR_{i,j} := (Ew, w')(Ep, q)(Unit_i(w, p) . Unit_j(w', q) . (Ex, y)(p(x, y) . ~p(y,
        x) . q(x, y) . ~q(y, x))) (i != j): units i and j are mixed with the same
        orientation.
    - A17 (any two worlds with the same completely general truths are isomorphic). Let w, w'
      agree on all completely general truths. Then for each i they agree on HT_i, on c_i :=
      the number of true markers of unit i (the MC_{i,k}), on the type (TT, FF or MIX), and,
      for mixed i, j, on OR_{i,j}. Build sigma in Aut(frame): in each unit a permutation of
      the markers carrying w's true markers onto w''s (same count); if no unit is mixed, id
      on {a, b}; else fix a mixed unit i_0 and take id or (a b) as the orientation of
      R_{i_0} in w matches that in w'. Every mixed j then matches (OR_{i_0,j}); TT and FF
      units are fixed by (a b); R_i(h, o_i) by HT_i. So sigma.w = w'. (X44's argument, with
      the families now proved to have sense and the stated values.)
    - A18 (MC-all at chi*). Let p be a proposition and w a minimal alteration of chi* that
      changes p's value; suppose w has chi*'s completely general truths. By A17, w =
      sigma.chi*. Marker permutations fix chi* (all markers true), and R_i(h, o_i) is true
      in both, so w = (a b).chi* =: w*. Its difference from chi* is D := {R_i(a, b), R_i(b,
      a) : i in S symdiff T}, infinite (genericity). V(p, .) is a Borel function of the
      world with a code in M (kinds 1-3: countable Boolean operations over atoms; sense is
      world-independent). (T, S) is Cohen-generic over M (the swap is an automorphism of the
      forcing in M). So a finite condition c true at w* forces V(p) = V(p, w*). Let w'' be
      chi* changed on the finite set D n dom(c) to agree with w*. w'' is a finite variant of
      a generic, hence generic over M; it meets c; so V(p, w'') = V(p, w*) != V(p, chi*).
      Its difference D n dom(c) is a proper subset of D: w* is not minimal. Contradiction.
      (X26's argument, with A17 now proved.)
    - A16 (at chi*, every object is singled out by one completely general description;
      "Both", X42: true of that object only, and its 5.5321 sentence (Ex)phi x : ~(Ex,
      y).phi x . phi y has sense).
      - o_i: U_i(x) (Lemma V).
      - h: (Ep)(Ey)(St(p, x, y) . Off(p, x, y)) . ~(Ep)(Ey)St(p, y, x): an out-form with an
        off-state (R_i(h, o_i)), and no in-edge. h' fails the first (markers only); a, b
        fail the second (R_n(b, a), R_n(a, b)); the o_i have no out-edge.
      - h': (Ep)(Ey)St(p, x, y) . ~(Ep)(Ey)(St(p, x, y) . Off(p, x, y)). h fails the second
        (R_i has off-states); a, b fail it (R_n(a, b) has the off-state (h, o_n)); the o_i
        fail the first.
      - a and b: let i_0 := min(S \ T) (nonempty: S \ T and T \ S are infinite by
        genericity). D_a(x) := (Ew)(Ep)(U_{i_0}(w) . (Eu)St(p, u, w) . (Ey)(p(x, y) . ~p(y,
        x))): the two-way pair excludes the markers, so p = R_{i_0}; at chi* R_{i_0}(a, b)
        is true and R_{i_0}(b, a) false; no other pair runs both ways. D_b likewise with
        (Ey)(p(y, x) . ~p(x, y)). (The draft's Unit_{i_0}(w, p) here had no admitted
        instance at x := a: the named two-way pair and Rf's off-state both need the hubs,
        (St); referee.)
      - Sense of each 5.5321 sentence: Lemma S (in the doubled instance the two copies sit
        in units m != m'; for D_a, x and x' on a and b, each copy's y on the other: y is
        constrained only by the letters free in its own body). The doubled sentence is false
        at chi* (uniqueness above), so each 5.5321 sentence is true.
    - Lemma C (A6a, A6s, A7). For n > i let e_{i,n} be the unit shift: R_i -> R_n, f_{i,j}
      -> f_{n,j}, o_i -> o_n, h, h', a, b fixed. A finite set of indices goes to fresh
      indices by an injective shift, a state-preserving embedding of the frame whose image
      shares no form with its source. A7: for a finite situation s (finitely many states,
      each with a value), the conjunction of the corresponding literals in decimal names has
      sense (AC: its atoms are states; Fit: its tokens on the shifted states), its
      projection r maps the tokens onto s's states, and its sense is s. A6s: tokens and
      senses lie on disjoint sets of forms, so no nonempty D' has r(D') = D' (hereditarily,
      no cycle). A6a: tokens are states of A by the definition of fit (M+). The same
      relocation is X50's Lemma 1.
    - Remaining axioms of Phi: A4, A5, A13, A14 and A19 by construction; A8 (definitions
      well-founded, uniform, one per sign; syntax settled without meaning) is a property of
      the notation (X49's decimal names, G*), not of the frame (A19: (a b) is a frame
      automorphism, so a and b are indiscernible, X26); A11 at kinds 1-3 for G* (X50-X52).
      With Lemma C and A16-A18 above, every axiom holds: Phi is a model of TLP.

ORDERS (rev. 21): two orders on the 526 propositions, recorded for formal scrutiny
- T, the canonical tree. Footnote to 1: "n.1, n.2, ... are comments on No. n; n.m1, n.m2
  ... comments on No. n.m". In the user's notation, X <-T X.Y and X.Y <-T X.YZ.
  - parent(x) = the longest proper prefix of x's digit string that is itself a
    proposition number. Example: parent(2.0121) = 2.012; parent(2.01) = 2, since 2.0 does
    not exist.
  - T is a forest with roots 1-7 and maximum depth 5.
  - Reading order L is the decimal order of the numbers.
- D, the derivation order: c <-D p when p is listed among c's premises after "<-" in the
  proposition tags.
  - Extraction rule: proposition numbers after "<-", "(cf. ...)" excluded, not preceded
    by a letter. Names like A4, D6b, S1 are premises outside the text and are not
    proposition numbers.
  - Facts (script, rev. 21; rev. 29: 335 edges into 252, after 2.02331 <- 5.526): D is
    acyclic. There are 335 textual edges into 252 propositions, and 83 propositions also
    cite axioms, derivations or signature items. Rev. 37: 333 edges (5.5262 <- 5.526 and
    5.5302 <- 2.0233 dropped; both tags are AX now). Rev. 38: 334 (2.026 <- 5.5302 added,
    a forward edge; A1 is D1). The audit could not reproduce "83"
    (it counted 77).
- D compared with T, edge by edge (c <-D p):
  - with the tree (p is a T-ancestor of c): 71 (rev. 37: 70);
  - rev. 37: backward cross 241 (5.5302 <- 2.0233 dropped); forward and inverted
    unchanged; rev. 38: forward 20 (2.026 <- 5.5302);
  - backward cross (p in another branch, earlier in L): 242;
  - forward cross (p later in L, not a descendant): 19 (rev. 29: + 2.02331 <- 5.526);
  - inverted (p is a T-descendant of c): 3. These are 2.02 <-D 2.021, 5.5 <-D 5.502 and
    6.4 <-D 6.41.
- D together with T (each comment taken as presupposing its parent) has exactly three
  cycles, the three inversions. So D does not extend T. The order the axiomatic system
  imposes is independent of the canonical tree, except that it agrees with it on 71 edges.
- Forward cross edges (19; 2.02331<-5.526 added in rev. 29): 1.11<-2.04, 1.11<-2.063, 1.13<-2.063, 2.0122<-3.3,
  2.15121<-2.222, 2.202<-2.203, 4.0312<-4.0621, 4.0312<-4.4, 4.062<-4.0641,
  4.0621<-4.4, 4.0641<-4.4, 4.1<-4.4, 4.1211<-4.4, 5.441<-5.52, 5.441<-5.53,
  5.474<-5.5, 6.031<-6.1231, 6.1265<-6.127, 2.02331<-5.526 (added in rev. 37; the
  list printed 18).
- Two depths. LI's level counts decimal digits (footnote: the figures "indicate the logical
  importance"). T-depth counts ancestors. They differ where a 0 digit skips a level (2.01
  has level 2 and T-depth 1). LI uses only the level, never T's edges.
- Open questions for scrutiny:
  - Is the inversion set minimal, i.e., the fewest D-edges whose removal makes D + T
    acyclic? It has size 3, and each inversion lies on its own cycle, so yes.
  - Does derivation depth correlate with T-depth or with level?
  - Are the 19 forward edges essential, or could each be rerouted through earlier
    premises?
  - Does the D-order of the axioms' textual sources match their LI levels?
- Correction: edge counts before rev. 21 (418) included spurious edges, read from axiom
  names (A4 as 4, S1 as 1). The cycle check was unaffected.

  - Internal properties cannot be de re too: then same-form objects would differ in more

REVISIONS 2026-10-31, rev. 56 (X50: E32a, Phi's A11 at kinds 1-2)
- X50. Phi's A11 under J-N's adequate notation is PROVED at kinds 1-2. In Phi, sense is the
  atom clause plus fit, since hereditary A6s never binds (fresh units). Fit is a finite tree
  problem over element types, so it is decidable. Ranges are quantifier-free, so each sign
  translates into a first-order formula with q variables. q-profiles of worlds decide
  every such formula (R2 Thm 6, rechecked), and finite representatives make tautologyhood
  decidable. Checked by an independent referee's literal implementations: 10,675 signs,
  9,700 signs with 8,520 worlds, 63,000 sentences, 81 end-to-end cases; 0 mismatches.
- Kind 3: OPEN. The drafted fit state was refuted on Phi (missing occurrence sets; missing
  reservations for promoted names). A repaired state matched brute force on cuts in every
  test. It has still to be proved on the infinite frame, with E31's grammar; E31 gains
  questions (typing, variabilization of a filler's name, holes in inner series signs).
- E32 stays open (kind 3; A16-A18 at proof level). No inconsistency is known. System
  numbers unchanged.

REVISIONS 2026-10-08, rev. 14 (THEOREM 3, independent check)
- An independent referee checked the rev. 13 graph encoding and found that it confirmed two
  gaps:
  - The rev. 13 formula for E was wrong under weak exclusion. In ~(Ez)phi z, x and y are
    not in z's scope, so z may take their values and E is empty. Fixed:
    E(x, y) := (Ephi)(phi x . phi y . ~(Ez)(phi z . phi x . phi y)).
  - Every arity bullet of THEOREM 3 (rev. 6-13) assumed full frames: every form applies to
    every tuple of objects. The ledger never commits to that (same form is an orbit,
    2.0233). Countermodels to the dichotomy, satisfying A1-A12 at every kind:
    - B3: a 2-place form whose frame is a perfect matching;
    - B5: infinitely many 1-place forms, each applicable to one object.
- THEOREM 3 restated as a condition on frames:
  - (a) and (b): necessary conditions at kinds 1-2;
  - (c): kind 3 restricts more. B4 (the successor frame) is decidable at kinds 1-2 but not
    at kind 3;
  - for full frames: the old dichotomy.
- Also corrected:
  - Church's reduction needs no infinite counter-models here (validity over all graphs
    suffices).
  - The every-world A12 argument for |A| = aleph_0 is now stated for full frames only. LI's
    rejection of it stands anyway, since it strengthens 5.526 beyond its wording.
  - Convention made explicit: an atom whose tuple is not a state of the frame is false.
- C11/6.125: under weak exclusion, kind 3 does define + and x in a world realizing
  (N, S) (B4 method), so 6.125 fails there, as claimed.

  are not readings.

SIGNATURE
O; A with kappa (nonempty finite partial slot maps P -> O); H (incidence hypergraph);
C (constraint hypergraph, finitary); Lambda = Sol(C); chi* in Lambda; Pi (designated class of
pictures (D, rho, tau)); r induced; sense at chi: sigma_{P,chi} = (chi|D) o r^-1
(sigma_P := sigma_{P,chi*}).
Prop (propositions; phase 1: finite truth-functions of elementary propositions; generality
in phase 2). [[phi]] is computed by Boolean operations: in Clopen(Lambda) for finite
truth-functions, in the target algebra (3.42) with generality. Truth at chi: chi in [[phi]].
- Elementary proposition: picture with D = {d}, sign present (pi(d) = 1), sense {r(d) -> 1}
  (4.21, 4.22). Negation is a truth-operation, not a medium value (4.0621).
- D_phi := union of the elementary media; operation signs have no rho-image (4.0312, 4.441).
- Pi contains the contingent propositions (4.01). Tautologies and contradictions are in
  Prop \ Pi (4.462). (Rev. 37: under M+ every contingent proposition has a nonempty
  medium, its own sign.)
- Self-settling: the truth value is fixed, at every world where the sign exists, by its own
  medium. This is the failure of literal 2.224. (Rev. 46, X41: s and p v s are
  self-settling and have sense; 2.224 is restricted.)
- Rev. 37 (X29, M+): the medium of any sign, general signs included, is the whole sign,
  every signifying token included. D_phi above is the finite stage. A completely general
  sign has sense iff its support misses its own tokens. (Rev. 46, X41: iff its whole sign
  fits the frame.) Rev. 52 (X47): a defined sign takes no tokens of its own; a sign with
  defined signs is possible, and has sense, iff its translation fits (unique up to
  renaming of bound letters, A8).
- Rev. 37: the value convention C-nv (rev. 32, X24) and (E1) are stated in ENTRYPOINT,
  under "Values". Until rev. 32 atoms outside the frame were false (C-false). Rev. 57
  (X51): vacuous binders are transparent, an exception to C-nv (3.328 s1; 3.313).
- Multiplicity of a state: |dom kappa(a)|. r preserves it (tau bijects slots; 4.04).
- Generality (phase 2): N(xi-bar) negates all values of a propositional variable (5.502).
  The values are described by enumeration, by a function fx, or by a formal law (formal
  series [a, x, O'x], 5.2522) (5.501). [[N(xi-bar)]] = intersection of the complements.
  Kind 2 is first-order generality; kind 3 adds the ancestral (4.1273). Kind 3's signs:
  the series grammar G* (X51).
  Quantifiers are exclusive (5.53) in the weak sense: a quantifier excludes the values of
  the variables free in its scope (LI; see THEOREM 3). Object and form variables alike
  (rev. 30, explicit; X23). Without it, B1'' with chi* = {R_0(a, b)} fails A12 (one true
  form vs two), and zeta fails A16 (its descriptions count forms). The system would stay
  consistent without it: B1'' with all R_i(a, b) true and all R_i(b, a) false.
- Senses in the target algebra are Borel (countable A), so the fair product measure mu on
  {0,1}^A (each atom 1/2, independent; 5.152) applies. Probability: P(s|r) =
  mu([[r]] ∩ [[s]]) / mu([[r]]), which is 5.15's Trs/Tr for finite truth-functions.
  Uncountable A needs the Radon extension of mu.
S1 Constant domain and form: every world shares O and kappa; F is not indexed by world.
   2.012, 2.021-2.024, 2.027.
   Built into the signature: worlds are points of {0,1}^A over a single A.
   Varying-domain models (which violate 2.024) lie outside this signature.
S2 Closedness: C is finitary, so each constraint is clopen and Lambda is closed.
   A nonempty flip-closed subset of {0,1}^A is dense. So under S2:
   - 1.21 <-> A4 for every A;
   - every finite projection full <-> Lambda = {0,1}^A;
   - hierarchy: pairwise < k-wise < finite = full.
   The finite-difference class of chi* is flip-closed with every finite projection full, yet
   is not {0,1}^A. It needs infinitary hyperedges.
   Rev. 50 (X45): dropped from TLP's commitments (congruent). A4 gives Lambda = {0,1}^A,
   which is closed, and no derivation cites S2; it bounds only countermodels (A4's).
   1.21's converse becomes a remark. K3 is the only commitment without a textual source.
S4 States: a state of affairs is a nonempty finite partial slot map kappa(a): P -> O.
   Sources: 2.01, 2.03, 2.031, 3.1432. Slots vs. labels is notation.
   Rev. 32 (X24): split.
   - The typing (states are partial slot maps) stays in the signature.
   - Nonemptiness follows from A14.
   - Finiteness is a derivation, D-S4 <- A11 (J-FS), A7, S3. Under J-FS every
     proposition is a finite sign. By A7, every state a is the sense of a picture whose
     medium d has the same multiplicity (tau bijects slots; 4.04: "die gleiche logische
     (mathematische) Mannigfaltigkeit"). So every state is finite.
   It is no longer a weight-0 commitment. 4.2211 stays unviolated: it is concessive, and
   its consequent holds by A1 and D3.
   (Formerly the typing half of A2; the distinctness half is now D2.)
S3 Natural pictures: Pi = all triples (D, rho, tau) with
   - D a finite nonempty set of states of a medium space M (rev. 30; was "of A");
   - rho injective on the names (4.0311, 5.53);
   - tau a bijection of slots;
   - r: D -> A well-defined;
   subject only to A6d (rev. 46, X41: to A6s, r(D) ≠ D). Source: 5.473 ("Everything which is possible in logic is also
   permitted"). LI: a gappy Pi would be a non-textual commitment, so S3 holds.
   Rev. 30 (E14, X23): "D ⊆ A" is no longer built in. It is A6a's content (M = A, from
   2.141), not 5.473's. S3 + A6a is the old S3, a congruent choice, and A6a stays
   independent: its CM (an external medium) now satisfies S3.
   Copy property (CP): every finite set of states has a disjoint isomorphic copy, i.e., a
   D' ⊆ A disjoint from it and (rho, tau) inducing a bijection onto it. The inverse of an
   admissible (rho, tau) is admissible, so the relation is symmetric.

A6 Pictures:
   (a) Media are facts of the world they depict (2.141, 3.14). P itself = medium + projection
       (2.1513); the projection is not a configuration.
       CM: external medium (M disjoint from A). Rev. 30: S3 no longer builds in D ⊆ A
       (E14), so the CM satisfies S3.
   D6b (THM under LI, <- A6d, A4; formerly A6b). Literal 2.224: no picture's truth value
       is fixed by its own configuration. For every P in Pi and chi in Lambda, some worlds
       agreeing with chi on D make P true and some make it false.
       Scope: all of Pi, hence (4.01) compound contingent propositions too. Elementary
       disjointness (2.173) does not settle compounds. Example: p v q with q depicting p's
       medium is true wherever the sign exists. Under that rho such a sign has no sense
       (cf. 4.442); D10 asks for some rho that gives it one.
   (c) DROPPED under LI. It was restriction closure, with no text, and is no longer needed
       for 2.173.
   Derived: r(D) ∩ D = empty (2.173) <- A6d. r(D) not ⊆ D <- D6b.
   (d) ADOPTED under LI (rev. 6-45). RETIRED in rev. 46 (X41): 3.332 is read as containment
       (X40), and s and p v s have sense. Literal 3.332 ("no proposition can say anything about itself"): for every
       picture or proposition, the support of its sense (the atoms [[phi]] depends on) is
       disjoint from its medium. Read as a condition on what counts as a meaning assignment.
       Textual: 3.332, 2.173, 4.442, 5.6331. (Rev. 45, X40: 3.332 is read as containment
       and 4.442 as formal; neither sources (d). 2.173 does on its material reading only.)
       CM [ok]: B3 with Pi = all well-formed triples (S3 without the A6d restriction;
       until rev. 19, B2, which violates A13).
       - Pi then contains p & q with q depicting p's medium, so A6d fails.
       - A1-A5, A6a, A8, A11-A13 do not mention admissibility.
       - A7 is met by the disjoint pictures already in Pi.
       Consequences: (d) + A4 imply (b) for every contingent proposition; (d) gives 2.173
       directly, so (c) is no longer needed for it.
       Why it matters: (b) alone admits reflexive compounds, e.g., p & q with q depicting p's
       medium. That sign is not self-settling but says something about itself. And for
       self-settling reflexive compounds, every name has a meaning but there is no sense,
       against 5.4733. With (d), such assignments are not meaning-giving, so 5.4733 holds.
       LI: adopted. The considerations that settled it:
       - 6.113, second sentence ("the truth or falsehood of non-logical propositions can not be
         recognized from the propositions alone"), is literal 2.224 for compounds.
       - With 5.4733, that forces at least A6d-: no meaning assignment makes a contingent
         sign self-settling.
       - Full (d) additionally excludes self-description that does not self-settle, e.g.
         p & q with q depicting p's medium. Only 3.332, read literally, asks for that.
       - Without (d), either 5.4733 fails (D6b applied per rho), or the "characteristic mark" of
         6.113 fails (D6b restricted to elementary pictures).
       - With (d), D6b is derived and A6c is unnecessary.
   (s) ADOPTED in rev. 46 (X41). 3.13, read (Sit): no picture's sense is its own sign-fact:
       sigma_{P,chi} ≠ chi|D for every P and chi; equivalently r(D) ≠ D. Rev. 47 (X42,
       J-sub): hereditary, since every part of a picture is a picture: no nonempty D' ⊆ D
       has r(D') = D', i.e. r has no cycle. Supported by
       4.024, 4.061 and 2.161. Senses that are not situations are not affected. CM:
       unrestricted Pi over Phi. With A7 it gives the THEOREM and D10. D6b (2.224) is
       retired; its kept content is the type reading.
A7 Adequacy (per-situation, modal): every nonempty finite situation sigma is the sense of some
   picture at some world, i.e., sigma = sigma_{P,chi} for some P in Pi and chi in Lambda.
   2.19, 2.171, 3.001, 4.5(ii).
   Equivalent to: atomic situations are depictable, and depictability is closed under finite
   conjunction. CM: any finite nonempty A.
   - Empty situation excluded. Its picture has D = empty, which is not a fact (A6a); admitting
     it gives [[sigma]] = Lambda, against 2.225.
   - Actual-world reading rejected. sigma_P preserves polarity, so A7 at chi* would force chi*
     to have infinitely many positive and infinitely many negative atomic facts. That is not a
     structure axiom.
   - A7c (collective): every nonempty finite situation is the union of the senses of finitely
     many pictures. 2.19 and 3.01 are collective, but they don't exclude A7. Under A7c alone,
     any finite |A| >= 2 is consistent.
   - 4.5(ii): "every possible sense can be expressed by a symbol, which falls under the
     description". That is per-situation, for propositions.
   LI: A7. A7c leaves out 4.5 (level 1). Either way, D10 forces infinitude (THEOREM,
   route 2).
A8 Syntax: definitions well-founded, uniform, one per sign; syntax established without
   mention of meaning (3.33). 3.23, 3.261, 3.33, 3.3442, 5.451. CM: circular definition.
   LI: A8e (effective syntax) is a strengthening, not a reading. It would also make names
   countable and, with infinite A, fix |A| = aleph_0, violating 4.128 and 5.453.
   (Rev. 55, X49: A11's adequate notation has the same corollary, now a J6 effect; A8e
   stays rejected as a strengthening.)
A11 Calculability: whether a proposition is a tautology is decidable, given the names
   (rev. 52, X47: and the definitions of its defined signs; A8e stays rejected).
   5.551, 6.126, 6.127 (also 6.1262, 6.125). Adopted under LI.
   With uncountably many names (rev. 22): "decidable, given the names" means computable
   from the finite type, i.e., the sign together with the frame restricted to its named
   objects. Rev. 32: under C-nv, the names' types in the whole frame. Rev. 41 (J-N, X36):
   that is, the named objects' finite (quantifier-free) frame type, as in rev. 22, not
   their complete type. Read as the complete type, the empty tuple's type would be the
   frame theory, and condition (d) would collapse.
   Rev. 55 (X49): J-N re-decided (provisional): "given the names" = names in an adequate
   notation. J-Ns: a name's symbol carries its real name (3.3411; 2.0123, 3.311, 4.126), so
   an input cut to the finite type or to forms up to isomorphism is a strengthening of
   6.126, not a reading. J-Nn: some adequate notation (6.122, "in einer entsprechenden
   Notation"), not every correct one (that would be a strengthening). J-Nf: names are
   finite strings ("mechanisch", 6.1262). Oracle inputs stay excluded (J-FS).
   Consequences: O and the forms countable, |A| = aleph_0 (J6; no new mark); Phi ⊔ eta_0
   fails A11.
   J-FS (rev. 32; admissibility judgment, logged): "decidable" is a finite procedure on
   the whole sign: 6.126 "kann man berechnen, indem man die logischen Eigenschaften des
   Symbols berechnet" (and, of proofs, "nach blossen Zeichenregeln"; rev. 44: two
   sentences, no longer run together), 6.122 "durch das
   blosse Ansehen", 6.1262 "mechanisches Hilfsmittel", 5.551 "ohne weiteres". So every
   proposition is a finite sign, and kind-1 enumerations are finite. It carries D-S4,
   A16's cap |O| <= aleph_0, and the finite signs of L_T.
   CM (rev. 24): the countable random loopless digraph as the actual world, on the
   irreflexive full frame (one 2-place form on all pairs of distinct objects). Until rev.
   24 the frame contained R(x, x), against A14.
   - A12, actual-world reading, holds: the theory is aleph_0-categorical, and exclusive
     quantifiers state its extension axioms.
   - A11 fails: the frame contains K_{X,Y} for disjoint infinite X and Y, so tautologyhood
     is undecidable (THEOREM 3 (a)).
   - A7 holds by CP; A13 and A14 hold. [ok, rev. 24 referee]
   (Rev. 9 claimed that A11 would follow from A12 under the every-world strengthening of
   5.526, which is not adopted. That holds for kinds 1-2 only. Under kind 3 it is open;
   see THEOREM 3.)
A12 (D12 since rev. 33, derived from A17; X25) Complete general description: if chi* is
   the actual world, it is fixed up to
   isomorphism (two-sorted; see Models), among the worlds of Lambda, by the completely
   general propositions true in it. Stated conditionally (rev. 22), so that A5 stays
   independent: with no chi*, A12 holds vacuously. Generality ranges

A15 Singling out (rev. 24; DERIVED since rev. 29: D15 <- A16, X22): if chi* is the actual
   world, every object fixed by
   Aut(H, C, chi*) is singled out by one completely general description: a single finite
   sign phi with "(Ex)phi x : ~(Ex, y).phi x . phi y" true in chi* and phi true of it
   (5.5321; kinds 1-3, weak exclusion, generality over forms).
   2.02331: "Entweder ein Ding hat Eigenschaften, die kein anderes hat, dann kann man es
   ohneweiteres durch eine Beschreibung aus den anderen herausheben, und darauf hinweisen;
   oder aber, es gibt mehrere Dinge, die ihre saemtlichen Eigenschaften gemeinsam haben,
   dann ist es ueberhaupt unmoeglich auf eines von ihnen zu zeigen." / "Either a thing has
   properties which no other has, and then one can distinguish it straight away from the
   others by a description and refer to it; or, on the other hand, there are several
   things which have the totality of their properties in common, and then it is quite
   impossible to point to any one of them." V1.
   - Reading (plain): "Eigenschaften" unqualified (every feature invariant under
     Aut(H, C, chi*)); horn 1 works through external properties (4.023), since a
     description sees only the facts; "eine Beschreibung" is one finite sign;
     "ueberhaupt unmoeglich ... zu zeigen" is pointing by any means, naming included; the
     either/or is exhaustive. Horn 1 under this reading is A15.
   - Admissibility judgments (rev. 25, after the referee; X20):
     - J2. "Pointing" is naming apart: no set of elucidations fixes which of two
       conjugates a name means (3.263). Read as "cannot be given a name", horn 2 would
       contradict D9 in B1'' and B3.
     - J4. "Eigenschaften" unqualified covers internal and external properties: 2.01231
       uses the word for both, and 2.0233 adds "externen" when it means only those. The
       group that preserves form (Aut(H, C)) and the facts is Aut(H, C, chi*).
       Contestable: 4.122 calls external relations the "eigentlichen", and 4.123 notes
       the "schwankenden Gebrauch" of the word "Eigenschaft".
     - J5. "Eine Beschreibung" is completely general. It follows from J4 with 4.023: a
       description describes by the properties, and these properties are not tied to
       particular objects. (The referee's ground, that names can be replaced by their
       descriptions, fails in beta: b's name has none.) The de re alternative, where
       properties and descriptions may involve particular objects, is E16.
   - LI: (A) adopt, with no restriction, over (B) a restricted reading and (C) a violation
     (LI RESOLUTION, E13; X20). Provisional: the de re reading is not yet costed (E16,
     a HIGH ALERT candidate). (Rev. 27-29: costed in X21, dissolved in X22. A15 is D15.)
   - Horn 2 and the "Denn" sentence are theorems (UNS part): objects with the same type
     cannot be singled out by any description, and Aut-conjugates cannot be named apart
     (3.263). At every |O|.
   - CM: alpha (finite O, all false). Also beta and gamma (FORMAL NOTES). Models: B1'' and
     B3 (no fixed objects, so A15 holds vacuously); B1'' with exactly one true fact (both
     objects fixed, both describable). (These held under C-false. Under C-nv alpha with
     chi* all false satisfies A16 and D15, so D15's CMs are beta and gamma (rev. 32). B1''
     with one fact fails A18 (rev. 34).)
   - Consequences:
     - with horn 2: describable <=> fixed by Aut(H, C, chi*) <=> can be named apart, at
       every |O| (this restores the old tag's biconditional, as a derivation from A15);
     - A15 alone (rev. 25: A12 is not needed) excludes an all-false actual world on every
       frame with an object fixed by Aut(H, C): M+ is empty, so all objects share one
       type (|O| >= 2). It excludes beta's and gamma's (frame, chi*) pairs, not their
       frames;
     - like A12, A15 limits which world can be actual: on alpha's frame, chi* =
       {R_0(a, b)} satisfies it, its single flip (all false) does not. 1.21 and 2.0231
       are about Lambda, so they are not violated;
     - the existing countermodels all satisfy A15 (A7's with chi* = R(a, b) true), so no
       axiom becomes derivable;
     - D9 stays congruent only under J2;
     - A15 implies A15'' ("every object with a unique type is singled out by one
       description", the old "(D)" reading of horn 1) and makes the either/or
       exhaustive.
   - Independent of the alternative convention for atoms outside the frame (E8): alpha
     disappears there, but beta and gamma remain. (Rev. 32: that convention, C-nv, is now
     adopted.)
   [E13 analyst, rev. 24; ok, rev. 25 referee, with corrections; X20 provisional, E16]

   - Models: B1'' with chi* = {R_0(a, b)}; zeta (infinite O). [ok, rev. 30 referee; zeta's

     - |O| <= aleph_0 (countably many completely general signs, each true of at most one
       object; finite signs by J-FS), restricting 4.128 and 5.453 together with D12 (A17)
       and D15 (J6; X45);

       may still move; the converse fails, beta);

       zeta has infinitely many;
     - at most one object occurs in no state of the frame (two would be swappable). (Rev.
