DERIVATIONS (D: no claim to independence; several were formerly axioms)
D2 (THM, rev. 9) Distinct states have distinct slot maps  <- A7, DEF 2.15 (r well-defined).
   Suppose kappa(a) = kappa(a') with a ≠ a'. Then for any d aimed at a, r(d) is ambiguous,
   so {a -> 1} has no picture, against A7. Formerly the distinctness half of A2.
D6b: see A6 (retired in rev. 46, X41).
D9 (THM) Naming: every object has a name  <- D3, A7, DEF r.
   By D3, o lies in some a. By A7, {a -> 1} is depicted, so r(d) = a for some d, and rho hits
   every object of kappa(a). Propositions = pictures in this signature ("perceptible", 3.1, is
   unformalized).
   The old CM (countably many names, uncountably many objects) violates A7.
   Converse: D3 <- D9 + 3.328.
D10 (rev. 46, X41) Every possible sign expresses a sense under some admissible projection
   <- A7, A6s, S3, A6a, A4, A8. A sign's tokens T have an image D ≠ T (A7 for {T -> 1}
   with A6s; isos invert), so the projection onto D is admissible; general signs are
   never barred. Rev. 47 (X42): the proof needs hereditary A6s (on X41's form as written
   the broom frame satisfies the premises and fails D10). For named components with
   tokens T_n, A7 gives a cycle-free picture D -> T_n, whose inverse is cycle-free; names
   occurring only in general parts go injectively outside rho's image; atoms not fully
   named never enter a cycle. The two entries below are the rev. 8-45 record.
D10s (rev. 37, X29; HIGH ALERT #2; retired in rev. 46, X41) Every finite truth-function of elementary signs
   expresses a sense under some admissible projection  <- A7, S3, A6a, A8. With
   generality, it suffices that under one projection every component's support misses
   the whole medium. D10 as stated below ("every well-formed sign") is false: p v s, with
   s := (E phi)(Ex, y) phi xy, contradicts A6d under every projection. Record:
D10 (THM, rev. 8; formerly A10) Expressibility of signs: every well-formed propositional
   sign expresses a sense under some admissible projection  <- A7, S3, A4, A8 (rev. 30:
   A8 added; a circularly defined sign counted as well-formed would have no sense).
   Sources: 4.5(iii) ("every symbol which falls under the description can express a sense,
   if the meanings of the names are chosen accordingly"); 5.473.
   Under S3, A7 <-> CP <-> D10 [ok]:
   - A7 for sigma with domain T needs a D disjoint from T with an iso D -> T (A6d); then
     A4 gives a world with chi|D = sigma o r.
   - D10 for a sign with medium D needs an iso from D onto states outside D. The worst case
     is the conjunction of all components; tautologies have the null sense under any rho.
   - Isos invert, so both say CP.
   D10 is independent only if Pi is gappy. CM: B2 with Pi barred from media containing one
   state; A7 still holds there. S3 excludes such a Pi.
   Under A6a the sign of a form is itself a state of that form, so writing a sign shows its
   form is instantiated (5.5542).

D20 (rev. 46, X41; WITHDRAWN in rev. 47, X42: for finite A, Theta'(o)'s fully named
   instance needs tokens whose map onto A is a permutation, which hereditary A6s bars;
   valid only without a token condition on components. Record follows) A is infinite.
   Lemma F: for finite A, A19 with Theta'(x) (every state written as "phi(...) v ~phi(...)", x in o's
   place) yields a frame automorphism g with g(o) = o'. A16 makes chi* rigid, so g.chi*

THEOREM, rev. 46 (X41): A6s replaces D6b and A6d in both routes. Route 1: for finite A,
   A7 for the total situation needs r(D) = D = A. Route 2: for a finite multiplicity class
   K, A7 for "all of K true" needs D ⊆ K with |D| = |K|, so r(D) = D. A6s bars both, so
   every nonempty multiplicity class is infinite  <- A7, A6s, A6a, S3, D2. (Rev. 46:
   "D20 is a second route"; withdrawn in rev. 47.) Both routes hold under hereditary A6s. The entry below is the rev. 6-45 record.
THEOREM: A1, D3, A6a, D6b, A7 imply A infinite. (Rev. 37, final referee: minimal premises
   A1, A13, A6a, A6d, A7, S3; rev. 38: A1 is D1 <- A19. A6d alone contradicts r(D) = D = A. Injectivity of r and A4
   are not needed. Route 2 uses D10 only on elementary truth-functions, i.e. D10s.)
   Proof. A1 + D3 give A nonempty. Suppose A is finite. A total situation is then a nonempty
   finite situation, so A7 gives a P with r(D) = A. Since r is injective, |D| = |A|, so D = A
   and r(D) ⊆ D. Then P is true iff pi o r = pi, which is a function of pi, against D6b.
   Without A1 + D3, O empty satisfies A6 and A7 vacuously with A finite.
   With 2.173: |dom sigma| <= |A|/2 for every picture.
   Route 1 depends on A7; it fails under A7c.
   Route 2 (A4, A6a, D6b, D10): every nonempty multiplicity class of A is infinite.
   Proof. Let K be a finite class. By A4, the conjunction whose elementary media are all of K
   can exist as a sign. Under every rho its depicted states have the same multiplicity, so
   they lie in K = D_phi. So under every rho it is true wherever the sign exists
   (self-settling), hence without sense by D6b. D10 requires some rho that gives it sense.
   Route 2 is independent of A7/A7c. Under S3, D10 <-> A7, so the two routes coincide.
   Textual standing:
   - 4.1272, read: the number of objects is unsayable (UNS), not unsettleable. A metatheorem
     does not say it.
   - 4.463 calls logical space infinite (Ogden: "the whole infinite logical space").
   - 4.128 (logical forms anumerical) fits "infinite": "infinite" is not a number. (Rev.
     29: the gloss "no finite number pre-eminent" was an unmarked restriction; 4.128 is
     now marked RESTRICTED for aleph_0 effects, J6.)
   - 5.55-5.557 (read): mild tension only. The axioms fix no form and no number of names:
     models exist with |O| = 2 (B1'; A13 excludes |O| = 1) and infinitely many slot types.
     Route 2 anticipates only that
     every occurring form has infinitely many instances.
   - 5.535: the axiom of infinity concerns names (|O|). The THEOREM concerns |A|, so it does
     not settle |O|.
   - Against infinite A: 5.5262, strong (minimal-change) reading, which its parenthesis
     suggests: "the truth or falsehood of every proposition alters something in the general
     structure of the world". Completely general propositions are isomorphism-invariant, so
     the strong reading fails wherever a single flip can yield an isomorphic world. Checked
     cases:
       - infinite O with a unary form (f true on infinitely many, false on infinitely many);
       - the countable random graph;
       - any form with infinitely many pairwise object-disjoint states;
       - finite O with infinitely many slot types, if generality ranges over relations
         (5.5261).
     Every infinite A: open (no infinite frame found where it holds). (Rev. 33: zeta
     under C-nv, X25.)
     5.526 (complete description by completely general propositions) fails for infinite O
     with a full binary form for kinds 1-2: (N, successor) and (N + Z, successor) agree on
     all first-order sentences. Kind 3 separates them (C32).
   - 5.551 ("every question which can be decided at all by logic can be decided without
     further trouble"):
     with a 2-place form full on an infinite set, tautologyhood is undecidable. So with
     infinite A, 5.551 restricts the frame (THEOREM 3). For full frames it needs O finite
     (infinitely many forms) or finitely many forms, all 1-place; with A13, O finite. The
     same holds for
     6.126 (calculability), 6.127 ("every tautology itself shows that it is a tautology")
     and 6.1262 (proof only an expedient).
   - 6.125 ("possible ... to give at the outset a description of all 'true' logical
     propositions"): with infinite O, first-order generality keeps the tautologies r.e.
     (describable). Kind-3 generality (formal series) makes them non-arithmetical (4.1273),
     so not describable.
   - Net: {1.1 + 2.141 (A6a), 2.224 (D6b), 4.5 (A7/D10)} force infinite A. 5.5262 (strong)
     fails in all checked infinite cases. The formalized text is inconsistent here.
     LI: keep A6a (1.1, 3.14: levels 1-2), D6b and 4.5 (level 1). 5.5262 is RESTRICTED to
     its special clause: the change alters the general structure whenever some count it
     changes is finite. That is the sense of its parenthesis. The general minimal-change
     reading is what fails. (Rev. 33-34: superseded. Under C-nv, zeta and Phi satisfy the
     strong reading; the checked failures are worlds that A18 excludes. 5.5262 is read
     plainly, X25, X26.)
   - Decidability and complete description: THEOREM 3.
COROLLARY (A8e): names are countable. With D9 (THM), |O| <= aleph_0. With countable P,
   |A| = aleph_0. So either O is infinite or there are infinitely many structures (2.033).
   That makes aleph_0 pre-eminent, against 4.128, and 4.1272 lists "there are aleph_0
   objects" as nonsense. LI: A8e rejected.
THEOREM 3 (forms) [rev. 14: a condition on frames]. A11 restricts the frame (which states
   exist), not |O| or arity as such. Convention (until rev. 32, C-false): an atom whose
   tuple is not a state of the frame is false. (The alternative, that it is not a value of its function (5.501), changes
   universal quantification; not checked.) Rev. 32: the alternative (C-nv) is adopted
   (X24). (a), (c) and Lemma U are re-checked under it; Lemma U_v needs classes in the
   frame-expanded signature. New necessary condition (d): the frame's own theory (kinds
   1-3) must be decidable.
   Necessary conditions for A11, already at kinds 1-2 [ok, rev. 14 referee]:
   (a) No 2-place form's frame contains K_{n,n} with disjoint sides for every n. In
       particular none is full on X x Y with X and Y infinite (X = Y allowed).
       - Encode a countable graph as an incidence structure on the two sides. From any
         world, Left(x) := (Ey)Rxy and Adj(u, v) := (Ee)(Rue . Rve) read back a graph.
       - So validity over graphs reduces to tautologyhood. That validity problem is
         undecidable (Church, plus a standard interpretation of binary structures in
         graphs).
       - X and Y need not be definable. The K_{n,n} version uses Trakhtenbrot-Vaught
         inseparability.
       - Forms with more places: the same argument by existential projection: E'(x, y) :=
         (Ez1)...(Ez_k-2) R(x, y, z...). [ok for full frames, rev. 22 referee; sparse
         frames not checked] Rev. 35: sparse frames checked, with the union over forms:
         condition (a_k*) (X27).
   (b) With generality over forms (5.5261), the 1-place forms do not realize every finite
       graph as an E-graph, where
         E(x, y) := (Ephi)(phi x . phi y . ~(Ez)(phi z . phi x . phi y)).
       - x and y must occur in z's scope, or weak exclusion lets z take their values. The
         rev. 13 formula ~(Ez)phi z made E empty.
       - Sufficient for failure: infinitely many 1-place forms on a common infinite set of
         objects. Then every countable graph is some world's E-graph. Relativize to objects
         with an E-neighbor; validity over graphs without isolated vertices is undecidable.
   (c) Kind 3 restricts more. Model B4: O = N; one 2-place form; frame = the successor
       states R(n, n+1).
       - Kinds 1-2: decidable. With P = {n : R(n, n+1) true}, tautologyhood becomes an S1S
         sentence, which Buechi's theorem decides.
       - Kind 3: true arithmetic reduces to tautologyhood [ok, referee].
         - Full := (x)(Ey)Rxy holds only in the all-true world.
         - There, Id(u, v) := (Ew)(Ruw . Rvw) defines identity.
         - Inclusive formal series translate into weakly exclusive ones, because
           substitution of variables commutes with the semantics. So + and x are definable.
           (Rev. 36: the step is X28 Claim 1 with Id for "=", and with the C-nv guards,
           which work since O = N.)
   Rev. 38 (X31): under M+ A11 is a promise problem (signs with sense). (a_k*) and (b_k)
       stay necessary through a named block, provided names may occur and quantifiers
       skip named objects. Without names they need an Aut-invariant witnessing
       sub-family and room for the encoding. (d) becomes (d+): decidable on the
       sentences that fit the frame. B4 at kind 3: open under M+.
   (d) Rev. 32 and 35 (X27): the frame's own theory (kinds 1-3) is decidable; necessary
       under C-nv, and it already bites at kind 2 (path forests). (c) is an instance of
       it. Necessary conditions in full: (a_k*), (b_k), (d). Not sufficient: S(K_omega).
   Sufficient for kind 3 to add nothing: a uniform bound on the orbit types of m-tuples
   over all worlds, as in Lemma U, or more generally (rev. 30) a bound B(v), computable in
   v and uniform over worlds, on the v-variable classes of tuples (Lemma U_v, FORMAL
   NOTES). Decidability at kinds 1-2 must then be checked per frame.
   B1, B2, B3 and B5 meet both.
   The rev. 6-13 dichotomy ("O finite or every form 1-place"; rev. 13 added "finitely many
   forms") is false in general. Countermodels satisfying A1-A12 at every kind [ok, referee]:
   - B3 (a 2-place form over infinite O);
   - B5 (infinitely many 1-place forms over infinite O).
   It holds for full frames. Rev. 24: a full frame is one where every form applies to
   every tuple with at least two distinct objects (the old "every tuple of objects"
   contains R(x, x), so under A14 there were none). Proof for k >= 3 under the new
   definition: E'(x, y) := (Ez1)...(Ez_k-2)R(x, y, z...) makes the variables pairwise
   distinct (weak exclusion); a world can make E' any loopless digraph on O, and only
   those, so (a)'s reduction goes through [ok, rev. 24 referee]:
   - (a) and (b) give: O finite (infinitely many slot types), or O infinite with finitely
     many slot types, all 1-place;
   - A13 (2.0121, rev. 19) excludes the second branch: with only 1-place forms, no object
     combines with another. So for full frames, O is finite and |O| >= 2;
   - A14 (rev. 23) excludes 1-place forms in every frame, full or sparse. So (b) does not
     arise in the adopted system; it stays as a result about the A1-A13 frames. Rev. 35:
     wrong in substance. The mechanism (forms as vertices) carries over to k-place forms
     as (b_k) (X27);
   - with O finite, infinite A needs infinitely many slot types (unconditional).
   Full frames are not a commitment: same form is an orbit (2.0233), and 2.0251 has
   objects of several forms. Which frames satisfy A11: open.
   - B1 satisfies A11 and A12 [ok]. With n objects, general propositions fix the number of
     relations of each arity and pattern; finitely many enumerations of O let one alignment
     serve all, so the world is fixed up to isomorphism. Decidable over the fixed finite
     domain; with generality over forms, the form sort has finitely many patterns, so it
     stays monadic.
   - B2 (countable O) satisfies A11 and A12 [ok]: monadic and decidable; the counts of each
     cell fix a countable world.
   - Retired in rev. 13: the proof of the 1-place exclusion through every-world A12, which
     compared a ray with a ray plus a Z-line encoded as unary forms (Hanf locality). It
     holds for kinds 1-2 only; kind 3 separates the two by the ancestral of E.
   Every-world strengthening of 5.526: not adopted. It strengthens 5.526 beyond its
   wording, so it is not a reading. (Rev. 33: adopted as A17 from 5.5262's second
   sentence (X25). The full-frame aleph_0 effect below is a J6 mark. Rev. 37: under M+
   no full frame admits a model.)
   - For full frames it forces |A| = aleph_0:
     - in B2-type frames, worlds with aleph_0 vs. aleph_1 f's agree on all general
       propositions (kind 3 collapses);
     - in B1-type frames, a pattern class of aleph_0 vs. aleph_1 slot types cannot be
       told apart in the same way.
     That singles out aleph_0, against 4.128 and 5.453. (The rev. 13 version, "at every
     kind for uncountable O" by Loewenheim-Skolem, was loose: L-S gives substructures,
     not worlds on the same O.)
   - Whether it would also exclude countable O with a full 2-place form, and so imply A11,
     depends on kind 3. For kinds 1-2 it does ((N, S) vs. (N + Z, S)). Under kind 3 (N, S)
     is fixed by its general propositions (C32), and the countable case is open.
   Textual fit: the number of names stays open (5.55, 5.535, 4.128); forms are not
   enumerated (5.554, 5.5541); which elementary propositions exist is left to application
   (5.557, read as "which").
   Operations and kind-3 generality (formal series):
   - If arbitrary computable operations were allowed, A11 would fail in every infinite A.
     A series "a cell has exactly h(n) members" (h computable) makes tautologyhood
     Pi^0_2-hard ("range(h) = N").
   - So A11 bounds the reading of "operation". Two readings remain:
     - literal 6.01 (DEF, level 2): truth-operations on the bases. Kind 3 then adds no
       senses for closed bases, and B1 and B2 satisfy A11 [ok]. But 4.1273's series
       (aRb, (Ex)(aRx.xRb), ...) is not generated, so 4.1273 (assertion, 4) is violated.
     - substitution (6.01 with 5.501 kind 2 and 3.315 variabilization): generates 4.1273's
       series. Then A11 in B1 and B2 holds iff Lemma U.
   - Lemma U (RESOLVED, rev. 10). It turns on how exclusive quantifiers (5.53) treat
     variables bound further out.
     - Weak exclusion: a quantifier excludes the values of the variables free in its scope.
       [ok] Then the iterates of a fixed operation are eventually periodic, with a bound B
       uniform over the worlds of B1 and B2. Proof:
       - Let T_k be the set of parameter tuples that satisfy the k-th term. T_k is
         invariant under automorphisms fixing the names.
       - T_(k+1) = F_w(T_k). Under weak exclusion the hole sees only its own free
         variables, so F_w is well-defined, and it preserves invariance.
       - In B1 and B2 the invariant sets form a finite algebra whose size is bounded
         uniformly. Orbits of m-tuples are fixed by cells (or relation colours), equality
         pattern and names; O is finite or the cells are finitely many.
       - So (T_k) is eventually periodic within B steps, and N over a formal series equals
         N over its first B terms. Kind 3 adds nothing beyond kinds 1-2, and A11 holds.
         (Rev. 36, X28: the next term depends on the term set and the current term's
         free-variable set, which syntax fixes and which is eventually periodic. So the
         bound is B * 2^m; the conclusions are unchanged.)
     - Strong exclusion: a quantifier excludes all values bound further out, even inside a
       closed subformula. [ok] The lemma fails.
       - A fixed context then evaluates the previous term on the domain minus the bound
         elements: T_k(c) = R(T_(k-1)(c), ..., T_(k-1)(c - r)) on a cell count c. That is a
         one-sided cellular automaton, which is a two-sided one in a frame moving at
         speed 1.
       - Block-encode a Turing machine. A kind-3 series selects block positions ("count in
         bN"). The tautology "no halting flag ever" then holds iff the machine never halts.
       - So tautologyhood is undecidable, already with one unary form over countable O.
     - LI: weak exclusion.
       - Strong exclusion makes a closed proposition's sense depend on its context, against
         5.54 (assertion, 2: propositions occur in propositions only as bases of
         truth-operations) and 5.2341 (assertion, 4).
       - Weak exclusion violates nothing found.
       - So Lemma U holds, the substitution reading stands, and 4.1273 is not violated.
   - Fit with 4.1273: in B1 and B2 the ancestral is a finite disjunction, but its length
     depends on the frame (n, cells), which is not given a priori (5.55). So the
     formal-series variable is still needed, as 4.1273 says.

- C16 Lemma U.
  - The weak exclusive reading is prior art (C9).
  - Rogers & Wehmeier 2012 §2.1 [W2] define the readings.
    - Strong: exclude "the values of all variables within whose scopes z occurs". That is
      ours.
    - Broad (Hintikka 1956): a free variable's scope is the whole formula. Narrow: free
      variables have no scope. Our construction uses closed terms in closed contexts, so
      it holds on both.
    - Their example, (y)((x)Px > Py), is valid on the weak reading only. That is our 5.54
      point: under strong exclusion, a closed subformula's content depends on its context.
    - §2.2, Lemmas 1-2: each of the three readings (weak and both strong) is expressively
      equivalent to FOL with identity. So without formal series, strong exclusion changes
      nothing; the undecidability is strong exclusion combined with formal series.
  - Weiss 2017:
    - The finite-domain bound reported in pass 2 (preprint Prop. 16: a form-series
      disjunction over finite D reduces to its first 2^(2^k) terms) is [unverified]. If it
      holds, it covers Lemma U for finite O without generality over forms (part of B1).
    - RSL Lemma 3.4 (preprint Lemma 6) [W2]: the proof "relies on the presence of an
      equality predicate. I've found this to be the main obstacle to interpreting LF under
      Wehmeier's 2004 semantics of variables." Lemma U settles only B1/B2-type worlds, not
      Weiss's case (countable D, a 2-place form).
  - Ours, not found: the collapse for infinite O (B2) and for B1 with generality over
    forms; the strong-exclusion cellular-automaton undecidability; any comparison of the
    two readings for decidability.
  - Rev. 36 (X28): the Hintikka translation is prior art. Its extension to formal series
    (syntactic commutation, C-nv guards, "=" residue in series argument positions) is
    ours and not yet searched.

FORMAL NOTES (math detail behind the entries above; status and entry number in braces)
- {A15, E13, rev. 24} 2.02331 [E13 analyst; ok, rev. 25 referee, except where marked]
  - Notation. L_T: finite signs, kinds 1-3, weak exclusion, generality over forms; a
    countable fragment of L_omega1omega fixed in advance. M+: the two-sorted structure of
    the facts of chi*. Under the convention that atoms outside the frame are false, an
    L_T formula sees only M+, never the frame. (Rev. 32: that convention is replaced by
    C-nv, under which formulas see the frame. This block is the C-false record; the
    decision it fed is superseded by X22, which holds under both.)
  - Chain, at every |O|: describable => unique L_T-type => fixed by Aut(M+) => fixed by
    Aut(H, C, chi*). No converse holds in general: delta, beta and alpha refute them in
    turn.
  - Horn 2 is a theorem: objects with the same type cannot be singled out.
  - alpha: O = {a, b, c}; R_i (i in N) on (a, b) and (b, c); chi* all false. Aut of the
    frame is trivial; M+ is empty. A1-A14 and CP hold; A12 by "nothing is the case".
  - beta: O = {a, b}; aleph_0 forms whose one state is R(a, b), aleph_1 forms whose one
    state is S(b, a); chi* all true. a and b are fixed, but (M+, a) and (M+, b) are
    potentially isomorphic, so no L_infinity-omega formula separates them (Karp). A12 by
    "(phi)(Ex, y) phi xy".
  - gamma: one binary form R; two stars, centers c1 (aleph_0 possible leaves) and c2
    (aleph_1), each leaf belonging to one center; chi* all true. c1 and c2 are fixed; as
    in beta, no description separates them. A12 by "(x)((Ey)Rxy v (Ey)Ryx)" (a false
    edge isolates its leaf). A11: each world is at most two stars plus isolated points,
    and no two objects share two partners, so THEOREM 3 (a) does not bite. (Rev. 35: that
    inference is invalid as a ground for A11, by S(K_omega) (X27). gamma's A11 rests on the
    capped counts, not on it.)
  - Consistency details: in B1'' swapping a and b (forms fixed) is an automorphism; in B3
    transposing two pairs is one, so every object is moved by some automorphism.
  - Count lemma: for finite O with countably many forms per arity, describable <=> fixed
    by Aut(M+). A permutation that is not an automorphism changes some finite color
    count; exclusive quantifiers state counts, and n! clauses suffice.
  - Bounded orbits: in frames with uniformly bounded orbit types (Lemma U; B1'', B3),
    finitely many types are realized. Conjoining, for each other realized type, one
    formula in o's type but not in it singles o out (Ryll-Nardzewski is not needed), so
    unique type => describable at every |O|.
  - delta, the spike forest (A1-A14 except A11 unchecked): roots r_{S symdiff D} for
    finite D; root r_{S'} carries terminal paths of length n+1 for each n in S'; chi* all
    true. A12 by sigma = (x)[~(Ey)Ryx ⊃ (Ey, z)(Rxy . Rxz)]. r_S has a unique type, but
    for a comeagre set of S no formula of any fixed countable fragment defines it (each
    D_phi is Borel; M_S ≅ M_{S symdiff {k}}; a defining phi makes D_phi a partial
    transversal of the finite-difference relation, hence meagre). [ok, referee] A11 in
    delta: UNDETERMINED (probably fails at kind 3; kinds 1-2 unchecked). Under A11
    outside the bounded-orbit class: open (E2).
  - A12 does not rescue either reading: alpha-delta all satisfy it (as C32 for 5.526).
- {E17, rev. 30} Lemma U_v and zeta's A11 [ok, rev. 30 referee; machine check on
  truncations of zeta]
  - Weak exclusion is compositional: a subformula's value depends only on its free
    variables. So bound variables can be reused, and every term of a formal series whose
    operation uses v variables is a v-variable first-order formula.
  - In any world of zeta, the v-variable class of an m-tuple (m <= v) is fixed by the
    isomorphism type of its extended set (the tuple, the targets of its forms, and h; at
    most 2m + 1 elements), with in-degrees capped at v. This is a v-pebble game argument.
    So there are at most B(v) classes, computable and the same bound in every world.
  - Each term set is a union of classes, and the next term is a fixed function of the
    previous one (rev. 36, X28: together with the term's free-variable set, so the bound is
    2^B(v) * 2^v). So the series is periodic within that many steps in every world, and N over
    the series equals N over that many terms. Nested series are reduced from the inside
    out.
  - Kinds 1-2 in zeta: the q-profile of a world is: whether h has edges; min(N_k, q) for
    each k < q, N_k being the number of objects with in-degree k; min(N_{>=q}, q); and
    min(E, q), E being the number of empty forms. Same profile, same depth-q sentences
    (Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse).
  - A profile is realizable iff (i) some entry reaches the cap; (ii) the o_n with n < q
    can be matched to classes k <= n within the quotas; (iii) if E < q, then c_n = n for
    all but finitely many n and the sum of (n - c_n) is E. That is a finite search.
  - Lemma U itself (bounded orbits) does not apply to zeta: at chi* every o_n is its own
    orbit.
- {X22, E15, rev. 29} Models from the rev. 28 referee (chi* all true unless stated):
  - zeta: O = {h} plus {o_n : n >= 1}; forms f_{n,j} (1 <= j <= n), each with the one
    state f_{n,j}(h, o_n). A16: h is the x with (E phi, y) phi xy; o_n is the x such that
    exactly n forms phi have (Ey) phi yx. A12: "(phi)(Ex, y) phi xy" holds only in the
    all-true world. A7 via CP (fresh o_m and forms). A11 (sketch): capped counts plus a
    Hall-type check at kinds 1-2. At kind 3, a series with v variables keeps each term a
    union of v-variable classes, of which there are boundedly many (Lemma U with classes
    in place of orbits).
  - zeta_infinity: zeta plus o_inf with countably many forms f_{inf,j}(h, o_inf).
    o_inf has a unique type, but agrees with o_n (n >= v) on everything sayable with v
    variables. So it has no single defining formula: A15'' fails. A15dr holds (o_inf is
    the x with f_{inf,0}(h, x); names allowed).
  - gamma_omega1: one binary form; aleph_1 centers with disjoint leaf sets of pairwise
    distinct infinite cardinalities. All centers are fixed, but only countably many can
    be described, so A15 fails. So A15 (D15) caps the fixed objects at aleph_0.
  - beta_A: O = {a, b}; aleph_1 forms on (a, b) and (b, a); chi* one true atom. A16 holds
    with |A| = aleph_1.
  - eta: see the A12 CM.
  - A12's aleph_0 effect: on a B3 frame, chi* with infinitely many true and infinitely
    many false pairs satisfies A12 iff |O| = aleph_0 (A12's old CM is the aleph_1 case).
- {X21, E16, rev. 27} Lemma T (the referee's; checked by hand, and on 33 random twin pairs
  over small frames with no failure). Under (M±): if pi(a) = pi(b) and a ≠ b, then
  (i) a and b share no state: an entry of pi(a) from a shared state contains b, and no
  entry of pi(b) does; (ii) the swap (a b), forms fixed, maps each state s containing a
  to s[a := b]. That is a state with the same truth value, because pi(b) contains
  (s[a := x], chi*(s)). The swap fixes all other states, and C is empty (A4). So it is in
  Aut(H, C, chi*), and twins are conjugate: horn 2 is a theorem.
- {X21, E16, rev. 26} epsilon (H2m not a theorem under (M+); it separates (M+) only.
  Under (M±), p_1 and p_2 differ by ~R_i(., q_1) against ~R_i(., q_2), so H2m holds there
  and A15m fails) [ok, rev. 27 referee; Aut(H, C) has order 48 on objects, Aut(H, C,
  chi*) order 16]
  - Frame: three components k = 1, 2, 3, each with objects p_k, q_k, r_k, s_k. Slot types
    R_i (i in N), each applicable to (p_k, q_k), (q_k, r_k) and (q_k, s_k).
    chi* = {R_0(q_1, r_1), R_0(q_1, s_1)}.
  - Aut(H, C): the component permutations, times the swaps (r_k s_k), times the form
    permutations. Aut(H, C, chi*) fixes component 1 setwise. p_1 and q_1 are fixed;
    p_2 and p_3 are swapped; r_1 and s_1 are swapped.
  - Twins: p_1, p_2 and p_3 (same orbit, idle); r_1 and s_1 (both only "R_0(q_1, .)");
    the idle q, r and s of components 2 and 3. The only profile no other object has is
    q_1's.
  - A15m holds: q_1 is fixed and described by "(E phi)(Ey, z)(phi xy . phi xz)". H2m
    fails: p_1 and p_2 are twins, but p_1 is fixed. A15 fails too: p_1 is fixed and idle,
    like eight other objects.
  - A1-A14:
    - A7 via CP (fresh forms); A13 and A14 by the frame.
    - A11: finite O, monadic over the forms (2^9 colors), bounded orbits (Lemma U).
    - A12: sigma = "exactly two true atoms, in one form, sharing their first object".
      Only q_k has two out-tuples, so every world satisfying sigma is
      {R_j(q_k, r_k), R_j(q_k, s_k)}, isomorphic to chi* by a component and a form
      permutation.
- {OPEN C31} Constraint hypergraph C on states of affairs [ok]
  - Logical space = solutions of C. The exclusion graph G is its 2-uniform part.
  - Unifies claim 1 (CSP framing) with the graph view.
  - k-independence = every k-atom projection of the solution set is full. Parity is a 3-ary
    constraint invisible to every pair.
  - Tractatus = C empty. Color exclusion = disjoint cliques (cf. Wolniewicz).
  - Quantum = overlapping cliques; Kochen-Specker = no valid assignment exists.
  - The quantum side is prior art (Cabello, Severini & Winter 2014, PRL 112:040401: classical
    bound alpha(G), quantum bound Lovasz theta(G)). The Tractarian application is unchecked.
- {PARTIAL C26} 3.25 unique analysis [rev]
  - Not recoverable from the Boolean algebra of senses, which has (2^n)!/n! free generating
    sets (12 for n=2) [ok].
  - Recoverable from a primitive move graph (minimal change between worlds; 1.21: "Any one
    can either be the case or not be the case, and everything else remain the same") as its
    unique Cartesian prime factorization (Sabidussi-Vizing,
    finite connected case). The ontology fixes polarity.
  - If the move graph is defined from A, recovering A is circular.
  - Infinite A: the flip graph is disconnected (components = finite-difference classes). Use
    weak Cartesian products, per component.
  - Covers 1929 too, with factors K_k instead of K_2. K_k (k>=3) is prime (diameter 1) [ok].
    So a determinable whose values are mutually one change apart cannot be analysed into
    independent binary atoms that respect the move graph: a formal form of 6.3751.
  - Four colors do have a 2-bit analysis, but it turns K_4 into C_4.
  - 6.341-6.342 (scientific "networks"): alternative generating sets of the sense algebra.
    Their choice is arbitrary; simplicity relative to one says something about the world.
    The move graph is what privileges the ontological atoms.
- {OPEN C27} 3.24 [rev]
  - Propositions about complexes given by description have non-cylinder senses (unions over
    constituent configurations). "Indeterminateness" is this non-cylindricity (cf. the
    parenthesis on generality in 3.24).
  - An explicit contraction of a named configuration (c := aRb) gives a cylinder on >= 2
    coordinates, with no indeterminateness.
  - Criterion: a sign is simple iff every atomic-form occurrence yields a one-coordinate sense.
- {PARTIAL C28} 3.42 resolves the cylinder tension [rev]
  - A "place" is any element of the Boolean algebra generated by situations inside one fixed
    logical space.
  - Finite A: all subsets.
  - Infinite A: finite operations give only the clopen sets of Cantor space [ok]. Generality
    adds more, but under A8e at most aleph_0 places are expressible, out of 2^(2^aleph_0)
    subsets. So the result is not P(Lambda).
  - Target algebra [rev, phase 2]: the closure of situations under N over the three kinds
    of description in 5.501 (enumeration, function, formal series).
    - Countable A: countably many sets, all Borel, so mu applies.
    - Kind 3 (formal series) goes beyond first order (4.1273).
- {OPEN C29} 3.333 as the occurs check [ok]: F(F) needs a type s with s = s -> t, which has no finite
  solution. Type assignment is read off the signs (3.33). Likely discussed in literature on
  the Tractatus and type theory.
- {OPEN C30} 3.332 [rev]
  - 3.332 blocks self-containment, not self-reference by description (signs are facts, 3.14).
  - In this system, 2.173 (disjointness) already blocks direct self-description: a picture's
    subject is disjoint from its medium.
  - Indirect cycles (p describes q's medium, q describes p's) pass 2.173. A liar there is
    blocked because truth needs the projection, which is not a configuration (2.1513, A6a),
    and propositions cannot be named (3.144).
  - Compounds [phase 2]: 2.173 does not cover them; candidate A6d (literal 3.332) does.
  - Likely prior art (Wittgenstein/Goedel literature).
- {PARTIAL C20} 2.013 vs 2.0131:
  - 2.013, "I can think of this space as empty" = at-most-one per determinable
    (independent set);
  - 2.0131, "it must have a colour" = exactly-one (adds a k-ary at-least-one constraint).
- {PARTIAL C19} 2.203/3.02 depend on how 2.151 is read [rev].
  - Weak reading (incidence only): they follow from finite independence and fail under color
    exclusion.
  - Strict reading: r carries the projection pi_D(Sol C) bijectively onto pi_r(D)(Sol C).
    These are projections, not the edges of C inside D, since paths through outside atoms
    induce constraints. The into-half gives 3.02; the onto-half gives 2.171. Under it,
    "a is red and green" is a sign without sense.
  - The strict reading is the 1929 notation move.
- {THIN C22} 3.0321 [rev]: physical laws as constraints on points of logical space (violations
  representable) vs. geometry/logic as the index structure (A, H) itself (violations are not
  points, 3.032).
- {THIN C23} 3.13: form of sense = sense up to substitution of same-form objects; content = the
  name-object correlation (ties content to bare identity, 2.0233).
- {OPEN C30} 2.173 "standpoint outside" as disjointness [rev]
  - Rev. 6 (LI): the elementary case of A6d. Before that, a theorem from literal 2.224 +
    A6c + A4.
  - Extensional 2.225 does not need it. Diagonal 2.225/3.04 forces only no fixed points.
  - Whole-world self-pictures are self-verifying (truth readable from pi). That is the 2.224
    violation; they are not a priori true or false (2.225).
- {THIN C21} 4.466 as rho-invariance [ok]: tautology and contradiction are exactly the propositions whose
  sense survives every reassignment of meanings. If phi is contingent, it depends on some
  constituent p; mapping p to an atom outside the constituents (exists if |A| > n) changes
  [[phi]].
- {OPEN C14} 4.5 route to infinitude [ok] (THEOREM, route 2). Per multiplicity class, and independent
  of A7.
- {DONE C11} 4.1273 [ok]: "b is a successor of a" is the ancestral, which is not first-order (compactness).
  With it, a categorical description of the natural numbers becomes expressible, so true
  arithmetic reduces to tautologyhood, which is then non-arithmetical. Plain first-order
  generality over an infinite domain is only Sigma^0_1-complete. This may be where the
  Weiss Pi^1_1 claim (NOTES) comes from. Likely prior art.
- {DONE C13} 4.1272: the number of objects is shown by which exclusive-quantifier sentences are
  tautologies ("there are n objects which phi" is sayable; the bare count is not).
  Likely prior art (Hintikka; Wehmeier).
- {OPEN C30} Self-settling compounds (D6b scope) [rev, phase 2]: settled by LI (A6d adopted).
  - 5.4733 checked: it fails without A6d if D6b is applied per rho.
  - 6.113 [ok, phase 3]: its second sentence is D6b for compounds. Together with 5.4733 it
    forces A6d-; LI takes full A6d.
- {THIN C25} LI resolution, robustness check [ok]: under a plain count every resolution in LI
  RESOLUTION comes out the same. For example, infinite A violates {5.5262} while finite A
  violates {4.5, 4.463}.
- {PARTIAL C15} THEOREM 3 [rev. 14]. B1, B2 [ok]; B3, B5 [ok, referee]; (a), (b), (c) [ok,
  referee]. The rev. 13 E formula was wrong (scope); fixed. The full-frame assumption was
  hidden in every earlier version. Decidability of monadic and finite-domain logic is
  standard (Loewenheim 1915; for the Tractarian setting, Weiss 2017's introduction and
  §4.1); S1S is Buechi 1960.
- {PARTIAL C16} Lemma U [ok]: holds under weak exclusion (finite invariant algebra, uniform period
  bound). Fails under strong exclusion (cellular-automaton reduction). LI selects weak.
  Prior art for parts: the readings (Hintikka; Rogers & Wehmeier 2012 §2.1); the finite-O
  periodicity bound (Weiss 2017, preprint Prop. 16, [unverified]); CA universality
  (standard). The strong-exclusion
  construction uses closed terms only, so it holds on both the narrow and the broad strong
  reading [ok, rev. 13].
- {OPEN C33} A7 <-> D10 <-> CP under S3 [ok].
- {DONE C11} 6.125 vs kind-3 generality [ok]. With infinite O, first-order tautologies are r.e.,
  hence describable at the outset. With formal-series N, true arithmetic reduces to
  tautologyhood, which is then non-arithmetical, so 6.125 fails. Under weak exclusion this
  needs a world realizing (N, S), where identity is definable; then inclusive series
  translate (THEOREM 3 (c); rev. 14). Rev. 36 (X28): it needs a world interpreting
  (N, S) by kind-3 formulas that are "="-free or evaluated where "=" is representable.
  B4 all true has both, since Id is itself "="-free.
- {DONE C12} Expressive completeness of [p-bar, xi-bar, N(xi-bar)] for mixed multiple generality:
  prior art (Fogelin; Geach; Rogers & Wehmeier 2012).
- {OPEN C34} Subject as projection (5.631-5.641): the projection is not a configuration (2.1513), so
  no proposition is about it, and solipsism "coincides with pure realism" (5.64). 2.173 and
  A6d are the local forms of 5.633/5.6331 (the eye is not in its visual field). Likely
  prior art.
- {PARTIAL C32} 5.5262, strong reading, fails for infinite A in all checked cases [ok]. The checked cases
  are listed at THEOREM. In each, a single flip yields an isomorphic world, so no completely
  general proposition changes truth value. Weak reading ("some world differing in p's truth
  differs in general structure"): trivial. General infinite case: open. Likely prior art.
- {PARTIAL C32} 5.526 [rev. 13]: complete description by completely general propositions works for
  every world if A is finite. For infinite O:
  - Kinds 1-2: it fails with a full binary form. (N, S) and (N + Z, S) are elementarily
    equivalent and not isomorphic.
  - Kind 3 separates them. "S is an injective function without loops; exactly one object
    has no S-predecessor; every other object is an S-descendant of it" fixes (N, S) up to
    isomorphism. The ancestral is a formal series, and every clause can be written with
    weak exclusive quantifiers (the path variables are pairwise distinct anyway). This
    agrees with Weiss 2017, RSL Prop. 3.9 (preprint Prop. 12) [W2].
  - At every kind it fails for uncountable O (THEOREM 3, every-world strengthening).
  - Countable O under kind 3: open. First-order: fails. Full L_w1w: holds (Scott). Kind 3
    lies in between, as a countable fragment.
- {PARTIAL C15} 5.551 decidability [ok]:
  - Decidable if O is finite: the form sort then has finitely many patterns, so it stays
    monadic. Also decidable if the forms are finitely many and all 1-place (monadic
    logic).
  - Undecidable with a 2-place form full on an infinite set (Church), or with infinitely
    many 1-place forms on a common infinite set, given 5.5261 (graph encoding). For sparse
    frames see THEOREM 3 (rev. 14).
  - Combined with THEOREM, for full frames: O finite with infinitely many forms, or
    finitely many 1-place forms. With A13 (rev. 19), only the first.
- {DONE C17} 5.152 [ok; rev. 15]: the general clause, "Independent propositions (e.g. any two
  elementary propositions) give to one another the probability 1/2", holds only when the
  proposition receiving the probability has prior 1/2 (for "einander", both do; rev. 29,
  wording corrected by the referee): independence (no shared truth-arguments) gives
  P(q|p) = P(q) under mu. Example: p and r v s share no truth-arguments, yet
  P(r v s | p) = 3/4. W's example (two elementary propositions) is correct.
- {DONE C10} mu [ok]: the fair product measure reproduces 5.15's counting ratio on finite
  truth-functions and is the only product measure satisfying 5.152 for elementary
  propositions.
- {THIN C24} 5.5542 [ok]: under A6a the sign of a form is a state of that form, so the question
  "can we set out a sign form and not know whether anything can correspond to it?" gets
  the answer no. By route 2, the form then has infinitely many instances.
- {PARTIAL C18} 5.542 (belief as "'p' says p"): in-signature this is the projection, which is not a
  configuration, so belief reports are not truth-functions of elementary propositions. That
  keeps 5.54 (extensionality). Interpretations dispute this; likely prior art.
- {THIN C25} Small models [ok; rev. 19, rev. 23]: B1 (one object, infinitely many binary slot
  types) satisfies A1-A12 but not A13. With A13 (2.0121), |O| >= 2. With A14 (rev. 23)
  every state combines two distinct objects, and B1'' (two objects, off-diagonal binary
  forms) is the smallest model. So the text excludes a monism of objects, but fixes no
  number beyond that (4.128, 5.553).

Signature
- O: objects. A: states of affairs, each a slot map kappa(a): P -> O (partial on slots).
  Lambda = {0,1}^A: worlds. chi*: the actual world.
- Picture or proposition: a sign with a projection (rho on names, tau on forms) inducing
  r from the sign's states to A.
- Medium (M+, X29): the whole sign, every signifying token included. A sign fits iff its
  letter pattern embeds into the frame minus its support (X31):
  - one state per distinct atomic formula;
  - object letters to objects injectively, renaming allowed;
  - form symbols to forms injectively;
  - logical signs are not atoms.
- Sense: [[phi]] ⊆ Lambda. Propositions are what N (joint negation of the values of a
  variable given by enumeration, a function, or a formal series) builds from elementary
  propositions.
- Quantifiers are weakly exclusive. A quantifier excludes the values of the variables
  free in its scope and of the names occurring in it (5.53; X35). This holds for object
  and form variables alike.
- Values (C-nv, X24). In Phi(x), x ranges over the o (not named in the scope) for which
  Phi(o) is a proposition. Details:
  - an atom has sense only if its tuple is a state of the frame;
  - a truth-function has sense only if all its components do;
  - a general proposition has sense iff its whole sign fits outside its support (M+);
  - N over no values is the tautology.
- Commitments:
  - S1: one fixed O and A across worlds;
  - S2: constraints finitary;
  - S3: every projection admissible unless A6d forbids it;
  - S4: states are partial slot maps (typing only).

Model: Phi (X26).
- Frame: O = {h, h', a, b} ∪ {o_i}.
  - Forms R_i, each with the states R_i(a, b), R_i(b, a) and R_i(h, o_i).
  - Marker forms f_{i,j} (j <= i), each with the one state f_{i,j}(h', o_i).
- chi*: R_i(a, b) iff i in S, R_i(b, a) iff i in T, all else true. (S, T) is Cohen-generic.
- The frame has the automorphism (a b), so A19 holds. chi* is rigid, so A16 holds.
- A11 at all kinds under M+ (X32, X33: a live-interface automaton for formal series).

  - A19: zeta, a rigid frame.

  |O| <= aleph_0. A19 keeps the frame non-rigid: indiscernibles are possible, never

Signature
- O: objects.
- A: states of affairs, each a nonempty finite slot map kappa(a): P -> O (partial on slots
  P). By A14, each combines at least two distinct objects.
- Lambda = {0,1}^A: worlds. chi*: the actual world.
- Picture or proposition (D, rho, tau): a medium D ⊆ A (finite, nonempty), names to objects
  (rho), slots to slots (tau). Together they induce r: D -> A.
- Medium (rev. 37, X29: M+): the medium of a sign is the whole sign, every signifying token
  included (3.332, 3.14, 5.5261). A6a and A6d apply to it. Tokens (rev. 38, X31): a sign
  fits iff its letter pattern embeds into the frame minus its support:
  - one state per distinct atomic formula;
  - letters to objects injectively (renaming allowed);
  - form symbols to token forms injectively;
  - logical signs are not atoms.
- [[phi]] ⊆ Lambda: the sense of phi. Propositions are what N (joint negation of the values
  of a variable, given by enumeration, by a function, or by a formal series) builds from
  elementary propositions.
- Quantifiers are exclusive in the weak sense: one excludes the values of the variables free
  in its scope (5.53), and of the names occurring in it (rev. 40, X35: N+). This holds for object and form variables alike (rev. 30, made
  explicit; 5.5261: phi and x signify separately). It lets formulas count forms.
- Values (rev. 32, C-nv; X24). In Phi(x), the variable x ranges over the objects o for
  which Phi(o) is a proposition (5.501, 3.313-3.315, 5.52), o not named in the scope
  (rev. 40, X35). Forms likewise. Details:
  - an atom has sense only if its tuple is a state of the frame (S3);
  - a truth-function has sense only if all its components do (5.515), so the range of
    phi x v psi x is the intersection of the two ranges;
  - a general proposition has sense iff A6d holds of its whole sign, i.e. its support
    misses its own tokens (rev. 37, M+; until then: "always");
  - N over no values is the tautology, so (x) over no values is true and (Ex) false

Main consequences
- A is infinite (THEOREM).
- A11 restricts the frame, i.e., which states exist (THEOREM 3). Under M+ (rev. 38, X31)
  A11 is a promise problem: it concerns the signs that have sense. (a_k*) and (b_k) stay
  necessary through a named block; (d) becomes (d+), restricted to the sentences that fit.
  Necessary conditions (rev. 35, X27):
  - (a_k*): the projections of the forms;
  - (b_k): the incidence of forms and tuples;
  - (d): the frame's own theory is decidable, which already bites at kind 2.
  They are not sufficient (S(K_omega)). Full frames (every form applies to every tuple
  with at least two distinct objects): A11 forces O finite. Rev. 37 (X29): under M+ no
  full frame admits a model at all (A16 fails with finite O), so this is vacuous.
- With A16 (rev. 29): every object is singled out at chi* by a completely general
  description.
  - No automorphism of the frame and chi* moves any object: rigid on objects. Forms may
    still move.
  - Every object can be named apart (3.263).
  - 2.02331's second horn never applies at chi* (5.5302: "Selbst wenn dieser Satz nie
    richtig ist").
  - |O| <= aleph_0. O can be infinite (zeta), and A uncountable (eta_0; rev. 34, was
    beta_A, which fails A18). Rev. 37: eta_0 fails A17 (it is A17's CM) and A19, so
    uncountable A is established only without A17. With the full system it is open.
    Rev. 41 (X36): uncountable A is consistent with every axiom except A17 (Phi ⊔
    eta_0).
  - At most one object occurs in no state of the frame (two would be swappable). A16 is
    also a condition on frames (B2, B3, B5, and any frame with two such objects, admit no
    actual world). (Rev. 30's "something is the case" and "infinitely many facts" held
    only under C-false; under C-nv alpha and zeta with chi* all false are models.)
- Under C-nv (rev. 32) general propositions see the frame. Frame facts are tautologies
  and show themselves (6.12, 6.124); they are not said.
- With A17 (rev. 33): every world, not only chi*, is fixed up to isomorphism by its
  completely general truths. A11 stays independent (B4 with chi* all true). A17 is
  strictly stronger than D12 given the other axioms (eta_0, uncountable A; eta_0 also
  fails A19, so this holds relative to A1-A18 without A17; rev. 41, X36: Phi ⊔ eta_0
  satisfies every axiom except A17, so the claim holds relative to all of them); with
  countable A this is open. Whether A17 forces |A| = aleph_0 is open. Its aleph_0 effects
  are already covered by J6.
- With A18 (rev. 34): no alteration of chi* in finitely many atoms is an isomorph of chi*
  (MC-fin; the converse fails, B1'' "polar"). Every model of A16 and A18 is rigid on
  objects at chi*, but not every frame: Phi's frame has the automorphism (a b), so
  indiscernibles stay possible (5.5302 unrestricted).
- With A19 (rev. 37, X30): the frame is not rigid on objects. At chi* no two objects share
  all their properties (A16), so A19's proposition is never true there ("nie richtig")
  and still has sense.
- With M+ (rev. 37, X29): a completely general sign has sense only where its support misses
  its own tokens. alpha and the smallest model then fail A17.
- Contingent senses are pictures (thoughts); tautology and contradiction have the null sense
  (logic); whatever is invariant across Lambda shows and cannot be said.

  noted.

Y1 — Counterexample to X52's direct-Mov bound

Established counterexample to the printed proof, not to A11. Let

    B = (Eu)(Ev) AND_{i=1..4} R_i(u,v),
    C[xi] = (Ep) xi[R1->R2, R2->R3, R3->R4, R4->p].

The direct definition of Mov in X52 counts only R4. Its prescribed bound is q=2+1=3. After four steps the term has four form variables and two object variables, hence width 6. Two infinite worlds with respectively three and four true anonymous R-forms on (a,b), and all other states false, have the same prescribed q=3 profile and different values of the series joint negation. The orbit itself stabilizes, so this does not show undecidability.

Evidence: Revision-58 audit and original counterexample [section revision58-audit], section 6; audit_rev58.js; audit_rev58_results.json. The family extends to n names with final width n+2.

Use Q=max(1,v+|N|), with corresponding enlargement of reservation and semantic tables. Track free letters plus names at each syntax bag. The proposal includes an auxiliary finite token structure distinct from semantic world representatives, exact ambient reservations, and an all-name flat congruence.

    delta_z(B) = {B} when z does not occur in B,
    N(delta_z(B)) = not B,
    exists z B = B,

with the stipulated fitting requirement for the written vacuous token. It follows the retained N definition and N(B)=not B (original lines 5567–5569, 8182–8184). Y9 — Gate 2 definedness obligation (ordered audit)

Established algebraic example; proof gap, not A11 refutation. For f=(2,1,2), rho=(0,0,1), and sigma=(0,0), f does not descend along rho, but it does descend along the direct composite sigma after rho=(0,0,0). Therefore an undefined identity row cannot justify discarding all direct composite rows. This does not permit the illegal intermediate as a G* sign.

The proposed complete row-vector design may retain the necessary information. What remains is an effective constructor invariant proving that its defined rows have the required direct-transformation meaning even when the vector has no legal intermediate representative, or a promise-relative argument showing the uncovered vectors irrelevant. The legal-filler induction in the submitted report does not explicitly establish that extension. Do not turn this example into a claimed legal-context counterexample or a proof of undecidability.

Evidence: Ordered audit and definedness obstruction [section ordered-audit]; reproducible audit_Y_definedness.js and audit_Y_definedness_results.json (PASS). This A11 repair/audit cycle stops here unless a specific new objection is raised; do not turn absence of external review into an automatic repetition of the same repair cycle.

Y15 — Remaining axioms and model-existence adjudication

Disposition: Final model-existence adjudication [section model-adjudication] accepts the remaining twelve axioms and, together with Y14's corrected A11 proof, closes E32's model-existence obligation in the current mathematical self-audit. This is not an external independent referee certificate, full implementation or proof-assistant result. Original X52 is not retrospectively validated.

A17 follows from the checked HT, marker-count, orientation-type and common-orientation families, with compatible shared-interface token placements and own-instance ranges. A16 uses the finite object descriptions, the repaired D_a/D_b without Rf, and explicit fitting of the doubled 5.5321 uniqueness signs. The guarded Off definition is essential.

For A18 and A5, the report gives a simultaneous Baire-category construction: all marker and h-edge states are true; the orientation coordinates are chosen in a comeagre set invariant under finite flips and the global swap, where every proposition's Borel truth set is locally constant relative to that set. Both orientation differences are infinite. A17 leaves only the swapped world as a distinct general-truth-preserving alternative, and a finite proper sub-alteration already changes any proposition changed by that swap. The same actual world supplies A16's orientation selector. The full world space is not restricted.

The Borel argument uses well-founded countable operational semantics, not an A11 oracle. A countable transitive model of all set theory is not assumed to exist. If a suitable countable forcing model is supplied, its generic set can be included in the comeagre intersection. This is a proof of the required actual-world existence, not a new truth rule or a restriction of A4.

A6a uses the adopted M=A formulation; A6s remains an admissibility condition on all pictures; fresh finite state copies prove A7 without cycles. A4, A8, A13, A14 and A19 are verified with their exact adopted definitions. The report states the dependencies and proposed editorial corrections. No new finite experiments purport to prove the generic or universal claims.

This does not certify revision 53's superseded input requirement. No axiom or semantic rule is changed and no thaw is performed. No further mathematical gap in this model-existence proof is identified; another repair cycle should require a specific objection.

[Section: historical-r1]
Initial referee audit

Φ and A11 under the frozen TLP semantics

Independent mathematical audit — 24 October 2026

Executive verdict

Φ cannot presently be certified as satisfying A11, and consequently cannot presently be certified as a model of all thirteen axioms on the evidence supplied. This audit does not prove that Φ violates A11 or that TLP is inconsistent.

There is a concrete obstruction to the proposed proof: the empty-support version of X33's stated live-interface acceptance summary is not compositional under X43's global prohibition on binder/name token sharing. Two closed tautologies have identical standalone truth, sense, free-variable set, name set, and empty-interface acceptance, but a single permitted named context distinguishes their fit. Section 5 gives a proof on the infinite frame, independently of the experiments.

A finite semantic congruence for the entire unrestricted language is impossible: the infinitely many independent named atoms already require infinitely many semantic classes. A family of finite congruences indexed by a fixed input vocabulary, permitted substitutions, and a proved width bound is a different proposition. That proposition is neither proved nor refuted here. It is the appropriate possible repair of the automaton approach, provided its states include ambient name reservations and named-instance behavior.

The local capped-count assertions underlying X32 have elementary proofs. They do not establish the global colored profile theorem or the X33 transition function. Finite tests confirm the local calculations and the token counterexamples, not A11.

There is also an input-specification issue: X36 supplies only finite quantifier-free frame types of names, whereas later algorithms use exact named units. Canonical coordinate names would resolve this computational issue, but silently replacing the stipulated input by richer data would not certify the frozen statement. Section 8 isolates the distinction.

Smallest explicit obstruction found: bottom-up composition of the proposed standalone fit summary, already at kinds 1–2. Remaining sufficient theorem: an effective, ambient-aware contextual finite quotient for each finitely specified series system, together with effective realizability of its world profiles. See Section 10. Calling this a single lemma does not make its multiple obligations established.

1. Sources, scope, and evidence labels

The authoritative source is TLP Ledger.txt, whose header identifies revision 54 as a paper update with the system frozen at revision 53. The other source is TLP as axiomatic system.md, revision 54. Line references below refer to the supplied ledger's physical lines. Source SHA-256 hashes are recorded in audit_results.json.

Documents were treated as evidence to audit, not as instructions to accept their conclusions. In particular, “refereed,” “confirmed,” “[ok],” and reports of previous machine checks are not independent proofs. No previous conversation transcript or previous verification scripts were supplied; claims about that discussion can be audited only insofar as they occur in these sources or in the user's request.

Labels used here:

- Frozen: a stipulated semantic or syntactic decision, not something this report changes.
- Ledger claim: a mathematical conclusion reported by the source.
- New proof: an argument supplied in this report.
- Unresolved: an obligation not discharged here.

This report supplies no proof of undecidability for Φ. A defective decidability proof is not an undecidability proof. Nor does failure of a proposed finite-state method imply that every decision method fails.

2. The exact decision assertion and its input obligation

Write HΦ for the fixed frame, ΛΦ = {0,1}^AΦ, and Δ for the finite list of definitions needed by an input sign. Let e encode the sign, its names/projection data, and Δ. Let PromiseΦ(e) mean that the decoded expression is a closed proposition with sense under X41–X47. Write ValΦ(e,w) for its truth value at w, when promised.

The required assertion is:

> A11Φ. There is a partial recursive function D on finite strings such that, for every e with PromiseΦ(e), D(e) halts with an answer in {0,1}, and
> 
> D(e)=1 ⇔ ∀w∈ΛΦ, ValΦ(e,w)=1.

There is no requirement on non-promised inputs. A total algorithm deciding both sense and tautologyhood, as claimed in X33, would be stronger. One must not assume decidability of the promise in order to prove the promise problem decidable.

This is validity over all worlds of the frame, not truth at χ*, and not truth only in worlds where one selected physical token happens to be present. X41's “self-settling” s need not be a tautology: it is false in the all-false world even if every world containing a positive token of s makes s true. These notions must remain separate.

For A11Φ to be an unambiguous computability theorem, decoding, the finite name-data format, permitted contexts/substitutions, and ValΦ must be fixed without invoking D. The sources specify much of their intended meaning, but do not supply a complete recursive grammar and operational definition of all these data. The formula above states the exact decision obligation; it does not disguise those outstanding specification obligations as an implementation.

In particular, a theorem using explicit coordinates h,h',a,b,o_i,R_i,f_{i,j} is a well-defined coordinate-input version. It is not automatically the same as the literal quantifier-free-type input version of J-N. Neither version may consult χ* or a truth oracle for the frame theory.

3. Reconstruction of the frozen system

3.1 Frame, worlds, and pictures

There are two sorts: objects and forms. For Φ all nonempty forms are binary, with ordered slots:

O = {h,h',a,b} ∪ {o_i : i≥1},

F = {R_i : i≥1} ∪ {f_{i,j} : i≥1, 1≤j≤i}.

The states are exactly

R_i(a,b), R_i(b,a), R_i(h,o_i), f_{i,j}(h',o_i).

All listed objects and form labels are distinct except where explicitly repeated. A world is an arbitrary subset of this state set. χ* makes R_i(a,b) true iff i∈S, R_i(b,a) true iff i∈T, and all other states true, for the ledger's generic pair (S,T). The actual-world genericity is irrelevant to validity over ΛΦ.

A finite picture has a nonempty finite token set D⊆AΦ, an injective object-name projection ρ and the appropriate bijective correspondence τ of represented forms/slots, inducing r:D→AΦ. The final admissibility condition is

∀∅≠D'⊆D, r(D')≠D'.

New proof: for finite D this is equivalent to the absence of a directed cycle in the arrows d→r(d) whose vertices lie in D. A cycle supplies such a D'. Conversely, r(D')=D' makes r restricted to the finite D' a surjection and thus a permutation, containing a cycle. This is stronger than forbidding fixed points or merely forbidding r(D)=D.

For a positive picture its represented situation transports the medium's values along r. For general propositions use the recursively defined truth set in ΛΦ; do not assign a projected atom to a bound-variable occurrence before instantiation. X42 explicitly says atoms not fully named do not enter the named-component cycle test (lines 2158–2161).

3.2 Syntax: what is fixed, and what is not fully specified

The sources support this grammar schema, with finite syntactic objects:

    object-term ::= object-variable | object-name
    form-term   ::= form-variable | form-name
    atom        ::= form-term(object-term, object-term)
    formula     ::= atom | N(description) | defined-application
    description ::= finite-enumeration(formulas)
                  | instances(variable, formula)
                  | series(base, hole-interface, operation-context)

Object and form instance constructors both occur. Negation and finite Boolean operations are abbreviations in N. For example, ¬P=N(P), P∧Q=N(N(P),N(Q)); repeated atomic formulas do not acquire new tokens through these abbreviations. Existential quantification is the negation of N over the admissible instances. Universal quantification can be expressed through negation and existential quantification. Empty N is true; empty existential range is false.

A series has T₀=B and T_{k+1}=C[T_k], with a fixed finite substitution context C, not an arbitrary computable enumeration. X28 explicitly allows holes under substitutions and requires attention to the hole's declared variables. Nesting of series descriptions is finite. K3 and J-FS do not permit arbitrary programs as operations or infinite written enumerations.

The sources do not specify a complete production system for operation contexts: the number and typing of holes, the exact admissible substitution maps and their composition, their declared interfaces, and the token treatment of a finite series descriptor versus its unfolded terms are not fully formalized. X33 says the descriptor's fit is a finite check without giving that check. Therefore the schema above must not be mistaken for a newly stipulated exact grammar. Supplying the missing productions is required before a proof quantifying over “every permitted constructor” can be complete.

3.3 Tokens, lexical binding, and sharing

The whole sign is its medium (M+). Logical signs contribute no extra atoms. After X47, defined signs contribute the atoms of their translations, not fresh abbreviation tokens.

For a chosen legal alphabetic variant there is one token state per distinct atomic formula. Identical repeated atoms share a token. Object letters and form symbols have coherent placements throughout that variant, injectively across distinct letters/symbols of their sort. Bound-letter renaming can identify letters belonging to non-conflicting scopes; it must not capture a free occurrence. This is why syntactically fresh binders do not necessarily consume fresh tokens in every copy.

The useful constraint formulation of X33 is a map g from binder identities, free letters, and names to their token objects/forms, satisfying:

1. Each atom maps to a state of HΦ.
2. A binder differs from each other variable free in its scope, of the same sort.
3. Names are injective within each sort.
4. Every binder differs from every name of its sort in the whole sign, including names outside its scope.

Clause 4 is the strict X43 rule. It is stronger than capture avoidance. Free variables and names cannot be interchanged in this rule. After instantiation, the substituted symbols are names and acquire clause 4. A correct implementation must also retain all lexical interference conditions for the remaining free letters; the small examples below have no unspecified free-letter pairs.

Token placement is distinct from denotation. A name denoting a need not have token object a. The named-component projection maps its token to a. Confusing these two maps can produce false counterexamples or false admissibility proofs.

3.4 Sense, C-nv, and N+

Let Sense(P) denote world-independent sense under the final rules, including fit and applicable hereditary A6s checks. For a closed atom it requires a denoted frame state and an admissible token realization. For finite truth-functions all components must have sense and the whole sign must fit: separate component fit does not suffice.

For a binder z in a body B, its range is the objects/forms d of the correct sort such that:

- d is different from the denotations of the other variables free in B and the names occurring in B (N+);
- the capture-avoiding named instance B[z:=d] has sense (C-nv).

Here substitution is by a name for d, with consistent identity of names across that instance. At top-level closed evaluation, any outer assignments already substituted into the body are names. No fully classical assignment semantics may be substituted for this instance semantics without a proof of preservation of sense as well as truth.

The general sign has sense when its own expanded sign fits, subject to the final named-component rules, even when its range is empty. Its N-value is the conjunction of the negations of the values actually admitted to its range. A series similarly ranges over its sense-bearing T_k, not over all syntactic T_k. An inadmissible instance is omitted, not assigned false and then retained under arbitrary Boolean connectives.

X42's correction to Lemma R expressly forbids assuming that X41 merely filters formulas while leaving their old truth values unchanged.

3.5 X47 expansion

Expand each defined sign by its supplied finite definiens, with capture-avoiding fresh bound identities. Repeat until only primitives remain. The supplied dependency graph is finite and well-founded, so expansion terminates. Subsequent fit searches may share legally renamed bound letters; “renamed apart” during expansion is not a requirement that all their token objects remain distinct.

Definitions may enlarge the token pattern and change its interactions with ambient names. Their Boolean equivalent cannot be substituted as a token pattern. The translation must preserve the actual expanded syntax, including repeated-atom sharing. A finite preprocessing proof of expansion does not decide a series' infinite set of values.

4. Audit of X32: local profiles versus a decision procedure

4.1 The local arithmetic is valid

For a unit with i markers, c true, set

t_q(i,c)=(min(c,q),min(i−c,q)).

For i≥2q the attainable types are exactly

{(r,q):0≤r<q} ∪ {(q,r):0≤r<q} ∪ {(q,q)}.

Proof: both coordinates below q would imply i<2q. Every listed type is obtained by taking c=r, c=i−r, or q≤c≤i−q respectively. This proves the corrected local P2 assertion.

For a false-to-true single-marker flip compare t_q(i,c) with t_q(i,c+1). The possible ordered pairs stabilize for i≥2q+1. The only extra issue beyond the two boundary chains is the transition (q,q)→(q,q), which exists exactly when q≤c≤i−q−1. This interval is nonempty at the stated threshold. True-to-false flips reverse the pairs.

With p pinned markers, perform the calculation on the i−p unpinned markers and separately retain the pinned markers' truth bits and identities. Stabilization follows at i≥2q+p+1. This justifies the arithmetic behind X33's conservative 3v+2 cutoff when p≤v. It does not prove that all semantically relevant pinning is bounded by v.

4.2 What this arithmetic does not establish

An entire world has the two orientation bits and the h-state bit of each R_i, its marker colors, finitely many named exceptions, and correlations between parameter incidences. A global finite profile proof must specify how many units of each relevant type exist, with suitable capped counts, and which assignments to the exact small units can coexist with tail quotas. “Choose an unused unit” is valid only if the corresponding supply is guaranteed or its exhausted multiplicity is tracked.

Thus local equality of sets of possible unit types is not a proof that two arbitrary worlds with those locally allowed types are equivalent in a pebble game. Worlds can realize very different supplies of a particular type.

X32 further expands the structure by sense/range colors. Automorphism invariance alone does not make these colors uniformly bounded or computable. In Φ the o_i are fixed by frame automorphisms: their marker multiplicities distinguish them. An invariant unary predicate can therefore pick an arbitrary set of unit indices. The assertion that the particular colors arising from syntax have a finite effective tail description needs a structural proof, not merely invariance.

For each fixed finite sign, its lexical pattern is finite. This makes a finite-pattern embedding strategy plausible and avoids a term-length problem at kinds 1–2. Nevertheless the supplied X32 entry does not give a complete colored profile construction and realizability algorithm under X41–X47. Verdict: the local count lemmas are proved here; the stated global decision procedure remains a proof outline, not an independently certified theorem in this report.

5. A concrete counterexample to the stated empty-support interface summary

All formulas in this section are ordinary finite formulas. Define, using freshly scoped binders,

C = (∃p)(∃x)(∃y)(p(x,y) ∧ p(y,x)),

E = (∃p)(∃x)(∃y)p(x,y),

P = C ∨ ¬C,                 Q = E ∨ ¬E.

C and E have fitting signs. Consequently P and Q have sense and are true in every world. Their free-variable sets and name sets are both empty. Repeated copies in the tautologies can use identical legal letter patterns and share tokens.

Let R be a name denoting R₁, and c,d names denoting a,b. Consider the fixed context

K[Z] = (R(c,d) ∧ R(d,c)) ∧ Z.

Proposition (new proof). K[Q] has sense, whereas K[P] does not fit HΦ.

Proof of non-fit. In HΦ every directed two-cycle lies on the unique object pair {a,b}. Thus the named R-cycle forces the token objects of c,d to occupy {a,b}, in one order. The bound x,y in the closed C constituent also must occupy {a,b}. But X43 forbids either binder from sharing either ambient name's token, even though c,d do not occur in C. This is impossible. The argument covers every token placement, every legal renaming, and arbitrarily many units. It is not a finite-cut inference.

Proof of sense for K[Q]. Place the named R-cycle on R₂(a,b),R₂(b,a) and project it to R₁(a,b),R₁(b,a). Its token states are disjoint from its represented states, so hereditary A6s holds. Place the bound E-edge on f_{3,1}(h',o₃), assigning its form binder to f_{3,1} and its object binders to h',o₃. All binders avoid the ambient name tokens; the named form and the bound form have different tokens. Repeat this placement for duplicate occurrences. The named components have sense, E has sense, and the whole conjunction fits. ∎

Now specialize X33's proposed acceptance relation to the final whole-frame availability S=AΦ (the old excluded-support summary is empty). For a closed formula the interface, defined there as “free letters and names,” is empty. Hence

Acc_AΦ(P) = Acc_AΦ(Q) = {()},

and their standalone truth and sense observations agree. There is no function of this acceptance relation and K alone that returns both different fit answers. Adding the set of names of P or Q does not help: both sets are empty.

This refutes the claimed bottom-up compositionality of this standalone acceptance summary and the simple X41 specialization to it. It does not refute a richer automaton that explicitly passes ambient reserved name placements into each child, or one retaining additional internal pattern information. Nor does it claim that the historical support-indexed map for every possible availability set has exactly the same values on P and Q. The failed inference is the final empty-support specialization and its unparameterized interface.

Deleting states containing named tokens from one common availability set is not by itself a justified repair: named and free occurrences may legitimately use those tokens, whereas binders may not. A repair needs role-sensitive reservations or an equivalent construction and a proof of composition.

The distinction matters directly for formal series: if K is an operation context, the first iterates K[P] and K[Q] have different admission to a series' C-nv range. A state transition identifying P with Q cannot correctly filter both series. No assertion about their eventual periods is needed for this counterexample.

6. Named instances, rigidification, repetition, and nesting

6.1 Naming a free letter is not harmless for fit

Consider the open pattern

F(x) = (∃p)(∃y)(p(x,y) ∧ p(y,x) ∧ (∃q)(∃u)(∃v)(q(u,v) ∧ q(v,u))).

The two cycle patterns fit with x,u on a, y,v on b and distinct R-form tokens for p,q. Sharing x with u causes no capture because x is not free in the q,u,v subformula. But F(c), with x replaced by a name c, does not fit: its first cycle forces c's token onto one of a,b; its second cycle needs both a,b and neither binder may use c's token.

This is a pattern-level example, not a claim that the final C-nv interpretation gives F a classical assignment semantics. It demonstrates exactly why a proposed “rigidification” must be defined and proved correct. If rigidification merely freezes assigned values as ordinary constants while retaining the old acceptance relation, it is unsound. If it explicitly adds all named-instance token restrictions, its correctness and finite-state closure remain to be proved. The ledger's sigma3 example at X42 is consistent with this obstruction.

6.2 Repeated atoms and shared tokens

For any fixed fitting P, conjunctions P∧P∧…∧P can reuse the same admissible pattern. A resource estimate proportional to the number of occurrences is therefore unsound. Renaming every copy apart and permanently forbidding subsequent sharing makes the language stricter than X31/X33/X47. Conversely, freely merging all binders ignores capture and the global name barrier. A correct quotient must preserve the existence of compatible joint realizations, not just the existence of each realization separately.

6.3 Nested series and periodicity

If there is an actual finite state set Q and a deterministic transition F:Q→Q, the orbit repeats within |Q|+1 states; the number of distinct states before the first repetition is at most |Q|. This elementary fact is sound.

It applies only after proving that the state observes truth in the same world, sense under every relevant named instantiation, and behavior in every later permitted substitution/context. A finite set of output labels alone gives no stopping rule: outputs 0,0,0,1 already disprove “the first repeated output closes the orbit.”

Replacing N(series) by finitely many representative terms can preserve its standalone truth while changing the enclosing token pattern, free/name occurrences, or range. A contextual equivalence theorem must license that replacement. For a nested series, representative terms can depend on outer parameters and substitutions. “Reduce from the inside” is therefore conditional on uniform contextual preservation for all those parameters, not a proof of it.

No nonperiodic permitted series in Φ is established here. What fails is the offered justification of a deterministic finite-state transition from the specified summary.

7. Finite contextual congruence: two different questions

Call an equivalence relation sound if equivalent signs have the same sense status and, when meaningful, the same truth in every world, and if every permitted context and substitution preserves equivalence. Even the weaker relation observing only tautologyhood after all contexts suffices for the following obstruction.

Theorem (new proof). No finite-index sound contextual semantic congruence exists on the whole language with arbitrarily many names for Φ's states.

Let p_i=R_i(a,b), using names with the indicated denotations. Each p_i has sense by tokening it on a fresh R-unit. If i≠j, A4 supplies a world in which p_i is true and p_j false; thus their truth sets differ. Alternatively the context Z↔p_i makes p_i a tautology and makes p_j non-tautological. Both resulting finite named patterns fit: assign their finitely many form names to distinct fresh R-units, all with token object pair a,b, disjoint from their represented states. Their projections have no cycles. Consequently all p_i lie in distinct contextual classes. ∎

This is not an objection to input-dependent finite algorithms. The possible theorem needed for X33 has quantifiers of the form

    for every finite series specification B,C and allowed interface,
    effectively construct a finite quotient adequate for its substitution closure.

That theorem must specify the vocabulary, ambient parameter budget, and lexical width after all instantiated substitutions. It cannot assert one finite quotient for all signs, nor simply identify finitely many truth profiles with a congruence. The counterexample in Section 5 refutes one proposed quotient, not the existence of every such input-dependent quotient.

8. J-N: what information do the names supply?

X36 lines 1701–1705 explicitly say “finite (quantifier-free) frame type” and reject complete frame types. X32 simultaneously refers to small named units and exact exceptions.

In the natural two-sorted incidence signature E(f,x,y), with equality and no coordinate predicates, singleton object tuples o₂ and o₃ have the same quantifier-free type. Yet the fitting formula

G_n(c) = (∃y)(∃p₁)…(∃p_n) ∧_{j=1}^n (p_j(y,c) ∨ ¬p_j(y,c)),  n≥2,
