is a tautology at c=o_i exactly when i≥n. N+ makes the forms distinct. For n≥2 the common source must be h', so the available forms are precisely the i marker forms of unit i. Their truth values are irrelevant. Named instances can be tokened on a sufficiently large fresh marker unit, avoiding all binder/name collisions and named projection cycles. The original sign can likewise be tokened on a large unit, even if its actual range is empty. Thus G_n is a promised proposition for every i.

For n=3 this distinguishes o₂ and o₃. Hence an algorithm whose entire input consists of the same anonymous symbol c and only its singleton quantifier-free incidence type cannot answer both cases. This is an information-theoretic failure, not a halting reduction.

This does not refute an interpretation where names carry additional effective coordinates or where “finite type” includes extra specified descriptors. Such interpretations supply different inputs. The sources do not give a coding contract sufficient to decide which computational version is intended. Certification must state it. Adding a complete frame-theory oracle is expressly disallowed; adding canonical coordinates requires justification against the frozen J-N interpretation.

9. Explicit disposition of X41–X47

| Decision | Required treatment in an A11 proof | Audit result |
|---|---|---|
| X41 | Fit in the whole frame; self-settling general signs allowed; no old support-disjointness requirement | Preserved. Does not remove the need to track lexical fit or named-instance ranges. |
| X42 | Hereditary A6s; named-instance C-nv; series values filtered by term fit | Preserved. The cycle equivalence is proved above. Lemma R's old semantics cannot be used. |
| X43 | No binder shares any ambient name's token, including outside its scope, for both sorts | Preserved. This is the source of the Section 5 obstruction. |
| X44 | Scope-sensitive guards, with names/parameters actually occurring in the scope; all four A17 invariants | A11 cannot erase those occurrences as semantically redundant. The reported A17 checks do not establish an automaton theorem. |
| X45 | Register/evidence audit; S2 no longer a separate commitment | No new algorithmic proof. A4 supplies the world class directly. |
| X46 | Textual classifications and interpretive grounds | No additional mathematical closure lemma or decision method. |
| X47 | Finite supplied definitions expanded before fit; no abbreviation tokens or binder exemptions | Effective preprocessing is justified for a finite acyclic dependency graph. It does not repair the contextual gap. |

No axiom or interpretive decision has been changed by this audit. None of the new counterexamples requires changing one: they invalidate proof claims, not the stipulated rules.

10. Remaining proof obligations, stated without circularity

Before a theorem, fix a finite encoding of names and the missing context/series productions. Then the following is a sufficient target for the proposed route.

Ambient-aware finite-quotient lemma (unproved). For each finite input specification I, including its expanded definitions, base formulas, finite operation contexts, substitution interfaces, and nesting structure, effectively construct:

1. A proved finite bound on the relevant lexical interfaces and on ambient reservations arising in its evaluation/substitution closure, or another finite representation replacing such a bound.
2. A finite, effectively realizable collection of world/parameter profiles preserving the truth observations needed by I, with exact named exceptions and correlations.
3. Finite states for terms recording sense and truth on these profiles, and fit conditional on ambient name placements, free-letter identifications, and fully named projection-cycle information.
4. Computable transitions for every actual constructor and substitution used in I, proved compatible with state equality.
5. A decoder for validity and a proof that replacing an inner series by its finite state orbit preserves the enclosing sign's sense and truth under all outer instantiations.

The finite representation must not encode an undecided semantic predicate in its transition table and call the table computable. It must not invoke A11 to compute colors or certify its realizable states.

Conditional deduction (new proof). Given these five items and finite effective handling of the non-series constructors, evaluate innermost series by finite state iteration until a state repeats; aggregate the admitted values on each realizable world/parameter profile. Item 5 licenses replacing that series in the enclosing evaluation. Induct on finite nesting depth. Finally use the validity decoder, which checks every realizable profile. Each step terminates by the constructed finite bound, and preservation gives the required answer on promised inputs. This proves A11Φ under the specified encoding.

The earliest precise missing lemma in the stated X33 proof is item 4 for fit with ambient names; Section 5 shows the stated summary does not satisfy it. Repairing that alone would still leave the width, realizability, named-instance, and nested-substitution obligations. There is no justified claim here that one minor lemma is all that separates the supplied text from a complete proof.

Other dependencies to keep explicit:

- A11 must not be used through D-S4 to prove its own decidability. Φ's states are binary by construction, so their finiteness is independently available.
- A7/state-disjoint copying is a finite pattern construction in Φ, not an oracle giving exact semantic colors.
- Frame automorphism invariance does not imply effective tail uniformity, since units are structurally distinguished.
- χ*'s genericity cannot decide validity over all worlds. The Baire argument for A18 requires its own uniform coding/regularity justification and supplies no A11 algorithm.
- Old finite-cut tests and the labels “refereed” cannot discharge any of these dependencies.
- An oracle for complete types of names would change J-N and trivialize some purported reductions; it is not an admissible hidden input.

11. Reproducible checks and their limits

Run from this directory:

    node audit_checks.js "C:\Users\ogmb\Downloads\TLP Ledger.txt" "C:\Users\ogmb\Downloads\TLP as axiomatic system.md"

The script uses only built-in Node.js modules. It writes audit_results.json. The run used Node.js v24.19.0.

| Test | Range | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Closed cycle and edge each fit | 1–6 units | All true |
| Ambient named cycle + closed cycle | 1–6 units | All false |
| Ambient named cycle + closed edge | 1–6 units | All true |
| Three identical cycle occurrences share tokens | 1–6 units | All true |
| Two-cycle pattern: free x versus named x | 2–6 units | Free fits; named fails |
| Capped types and flip transitions after removing pinned markers | q=1…8, p=0…q, i=2q+p+1…100 | 3,800 parameter cases, all pass |

The token checker exhaustively searches assignments for finite atomic patterns with explicitly supplied inequality constraints. It is not a TLP parser, full evaluator, full alpha-renaming enumerator, or hereditary-projection checker. It tests the constraints used in the displayed examples; admissible infinite-frame projections are proved separately in Section 5. It does not reproduce the old ledger's reported scripts, which were not supplied.

During development, an expected result incorrectly required two units for the context/edge fit; the checker found a one-unit placement using a marker form. The expectation was corrected, not the solver. The final script and stored results include that case. This reinforces the distinction between token form placement and the semantic role of an R-form.

The finite runs confirm the examples and local arithmetic. Infinite non-fit follows from the unique cycle-pair argument; local arithmetic stabilization follows from Section 4. Neither conclusion relies on extrapolation from these tests.

12. Certification of all thirteen axioms

The implication “A11 remains unproved, therefore Φ is not yet a certified model of all thirteen” is conclusive. It does not mean that any axiom is false in Φ.

| Axioms | Assessment in this audit |
|---|---|
| A4, A13, A14 | Immediate from the explicitly given frame/world construction. |
| A5 | Requires choosing the stated χ*; existence is part of the construction, subject to its genericity setup. |
| A6a, A6s | Enforced by the final medium and admissibility definitions; do not themselves prove expressive sufficiency. |
| A7 | Finite patterns can be copied onto fresh, sufficiently large units, with distinct source units assigned distinct destination units and marker multiplicities preserved. This is compatible with hereditary A6s. |
| A8 | Holds for a notation with the stipulated finite well-founded uniform definitions; exact notation still needs specification for the decision theorem. |
| A19 | The swap a↔b fixes the frame and worlds with symmetric orientation bits. An invariant semantics gives the asserted indiscernibility there. |
| A11 | Not certified; stated automaton summary fails a contextual fit test. |
| A16, A17, A18 | Ledger arguments and finite tests are recorded, but not independently proved in full by this A11-focused audit. None supplies the missing A11 proof. |

For A7's copy claim, a finite situation uses finitely many units and finitely many marker forms from each. Select distinct unused larger indices, map R-forms to their R-forms, marker forms to enough distinct markers of each destination unit, o_i to the chosen destination o_j, and retain the shared hubs and pair. The token and represented states are disjoint even though hubs may be shared; hence r has no cycle. Truth assignments to the represented finite situation impose no obstruction under A4.

Also, failure to certify this particular Φ does not settle whether some other model of all thirteen axioms exists. Independence is a separate claim and cannot be inferred from model existence; the paper itself records incomplete countermodel proofs.

13. Precise necessary corrections

These are corrections to mathematical claims and evidential status, not amendments to axioms.

1. X33, acceptance/composition step (lines 1531–1544): replace the unconditional compositionality and finite computable-state claim by: “The displayed standalone interface is insufficient under the final strict name/binder rule. A context-dependent acceptance relation with ambient name reservations and a proof of finite effective closure is required.” Retain eventual periodicity only as a conditional consequence of a proved deterministic finite-state transition.

2. X41/X42 A11 transfer (including lines 2086 and 2199–2202): replace “X32/X33 with empty support” as a proof by: “The old support restriction is removed, but the final range/fit semantics requires a new contextual closure proof; A11 in Φ remains open on the supplied argument.”

3. X32 P2/K1 use: keep the corrected local capped-count thresholds. Separate them from global world-profile realizability, colored-structure equivalence, and the uniform bound through substitution. Do not label those consequences proved merely by the local calculation.

4. X36/J-N and the signature: specify an effective input format for names, what exact finite information it contains, and how the decision procedure obtains named-unit information from it. If only a quantifier-free incidence type of the supplied tuple is intended, address Section 8's indistinguishable-input obstruction before asserting A11.

5. X47: retain finite definitional expansion, but add that semantic equivalence alone does not justify replacing an expansion or an inner series for purposes of fit. All reductions used by an A11 procedure must preserve contextual sense.

6. Ledger entrypoint/model declarations and X42/X44/X45 conclusions: change unconditional “Φ is a model” to “Φ is the proposed model; certification of A11 under the frozen semantics remains outstanding.” Preserve historical claims as history, explicitly marked as superseded in status.

7. Paper abstract and opening claim “It has a model, so it is self-consistent”: replace the unconditional model-based certification by “A candidate model Φ is given. Its A11 verification under the final semantics remains incomplete, so the present argument does not yet establish consistency by this model.” Footnote [4] already notes an incomplete re-proof, but that caveat does not warrant the stronger main-text assertion.

8. Paper Appendix A, A11 row: replace the evidence cell with “Unproved under X41–X47; the stated empty-support interface is not contextually adequate.” The reason cell should identify the ambient-aware congruence and realizability obligations rather than present an automaton as already constructed.

9. Paper's independence claim: retain it only with explicit provisional status unless the incomplete countermodel verifications are supplied. This audit does not resolve the A8, A13, A14, A4-countermodel-A11, or A7-countermodel-A11 gaps acknowledged in the sources.

No source files were edited. These amendments are proposed verbatim corrections to the strength and precision of the claims. The frozen semantics was used to expose the proof obstruction, not modified to eliminate it.



[Section: historical-r2]
Second referee audit

TLP — A11 certification, second independent audit

24 October 2026. Deliverable for subsequent adjudication. No change to the frozen system is made or proposed as an accomplished fact.

1. Executive verdict

Overall: UNRESOLVED for the frozen model specification. Not PROVED. There are, however, two rigorous negative results about versions of the proposed certification:

1. REFUTED — input consisting only of an abstract sign pattern and its finite quantifier-free named diagram. This input does not determine the answer, already for the ordinary finite formulas G₃(c). No automaton can remedy information absent from its input.
2. REFUTED — the stated standalone, empty-support acceptance summary as a compositional state under X43. The closed-cycle/closed-edge test remains valid. Adding only the names occurring in the substituted term does not repair it.

These statements must not be promoted to a proof that Φ with a specified effective coordinate naming violates A11. The ledger does not settle whether its algorithm receives abstract names with only their finite diagrams, or fixed name strings in a chosen effective presentation. It supplies no effective presentation of the latter kind. Consequently J-N, as documented, does not uniquely specify a computability problem. Under its strict finite-diagram-only reading the answer is negative; under a fixed-coordinate reading it is meaningful but remains unproved.

The first report's separator is independently verified here, including whole-sign fit, all successful named-instance prefixes, N+, and hereditary A6s. A stronger result addresses the objection that different name spellings might distinguish the inputs: one can give this same frame an ineffective naming presentation for which A11 is undecidable already on the G_n fragment, while each query supplies the same trivial singleton diagram. Conversely the G_n fragment is decidable with canonical coordinate names. Thus the distinction between presentations is mathematically substantive, not punctuation.

For the automaton question, this audit proves two limited positive results:

- a uniform lexical interface bound for a fully specified, fixed-rank, capture-avoiding substitution grammar;
- finite effective profiles and realizability for ordinary bounded-variable logic on the colored frame Φ, with fixed coordinate names.

It does not prove that every operation allowed by the ledger has that grammar, or that final TLP truth/sense can be compositionally translated into that bounded-variable logic. The latter is the principal remaining mathematical lemma after an input and grammar contract is fixed. A finite number of pebbles and local marker caps alone do not supply that translation.

Thaw assessment: the literal finite-diagram-only certification fails, and the displayed X33 compositionality check fails. These fall within the scope of X48's failed model/countermodel-check trigger, L2900–2906, when adjudicated as failures of the recorded certification. They do not establish that an axiom is contradictory, or that the model fails under every possible naming convention. No thaw is performed. A proposed addition of coordinate data must be adjudicated as a presentation clarification or a change to J-N; it is not silently adopted here.

2. Evidence conventions and source identification

[S] denotes a source statement or stipulated rule; [P] an independently proved result; [C] a finite computational observation; [A] an explicit assumption for a conditional result; [U] an unresolved issue.

Lnnnn means physical line nnnn of the supplied TLP Ledger.txt. Its header is revision 54, with the system frozen at revision 53, L3 and L2881–2895. Pnn means a physical line of TLP as axiomatic system.md. References to R1 mean Initial referee audit [section historical-r1], 24 October 2026. R1 and the previous tests were inspected as claims, not authorities. Source hashes are in audit_R2_results.json.

No external theorem about tractarian logic is assumed from an uninspected citation. The arguments below about finite profiles, lexical width, and the input obstruction are given directly. In particular, no ledger label “refereed” is used as a premise.

3. J-N: reconstruction and precise distinctions

3.1 Documentary sequence

| Stage | Exact content relevant to input | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Revision 22 | A11 read as “computable from the finite type” when names are uncountable, L4000–4010 | [S] Original motivation avoids requiring an effective enumeration of all names. |
| Core A11 entry | “the sign together with the frame restricted to its named objects,” L4685–4687 | [S] The clearest finite-diagram gloss. |
| Revision 32 | “under C-nv, the names' types in the whole frame,” L4687 | [S] Potentially broader wording, subsequently narrowed. |
| X36, revision 41 | “finite (quantifier-free) frame type”; whole-frame gloss “means no more”; not complete type, L1701–1705 | [S] Explicit limitation. |
| Consolidated A11 | Same correction, with complete types rejected because the empty tuple's type contains the frame theory, L4688–4690 | [S] No full-theory oracle. |
| X45 register | Failure of J-N was described as moving to decidability relative to frame theory, L2482–2483 | [S] Records one alternative, not a proof that no intermediate representation is possible. |
| X47, revision 52 | Definitions of occurring defined signs are additionally supplied, L2798–2802 | [S] Finite expansion is allowed; A8e remains rejected. No coordinate decoder is added. |
| Frozen entrypoint/paper | “given the names” plus definitions, L134–136; paper P37 and P115 | [S] Refers back to J-N, does not resolve the coding issue. |

The textual warrant for a finite procedure is J-FS, not an effective-name theorem: L4691–4697 cites 6.126, 6.122, 6.1262, and 5.551. A8 is explicitly non-effective as a general axiom; the stronger A8e is rejected, L4678–4681. This does not prohibit choosing an effective notation for a particular countable model. It also does not provide that notation or prove that every permitted notation is computationally interchangeable.

3.2 Five distinct objects

1. Syntactic identity: a finite symbol/string such as c17, its sort, and which occurrences co-refer. Distinct strings can be recognized without knowing their meanings.
2. Referent: the object ν(c)∈O or form ν(R)∈F designated by a name. This is semantic data, not its physical token location.
3. Finite quantifier-free named diagram: in the relational frame language with sorts O,F, equality, and incidence E(f,x,y), the atomic and negated atomic facts on the names occurring in the sign. For a lone object name c and no form names it contains no incident binary states. The frame restricted to {o_i} has no states for every i.
4. Full first-order type: truth of every first-order frame formula with those parameters. This can distinguish o₂ from o₃ and includes arbitrarily deep quantified information. The full empty-tuple type contains the whole first-order frame theory. J-N rejects supplying this as an oracle.
5. Effective presentation: a specified finite code and effective access to what its symbols designate, e.g. ν(o:17)=o₁₇, ν(f:17:3)=f₁₇,₃. A notation with such a decoder supplies more usable information than an anonymous singleton diagram. It need not supply a full-type oracle, and need not make χ* computable.

If “quantifier-free type” is instead taken in a language containing all background coordinate constants, it can have infinitely many atomic facts such as E(f_{i,j},h',c). That is not the finite restricted diagram described at L4685–4688. A finite code for a mechanism answering those infinitely many queries is again additional presentation information. The background signature and coding must be specified, not varied mid-proof.

3.3 What the original objection did and did not prove

R1 correctly identifies that a singleton diagram cannot distinguish o₂ and o₃. It would be incorrect to infer solely from this that two differently spelled, fixed names in one effective presentation give the same complete machine input. Their strings differ. One cannot use the same fixed constant c with two different interpretations within one already fixed interpreted language and call that an indistinguishable-input counterexample to that language's algorithm.

The finite-diagram-only counterexample below explicitly quantifies over named parameter presentations, or normalizes names to an abstract sign pattern. The separate ineffective-naming theorem uses one fixed interpreted language and does not make this mistake.

3.4 The decision theorem once a presentation is fixed

Let Γ specify finite syntax, an interpretation ν of its primitive name strings, the supplied finite-diagram format, and the definition input format. Let Prom_Γ(e) mean that e codes a closed proposition with sense under the final rules, and V_Γ(e,w) its truth at w. The exact promise-problem assertion is

    ∃ partial recursive D  ∀e:
      Prom_Γ(e) ⇒ [D(e) halts in {0,1} and
                    (D(e)=1 ⇔ ∀w∈{0,1}^A V_Γ(e,w)=1)].

No behavior is required off the promise. An algorithm deciding sense as well would prove a stronger statement. This is validity over all worlds, not truth at χ* and not truth only where a particular physical token sign is present. A self-settling sign in X41 need not be a tautology under this definition.

If the input specification erases Γ's reference information except for finite diagrams, the assertion must additionally be uniform over every realization of that same input. Theorem 2 refutes that requirement. Fixing Γ instead leaves its presentation relevant, as Theorem 3 shows.

4. Exact audit of G_n(c)

4.1 Frame and rules used

The fixed frame, L1063–1068, has

O={a,b,h,h'}∪{o_i:i≥1};

A={R_i(a,b),R_i(b,a),R_i(h,o_i):i≥1}
  ∪{f_{i,j}(h',o_i):i≥1,1≤j≤i}.

Λ={0,1}^A. All these labeled objects/forms are distinct as specified. For the theorem c designates o_i; the token of c may be elsewhere.

The proof uses only: C-nv and empty ranges, L100–106 and L935–951; N+, L1596–1598 and L1631–1638; shared tokens and injective letter/form placement, L1343–1354; hereditary A6s and named-component restriction, L2141–2162; X43's global name/binder exclusion for both sorts, L2277–2285. It uses no series production.

Let H_j=p_j(y,c)∨¬p_j(y,c), and

G_n(c)=(∃y)(∃p₁)…(∃p_n)∧_{j=1}^n H_j,  n≥2.

Boolean symbols are finite N-abbreviations. Repeated positive/negative occurrences of the same atom share a token. All form binders occur in their later bodies, so N+ enforces pairwise distinct semantic form values along a successful quantifier chain. The object y excludes ν(c).

4.2 The separator theorem

[P, Theorem 1] For every i≥1 and n≥2, G_n(c) with ν(c)=o_i is a proposition with sense under the frozen rules. It has the same truth value in every world, and

    G_n(o_i) is a tautology  ⇔  i≥n.

If i<n it is a contradiction with sense, not a senseless input.

Proof — whole-sign fit. Choose m>max(i,n). Place the token of c at o_m, the token of y at h', and the n form-binder tokens at distinct f_{m,1},…,f_{m,n}. Every atomic occurrence is a frame state, all distinct simultaneous form symbols have distinct tokens, and the only object binder avoids c's token. The repeated occurrences in H_j share their state. No atom is fully named, so no named projected cycle arises. Thus the original general sign has sense independently of i and of all world bits.

Proof — successful named instances exist when i≥n. Choose the semantic witness y=h' and n distinct markers f_{i,j₁},…,f_{i,j_n}. At each prefix of the substitutions use the same token unit m, larger than i and n. The names now present for y,c have distinct token objects h',o_m. An assigned form name receives its corresponding f_{m,k}; every remaining form binder receives a different f_{m,l}. Thus no binder token equals a name token, in either sort, and form injectivity holds.

Every fully named atom denotes f_{i,j_k}(h',o_i), a state of the frame. Its token is f_{m,k}(h',o_m). The set of such tokens and the set of such denotations are state-disjoint, since m≠i. Hence the induced partial map on named components has no cycle, including cycles among several components. Each successful prefix has a fitting, admissible instance. At the final matrix each H_j is true regardless of its state's truth bit. All existential steps therefore have a true admitted witness in every world.

Proof — necessity. Truth of the nested existential formula requires an actual chain of admitted named instances ending in a true matrix. A terminal H_j has sense only if its named atom is a state; C-nv cannot turn an out-of-frame atom into a true tautological disjunct. The successful chain therefore requires n distinct forms with states (y,o_i). The only possible incoming states to o_i are the single R_i(h,o_i) and the i markers f_{i,j}(h',o_i). With a common y and n≥2, the source cannot be h. It must be h', and there must be at least n markers. Thus i≥n.

If there is no such chain, no existential evaluation can be true. Some unsuccessful prefixes might have sense and evaluate false; others might be filtered out. This distinction cannot create a successful chain. Empty existential ranges are false. The original sign's sense was already established. This proves the theorem. ∎

In particular, G₃(o₂) is a contradiction and G₃(o₃) is a tautology. Tokening c at a fresh o_m does not change ν(c). The proof deliberately uses different locations for those two functions.

4.3 Quantifier ranges and hereditary restrictions: points that could have invalidated the proof

- Merely counting semantic incoming forms would not suffice if a witness prefix failed fit. The common fresh-unit construction verifies every successful prefix.
- A fixed point test on single atoms would not suffice for A6s. State-disjointness excludes every finite directed cycle at once.
- Distinct p_j are enforced semantically because each prior form name occurs in the scope of every later form binder. They are enforced syntactically by distinct token forms.
- The count does not depend on χ*, the generic pair, or truth probabilities.
- The n=1 case has an extra h-witness and is intentionally excluded from the stated threshold theorem.
- The proof does not invoke R1's potentially ambiguous general semantics of open formulas. It uses only closed formulas and their named instances.

5. Consequences for input, including one fixed ineffective presentation

5.1 Diagram-only impossibility

[P, Theorem 2] Suppose the input to validity consists of the sign up to renaming of its names, their sorts/co-reference, the finite restricted named frame diagram, and any occurring definitions. No function of that input, computable or otherwise, decides validity for all promised named propositions on HΦ.

Proof. G₃(c) with c=o₂ and with c=o₃ has the same abstract sign, empty definition list, and singleton named diagram. By Theorem 1 both inputs satisfy the promise and require opposite answers. ∎

This refutes the strict input interpretation. It is insufficiency of information, not an internal contradiction of the token semantics.

5.2 Different name strings do not automatically rescue decidability

[P, Theorem 3] There is one fixed, countable naming presentation of HΦ, with finite strings and the same finite-diagram inputs, in which A11 fails already on the G_n fragment.

Proof. Let K⊆ℕ be a nonrecursive set. Introduce effectively readable object-name strings c₀,c₁,… . For each k, interpret the pair c_{2k},c_{2k+1} by the pair o_{2k+2},o_{2k+3}, swapping the two exactly when k∈K. Add names for o₁ and the four distinguished objects; forms can keep their ordinary indexed strings. This is an injective naming of all the objects; syntax, name equality, and finite parsing are unaffected. No definitions or self-referential abbreviations are used.

The machine can construct the syntactic input G_{2k+3}(c_{2k}) from k. Only c_{2k} is a name occurring in this sign; its finite restricted diagram is the same trivial singleton diagram for every k. These are all promised signs by Theorem 1. Again by that theorem,

    G_{2k+3}(c_{2k}) is a tautology  ⇔  k∈K.

An A11 algorithm for this fixed presentation would decide K. Contradiction. ∎

The construction changes a naming presentation, not HΦ, Λ, the token rules, or χ*. It is not asserted to be the presentation actually chosen by the ledger: the missing specification is precisely the problem. A8's rejection of a globally effective syntax requirement does not itself forbid this naming, but A11 could exclude it if A11 is explicitly imposed as a restriction on presentations. That would make a presentation part of the model specification to be verified.

For canonical coordinate strings, the G_n fragment is decidable by parsing i and comparing it with n. This is only a theorem about the fragment, not a full A11 proof. A noncomputable renaming need not preserve computability; an effectively invertible renaming does.

5.3 Definitive input verdict and the minimum clarification

[U, documentary conclusion] J-N leaves the intended computational object underdetermined. The system does not give a unique encoding/decoder contract from which a single A11 decision problem can be extracted. This is a definite finding about the specification, rather than a claim that all possible completions are undecidable.

| Interpretation | Well-posed? | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Abstract sign plus finite restricted diagram only, uniformly over its realizations | Yes as a proposed factorization requirement | Refuted by Theorem 2. |
| Fixed readable name strings, arbitrary fixed interpretation, no effective semantic access beyond local diagrams | Yes after that interpretation is fixed | Not guaranteed; Theorem 3 supplies a counterpresentation. |
| Fixed canonical coordinate names, or an explicitly supplied computable decoder into those coordinates | Yes | G_n obstruction disappears; full A11 unresolved. |
| Complete parameter-type/frame-theory oracle | A relative problem can be defined | Not the frozen J-N problem; expressly rejected at L1701–1705. |

The smallest useful clarification is a sentence specifying whether and how the finite input identifies a referent beyond its restricted diagram, and whether A11 is uniform over renamings or concerns a chosen presentation. For example, a coordinate version would have to say that object/form names are finite codes with a fixed effective decoder into the indexed frame, and that decoding is available to the algorithm.

Such a convention is compatible with the existence of a particular countable notation and does not imply A8e for all models. But compatibility is not evidence that it was already selected. Relative to the strict finite-diagram-only interpretation, it adds information and is not computationally conservative: Theorems 2–3 prove this. Relative to an intended but unstated canonical presentation, it would specify that intention rather than alter the frame. The ledger must adjudicate which is intended; this report does not silently make the selection.

The distinction cannot be dismissed by saying “the frame is explicitly listed.” A metamathematical index i labeling a vertex in the construction is not automatically a symbol the decision procedure can recover from an arbitrary name for that vertex.

6. Syntax and final semantic interpretation

6.1 Exact finite fragment used in the negative results

The following sorted grammar is sufficient for Theorems 1–3 and the cycle tests. It has no disputed series productions:

    tO ::= object variable | object name
    tF ::= form variable   | form name
    A  ::= tF(tO,tO)
    F  ::= A | N_enum(F1,...,Fm) | N_inst(z,F)

Here m≥1 is finite and z has one of the two sorts; for this verified fragment require z to occur free in its body. Ordinary finite Boolean operations and ∃ are finite N-abbreviations. Binding uses distinct identities; spellings may subsequently be shared exactly where legal renaming allows. There is no primitive object equality required by these results; meta-level equality is used for typing and exclusion. This fragment is directly supported by L100–106, L1343–1354, L1596–1598, and L6944–6953. The stipulated truth value of N over an empty range does not by itself settle whether a literally empty enumeration or a vacuous binder is an admitted written sign; neither production is needed for the counterexamples.

For closed instances let S(F) mean sense and V(F,w) mean truth when S(F). A named atom needs its denoted frame state and an admissible token realization. Finite Boolean constructions require sense of their components and fit of the entire sign. For an instance description its range is

    R_z(B)={d of the right sort : d avoids the other free values/names
            in B's scope and S(B[z:=name(d)])}.

N_inst(z,B) is true exactly when every admitted instance is false. An empty range gives true. Sense of the general sign is its final whole-sign fit with the applicable named-component checks; it does not require any admitted value. The diagram-only objection uses this last distinction essentially.

For an open expression this is a named-instance semantics: evaluation at parameters means substitution of names, not an unproved identification with a classical variable assignment. X42 explicitly makes that distinction consequential, L2130–2139.

6.2 Shared tokens and two separate maps

Keep ν, the semantic name interpretation, separate from g, token placement. A fully named atom R(c,d) has token E(g(R),g(c),g(d)) and target E(ν(R),ν(c),ν(d)). The induced named-component map must be well-defined and acyclic on its finite token domain.

For fit, repeat occurrences of one atom contribute one state, L1346. Form symbols and object letters are injective in a chosen legal alphabetic variant, L1347–1351. Bound identities in different scopes may use the same spelling/token when no capture occurs, but a bound token can never equal a name token anywhere in the whole sign, L2277–2285. Form and object sorts obey this rule separately.

The N+ semantic guard and X43's token prohibition differ: the former looks at a binder's scope and semantic values; the latter reserves all names of the whole sign, even outside that scope, and concerns token placements.

6.3 Series and definition productions: supported schema versus missing choices

The supported schema adds

    D ::= Enum(...) | Inst(z,F) | Ser(B,interface,C)
    F ::= Atom | N(D) | DefinedApplication

with T₀=B and T_{k+1}=C[T_k]. X10 selects substitution, L722–723. X28 explicitly mentions a fixed context with holes under substitutions and variables declared in the hole, L1188–1192. Iteration is supported at L6890–6892; finite written descriptions and K3 at L911–934 and L6944–6952. Formal-series values are the terms that have sense, L2136–2139. The scheme is not arbitrary recursive enumeration: the latter is expressly rejected in the discussion at L5112–5121.

The following productions are not supplied as a complete formal grammar in the ledger:

| Missing item | Why certification needs it |
|---|---|
| Exact number, sorts, and ranks of holes, including multiple copies | Determines substitution state and width. |
| Allowed maps at a hole: variables, names, identifications, parameter permutations, variabilization | Determines whether interfaces/names remain bounded. |
| Whether a generator may inspect its filler or introduce fresh semantic names | Distinguishes a fixed syntactic context from a general algorithm. No such inspection rule is assumed here. |
| Interface changes between iterates and their finite control | A fixed written operation does not by itself prove a fixed-rank theorem. |
| Token pattern of a finite series descriptor | L1545–1546 says its fit is a finite check but gives no complete production-to-token rule. |
| Parameterized nested series and how a substitution acts on their descriptors | Required for an inside-out reduction preserving sense, not only truth. |
| Full rules for aliases of names and encoding of the supplied named diagram | Required for J-N; X47 resolves defined aliases by expansion, not arbitrary presentation access. |
| Literal empty enumerations and tokening of vacuous binders | Empty-range semantics alone is not a production rule for their written signs. |

This report therefore does not call a newly chosen full grammar “the exact frozen grammar.” It gives an exact supported fragment, a documented schema, and a precisely defined conditional extension below. Faithfulness of that extension to all permitted series remains a proof obligation. The assertion at L6952 that construction is expressible by a formal grammar is not itself a list of its productions.

6.4 X47

For a finite dependency graph of supplied finite, uniform definitions, expand in dependency order with fresh bound identities. Well-foundedness gives termination; capture-avoiding variants give the same allowed pattern class. This is the effective preprocessing licensed at L2705–2715 and L2793–2802.

Fresh identities during expansion are not a permanent prohibition on later legal token sharing. Conversely replacing the expansion by an arbitrary truth-equivalent formula is not licensed: it may change fit and names. A defined symbol adds no independent token. No proof below uses a binder exemption for an abbreviation.

7. Recheck of the previous counterexamples

7.1 The closed-cycle/closed-edge context

Let

C=(∃p)(∃x)(∃y)(p(x,y)∧p(y,x)),
E=(∃p)(∃x)(∃y)p(x,y),
P=C∨¬C,  Q=E∨¬E.

Both C and E have fitting general signs. Thus P and Q have sense and are tautologies with no names and no free variables. Identical occurrences may share tokens.

Let R denote R₁ and c,d denote a,b. Put K[Z]=(R(c,d)∧R(d,c))∧Z.

[P, Proposition 4] K[P] does not fit; K[Q] has sense.

Proof. The unique object pair supporting any two-cycle in HΦ is {a,b}. The named cycle forces g(c),g(d) to occupy that pair. The bound cycle in P also needs both objects, prohibited by the ambient name reservations. This covers all units and all legal renamings. For Q, token the named cycle on R₂(a,b),R₂(b,a) and project it to R₁(a,b),R₁(b,a); token its bound edge on a marker state f_{3,1}(h',o₃). Form injectivity and both sorts of name reservations hold. The named projected states are disjoint from their tokens. ∎

At empty interface, the whole-frame acceptance of P and Q is the same singleton {()}. Their standalone truth, sense, free sets and name sets also agree. Hence the corresponding standalone summary cannot determine K's fit. This verifies R1's objection to the empty-support specialization of L1532–1542.

Limit of this result: it does not show that P and Q have the same historical map for every possible availability set S, or the same ambient-aware summary. It refutes neither every richer state nor every input-dependent finite quotient. A quotient permitted to carry ambient name placements distinguishes them.

7.2 X42's sigma3 and named-instance behavior

The ledger's sigma3 is displayed at L2131. With x uninstantiated its two cycle components can share the object token pair. After substituting any name c for x, the first cycle forces c's token onto a or b; the second cycle's two binders need both and may use neither occurrence of that reserved token. Thus every first named instance fails fit. Sigma3's whole sign fits, but its outer existential range is empty and it is false in every world under X41–X43.

This argument is about token names, regardless of what object c denotes. It confirms the pattern phenomenon used in R1 and falsifies any rigidification lemma that replaces “free variable” by “name” without changing its token role. A role-aware translation is possible in principle; this example is a required test, not a proof that every translation fails.

7.3 Repetition and inherited cycles

Duplicating the same fitting atomic pattern does not force duplicate token resources. A conjunction of copies of C fits on the same two states. Conversely replacing every separate binder by a shared token regardless of scope is illegal. Both extremes fail.

For named-component admissibility, checking each component in isolation is insufficient: arrows d₁→d₂ and d₂→d₁ are individually acyclic and jointly cyclic. A compositional state must retain enough boundary projection information, or the full finite set of fully named atom patterns, to reject such a union. This is a general A6s composition check; it is not offered as a new Φ countermodel.

8. An ambient-aware exact state, and what it does not yet prove

8.1 Exact token acceptance relation

For a finite expression T define a relation

    Acc_T(B_O,B_F,β,ν)

where B_O,B_F are reserved token sets for all names in the surrounding sign; β assigns tokens to T's interface letters/names; and ν gives the semantic references of its actual names. Acceptance means there is a placement of its internal binder identities such that:

- all atoms are frame states;
- same letters and identical atoms are treated coherently, with repeated atoms counted once;
- all lexical capture/interference constraints hold;
- each binder avoids the reserved sets of its sort;
- distinct simultaneous form/object symbols satisfy injectivity;
- its fully named atoms denote valid states and the applicable combined projection has no directed cycle.

For composition, retain the finite set J_T of fully named atom patterns, with their token/target information, rather than only a Boolean saying “acyclic.” Take the union before testing hereditary A6s. No multiplicity is added for a duplicate pattern. For a fixed finite name alphabet there are at most |N_F||N_O|² such binary patterns, though promoted parameter names must also be accounted for.

This is an exact relational specification of fit under the stipulated lexical constraint interpretation, not a finite-state assertion. Its parameter domains can be infinite. Boolean combination takes compatible joint placements, not a product of independent yes/no answers; a binder existentially chooses a token satisfying its local interference constraints and all ambient reservations. A conjunction may allow two independent scoped binders to share a token, exactly as the rules permit.

On the cycle example, the reserved object set {a,b} makes Acc_P empty and leaves Acc_Q nonempty. Thus this relation repairs that particular loss of information. No general finite computability claim follows merely by writing it down.

8.2 Exact contextual semantic equivalence

Fix an input interpretation and an actual admissible-context grammar. Define Obs(T,K,θ,w) to contain the sense status and, when meaningful, the truth of K[T] under the permitted named substitutions θ at world w. Include token acceptance queries with arbitrary consistent ambient name placements and the named projection boundary information above. A context may introduce names absent from T.

Define T≈U when their interfaces agree and all these observations agree, for every admissible K,θ,w and boundary query.

[P, formal fact] This is a contextual congruence: for a permitted context C, each observation of C[T] is an observation of T in the composed context K∘C with the corresponding substitutions. The same holds for a specified substitution constructor by composing substitutions capture-avoidantly. The definition therefore preserves fit, truth, sense, C-nv filtering, name reservations, token sharing, form injectivity and hereditary A6s.

This establishes existence of an exact possibly infinite congruence. It establishes neither finite index nor computability. Defining a state as this whole response function and then claiming it has finitely many values would be precisely the missing proof, not its solution.

No finite quotient for the entire language with arbitrary names can preserve all semantic observations: the independent atoms R_i(a,b) have distinct truth sets under A4. That fact does not rule out a separate finite quotient for the substitution closure of a fixed finite input system.

9. A uniform width result, explicitly conditional on a precise grammar

9.1 The ranked-context grammar used for this theorem

[A, RCG] Each hole has a fixed finite sorted interface. A hole occurrence supplies a simultaneous map from its declared interface variables to variables or names of the same sort. Each map is fixed by the finite template; it does not inspect the filler. It may identify arguments. Internal binders of a filler are freshened to avoid unintended capture; binding of the supplied interface variables by the surrounding template is allowed and explicit. There are finitely many contexts/base templates and a finite family of interface ranks; every transition has a declared input and output rank. No operation manufactures new name strings depending on the iteration index. Nested descriptors, if present in the templates, have the same declared finite interfaces.

This gives exact productions by adding typed holes H(σ) to the finite fragment and forming finite templates by its constructors; substitutions replace all holes by the corresponding freshened filler instances. Multiple occurrences are allowed. It is consistent with X28's explicit declared-hole wording, L1188–1192. [U] The ledger does not prove that this captures every permitted operation.

9.2 Definition and proof of the bound

For a finite binder-identity syntax tree define lexical width w(T) as the maximum of:

- |FV(U)| at every subexpression U;
- |FV(B)∪{z}| at every binder z with body B.

Count object and form variables together for a conservative bound. Names are not counted as variables. In a template, treat each hole as an atom mentioning all its supplied interface variables, even if a particular filler might not use them. Let v be the maximum of these widths over the finitely many base/context templates and their declared interfaces.

[P, conditional Theorem 5] Every finite iterate generated by RCG has lexical width at most v. If n distinct syntactic names occur in the finite specification, every evaluated named instance of a subtree has at most n+v names. For checking an internal piece of that instance, carrying its local live variables plus all ambient name reservations needs at most n+2v+1 handles. These bounds are independent of iteration index.

Proof. On substituting T into a hole, an internal subexpression of its freshened copy has the same internally bound identities as before and its external free variables mapped one-for-one to supplied variables or names. Their number cannot increase; identification or replacement by a name can only decrease the variable count. Freshening prevents collisions with internal binders. A subexpression outside the inserted copy sees at most the declared supplied interface of the hole, already counted when computing the template's width. Taking the maximum proves w(C[T])≤max(w(C),w(T)), and induction proves the iterate bound. Multiple copies do not change the argument: a common ancestor's template already contains their supplied interfaces; a node inside a copy sees only that copy.

During named-instance evaluation, only variables free in the evaluated original subtree can contribute new names to that subtree. There are at most v of them. Any outer name whose variable has no occurrence in that subtree disappears from its syntax; names already written in the finite templates are among the n original names. Hence its name set has size at most n+v. In a descendant piece, keep those ambient names even when absent locally, plus at most v live variables and one binder being processed. This gives n+2v+1. ∎

This proof does not assume that distinct binders everywhere have distinct token objects; it counts simultaneous interface handles. It also does not use the erroneous inference that a fixed written generator automatically bounds unfolded width. The declared interface and allowed-substitution hypotheses do that work explicitly.

Limit: this is a syntactic bound, not a proof of a bounded-variable semantic translation. New role-dependent sense predicates may still lack the required uniform interpretation. If the ledger permits interface-growing or name-generating operations outside RCG, the theorem does not apply to them. No such operations are silently excluded from the frozen system here.

10. Effective world profiles: what can be proved independently

10.1 Scope of the result

[A] For this section only, names have fixed effective coordinates. Use the ordinary two-sorted relational language with frame relation E(f,x,y), world relation W(f,x,y)⊆E, equality, and the finitely many coordinate constants under consideration. This is ordinary bounded-variable logic on a colored frame, not yet final TLP semantics. Distinguished objects a,b,h,h' may be fixed as auxiliary constants; validity in a reduct is still covered. Choosing a fixed orientation of a,b for the analysis does not assert their definability.

[P, Theorem 6] For every q≥1 and finite coordinate constant set, there is a computable finite family of realizable profiles for all worlds of Φ with those constants. Each profile determines the truth of every ordinary formula using at most q additional variables, at every compatible finite parameter configuration. Profile realizability and the finite transition graph of parameter configurations are decidable.

10.2 Profiles

Each unit i has:

- its three R_i truth bits, in the fixed order (a,b),(b,a),(h,o_i);
- c_i true markers and i−c_i false markers.

For anonymous units record the three bits and (min(c_i,q),min(i−c_i,q)). For each such type τ record min(number of anonymous units of type τ,q). Thus a supply of q means at least q, not exactly q.

Any named form or named o_i pins its entire unit for bookkeeping. Keep those finitely many units separately. In each keep the three R bits, the identity and truth of every named marker, and the true/false counts of the remaining markers capped at q. The exact known capacity i is used in realizability, even if residual counts are capped. Object constants among the four distinguished objects are retained exactly. Duplicate or colliding references are handled by the input diagram/coordinate equality.

For a parameter tuple also record its equality pattern, sort, distinguished-object positions, which pinned or anonymous units its non-distinguished elements/form values belong to, which forms are R-forms or true/false markers, and identifications among the selected markers. At most q anonymous units can be touched by q parameter handles. A form parameter touches its unit even if o_i is not presently a parameter.

These data include correlations: R_i's three bits travel together; all markers sharing o_i belong to one unit; all units share the same globally chosen a,b,h,h'. They do not independently rematch orientation bits from different units.

10.3 Proof of bounded-variable invariance

Maintain a matching of all units touched by currently placed variable handles, and all pinned units. Match their recorded types and map selected marker forms injectively within true and false classes; match R-form and o_i positions coherently. Keep a,b,h,h' and constants fixed.

If a variable moves to a previously untouched anonymous unit of type τ, at most q−1 other anonymous units are occupied. Equal supplies capped at q guarantee an unused corresponding unit: if the supply is below q its exact count is equal; if it is q there are enough. Inside an already matched unit, a new true or false marker has a mate because the corresponding remaining marker class has equal size below q or at least q elements, and at most q−1 nonconstant markers are currently occupied. Named marker constants were removed from these residual counts and are already matched. Moving to an already selected element preserves equality. Moving to an R-form, its target object, or a distinguished object is forced coherently by the maintained unit map.

Every E-atom is preserved by this correspondence, and every W-atom by the three bits and marker colors. The invariant can be maintained for arbitrarily many moves with q handles. A structural induction on formulas now proves agreement: atoms agree; Boolean operations preserve agreement; for an existential step take the matching response for that variable and apply the induction hypothesis. There is no quantifier-depth cutoff. This supplies the claimed ordinary q-variable invariance without citing a pebble-game theorem as an unexplained black box.

10.4 Local capacities and effective realizability

For i≥2q the possible anonymous capped marker pairs are exactly

    {(r,q):0≤r<q} ∪ {(q,r):0≤r<q} ∪ {(q,q)}.

If both counts were below q their sum would be below 2q. Conversely each listed pair has a realization; choose c=r, c=i−r, or q≤c≤i−q. The three R bits are independently arbitrary by A4.

Separate the finite set of unpinned small units i<2q and the finitely many pinned units. Enumerate their possible local records, checking exact capacity i and named marker values. For each anonymous type, a desired capped supply below q is an exact finite quota; a supply q is a lower bound q without an upper bound. Assign the finitely many small units to their possible types subject to the upper quotas. This is a finite search. The infinitely many remaining indices are all large and allow exactly the same finite set of tail types just displayed.

After the finite assignment, residual exact quotas and lower bounds can be filled from finitely many tail units precisely when their types are tail-allowed. All surplus infinitely many tail units can be assigned iff at least one tail-allowed type has a saturated supply q. If no such type exists, all type quotas are finite and cannot accommodate the infinite tail. These conditions are both necessary and sufficient, yielding an explicit finite decision procedure. Named units are handled separately and finitely even when their indices are large.

Parameter configurations are realized by the same finite quota search with at most q additional distinguished choices. Equalities, unit incidences and marker selections impose only finite lower demands and exact-count constraints. This decides both vertices and moves of the finite configuration graph. Equivalently, one can form a finite representative with q units for a saturated anonymous type and q markers for a saturated residual color; it need not itself be a cut of Φ, but the invariant above proves its bounded-variable adequacy after the profile has been certified realizable in Φ.

The single-flip variant used historically in X32 stabilizes from i≥2q+1: the only new central transition is (q,q)→(q,q), possible when q≤c≤i−q−1. With p pinned markers replace i by i−p; the threshold becomes 2q+p+1. The reproducible tests check these arithmetic statements, not the full semantic translation.

10.5 What remains outside this theorem

No arbitrary contextual sense color has been included for free. Frame automorphism invariance does not suffice: the units o_i have distinct marker capacities, so invariant predicates can select arbitrary sets of indices. A particular color must have a proved bounded-variable interpretation, or another effective profile-preservation proof.

Likewise “availability” in a fit state includes role-specific ambient reservations and named projection constraints. The raw E,W profiles do not automatically describe all those predicates. One cannot append them to the signature and reuse Theorem 6 without proving they preserve its equivalence or providing a larger effective bound/profile construction.

11. The precise remaining congruence lemma and series analysis

11.1 A sufficient, non-circular target

[U, Role-aware translation/congruence lemma] Given a finite specification I in the actually permitted grammar, with a legitimate effective input presentation, construct a finite bound K(I), a finite set of syntactic role summaries, and effective translations/states for its entire substitution closure, such that:

1. Each summary records actual free/name occurrence sets, allowed identification patterns, and fully named atomic patterns after each permitted promotion/substitution. Repeated atoms use sets, not multiplicities.
2. For every role assignment of interface variables as free letters or instantiated names, and every ambient name reservation, the translated sense/fit and truth predicates exactly match frozen C-nv, N+, X43 and hereditary A6s, keeping ν and g distinct.
3. The translated predicates use at most K(I) variables over the ordinary colored frame, or an equivalently finite effective profile system whose realizability is proved.
4. Each permitted constructor, promotion of a parameter to a name, and substitution induces a computable function of these states, independent of which representative term is used.
5. The finite descriptor for N(series) and its occurrence inside any enclosing descriptor have a corresponding translation preserving their own token patterns as well as their admitted term values.

The exact response relation of Section 8 satisfies semantic correctness but is not known finite/effective. The width theorem helps bound syntactic handles under RCG. The raw profile theorem proves finite effective observation once a fixed bounded-variable translation exists. Neither proves item 2 or the compositionality in item 4, and item 5 also needs the descriptor grammar.

The failed attempted construction is therefore documented precisely: taking ordinary truth profiles plus a standalone fit bit/interface loses ambient name information; adding a reserved-name argument repairs the displayed example but does not by itself establish a finite role-indexed translation or deterministic transition. This report does not advertise that repaired definition as a completed automaton.

11.2 Conditional finite-state theorem

[P, conditional Theorem 7] If the preceding lemma holds, and the input/grammar contracts are fixed, A11 for that interpretation follows.

Proof. Theorem 6, or the alternative proved finite profile system in item 3, supplies finitely many realizable configurations. Each translated predicate is a finite truth table on them; with finitely many role summaries there are finitely many states. Item 4 makes the successor a computable deterministic function F on that state set. Thus for T₀=B,T_{k+1}=C[T_k], iteration reaches a repeated state after at most |Q|+1 visited states. If the first repeat is between indices r<s, all subsequent states repeat with period s−r, by induction using determinism.

For each world/parameter observation, item 2 marks which terms have sense and gives their truth. All distinct such observations along the orbit occur among 0,…,s−1, so joint negation over the admitted series values is computable from this finite list. Item 5 supplies its correct enclosing token/sense behavior; the raw conjunction of representative signs is not substituted blindly. Induct on finite series nesting, using the uniform states for all outer parameter substitutions. Finally validity means truth on every realizable world profile, which is a finite effective test. ∎

This proof is conditional and non-circular. In particular the transition table is not supplied by an A11 oracle; item 4 must construct it. It distinguishes a computable state bound from an observed repetition of coarse outputs.

11.3 What the adversarial tests establish

- Contexts introducing c,d outside a closed filler must still reserve their token locations within it: Proposition 4.
- Named promotion is a real state operation, not an extensional equality: sigma3.
- Copied patterns may share states; a token count proportional to the unfolded length is wrong.
- Independently acyclic named fragments can form a forbidden cycle on union.
- Same standalone truth/sense does not license a replacement inside an inner series descriptor or a quantifier body.
- No nonperiodic permitted Φ-series or undecidable coordinate-input series fragment is proved here. Failure of these candidate summaries is not evidence of either.

12. Computation: independently reproducible scope and results

New files are audit_R2_checks.js and audit_R2_results.json. Run from this directory with Node.js:

    node audit_R2_checks.js

Only built-in modules are used. Source paths at the bottom of the script can be adjusted if the evidence files are moved; the mathematical checks do not otherwise depend on external packages. The run used Node.js v24.19.0.

| Check | Scope | Observed result |
|---|---|---|
| G_n star witnesses | i=1,…,4; n=2,…,4; six-unit token frame | Whole signs fit in all 12 cases. Successful chains occur exactly for i≥n. |
| Named-prefix token/projection witnesses | 306 checked prefixes | All token constraints and acyclicity assertions pass. |
| Terminal tautological matrices | 704 truth-bit assignments across successful chains | All true. |
| Closed cycle/edge with reserved a,b | Whole-frame pattern test on six units | Cycle rejected; edge accepted. Both fit without reservations. |
| Repeated cycles | Three copies of the identical atomic pattern | Fits with shared states. |
| Sigma3 pattern | Uninstantiated versus first named instance constraints | Fits before promotion; fails after promotion. |
| RCG path-like iterates | 25 explicit unfolds | Lexical width remains 2. This is an illustration, not the proof of Theorem 5. |
| Local capped counts/flip transitions | q=1,…,8; p=0,…,q; i=2q+p+1,…,100 | All 3,800 cases pass. |
| Ineffective-naming reduction skeleton | Eight arbitrary finite membership bits | Threshold answers recover those bits. This does not compute a nonrecursive set. |

The G_n computation enumerates successful semantic witness chains with pruning of branches that cannot lead to a terminal sense-bearing matrix. It supplies explicit token witnesses for each retained prefix and checks the corresponding named projection for cycles. It is not a full evaluator of every unsuccessful partial instance, and does not claim to be one. Such an instance can either be filtered out or admitted but false; the universal proof explains why neither produces a successful existential chain.

Finite cuts can distort arbitrary TLP ranges. The infinite-frame theorems here are established by the fresh-unit constructions and structural arguments, not by extrapolation from cuts. The ordinary-profile theorem is also proved separately; the script checks only its local arithmetic. There is no full A11 implementation among these files.

The older script/results and R1 were not modified or rerun in a way that overwrites their outputs. Their hashes, together with those of the authoritative sources, are recorded in the new result file.

13. X41–X47, consistency certification, and thaw scope

| Decision | Treatment here |
|---|---|
| X41 | Whole-frame fit replaces the retired support-disjointness condition. No old support rule is used. General signs can have empty ranges. |
| X42 | Named-instance filtering and hereditary A6s are used in Theorem 1 and sigma3. No assumption that X41 merely filters unchanged truth values. |
| X43 | The strict global name/binder token rule is preserved in both sorts; no scope-local weakening. |
| X44 | Scope occurrence and guard data cannot be erased. Raw profiles do not purport to certify the four invariant-family descriptions automatically. |
| X45 | Its evidential register and input alternative are distinguished from mathematical proofs. |
| X46 | Textual classifications supply no transition construction; none are retagged here. |
| X47 | Supplied finite definitions are expanded; they have no extra tokens and no binder exemption. |

Φ/A11: under normalized finite-diagram-only input, its proposed certification is refuted already at kind 2. Under a fixed effective-coordinate presentation, it is unresolved. The naming and grammar ambiguities prevent assigning an unconditional PROVED/REFUTED verdict to every interpretation of the frozen specification. The unconditional result is not certified.

Thirteen axioms: a claim that Φ witnesses all thirteen needs A11 with its legitimate input semantics, plus complete verification of the other axioms. Neither R1 nor this report supplies that full certification. The present analysis does not find a contradiction in A4, A6s, C-nv, or the token semantics. A failed certificate for Φ is not a proof that TLP has no model. Genericity arguments about χ* do not decide truth over all Λ and cannot repair J-N.

Thaw triggers: X48 explicitly includes a failed model or countermodel check, L2906, not just an established inconsistency. The tested compositionality claim used to certify Φ fails as stated. This warrants reopening the affected certification step under that recorded trigger. If J-N is adjudicated to mean finite-diagram-only input, Theorem 2 is additionally a failed Φ/A11 check, and a coordinate remedy would change that input requirement. If coordinates are adjudicated to be implicit in a fixed presentation, supplying their decoder is a specification action whose conservativity must be documented. Neither finding automatically activates the separate “derivation whose proof fails” trigger L2907: A11 is an axiom, and the failed step is its model verification, not a proof deriving A11 from the other axioms.

This report evaluates trigger conditions; it does not alter the freeze, register, axiom list, or interpretive selections. It also does not decide an LI comparison between possible repairs.

14. Precise proposed corrections, separated by kind

14.1 Corrections of proof/evidence claims, with no semantic change

1. X33 L1531–1546: replace the unconditional finite-state conclusion by: “The displayed standalone acceptance relation does not account for ambient names absent from a subterm under X43. A finite effective contextual quotient, including named-instance behavior and nested-series descriptor fit, has not been established. Periodicity follows only after a deterministic transition on such states is proved.”
2. X42 L2137–2140: keep Lemma R' as the intended final range rule, but replace “X33's automaton … track[s] exactly this” by “an automaton used for A11 must track exactly this; the stated standalone summary is insufficient.”
3. X32 L1468–1477: distinguish the valid local count calculation from the unproved transfer to final contextual sense colors. The raw ordinary-profile theorem in Section 10 may be cited as a new result only with its coordinate and ordinary-logic hypotheses.
4. Frozen model statements, including L2892–2895: replace certification language by “Φ is the proposed model; its A11 verification depends on an explicit input presentation and an unproved contextual congruence/translation theorem.”
5. Paper main consistency assertion and P79: state that the provided argument does not yet establish consistency by Φ. This is a correction of evidential strength, not a claim that the system is inconsistent.
6. Paper Appendix A A11 row, P186: use “Unresolved. Diagram-only input is insufficient; the fixed-presentation version requires a contextual closure proof.” Keep the interpretations separate rather than writing simply “A11 false.”

14.2 Necessary specification decisions, not silently adopted corrections

7. J-N L1701–1705 and L4685–4690 / paper P115: specify the background signature of the finite diagram, the status of name strings, the interpretation/decoder available to the algorithm, and the quantification over naming presentations. If “finite type only” is retained literally, record Theorem 2's negative result. If a coordinate decoder is supplied, explicitly justify whether this clarifies a chosen presentation or changes the input contract; do not call it a full-type oracle.
8. X10/X28/X33: give an actual typed context grammar, with hole interfaces, substitution maps, alias handling, and descriptor-to-token rules. RCG is one precise candidate, not an amendment already licensed by this report. Its adequacy for the frozen operation reading must be adjudicated.
9. X47: retain its finite expansion rule. Add the proof obligation that every series reduction used by A11 preserves the expanded sign's contextual fit and named-instance semantics; do not replace an expansion by a truth-equivalent sign without that theorem.

14.3 Corrections to the first referee report's interpretation

10. R1's G_n claim is confirmed. Its input objection must be read with the qualification in Section 3.3: equality of singleton diagrams does not make distinct fixed name strings identical inputs. Theorems 2–3 give the correctly quantified replacements.
11. R1's empty-support counterexample is confirmed in its stated limited scope. It is not a counterexample to every ambient-aware state or to the historical acceptance map over all availability sets.
12. R1's blanket unresolved-profile discussion can now be narrowed: raw bounded-variable colored-frame profiles and realizability are proved here under coordinate input; the transfer to contextual sense colors remains unproved.

These are proposals for adjudication. The ledger, paper, and R1 have not been edited.

15. Compact outstanding obligations

1. Input contract: adjudicate fixed presentation versus finite-diagram-only uniformity. The latter is refuted; the former needs an explicit effective decoder or equivalent legitimate access.
2. Grammar faithfulness: specify the permitted operations, interface transitions, nested descriptors, and their token patterns. Prove that any proposed RCG restriction is faithful, or prove a width theorem for the larger grammar actually permitted.
3. Role-aware semantic translation/congruence: establish Section 11.1, particularly the uniform bounded interpretation of named-instance sense under ambient reservations and substitutions. The raw profile theorem and conditional width bound are available premises; the congruence itself is not.
4. Nested replacement: retain descriptor token behavior while replacing the infinite value orbit by a finite state computation. Standalone truth equivalence is insufficient.
5. Final certification: only after 1–4, instantiate the conditional finite-state theorem and present a terminating algorithm with a correctness proof. Reassess the thirteen-axiom model claim separately from independence claims.

No remaining obligation is supplied by finite experiments, by χ*'s genericity, or by the labels attached to prior referee discussions.



[Section: revision58-audit]
Revision-58 audit and original counterexample

TLP revision 58 — full independent audit of the model certificate

31 October 2026

Executive verdict

The revision-58 certificate does not pass. Φ's A11 remains unproved by X50–X52 as written. The claim that E32 is closed and that Φ has been certified as a model of all thirteen axioms is premature.

This verdict rests on a new, explicit counterexample, not a repetition of the objections to revision 53. X49 has changed the input requirement, and X51 has made substantial choices about the language. Those changes must be acknowledged and assessed on their own terms.

Decisive finding: X52's definition of Mov counts names directly mapped to variables, but permits maps that first send a name to another name and only subsequently to a variable. Its asserted bound q=v+|Mov| therefore fails. A legal four-name G* series has v=2 and |Mov|=1, yet its fourth term has lexical width 6. More significantly, its joint negation has different truth values in two infinite Φ-worlds with exactly the same claimed q=3 profile. Thus X52's profile-preservation assertion and the use of its finite representative are false for this permitted input.

This is a counterexample to the proposed proof and state bound. It is not a proof that A11 is false in the revised adequate-notation sense. The example itself becomes constant after four steps. Counting all potentially moved names, rather than only directly moved names, is an evident repair direction; the dependent state definitions and proof must then be updated and checked. That repair is not already the theorem printed in X52.

The other parts of the audit have substantially better outcomes:

- X49: the old input objection is addressed by an explicit, acknowledged change to A11, not by claiming coordinates were always implicit. With Φ's decimal notation, the input problem is well posed.
- X50: the non-series decidability argument can be justified by finite fitting, the corrected atom clause, and ordinary bounded-variable profiles. Its handling of vacuous N needs a precise notation convention, explained below; the counterexample here uses no vacuous binder until normalization removes an idle outer binder.
- X51: G* is materially more explicit than the old grammar. The four-name counterexample satisfies its rules, including its closure, declaration, normal-form and no-inspection requirements. It does not rely on an undecided edge case of the grammar.
- X53: the finite-copy argument, structural invariants, and repaired object descriptions withstand the specific checks below. A17 has an independent constructive proof once the displayed definitions are verified, and the requisite token placements are given here. A18's genericity argument is sound with its stated regularity assumptions; a direct Baire-category version explains why no A11 algorithm is needed for that step.
- Independence: the paper now correctly separates consistency from independence/minimality. Nothing here closes E33 or the remaining countermodel-A11 obligations.

Required disposition: correct X52's movement accounting and withdraw its unconditional certification pending a complete amended argument. Reopen the A11 portion of E32. No axiom, notation choice, grammar rule, or interpretive selection has been altered by this audit.

1. Scope, sources and evidence standard

This is a mathematical audit of the revision-58 model certificate: X49's input change, X50's kind-1/2 argument, X51's grammar and semantic choices, X52's series argument, and X53's verification of the remaining axioms. It also checks the implications for the paper's consistency and independence claims. It does not independently establish the correctness of every philosophical reading of all 526 Tractatus propositions; the interpretive selections are distinguished from mathematical deductions throughout.
