2. What changed since the previous audits

X49, L3015–3020 and L3172–3175, expressly says A11's content changes and that coordinates do not merely clarify the former finite-type input. Its revised assertion, L3194–3197, asks for an adequate notation with finite-string names in which the promise problem is decidable. Φ's selected notation is specified at L3198–3201.

X51, L3412–3416 and L3640–3669, selects G*, including name variabilization, multiple mapped holes, nested series, written interface images, term normalization, and a special rule for vacuous binders. It adds a restriction of 5.24. This is a real change in the formal specification relative to the incomplete grammar audited earlier.

Therefore it would be incorrect to continue applying the old diagram-only impossibility theorem as a refutation of the revised A11. It would be equally incorrect to describe the current effort as a proof of precisely the old, unchanged statement.

2.1 Exact revised A11 obligation

For a selected adequate notation ν, let e be a finite closed G* sign with its finite definition data Δ, and let S(e) mean that it is a proposition under the final sense rules. The required assertion is:

    there exists a partial recursive D such that, for every e with S(e),
    D(e) halts in {0,1}, and
    D(e)=1 iff V(e,w)=1 for every w in {0,1}^A.

There is no requirement on non-promised inputs. Deciding all of G* membership and sense is stronger. The notation selected for Φ is effective: a,b,h,h',o_i,R_i,f_{i,j}, with finite decimal indices and the elementary constraints i≥1, 1≤j≤i.

Validity is over every world of the frame, not merely χ* and not merely worlds where a particular token sign is physically present. Actual-world genericity does not decide this problem.

2.2 J-N disposition

Proved here: the revised coordinate input supplies the information missing from the previous G_n example. Parsing c=o_i makes its threshold i≥n effective. The previous noncomputable-naming example does not refute existence of some adequate notation. X49 recognizes this distinction.

The selection of the existential “some notation” reading is an interpretive decision, supported by the arguments at L3072–3175. Its mathematical formulation is coherent; the audit does not turn that interpretive argument into a theorem about the uniquely correct reading of Wittgenstein. A8e need not be imposed on all models to choose an effective notation for this particular model.

The cardinality consequence is correct under the adopted injective finite-string naming: objects and forms are countable. Since every state is finite, states are determined by finite form/slot/object data, and the existing infinite-multiplicity theorem gives infinitely many states, |A|=aleph₀. The old uncountable-form A17 countermodel consequently cannot satisfy revised A11, as the paper now records.

3. Frame, fit and semantic rules used in the audit

The frame is

    O={a,b,h,h'} ∪ {o_i : i≥1},
    A={R_i(a,b), R_i(b,a), R_i(h,o_i)}_i
       ∪ {f_{i,j}(h',o_i) : 1≤j≤i}.

All indicated objects/forms are distinct except where repeated. Worlds are arbitrary subsets of A. A token map g is not the semantic reference map ν. In particular, a name denoting o_i may have token object a, b or another o_m where the whole pattern permits; projection subsequently takes that token to its referent.

Fit is existential over legal alphabetic variants and token placements. Repeated atoms share one state. Binders can share tokens where the lexical interference constraints permit, but every binder must avoid every name token of its sort in the checked sign, even outside its scope. Names are injective. The additional restriction on fully named projections is hereditary A6s: their finite token-to-target graph has no directed cycle.

X50 L3285–3298 and X52 L3743–3755 select the literal atom clause: named atoms visible outside non-vacuous binders must denote frame states. A non-vacuous general sign may have sense even though its instance range is empty. C-nv filters by the instance's own sense. N+ excludes other free values and names in the binder's scope. These decisions are essential in both the counterexample and X53.

3.1 A6s elimination for existential fitting in Φ

Proved here; verifies X50 Lemma 1, L3300–3309. Suppose a finite sign has a fitting token map and its exposed fully named atoms satisfy the atom clause. List every unit used by its token objects/forms. Replace those units injectively by distinct fresh units of sufficiently large index, above every unit named semantically in the sign. Preserve a,b,h,h', map o_i to the fresh o_m, R_i to R_m, and markers injectively to enough markers of the fresh unit.

Every frame state and every equality/inequality between token symbols is preserved. Every fully named token state now has a fresh form; its target has a named form. Thus the token-domain and named-target states are disjoint, so the induced map has no directed cycle. Additional atom-free slots or propositional-letter states, where the grammar supplies them, can be placed on further fresh resources.

This proves that an admissible placement exists whenever the relevant fit and atom conditions hold. It does not say that every placement is acyclic, or that A6s can be dropped from the definition of pictures.

4. Audit of X50: ordinary finite signs

4.1 Fit is decidable independently of semantic reference

X50's tree acceptance relation, L3310–3320, now carries all names of the checked sign. That repairs the particular ambient-name omission found in the earlier audits. The accepted placements remain relational, not merely a yes/no bit for each child. Compatibility of shared free letters is required at a Boolean node; internal sibling binders may share a token where no constraint forbids it.

An independent finite-model argument also establishes decidability of this finite fitting problem. Let m exceed the total number of distinct object/form identities in a sign, including its names and active binders. Construct a finite auxiliary token frame with the four distinguished objects, m leaf units, one R-form per unit, and m marker forms per unit. Keep the same two common oriented states for every R-form and the same h/h' incidence rules. This is an auxiliary frame, not necessarily a literal initial cut of Φ.

Any finite fitting assignment in Φ uses at most m units and at most m distinct markers in one unit, so it transports to this auxiliary frame. Conversely embed its units into m distinct Φ-units of index at least m. Thus exhaustive assignment, with the lexical/name inequalities and repeated-atom identification, decides infinite-frame fit. This bound is deliberately inefficient; it avoids relying on an unproved small-cut heuristic.

4.2 Sense and first-order translation

For a fixed finite sign, parsing its decimal names decides the exposed atom clause, and the preceding fit test decides the remaining syntactic condition. At a non-vacuous quantifier, replacing its active free values by names changes token roles; the resulting fit test is made on that named instance. N+ ensures the co-occurring named parameters in an admitted ordinary binder instance are distinct. There are finitely many relevant syntactic role/equality patterns for this one finite input.

Consequently its range is expressible in the ordinary colored frame by sort and inequality conditions, the exposed frame-incidence tests E, and the appropriate computed fit constant. Replace an atom by W, finite N by conjunction of negations, and joint negation over z by

    ¬∃z (Range_B(z,parameters) ∧ B*).

The exposed-atom selection must be by scope, after treating vacuous binders as specified, not merely by checking whether an atom's letters belong to a given set. X52 L3754–3755 itself corrects the older wording of X50 Lemma 3. This qualification is necessary.

For a single finite non-series formula there is an effective finite variable bound—for example its total binder/parameter count after hygienic expansion. The ordinary profile theorem then applies. There is no requirement here to prove the iteration-uniform bound that fails in X52.

4.3 Ordinary profiles remain valid

For q variables and fixed coordinate names, pin the finitely many named units. Record their three R truth bits, named marker truth bits, and remaining marker-color counts capped at q. Anonymous units have a type consisting of their three R bits and capped true/false marker counts; cap the number of units of each type at q.

Maintain a matching of units touched by the at most q current variable values, including units touched by a form value whose target object is not selected. An unused unit of the same type exists because supplies agree below q and are sufficient at the cap. Within a matched unit, an unused marker of a color exists by the same argument. Named markers are already matched separately. The four distinguished objects are fixed. All E and W atoms and equality facts are preserved. Induction on ordinary formulas proves agreement for q variables at arbitrary quantifier depth. The corresponding back-and-forth relation also preserves infinitary Boolean combinations of formulas that actually obey this q-variable bound.

Realizability is effective: below 2q, capacities are finite exact exceptions; at indices i≥2q the attainable anonymous marker-count pairs are precisely

    (r,q), (q,r) for r<q, and (q,q).

The named units use their exact capacities. Finite exceptional-unit assignment is a finite matching problem with exact quotas for supplies below q and lower quotas at q. Infinitely many remaining units can be allocated exactly when a tail-allowed saturated type can absorb the surplus. This is the finite construction given in R2 and reused by X50.

Disposition: the ordinary profile theorem is not the defect found here. It is incorrectly applied by X52 to terms exceeding its stated q-variable bound. A finite representative of a profile need not be a cut of Φ, but it must only be used within the logical fragment for which its adequacy was proved.

4.4 Vacuous N: a notation issue requiring an explicit statement

X51 L3601–3606 says a vacuous existential binder has the body's truth, “likewise for N over z”; X52 L3819–3820 says a vacuous binder is evaluated as its body. If ∃z B is an abbreviation for ¬N_z B, coherence requires, for vacuous z and meaningful B,

    ∃z B = B,          N_z B = ¬B.

The transparent description of values is the singleton B; the N operation still negates it. Reading both expressions literally as B contradicts the existential abbreviation and the N definition. The charitable coherent reading is binder transparency with the outer operation retained. Under that reading X50's finite procedure stands. If literal identity for N_z itself is intended, the source must resolve the inconsistency. This audit does not silently use that identity.

The main counterexample below is unaffected by this issue: all its effective quantifiers are non-vacuous, and from step five the expressly prescribed normal form simply deletes a newly idle existential binder.

5. G*: exact rules relevant to the counterexample and audit

The adopted productions at L3641–3664 provide sorted object, k-ary-form and proposition positions. A series [B,ξ,C] has a hole-free base B and a finite operation context C. Each occurrence has a sorted map on the declared free letters and written names; maps may send names to names or to variables bound above that hole. Bound identities are hygienically freshened. Multiple holes and nested series are allowed. No fresh name strings are manufactured by iteration, and no arbitrary inspection of the filler is allowed.

The written hole exposes its interface image, including identity entries (H1). The closure is computed as in L3535–3547. Generated terms recompute inner closure declarations and remove idle units/vacuous binders (Ht2), L3562–3588 and L3650–3653. Undefined inner-map mergers are excluded. Written series tokens include those of the base/context/declarations and one additional state per propositional letter. Terms are admitted to the value range by their own sense.

These rules are sufficiently explicit to admit and unfold the example in Section 6 without choosing a new production or changing a rule. In particular:

- name-to-name maps are expressly permitted, L3451–3453 and L3645–3646;
- the interface may be empty;
- a form binder whose only written occurrence is at a hole is allowed, L3589–3590;
- no internal series or merger is needed;
- after all names have disappeared from a term, an unused newly introduced binder is deleted by the stipulated normal form.

G* still requires care at the boundaries of a complete implementation. “Per inner-sign occurrence” data in Pi(T), L3803–3808, do not by themselves prove finiteness when the number of occurrences grows; one needs an explicit finite set of pattern types and a quotient justification. Likewise the input promise must be separated from the stronger claim that all illegal future mergers can be decided. These are proof-presentation obligations, not the decisive counterexample below.

6. A legal counterexample to X52's bound and profile theorem

6.1 The input

Write R₁,R₂,R₃,R₄ for Φ's ordinary named binary forms. Set

    B = (∃u)(∃v) [R₁(u,v) ∧ R₂(u,v) ∧ R₃(u,v) ∧ R₄(u,v)].

Let the operation context be

    C[ξ] = (∃p) ξ[ R₁↦R₂, R₂↦R₃, R₃↦R₄, R₄↦p ],

where p is a fresh binary-form binder. Let T₀=B and T_{k+1}=C[T_k] in G* normal form. The tested closed sign is N([B,ξ,C]).

The fixed outer interface V is empty. The closure's name set is {R₁,R₂,R₃,R₄}. The hole writes {R₂,R₃,R₄,p}. The map is sort/arity preserving and has no collision. There are no inner series, no inspection, and no name generation.

Source definition: at L3736–3738, Mov is “the names that some map of the sign, inner series' maps included, sends to a variable.” There is just one written map here, and it sends only R₄ to a variable. Hence Mov={R₄}. The largest template variable width v is 2: B uses u,v; C has just p at its artificial hole atom. Thus X52's L3757–3766 prescribe q=2+1=3.

This uses the literal defined Mov, not an enlarged transitive closure. Reading Mov as all names eventually movable would change the definition and repair this example's accounting; that is a proposed proof correction, not what L3736–3738 says.

6.2 Unfolding

Up to hygienic renaming, the first terms are:

    T₀ = ∃u v [R₁uv ∧ R₂uv ∧ R₃uv ∧ R₄uv]
    T₁ = ∃p₁ ∃u v [R₂uv ∧ R₃uv ∧ R₄uv ∧ p₁uv]
    T₂ = ∃p₂ ∃p₁ ∃u v [R₃uv ∧ R₄uv ∧ p₂uv ∧ p₁uv]
    T₃ = ∃p₃ ∃p₂ ∃p₁ ∃u v [R₄uv ∧ p₃uv ∧ p₂uv ∧ p₁uv]
    T₄ = ∃p₄ ∃p₃ ∃p₂ ∃p₁ ∃u v [p₄uv ∧ p₃uv ∧ p₂uv ∧ p₁uv].

Here ∃u v abbreviates the ordinary nested object quantifiers, not a new tuple-series constructor. At T₄ there are six variables simultaneously free in the displayed matrix. Every later term is an alpha-variant of T₄: the operation acts on names no longer occurring, and its new outer p is vacuous and deleted. Widths are therefore

    2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, ... .

Proved here: X52 Lemma 5's claimed bound 3 is false. At the transition R₃↦R₄, an uncounted name becomes a counted movable name; at the next transition it becomes a variable. Consequently the asserted conservation of “variables plus moved names” at L3759–3762 does not hold for the defined set Mov.

6.3 Every relevant sign and witness has sense

Each T_k's finite pattern consists of distinct active form symbols on the common directed pair (u,v), with a nested prefix. Assign u,v tokens a,b and assign all active form letters/names distinct fresh R-unit tokens. Every atom is a state. Active form binders are different from the names and from each other when required by their scopes. The two object binders are distinct and there are no object names in the original term.

For a successful semantic witness to T₄, choose four distinct true R-forms on the actual pair (a,b). At each partially named prefix keep the active token forms on distinct units above every semantically named index. A named u or v occupies a or b and the remaining object binder occupies the other. No binder/name collision occurs. Once atoms are fully named, their token forms and target forms are disjoint, so hereditary A6s holds. Thus these are genuine C-nv witnesses, not merely ordinary-logic assignments bypassing sense.

The descriptor [B,ξ,C] itself fits: B's four form-name tokens are distinct fresh R-forms on the common pair; p has a fresh token different from those names, and the propositional letter has its stipulated extra fresh state. B's atoms are under its active u,v binders, so the descriptor has no failing exposed named atom. The written hole declarations add exactly the stipulated form/name reservations. Therefore N over this series is a promised input.

6.4 Two infinite worlds with the same q=3 profile

Define W₃ to have exactly the three true states

    R₅(a,b), R₆(a,b), R₇(a,b),

and W₄ to have exactly

    R₅(a,b), R₆(a,b), R₇(a,b), R₈(a,b).

All other states of the infinite frame are false in both worlds. The named units 1–4 have exactly the same data in both worlds. Every anonymous unit i≥5 has zero true markers and at least three false markers. There are only two anonymous unit types:

- (R-bits 1,0,0; marker counts 0,3), with supply 3 in W₃ and 4 in W₄, both capped to 3;
- (R-bits 0,0,0; marker counts 0,3), with infinite supply in both.

Thus the complete profiles specified at L3330–3339, with q=3 and these fixed names, coincide. There are no hidden correlations left unequal in that profile.

6.5 Their series truth values differ

For k<4, T_k still requires at least one of R₁,…,R₄ to be true on its witness pair. Those forms have no true states in either world, so these terms are false. Their signs nevertheless have sense: false fully named states are legitimate propositions; they are not excluded by C-nv.

At T₄, N+ makes the four chosen form values distinct because each remains free in the scope of every later form binder. The only true pair in either world is (a,b). Hence T₄ is true in W₄ and false in W₃. The successful W₄ chain passes the sense checks proved above. Every later term has the same value as T₄.

Therefore

    V(N([B,ξ,C]), W₃)=true,
    V(N([B,ξ,C]), W₄)=false,

despite equality of their prescribed q=3 profiles.

Proved here: the profile-preservation step at L3827–3828 is false on a legal G* sign. The ordinary q-profile theorem has not failed: these terms are outside the asserted q-variable fragment.

The finite representative prescribed at L3340–3342 retains only three units of the saturated true type. Its true-edge reduct has no four-form witness. It therefore does not reproduce W₄'s value of T₄ or this series, although W₄ realizes its profile.

This establishes a failed semantic reduction, not necessarily a wrong final tautology answer on this particular formula: a global algorithm could also encounter other profiles where the series is false. No unverified claim of an end-to-end false-positive validity verdict is needed for the counterexample.

6.6 An arbitrary finite family of failures

Replace four form names by n≥4 and use the map R₁↦R₂↦…↦R_n↦p. Still v=2 and direct |Mov|=1. At step n the term has width n+2. The two worlds with respectively n−1 and n true anonymous R-forms on (a,b) have the same q=3 profile, while the series distinguishes them. This is a uniform mathematical family, not an inference from several tested n.

For each fixed n the orbit stabilizes. The result does not refute existence of an input-dependent finite congruence with a correctly enlarged state space.

7. Consequences for the finite-state construction and nesting

The undercount affects more than the sentence stating a numerical bound:

1. Lemma 5, L3757–3766: width is not bounded by the defined v+|Mov|.
2. Lemma 6, L3773–3774: the promoted-name reservation budget uses the same number. It can undercount simultaneous promotions in generated subterms.
3. Lemma 7, L3809–3823: the truth table varies only FV(T) and Mov∩names(T). A name not directly moved may still need to be varied after passing through another name. The table definition must support that action as well.
4. Theorem, L3824–3833: finite-profile agreement cannot be applied to the generated terms under the wrong bound. Nesting cannot repair a failure already present in a single non-nested series.

The exactness argument for ambient fitting at L3780–3787 is a substantial improvement over X33. With the context's letters and all reserved name tokens fixed, constraints in separate copies communicate through their interfaces and the ambient reservations; their internal binders do not acquire arbitrary disequalities with sibling binders. This correctly addresses the old closed-cycle/closed-edge obstruction. The new counterexample does not challenge that relational idea; it challenges the claimed finite coverage of all roles and truth observations.

7.1 A repair direction, carefully bounded

A safe accounting scheme should include every name that can eventually become a variable through a chain of allowed maps, including those in nested templates. The simplest conservative overapproximation is all names N of the finite specification. One would then use a bound based on v+|N| and parameterize the corresponding name slots in the truth tables, rather than change only the number q in one sentence.

For ordinary ranked hygienic copying this enlarged syntactic bound follows by tracking free variables plus all name occurrences at each node: a letterwise substitution cannot increase the number of distinct images of those entries. A node outside a copied term sees its declared full interface; a node inside a copy inherits that copy's bound identities and the images of its external entries. This proves the required bound for the displayed family and the ordinary ranked context setting. For full G*, the proof must also explicitly cover recomputed inner declarations, all legal mergers, and normalization. Deletion alone cannot increase width, but that observation is not a substitute for specifying which declaration set is counted before each operation.

This is a repair to a proof/state construction, not a demand to change G*, A11, or the adequate notation. It has not been completed into a fully audited corrected decision procedure here. In particular, Pi(T)'s finite pattern encoding, the truth tables' parameterization under all name maps, and the recursive computation for holes within inner operations need a single coherent amended construction.

Once a genuinely finite effective congruence is established, deterministic iteration and eventual periodicity are elementary. They cannot be used to justify the congruence retrospectively. Replacing a series by a bare conjunction of representative term signs would also be insufficient: the written descriptor's token behavior must be retained separately. X52 correctly recognizes this distinction at L3829–3833, but its amended theorem must preserve it.

8. X53: independent verification of the descriptions and invariants

This section does not use X52 or A11. All displayed definitions are ordinary finite formulas. It preserves the own-sign instance rule and the strict token rule.

The definitions at L3914–3924 are:

    St(p,u,v) := p(u,v) ∨ ¬p(u,v)
    Off(p,u,v) := ∃s t [St(p,s,t) ∧ St(p,u,v)]
    M_k(x) := ∃y ∃p₁...p_k ∧_j St(p_j,y,x)
    U_i(x) := M_i(x) ∧ ¬M_{i+1}(x)
    Rf(p,w) := ∃u [St(p,u,w) ∧ Off(p,u,w)]
    Unit_i(w,p) := U_i(w) ∧ Rf(p,w).

The duplicated St guard in Off is essential: it makes u,v occur in the scope and hence excludes their values from s,t. It is not a dispensable tautology under this semantics.

8.1 Values of the frame descriptions

Proved here. At o_i, M_k holds exactly for k≤i: for k≥2 its common source must be h' and its forms are distinct markers; for k=1 the h-source also witnesses it. At a and b it holds for every finite k through the infinitely many R-forms, and it fails at h,h'. Thus U_i picks out exactly o_i. The fresh-star token proof used in the previous G_n audit applies to every positive witness prefix, including arbitrary large k.

Rf(p,o_i) holds precisely for p=R_i. A qualifying p must have a state into o_i and a state on a disjoint object pair. R_i does; a marker does not. The guarded Off definition enforces the disjointness semantically. Every successful R_i chain has a compatible fresh token placement.

8.2 Token placements are not independent-block counts

The broad sentence at L3929–3933, “blocks under different binders share no disequality,” is too compressed if read literally: shared interface letters, names, and nested scopes still constrain them. The following joint placements supply the missing detail for the actual families. Fresh token indices m,n,l_j are distinct where indicated and exceed all finitely many semantic form indices in the checked instance.

| Family / checked instance | A compatible token assignment |
|---|---|
| U_i(w) within HT/TT/FF/MIX | w↦o_m; counting-source binders↦h'; their form binders to sufficiently many f_{m,j}. |
| Rf(p,w), with p,w named | p↦R_m, w↦o_m; u↦h; Off's s,t↦a,b. |
| HT_i | Use the preceding two rows jointly; its additional u-edge uses h,o_m and the same R_m. |
| TT_i, FF_i, MIX_i | Use the same w,p placement; the cycle binders use a,b. They occur in a separate scoped block from Off, so sharing a,b is permitted. |
| OR_{i,j}, i≠j | w,w'↦o_m,o_n; p,q↦R_m,R_n; counting forms on the respective marker units; both cycle tests use the common a,b. |
| MC_{i,k}, inside its named u,w/form prefix | Use u↦a,w↦b and p_j↦R_{l_j}. Each Off block uses its own h,o_{l_j}. All its binders avoid the named a,b token pair. |

The last row matters. It would be wrong to insist that a semantic marker name must have a marker-form token: a form name denoting f_{i,j} can be tokened by R_{l_j}. Projection concerns the displayed named states, not a global isomorphism of the entire denoted form's extension. The negative Off test has a fitting sign even when its semantic range contains no successful disjoint-state witness.

For MC's outer w-instance, U_i(w) can be placed with w↦b and its source↦a using enough R-form tokens. The later u name is not yet present in that checked outer instance. When the u-quantifier is evaluated, its body is its own instance and the U_i sibling is not inside that body. This is precisely where the own-sign range rule must be respected. It prevents an unjustified accumulation of semantic names from discarded siblings.

All fully named successful states can have token forms moved away from their target forms, by Section 3.1. These placements check strict object/form name reservations, shared letters, and hereditary A6s; a claim that independent blocks simply receive arbitrary independent placements would not suffice.

8.3 The four families have their advertised values

Using those sense witnesses and the finite frame analysis:

- HT_i, L3944, is true iff R_i(h,o_i) is true.
- MC_{i,k}, L3945–3946, is true iff at least k of the i marker states of unit i are true. The negative Off condition excludes the R_i h-edge and retains marker forms. Pairwise distinct forms are enforced by N+.
- TT_i/FF_i/MIX_i, L3947–3949, give the two orientation bits up to their simultaneous reversal. Both directed atoms must be meaningful, so the witness pair is {a,b}.
- OR_{i,j}, L3950–3952, tells whether two mixed units have the same orientation. Its common x,y pair is shared between p and q, not independently chosen.

These deductions concern all i and k, not just the units sampled in the ledger's checks.

8.4 A17

Proved here from the verified finite families. Let two worlds agree on every completely general truth. The HT family gives equality of h-state bits unit by unit. All MC thresholds give equality of the finite true-marker counts c_i. TT/FF/MIX give each unit's orientation type. If any unit is mixed, choose one mixed unit i₀; its orientation determines whether to use id or the global swap (a b). Each other mixed unit then matches by OR_{i₀,j}. Nonmixed orientation pairs are already invariant under the swap. In each unit choose a marker permutation taking its true marker set onto the other world's true marker set. The product of these permutations and the one global object swap carries the first world onto the second.

This constructs an automorphism; no effective recovery of an arbitrary infinite world is claimed or needed. Thus A17's model verification is independent of the disputed A11 proof.

9. A16 and its “Both” sense requirement

The o_i descriptions U_i were verified above. The descriptions of h and h' at L3978–3983 distinguish an outgoing form with an off-state from an outgoing one-state form; the h description additionally excludes an in-edge. At h these conditions are true; at h' only the one-state outgoing condition is true; a,b have incoming states and multi-state R-forms; the o_i have no outgoing states. This is direct frame analysis, not an inference from rigidity alone.

For their named instances, a useful token location for x is a. Outgoing-edge tokens use a,b; off-state tokens use h,o_m; the independent incoming test uses b,a with another R-form token. All object binders avoid x's named token a. As always, ν(x) need not equal g(x). Corresponding semantic positive witnesses have fully named target states in the frame; negative branches have no successful unwanted witnesses. The full expressions and their claimed values therefore have sense.

For a,b, take i₀∈S\T as in L3984–3989. The corrected D_a and D_b use U_{i₀}(w), an incoming p-edge to w, and a two-way p-test at x; they deliberately do not add Rf. Place x↦a, w↦o_m, p↦R_m; the incoming-edge binder u uses h; the counting blocks use h' and markers; the reverse-edge binder y uses b. This verifies the crucial named instance without exhausting the pair a,b in a second Off block. Semantically the two-way condition forces p=R_{i₀}, and its asymmetric truth bits select exactly a or b respectively.

For each 5.5321 sentence, one must verify the written doubled description fits; one need not require two distinct named satisfying instances to exist. For U_i use two fresh leaf units. For descriptions requiring the two-way pair, place the two outer bound argument letters at a,b; each copy's inner reverse-edge binder may use the other letter's token because that other outer letter is not free in its local body. The other blocks use fresh units as in Section 8. At this written stage those outer letters are binders, not two ambient names. After instantiation, some doubled ranges may become empty—exactly the known X43 phenomenon. Since the semantic description is true of only one object, the existential doubled assertion is false in any event, and its negation is true. The full uniqueness sign has sense.

Disposition: A16 holds for the selected generic orientation pair, with the ledger's “Both” requirement. The repair from Rf to an incoming-edge test in D_a/D_b is essential and is actually present in revision 58.

10. A18, genericity and foundational assumptions

10.1 Audit of the supplied forcing argument

X53 L3962–3973 assumes a countable transitive M coding the signs and their Borel evaluations. With all h-states and marker states true at χ, any world with the same completely general truths is, by A17, either χ or χ†=(a b)χ*. The latter differs on infinitely many orientation coordinates for a generic pair.

A Borel set coded in M is decided on a neighborhood of a Cohen-generic point among generics: one must not conclude it is constant on that neighborhood for all arbitrary worlds. X53 avoids that error by making the finite-change witness another generic. Swapping S,T and flipping finitely many coordinates preserve genericity over M, since these finite-coordinate operations are coded automorphisms of the forcing. Thus its finite-change witness has the required truth value and is a proper sub-alteration of the infinite difference.

This argument is valid with its coding/model hypotheses. “There exists a countable transitive model of all of set theory” should not be silently treated as an elementary theorem. The following direct version exhibits the needed mathematical content without that stronger-looking formulation.

10.2 A direct Baire-category proof

**Proved here, given the stipulated well-defined countable Borel semantics of finite G* signs.** Restrict worlds to the space X in which all marker and h-states are true and only the two orientation bits at each unit vary. This is a Cantor space. Each proposition determines a Borel subset B_p of X: atoms are clopen, finite Boolean operations preserve Borelness, and the countable named-instance/series ranges are world-independent and give countable Boolean operations. Nested fixed series are evaluated through their finite templates and natural-number iterates; no operation inspects the world to select its range. This Borel statement does not require decidability of tautologyhood.

For each B_p choose an open U_p with B_p△U_p meagre. Such approximations hold for Borel sets: sets admitting an open approximation modulo a meagre set form a sigma algebra containing the open sets (complements introduce only the nowhere-dense boundary, and countable unions preserve meagreness). Enlarge the exceptional set by the boundary of U_p. Let G be the complement of all these exceptional sets, for all countably many propositions, and of all their images under finite coordinate flips and the global orientation swap. This removes only countably many meagre sets. Intersect also with the comeagre set where S\T and T\S are both infinite.

By the Baire theorem, G is nonempty. It is invariant under the specified flips and swap. At a point of G each B_p is locally constant relative to G: membership agrees with U_p, and the point is off its boundary.

Choose χ∈G. If χ† changes p, take a basic neighborhood of χ† on which p is constant relative to G. Change χ on just the finitely many differing coordinates needed to enter that neighborhood. The resulting χ' belongs to G by flip invariance and has p's value at χ†. Its difference from χ is finite and is a proper subset of the infinite difference between χ and χ†. Therefore χ† is not a minimal alteration changing p. A17 excludes every other isomorphic alternative. This proves A18.

This supplies an existence argument for an actual world with the required property. It does not compute χ*, need an A11 oracle, or assert global local constancy of all Borel truth sets. It also makes clear which regularity hypothesis must be retained if the series language is changed in the future.

The series evaluator is an independently implemented positive-existential checker with the actual N+ exclusions and hygienic syntax substitution. It is not a general final-TLP evaluator. Sense and A6s for this fragment are justified separately by the fresh-token proof in Section 6. Pruning only rejects a branch when some atom has no compatible true state; it cannot remove a successful positive existential witness. The infinite worlds used in the proof have no true states outside the explicitly listed finite sets, so enlarging the semantic cut cannot introduce a new successful positive witness.

The A17 computation tests the separating power of the structural invariant tuple, not the interpretation of the TLP formulas defining it. Their interpretation and sense were checked mathematically in Section 8. The orbit computation explicitly permutes markers and optionally swaps a,b globally; it does not independently swap each unit's orientation. This distinction is essential.

No experiment is used as a substitute for the general width/profile counterexample, the infinite automorphism construction, or the Baire argument. The ledger's previous reported random checks cannot exclude the name-chain family, which they did not establish as covered.
