[Section: bounded-kernel]
Bounded kernel and flat-series proof

TLP X52 — bounded repair attempt

31 October 2026. Independent follow-up to Revision-58 audit and original counterexample [section revision58-audit].

Executive disposition

Partial repair; full A11 certification remains UNRESOLVED.

The direct-Mov bound is replaced here by a bound counting all names of the finite specification. A provenance argument supplies the corresponding syntactic width invariant. An independent finite token construction supplies ambient-aware fitting tables. With all names parameterized, these give a finite effective contextual congruence for non-nested series, under the coherent binder-transparency convention specified below.

The argument is not extended by assertion to all G*. The remaining obligation is a finite, effective summary of normalized nested descriptors, preserved when holes occur in inner bases or operations. In particular, the ledger's per-occurrence Pi data have not been proved to have the claimed finite deterministic update. A bounded immediate-merge summary is proved here, but that is weaker than a summary preserved by closure recomputation and nesting.

No new counterexample to A11 is established. No authoritative document is edited. The repair changes proof bounds and proposed states, not the stipulated grammar or semantic rules. This attempt stops at the stated obstruction rather than treating a plausible completion as certification.

1. Sources, conventions and exact scope

Physical ledger lines refer to C:\Users\ogmb\Downloads\TLP Ledger.md, revision 58, SHA-256:

    c64649c2058e6da7dcdd34eb3bed0e3c7db0a63cb517978a72dff894b7033c23

Relevant provisions are X50's fitting recursion, L3310–3320; X51's name maps, L3451–3453; fixed interfaces and no name generation, L3486–3493; nesting, L3494–3497; closure and H1, L3535–3547; normalization and mergers, L3562–3588; the grammar, L3641–3664; and X52, L3730–3833. The prior audit documents the four-name counterexample and the ordinary world-profile theorem.

Labels used below: Source for adopted rules, Proved here for a mathematical deduction, Conditional for an explicitly stated semantic convention, Observation for finite computation, and Open for a missing proof.

Conditional convention, not a silent amendment. A vacuous value description has the singleton value B. Thus a vacuous existential has B's value, while joint negation over that description has value not-B. This is the coherent reading of transparency used in the prior audit. Reading both existential and joint negation literally as identity would conflict with their defining relationship. The present work does not resolve that wording by changing N.

Source. Token placement g and semantic assignment nu are separate. Named tokens need not occupy their referents. X50's lexical fitting recursion permits sibling bound letters to reuse tokens through legal alphabetic variants; every name of the checked sign reserves its token against every same-sort binder. This is the rule being analyzed, not a new global fresh-token requirement for all binder occurrences.

Scope of the positive semantic theorem. A flat series has bracket-free base and operation context. Multiple mapped holes, name-to-name maps, name-to-variable maps, repeated atoms, and identifications are allowed. Finite Boolean and quantifier combinations of such series are also covered when no bracket lies inside another bracket. The full G language permits more than this fragment; restricting the positive theorem does not restrict G itself.

Definitions are expanded before computing the finite specification, as X47 requires. Expansion must be finite and hygienic under the adopted definition rules. No claim here licenses recursive macro definitions.

2. A corrected syntactic bound

Let N be the set of all names in the finite expanded specification, including names in declarations, and let n=|N|. Count sorts separately if useful; a combined bound is sufficient. For each original template node t, compute its free variable identities using H1 at every hole: the hole writes the full image of the declared closure, including identities. Include binder-body bags so that an active binder and the other free letters of its body are counted together. Let v be the maximum variable count of these bags over all bases and operation templates, outer and inner. Put

    Q = max(1, v+n).

This definition uses the written finite specification, not a search through generated terms. Closure is a finite least-fixed-point computation on the written words. Sources of map declarations are scope-inert; their images, rather than their textual source spellings, determine free-variable bags.

For a node u, define its augmented live set

    L(u) = FV(u) union Names(u).

Here FV is relative to u: a letter bound above u is free at u, while a binder strictly inside u does not contribute unless one is looking at its body. Written series nodes use the adopted written scopes and H1 words. Binder-body bags also include the binder itself where needed. This is a lexical width, not the total number of binders in the entire sign.

Proposition 1 — provenance bound

Proved here. Every legal finite syntactic unfolding of the given templates, with hygienic copying and Ht2 normalization, has augmented live bags of size at most Q. Consequently its variable width is at most Q. This assertion concerns syntax and does not decide the truth of a nested series.

Proof. Initially each bag contains at most v variable identities and n name identities. Track the origin of every retained syntax node through copying and substitution.

At a node inside a copied filler, freshening changes its locally bound identities bijectively. Every external letter and name has one image under the applied map. An original name may acquire a variable image, but it was already counted in the augmented live set. Identifications can reduce the cardinality of the image; they cannot increase it. Internal binders are fresh and are not targets of the external map. Hence a copied bag contains at most as many identities as its ancestor bag.

At a node belonging to the receiving context, replacing a hole cannot introduce an external word absent from its H1 interface image: the filler's free letters and names are contained in that hole's declared closure. The union at an ancestor node is therefore contained in the union already supplied by the full hole images and the context's own words. Internal binders of a filler do not become free at such an ancestor. Thus receiving-context bags do not grow beyond their template bags.

This argument also applies when the receiving hole is in an inner base or operation. Its declaration includes the image of the enclosing series' closure by L3535–3538. Internal hole declarations are recomputed after substitution. For legal maps, taking the image of the old closed declaration gives a closed set containing the substituted generators: each map edge is transported to its corresponding edge. Its least closure is consequently a subset of that image. Ht2 then deletes idle units and vacuous binders and leaves every retained scope unchanged, L3571–3574. Neither operation increases a bag. Undefined map mergers are excluded by the statement's legality hypothesis; no resolution rule for them is presumed.

Induction on the finite sequence of unfoldings proves the bound. This includes arbitrary interleavings of finite outer and inner unfolding steps. It is not an induction claiming that generated nesting depth stays bounded. QED.

Limits. The proposition is not a membership algorithm for G*. It does not decide whether every future step avoids an undefined merger. Nor does a width bound alone imply a semantic congruence.

Why this repairs the exhibited failure

In the n-name chain from the prior audit, v=2 and Q=n+2. Its nth term has n simultaneously active form variables and two object variables, so width n+2. The bound is attained. The original direct-Mov count gives 3 irrespective of n and is false.

One can seek a smaller backward closure of movable names through the maps, but that optimization is unnecessary for this proof. In particular, this report does not silently redefine the ledger's Mov and retain its old theorem label.

3. Uniform finite token resources

This section removes an avoidable dependence on unbounded token-unit capacities. It does not replace semantic referents with tokens.

Let Omega have four hubs a,b,h,h', countably many leaves u_i, one R_i per leaf with states R_i(a,b), R_i(b,a), R_i(h,u_i), and countably many marker forms per leaf with states f_{i,j}(h',u_i). Ignore truth colors. Omega is an auxiliary fitting structure, not the proposed TLP model.

For an integer b, let H_b have the same hubs, b leaves, their b R-forms, and b marker forms per leaf, with the same state incidences. H_b is also auxiliary; its uniform capacities need not be an initial segment of Phi.

Proposition 2 — fitting transfer

Proved here. For any finite relational object/form token pattern, unrestricted fitting into Phi is equivalent to fitting into Omega. For a family of these lexical patterns whose constraint bags, after ambient name reservations are added, contain at most b identities, fitting into Omega is equivalent to fitting into H_b. One may enlarge b without changing this conclusion.

The extra state assigned to each propositional letter by X51 (7b) is handled separately. It has no prescribed incidence with the letter's exposed object/form words. After a finite relational witness is chosen, assign these finitely many letters distinct fresh R-unit states, avoiding all existing token and named-target states. Phi and Omega always supply them. Their possibly growing number is not forced into H_b. Thus eliminating these unconstrained state choices preserves whole-sign fit, but a claim that the entire written sign, including arbitrarily many globally distinct propositional-letter states, embeds in this one H_b would be unjustified.

Proof, first equivalence. Phi embeds into Omega unit by unit. A finite Omega witness uses finitely many units and finitely many markers per used unit. Send these units injectively to distinct Phi units with sufficiently large indices, retaining the four hubs and injecting the used markers. Every state and every required inequality is preserved.

Proof, second equivalence. The only data about a tuple of at most b token identities are: exact hubs; object/form sort and role; which identities touch the same unit; which marker identities coincide; and equality. Match these data between Omega and H_b. When extending a partial match with fewer than b selected identities, a newly touched unit can be chosen unused on the other side: fewer than b units are already touched. If a new marker is required in a touched unit, fewer than b markers in that unit are already selected. Its R-form and leaf, if selected later, are uniquely determined by the unit. Thus the match has the b-pebble back-and-forth extension property for the incidence and equality vocabulary.

The fitting recursion in X50 is a bounded-bag existential constraint formula: atoms impose incidence; Boolean combinations of proposition signs impose conjunction of their fitting constraints; a binder existentially chooses its token subject to the lexical inequalities; all ambient names remain in the bags. Sibling internal choices are independent once their boundary is fixed. By reusing variable labels between branches, this formula uses at most b variable labels. Induction on that finite formula, using the extension property, transfers its truth between Omega and H_b. Equivalently, its constraint tree can be evaluated directly by finite boundary tables. QED.

This argument handles repeated atoms: an assignment fixes the same tuple, hence the same state, at every occurrence of the same atom. It does not multiply the token demand for repetitions. It also handles shared token units, because the boundary records unit sharing rather than just counts.

For the present specification a deliberately loose budget is

    b = 4Q + 2n + 8.

Ordinary bags have at most Q live identities. A named instance adds at most Q active parameter-name reservations; at most n original names can be reserved from outside the current component. Even allowing a further Q slots for boundary role bookkeeping stays below this b. Anonymous reservations are bounded by the number of active named parameters, not by the total number of binders in an unfolded sign. All names of an ambient context in the fixed finite specification are included in N, even when absent from the filler.

A6s. After obtaining a finite witness, relocate its used units to distinct Phi units beyond every semantic name index in the checked instance. Named target states then have forms disjoint from the relocated token-state forms. The finite token-to-target graph is acyclic. This proves existence of an admissible projection whenever the atom clause and fitting requirements hold. It does not assert that arbitrary token placements are admissible. The construction uses concrete finite instance names, whose decimal coordinates are available under X49.

Boundary qualification. An externally fixed token assignment is represented by its full finite type in Omega/H_b, not by its actual small Phi unit index. This is legitimate for existential whole-sign fitting, which chooses and relocates the entire finite witness. It would be false for a different task that fixes a token to a particular capacity-one Phi unit and forbids relocating it. Semantic names do not impose that token anchoring here.

4. The repaired flat-series congruence

4.1 Finite observations

Fix a flat series system and the finite budgets above. Use a finite pool of Q variable slots, the original names N, and Q fresh parameter-name slots, with sorts. A role substitution maps each exposed identity of a term to this pool, respecting sorts. Include non-injective substitutions: coincident semantic values must be represented by the same name, not by distinct names with equal referents. Bound identities inside the copied term remain hygienically fresh.

For each such substitution, retain:

1. The exact sets of occurring free letters and names.
2. The set J of exposed atoms, after removal/transparency of vacuous binders. J is a subset of a finite set of binary atoms over the exposed slots. Nonbinary atoms cannot fit Phi.
3. For every ambient name-presence set and every assignment of its names and the exposed slots to H_b, whether that assignment extends to a fitting placement of the internal bound letters. Name injectivity and binder exclusions are tested explicitly. The same slot serving different roles in different entries is intentional.
4. For each realizable world profile at cap b, each relevant tuple in its finite representative M_P, and each role substitution, a sense/value bit and a truth bit when the instance has sense.

The fourth entry uses semantic assignments in M_P; the third entry uses token assignments in H_b. They are never identified. To evaluate a binder's range, use the body's own named-instance fitting test, its exposed-atom incidence test in M_P, and N+ against the names and other free values of that body. Ambient reservations from an enclosing token check are not imported into that semantic range check.

Each factor is finite. The profile list is effective under the ordinary profile construction audited previously: exact named exceptions, capped true/false marker supplies, orientation bits, capped unit supplies, and finite exceptional-capacity realizability checks. The larger cap b is harmless. The finite representative is not used as a token structure.

For a finite bracket-free term, these tables are computable by exhaustive finite recursion. Efficiency is not claimed. The construction does not inspect an unbounded list of generated terms to define its state space.

Proposition 3 — flat contextual congruence

Proved here, conditional only on the stated transparency convention and the adopted X50 fitting semantics. Equality of the above states is preserved by every permitted bracket-free context from the fixed finite specification, including its declared maps and normal-form deletion. The successor induces a computable deterministic function on states.

Proof. For an atom, all required information is explicit. At a finite truth-function node, combine truth bits by the specified Boolean function. To compute fit, fix the entire boundary and ambient reservation assignment; each child must accept its restricted assignment. Their internal binders can be chosen independently under the adopted lexical token rule. This uses acceptance relations, not standalone yes/no fitting summaries.

At a binder, occurrence sets decide whether it is vacuous. If not, the fitting table existentially chooses a token avoiding the other live same-sort letters and every reserved name. Its semantic table ranges over the finite semantic structure with the own-instance fitting and incidence filter and N+. These filters are available from the child's fitting, occurrence and exposed-atom tables. If vacuous, apply transparency with the surrounding truth operation retained.

At a mapped hole, compose its letter map with the current role substitution. Bound identities of the filler are freshened; any coincidence among external images is already an entry of the role tables. A name sent to a bound variable no longer imposes a global name reservation unless that variable is itself promoted in the current instance check. A name sent through several intermediate names is still handled because all names have entries. An ambient name absent from the filler is still reserved through the ambient table.

By structural induction on the fixed bracket-free context, equal child states give equal resulting tables. The normal form in this fragment deletes vacuous binders, whose occurrence status and effect have just been accounted for. There are no inner hole declarations to recompute. Every operation used in the induction is a finite computation, so the resulting transition depends only on the input state and is deterministic. QED.

This proves compositionality before using periodicity. It also explains why merely increasing q in the old tau definition is insufficient: its name parameters and role/reservation tables must be enlarged consistently.

Corollary — decidability of the flat fragment

Proved here under the same convention. Iterate the computed transition from the base state until a state repeats. Because the state space is finite, this terminates. At each profile and parameter tuple, the series' joint negation is true precisely when no state on the finite preperiod or cycle contributes an admitted true term. The written descriptor's own fitting and atom clause are checked separately from those term values.

The width bound and ordinary profile back-and-forth apply to every generated finite term, including the range-incidence tests. Thus agreement on profiles preserves each term's sense/value condition and truth, and therefore the countable joint negation. No bound on the number of terms is inferred from finite testing. Finite outer Boolean/quantifier constructors use the same tables and own-instance filtering. This gives a decision procedure on promised meaningful inputs in the flat fragment.

This is a fragment theorem, not Phi |= A11 for all G*. Nor does it establish one finite quotient uniform over arbitrarily many new context names. The quotient is built for each fixed finite input specification; a newly enlarged specification requires a correspondingly enlarged finite state space.

5. What can be proved about inner-map mergers

The statement “one record per inner occurrence” is not by itself a finiteness proof: the number of occurrences may grow. There is, however, a finite summary for an immediate, more limited question.

Proposition 4 — immediate consistency patterns

Proved here. Fix an already written finite term T, with exposed alphabet L=FV(T) union Names(T). For each existing inner map f, restrict its domain to the closure entries belonging to L. Record each image as either an exposed word of L or a hidden bound identity; for hidden images retain only their equality partition and sorts. Take the set of these records, discarding duplicate records.

There are finitely many possible records for bounded |L|, independently of how many inner occurrences T contains. This set decides whether an outer letter map mu produces an inconsistent identification in any of those existing inner maps, before any separate deletion of entries.

Proof. The outer map cannot identify two distinct hidden binders or identify a hidden binder with an external word: freshening and the scope restriction prohibit that. Therefore only two distinct exposed source entries can newly collide. Their collision is inconsistent precisely when

    mu(a)=mu(b), but mu_extended(f(a)) != mu_extended(f(b)).

The extension acts as mu on exposed images and as the unchanged, fresh hidden identity on hidden images. The record contains exactly the equality information needed for this test. At most |L| hidden images occur in a record, so equality partitions give finitely many records. A conflict in any occurrence is equivalent to a conflict in some member of the record set; multiplicity is irrelevant to this immediate question. QED.

What this does not prove. It is not a transition theorem for normalized Pi. After plugging into an inner base or operation, the least closure and the retained declarations must be recomputed. A record of the existing restricted map does not itself specify which sources remain reachable in the normalized descriptor or how its nested descendants' summaries are to be updated. The argument also does not decide the universal promise that all future generated terms have defined maps.

One must not use Proposition 4 as though it supplied these missing statements. It is useful to separate the finite immediate merger test from the stronger claim the ledger makes at L3803–3808.

6. The exact stopping point for full G*

X52 L3830–3833 says an inner orbit can be recomputed from the outer state and that the computation terminates by finite nesting. This requires a theorem about states, not just syntactic permission to nest.

For example a permitted outer context can have the shape

    C[xi] = N([xi, eta, D[eta]]).

Successive outer terms can have increasing written nesting depth. If the outer hole is in the inner operation instead, the operation whose orbit is being computed changes with the substituted term. Therefore “the input is finite” is not, by itself, a decreasing measure for the proposed recursive evaluation of generated terms. This observation is not an undecidability proof: a finite algebra of operation transformers could still handle it.

Missing lemma — normalized nested extension

Open. For each fixed finite G* specification, construct an effective finite extension K of the flat state above, with the following properties:

1. It determines occurrence sets, exposed atoms, and all ambient-role fitting tables of the normalized written descriptor.
2. It determines the legal induced declaration maps after H1 closure recomputation and Ht2 deletion, or supplies enough information to propagate the relevant legality promise without assuming a membership algorithm.
3. Every permitted fixed context, including holes in an inner base or operation, induces a computable function K -> K, independent of the representative term.
4. The inner series evaluation derived from that function agrees with C-nv-filtered operational term values at every relevant profile and parameter assignment. Written descriptor fit is retained separately.

A proof must give the finite encoding and its update rules and justify the semantic correspondence by an induction or other well-founded argument. It cannot invoke eventual periodicity until representative independence is established. It also cannot justify a finite encoding merely by retaining unboundedly many “per-occurrence” records.

Propositions 1–3 supply the width, token resources and non-nested kernel for this lemma. Proposition 4 supplies one bounded component of a possible legality summary. They do not prove the lemma. No counterexample to every possible finite extension is known from this attempt.

This is the precise remaining obstruction to the proposed repair route. It is not claimed to be logically necessary for every conceivable decision procedure for A11; a different method could avoid a finite contextual quotient.

7. Computational checks

Run, from the report directory:

    node audit_X52_repair.js

Only Node's built-in modules are used. Output is written to audit_X52_repair_results.json. The checker is deliberately restricted to syntactic substitution and immediate map consistency. It is not a full G* parser, nested normalizer, or truth evaluator.

Observations, all assertions passed:

- Name chains with 1 through 12 names: the nth term has width n+2; every tested augmented live set satisfies v+n.
- 120 generated bracket-free contexts, seed 20261031, with one or two mapped holes, name-to-name and name-to-variable maps, identifications, and deletion of vacuous binders: 720 term checks passed the enlarged bound. The direct-Mov bound failed in 114 checked terms.
- 625 immediate map-consistency cases: all maps from three exposed sources to three exposed and two hidden images, tested against all five equality partitions of the three exposed sources. The record test agrees with the direct quotient-map consistency test.

These counts support debugging only. Proposition 1 is proved by provenance, Proposition 2 by back-and-forth, Proposition 3 by structural composition, and Proposition 4 by the explicit equality criterion. The experiments establish none of the unresolved nested claims.

8. Proposed corrections and certification consequences

Proof corrections, without changing the frozen semantics:

- Replace X52's direct-Mov width argument, L3757–3766, by augmented live-set accounting over all names. Specify the template bags and H1 images explicitly.
- Replace the reservation budgets and truth-table name parameters, L3773–3774 and L3809–3823, consistently. Merely changing the scalar q is insufficient.
- Retain exact ambient-name and role information. Preserve the distinction between the finite auxiliary token structure H_b and the finite semantic profile representative M_P.
- Restrict the currently justified periodicity theorem to the flat fragment. Mark the full nested theorem, L3824–3833, unproved pending the normalized nested extension lemma.
- Separate immediate finite merger testing from the stronger assertions about normalized Pi transitions and G* membership.

Semantic wording requiring adjudication: make the vacuous-N convention explicit. A clarification preserving joint negation is not the same as adding a new identity rule for N. If the source intended the latter, the conflict must be resolved before relying on even the conditional fragment theorem.

Status: the known counterexample to the printed bound is repaired at the syntactic level, and a finite congruence is justified for non-nested series. Full Phi/A11 and the thirteen-axiom model certificate remain unproved. A failure of the nested proof route would still not by itself refute A11 or the consistency of the axioms.

No thaw is performed or demanded by these proof corrections: the revised budget does not alter names, constructors, token rules, ranges, or truth conditions. Any decision to restrict G* to the flat fragment would, in contrast, change the system and is not proposed as a way to obtain the desired full certificate.

The bounded attempt ends here. The next admissible claim of full certification needs the finite normalized nested extension lemma, not another batch of finite examples.



[Section: nested-draft]
Nested construction: historical draft

TLP X52 — normalized nested-series extension

31 October 2026. Independent follow-up to Bounded kernel and flat-series proof [section bounded-kernel].

Executive verdict

The normalized-nesting obstacle admits the finite-state construction below. The construction replaces the proposed per-occurrence Pi list with a table over all bounded external letter substitutions, including an undefinedness flag. Existing copied descriptors commute with legal substitution; newly constructed descriptors compute their closures from the substituted fillers' finite occurrence sets. Inner operations are interpreted as functions on a fixed finite carrier, rather than evaluated by recursively expanding their filler terms.

This yields a conditional A11 theorem for revision 58's G*, using the repaired all-name bound and the fitting/profile kernel established in the preceding reports. The remaining explicit semantic condition is the coherent interpretation of vacuous N: the value description becomes a singleton, and N still negates it. It is not a theorem under the incompatible reading that both vacuous existential quantification and vacuous joint negation are identity operations.

Accordingly:

- Nested extension: proved below for the stated kernel and scope-preserving, well-defined substitution rules.
- Phi/A11 under the coherent transparency reading: the resulting finite decision procedure is specified and justified below.
- An unconditional certificate for every reading of the current wording: not issued. The vacuous-N wording still requires explicit disposition. No semantic change is made here.
- All thirteen axioms: this work supplies the previously missing A11 argument under that reading; it does not replace the separate verifications and qualifications for the other axioms in the full revision-58 audit.

This is a mathematical construction, not a claim that a complete G* implementation has been run. The accompanying executable checks test two algebraic lemmas only.

1. Sources and inherited results

Physical ledger line numbers refer to C:\Users\ogmb\Downloads\TLP Ledger.md, SHA-256

    c64649c2058e6da7dcdd34eb3bed0e3c7db0a63cb517978a72dff894b7033c23

The relevant source rules are:

- X49's adequate effective notation and revised A11, L3194–3201.
- X50's literal atom clause, own-instance ranges, and lexical fitting recursion, L3285–3327.
- G*'s fixed interfaces, absence of name generation, and nested holes, L3486–3497.
- The no-inspection rule, L3498–3502.
- Least closures, scope-inert sources, and full hole images H1, L3531–3547.
- Ht2 normalization and the prohibition on undefined inner-map mergers, L3562–3588.
- Binder transparency, L3601–3606; instance behavior, L3626–3634; and the grammar, L3641–3664.
- The disputed X52 finite-state construction, L3757–3833.

The preceding bounded-repair report proves the following kernel results; they are premises of the extension theorem here, not new source claims:

K1. Width. After finite definition expansion, let N contain every name in the specification, n=|N|, and let v count maximum template variable bags with full H1 images. Put Q=max(1,v+n). Every legal finite unfolding has augmented live bags of at most Q letters, counting names as well as variables.

K2. Token tables. Bounded bags and ambient name reservations admit exact finite acceptance relations in the auxiliary uniform token structure H_b, for b=4Q+2n+8. Propositional-letter states are assigned separately on fresh units. H_b is not a semantic world representative. Relocation of a whole finite witness in Phi enforces hereditary A6s without fixing tokens to referents.

K3. Ordinary semantic tables. At each realizable b-profile P, a finite semantic representative M_P supports the ordinary sense/range/truth computation with exact named exceptions, N+, C-nv, and the literal exposed-atom clause. The profile matching has the bounded-variable back-and-forth extension property.

K4. Ordinary composition. Occurrence sets, exposed-atom sets, ambient fitting tables, and sense/truth tables parameterized by all names compose effectively under finite truth functions, ordinary binders, and letter maps. Occurrence sets decide vacuity. Coincident values are treated as identified names, not as distinct name strings sharing a referent. For the explicit N() exception, retain root/component mode and token-state presence as described in Section 3.2; the earlier table description did not spell out these finite flags.

The extension is relative to those kernel results and their stated transparency convention. In particular, it does not revive X52's false direct-Mov bound, or silently revert to the original J-N input requirement.

Labels below distinguish proved here, construction, conditional theorem, computational observation, and source ambiguity.

2. Closure naturality: the missing normalization fact

Consider a finite word set A, generator set S, and a finite family of maps f_j. Map targets may include locally bound words. Such words are fresh relative to external substitutions; terminal targets need not have outgoing map edges. Let Cl_f(S) be the least set containing S and closed under the applicable map edges.

Let rho act on the external words and act bijectively on freshened internal bound words. Assume the maps descend to well-defined maps bar-f_j on the image words:

    bar-f_j(rho(a)) = rho(f_j(a)).                         (1)

For partial maps, the domain is respected: rho does not merge an internal terminal word with a source word. In G*, maps are total on the declared interface and names, and hygiene prevents the forbidden collision with a private bound word. If two source entries are identified, (1) is exactly the consistency condition that their resulting images agree. No convention for resolving an inconsistent merger is supplied.

Lemma 1 — least closures commute with legal maps

Proved here.

    rho(Cl_f(S)) = Cl_bar-f(rho(S)).                       (2)

Proof. Every finite path of applicable map edges from a generator maps, by (1), to a path from its image generator. This gives the left-to-right inclusion. Conversely, start with the image of a generator and follow a path in the quotient. At each step choose the already reached source preimage. Equation (1) takes its successor to the required quotient successor. The domain condition makes this step applicable. Induction on path length gives the opposite inclusion. Every element of a least closure is reached by a finite path. QED.

Equation (2) applies simultaneously to the family of maps of one bracket, not merely to one map at a time. It also applies when a name becomes a variable or two external names merge, provided (1) remains well defined. Fresh internal binders are not merged with external words.

Lemma 2 — normalization of an existing copy commutes

Proved here. If T is already normalized and rho is a legal external letter map, its existing inner declarations after substitution are exactly the corresponding images, with duplicate word entries removed. No independent list of inner occurrences is needed to determine the effect of the map on T's observed behavior.

Proof. Apply Lemma 1 at each inner bracket. Its generators are its free words/names outside local holes and the stipulated images contributed by enclosing holes. These generators transform letterwise. H1 then writes precisely the images of the recomputed closure. Removing the bracket's locally bound words from the external interface commutes with rho, since those words are fresh and are not external targets.

A retained occurrence of an internal bound variable remains an occurrence of that fresh variable: external substitutions do not target or remove it. Removing duplicate external words cannot remove a private bound variable. Hence a non-vacuous internal binder remains non-vacuous. An already vacuous binder, when a written base retains one, has the stipulated transparent behavior. Ht2 only deletes idle declaration entries and vacuous binders and never moves a retained scope. Thus existing normalized copies require only the induced external substitution, not a structural reanalysis by the receiving context. QED.

This does not say that every newly created descriptor keeps its old declaration. When an outer filler is placed in an inner base or operation, the receiving descriptor's generators must be recomputed from that filler's actual occurrence set. That is a finite, local computation, dealt with below. The distinction between an existing copied descriptor and a newly constructed receiving descriptor is essential.

Consequence for the former Pi objection

The bounded report correctly did not prove a finite update for the proposed list of per-occurrence patterns. That exact encoding is unnecessary. A complete table of external substitution outcomes stores the effect of legal substitutions on a filler as a whole. It can also record that a substitution is undefined. Lemmas 1–2 show why future contexts cannot inspect some additional hidden normalization history of a legal copy.

This consequence relies on the no-inspection rule and scope-preserving Ht2. Prefix merging, syntax-sensitive operations, or a new rule resolving undefined maps would require a different argument.

3. The finite carrier

3.1 Ports are bookkeeping, not new object names

At each syntax boundary use local canonical ports for its at most Q exposed words. A port records sort and whether it is a variable, an original name, or an active parameter name. These port identifiers are not added to the language. The finite set N contains names absent from a particular filler but present elsewhere in its allowed contexts.

Use finite pools of variable and parameter-name ports large enough for the K1/K2 budgets. Tables include every sort-preserving external map into these pools, with all identification patterns. Internal binders are handled by local fresh ports and boundary restriction; no claim is made that a whole unfolded sign can be printed with globally only Q variable spellings. Local boundary charts are sufficient.

3.2 Row contents

For every external substitution row rho, record:

1. Definedness. Whether the transformed expression has well-defined declared maps, including every generated term of its inner series. This is syntactic admissibility, not sense. A meaningfulness failure must not be confused with an undefined map.
2. Occurrence data. Its normalized exposed words and name identities, with their roles and sorts.
3. Exposed atoms. The finite set J selected by the literal atom clause after the prescribed treatment of vacuity.
4. Token acceptance. For every allowed ambient name-reservation set and boundary assignment into H_b, the exact extension-to-fit bit. This includes names absent from the filler.
5. Semantic observations. For every realizable b-profile P and parameter assignment in M_P, the own-instance sense bit and, where meaningful, the truth bit. Assignment equalities first induce the appropriate name-identification row.

Also retain token-state presence and root/component mode. X51 L3591–3592 permits N() as a true component but refuses it as a standalone sign. A table that simply discards its value whenever standalone sense fails would lose that case. Store its component observation separately; the own-value filter of a series still uses standalone proposition sense. Token-state presence is the disjunction of the children's presence flags for ordinary constructors, true at an elementary atom and at a written bracket's propositional-letter state. Bound object/form slots alone are not elementary states. These are finite compositional flags implementing the existing exception, not a new supply of token states or a change to N(). This addition is a precision correction to the preceding flat-state description.

An undefined row has an explicit sentinel, rather than an invented truth value. Rows not meaningful but syntactically defined still retain their occurrence and token information. A series may have no meaningful terms and nonetheless have a meaningful written descriptor and true joint negation.

There are finitely many rows and entries. Take K to be the full finite product of these finite entry sets, with finite interface tags and an error tag for budget violations. Many elements of K need not be realizable by a sign. Defining the transition on this finite product does not presuppose a decision procedure for realizability. Only its correctness on actual generated states matters; K1 guarantees no budget error on the promised legal input and its legal substitutions.

Important: definedness entries are not an oracle hidden in the construction. Section 4 gives their computation together with the other entries. There is no unbounded scan through actual terms in order to initialize them.

3.3 Letter maps act by reindexing rows

For external maps mu and rho, the row of the copied filler is selected by the composite rho after mu, with canonical port renaming. An undefined row remains undefined. For a defined row, Lemmas 1–2 justify using that stored row rather than revisiting the filler's syntax.

The all-name parameterization is indispensable here. A name that reaches a variable only through several name-to-name substitutions is still present in the table's domain. This is the repair missing from the original tau at L3809–3823.

4. A structural compiler for nested brackets

An expression with free propositional holes is compiled with an environment Gamma assigning a K-value to each free hole. Object/form maps at hole occurrences select the corresponding rows of that value. The compiler walks the finite written expression, never the syntax of an expression represented by an environment value.

Ordinary constructors use K4. The new case is N over a bracket [B,x,C]. Holes belonging to enclosing series have K-values in Gamma. The locally bound propositional hole x is treated in two different modes.

4.1 Written-descriptor mode

First compute the finite local closure L of the bracket under the source rule. Contributions from an enclosing hole use its substituted occurrence set from Gamma. The bracket's own x-holes are symbolic interface occurrences: they write mu_j(L), not a selected term of the series.

This is a finite least-fixed-point calculation over the local written word pool. Incoming occurrence sets are bounded by K1; each outgoing map and its binder scope are part of the finite context syntax. H1 ensures all potentially needed target words are already in that pool. Recompute the receiving descriptor's declarations, then delete vacuous binders as Ht2 prescribes for a produced term. A written initial base can retain transparent vacuous binders; K2/K4 give their stipulated behavior.

To compute the written fitting and exposed-atom data, an x-hole contributes its word occurrences and their token slots, but no elementary atom incidence. The extra state for x is supplied separately on a fresh R-unit; repeated occurrences of the same propositional letter use that same fresh state. This is the adopted written-token rule, not a choice of a truth value for x. Use K4 on B and this displayed C. No truth information from the following orbit replaces the descriptor's own tokens.

Check that the local maps descend under the current external row: equal source words must have equal resulting images. An inconsistent merger marks that row undefined. A context may not repair it by choosing one of the conflicting images.

4.2 Value-orbit mode

Compile the base and compile the operation as a function on K:

    k0 = Compile(B, Gamma),
    F(k) = Compile(C, Gamma[x := k]), with the required term normalization.

The expression C is a proper syntactic component of the current bracket. If C contains an inner bracket, that bracket is compiled by the same rule on its own proper syntactic components. A supplied k is a finite table: the compiler does not recurse into the syntax that produced k.

Enumerate the orbit

    k0, F(k0), F^2(k0), ...

until an entire K-state repeats. This is a finite computation because K was fixed before the compiler was defined. It is not yet a semantic claim about actual terms; the substitution theorem below supplies that claim.

For a row rho, its series-definedness bit is true exactly when the local descriptor maps are defined and every state on this finite orbit has a defined rho-row. Undefinedness in an unused alternative row does not poison the current row. All possible rows remain stored because later substitution may request one of them.

For a defined row and a semantic assignment alpha, put

    V_series(rho,P,alpha)
      = AND over orbit states k of
          NOT(S_value(k,rho,P,alpha) AND V_value(k,rho,P,alpha)).       (3)

The series sign's own sense comes from written-descriptor mode. Equation (3) uses each term's own sense; it does not filter by the descriptor's fit or by ambient reservations inherited from an enclosing token check. If no state supplies a meaningful term, the value is true.

Its output K-value combines this semantic table with the written descriptor's occurrence, atom and token tables. It does not replace the bracket by a printed conjunction of representative terms.

4.3 Why this computation terminates

Proved here. Induct on the size of the finite compiler input expression. Ordinary cases invoke the compiler only on proper subexpressions. At a bracket, compiling its base and each evaluation of its operation invokes it on proper subexpressions. The orbit loop makes at most |K|+1 such evaluations before repetition is detected. Nested loops may be enormous, but every recursive compiler call decreases syntax size. Looking up or transforming an environment table is not a recursive call on its represented syntax. Therefore compilation terminates.

This is the missing termination argument. Generated terms may have unbounded nesting depth. Nothing in this argument assumes otherwise.

5. Substitution and operational correctness

5.1 A well-founded reference semantics

For completeness, infinite term enumeration does not require an unexplained recursive truth definition. Assign countable ordinal bounds to finite expressions with propositional holes. Give an atom rank 1; use the maximum child rank plus 1 for ordinary constructors. Hole ranks are parameters. For a bracket with rank functions b and c for its base and operation, define

    beta_0 = b,
    beta_(m+1) = c(beta_m),
    rank(bracket) = sup_m(beta_m + 1) + 1.                         (4)

Other free-hole ranks remain fixed parameters. By structural induction these are monotone functions of countable ordinal parameters and have countable values. Finite hygienic substitution obeys the corresponding rank bound; deletion of idle units or binders cannot increase it. Every operational term of a bracket has rank strictly smaller than (4). Ordinary children also have smaller rank.

Thus the semantic dependency tree obtained by choosing finite term indices at series nodes is well founded. Truth can be assigned by transfinite recursion, using ordinary Boolean operations, own-instance quantifier ranges, and joint negation over all admitted terms. This is a mathematical well-foundedness argument, not an algorithm that computes ordinals.

5.2 Strong substitution theorem

Proved here, relative to K1–K4. For any finite expression E with free propositional holes and any legal fillers T_i whose states are supplied as Gamma, Compile(E,Gamma) is the state of the normalized syntactic substitution E[T_i]. This includes holes in inner bases and inner operations. The corresponding assertion holds with undefined rows marked as such.

Proof. Use structural induction on E, with the induction hypothesis quantified over arbitrary legal fillers, not just fillers of smaller syntax size. At a hole, the assertion is the row lookup rule and Lemma 2. At ordinary constructors it is K4. A receiving context's occurrence-dependent vacuity is decided from the substituted occurrence sets.

At a bracket, written-descriptor mode computes the stipulated least closure from precisely those substituted occurrence sets; Lemma 1 justifies transport of existing copied declarations. The token and atom data therefore agree with the actual normalized written descriptor. Local inconsistent mergers are detected by their equality test.

Let T_0 be the actual substituted base and T_(m+1) its actual normalized successor. The structural induction hypothesis applies to the strictly smaller written operation C with any current filler T_m. An ordinary induction on m consequently gives

    state(T_m) = F^m(k0).                                       (5)

The smaller-operation hypothesis includes its inner brackets; it does not require T_m itself to have bounded syntactic nesting depth. The same equality holds for each external row. A locally undefined descriptor is undefined immediately; otherwise it is a legal series exactly when all of its generated terms have defined maps. This is the definedness test used above. Failure of sense is not failure of map definedness.

For every defined row, the reference semantics is the joint negation over the actual terms with their own sense. Equation (5) turns that enumeration into (3), once orbit repetition is used. Hence the semantic tables agree. This completes the structural induction. The well-founded rank argument ensures that the referenced operational observations have their stipulated meaning; no fixed point of an unverified semantic recurrence is being selected. QED.

An equivalent proof separates the all-natural-number orbit equation from finite orbit truncation: first obtain (5) at every finite m by the substitution induction, then truncate only because the deterministic finite state has repeated. This order avoids using periodicity to establish compositionality.

5.3 Contextual congruence

Corollary. Define T approximately-equal U when their K-states are equal. Then every permitted context D from the fixed specification satisfies

    state(T)=state(U)  implies  state(nf(D[T]))=state(nf(D[U])).

The induced transition is computable and deterministic. It preserves all stored role-sensitive fitting, exposed atoms, sense, C-nv filters, truth, and definedness information. This is an input-dependent finite congruence; it is not one finite quotient that handles unboundedly many new names from arbitrary enlarged specifications.

The ledger's closed-cycle/closed-edge obstruction cannot be bypassed by discarding the ambient rows: those rows remain part of K. Names absent from T but present in D still reserve their tokens. Token placements remain separate from semantic references throughout. Repeated atoms and shared tokens are handled by the relational fitting kernel, not by independent atom counts.

6. World-profile adequacy with nesting

One must still justify using M_P rather than an arbitrary infinite world W realizing P.

Proved here from K3 and the substitution construction. The profile relation extends to all compiled nested expressions. For ordinary constructors, K3's back-and-forth matches each newly quantified object/form value and preserves incidence, truth, equality, exact named exceptions and capped supplies. K2 supplies the same syntactic fitting constants; own-instance filters therefore match. The tables range over all required parameter assignments and role patterns, not just a standalone sentence value.

For a series constructor, assume corresponding base observations and corresponding operation observations, as supplied by structural induction on the written base and operation. Induction on the finite iteration index matches the observations of every pair of corresponding terms. Each term is admitted on one side exactly when admitted on the other, and corresponding admitted terms have the same truth. Joint negation over all indices therefore agrees. Written descriptor fit and exposed-atom sense agree separately.

This argument does not assume that the infinite-world carrier itself is finite or that its orbit has already been shown periodic. Periodicity is needed only on the finite representative side to compute the common result. Nor does it treat unrelated units as independent when the profile fixes their correlations: the K3 matching carries the whole selected tuple and its unit incidence.

The profile list is effectively realizable under the ordinary construction: finitely many small-capacity exceptions are assigned explicitly; large-unit color supplies satisfy the capped quotas, and a saturated tail type absorbs the infinitely many remaining units. Thus no nonexistent profile is used as a counterworld. Enlarging the cap from Q to b preserves the applicability of that construction.

7. Conditional A11 theorem and algorithm

Theorem

Conditional theorem. Adopt revision 58's effective decimal naming, G*, X47 finite definition expansion, the own-instance C-nv and N+ rules, H1/Ht2 and the prohibition on undefined mergers, and the coherent transparency convention stated in Section 9. Under K1–K4, there is an effective procedure D such that, for every closed sign e with sense,

    D(e) halts, and D(e)=1 iff for every world w of Phi, V(e,w)=1.

The procedure may be left unspecified on strings outside the promise. The construction in fact includes map-definedness information, but this stronger bookkeeping is not an extra oracle or a change in the A11 input.

Algorithm

1. Expand the finite definitions hygienically. Collect all original names and template interfaces. Compute Q and the larger budget b.
2. Construct the finite role/ambient/token table formats and enumerate the realizable b-profiles and their semantic representatives. Exact decimal name coordinates are used where needed.
3. Form the finite product carrier K. Compile e structurally as in Section 4, with empty free-hole environment. Every nested operation is a function on K; orbit repetition is tested on entire K-states.
4. Read the closed sign's truth entry in every realizable profile. Return 1 exactly when all are true. For promised input its required sense and map-definedness conditions hold.

All steps are effective. Their feasible running time is not asserted. The finite table space and the nested orbit loops may be far beyond practical computation.

Correctness. The substitution theorem identifies the compiler's observations with the operational semantics. Profile adequacy identifies each finite representative's result with all worlds realizing its profile. Effective realizability covers exactly the possible profiles. The all-profile test therefore decides tautologyhood on the promised inputs. QED.

This theorem repairs an argument; it does not validate the original X52 wording as printed. Its bound, all-name tables, complete substitution rows, explicit descriptor mode, and structural nested compiler must replace the inadequate statements there.

8. Reproducible checks and their limits

Run:

    node audit_X52_nested.js

Output is written to audit_X52_nested_results.json. Only built-in Node modules are needed.

Computational observations; all assertions passed:

- One total map on four words: 27,648 seed/quotient closure equalities across 1,728 legal map quotients. Another 2,112 candidate quotients were rejected as inconsistent.
- Two simultaneous maps on three words: 17,064 seed checks across 2,133 legal quotients; 1,512 inconsistent candidates rejected.
- Three exposed sources and two fresh hidden terminal targets: 8,288 seed checks across 259 legal quotients; 366 inconsistent candidates rejected.
- 4,320 finite orbit-observation checks: whenever a quotient intertwines two deterministic transitions and preserves admission/truth observations, joint negation of admitted orbit values agrees.

The checker also exhibits a failure if an inconsistent quotient is arbitrarily resolved. With f=(2,1,2), rho=(0,0,1), and seed {1}, the image of the original closure is {0}. Choosing the quotient transition (1,1) instead produces closure {0,1}. Such a resolution would change the stipulated system and is not used.

These experiments do not implement G* fitting, named-instance semantics, full nested normalization, or the A11 decision procedure. They cannot certify the theorem. The universal arguments are Lemma 1, the finite compiler construction, the substitution induction, and profile preservation.

9. Residual semantic qualification and exact correction requests

Vacuous N

Source ambiguity. X51 L3601–3606 says the vacuous existential has its body's truth and says “likewise for N over z”; X52 L3819–3820 says a vacuous binder is evaluated as its body. If existential quantification is defined by negating joint negation, the coherent equations are

    exists z B = B,       N_z B = not B

when z has no occurrence in B and the stipulated token can be placed. The value description is transparent; its enclosing truth operation is retained.

Every positive theorem in this repair uses those equations. It does not use N_z B=B. If the latter identity is intended simultaneously with the existential identity and its defining relationship to N, there is a contradiction for any meaningful B. No automaton proof can repair that semantic conflict.

Smallest clarification: state that transparency applies to the value description, and that joint negation of the resulting singleton retains its negation. If this expresses the intended existing semantics, it is a clarification. If the intended adopted rule instead makes N_z itself the identity, substituting the coherent rule would be a semantic change and must be adjudicated as such. This report does not perform that change or declare a thaw.

Ledger and paper corrections

1. Retain the prior counterexample to the printed direct-Mov bound as a genuine correction. Replace the bound by the all-name provenance bound and enlarge the role and truth tables consistently. Spell out the root/component and token-state-presence flags required by the N() exception; a standalone undefined truth entry is not enough to evaluate that expression as a component.
2. Replace “per inner-sign occurrence” Pi bookkeeping with the finite complete external-substitution table, including undefinedness outcomes, or supply an independently equivalent encoding. Do not claim the previous Pi list was proved finite by this report.
3. Add closure naturality under legal maps and distinguish existing copied descriptors from newly constructed receiving descriptors.
4. Replace “terminates by finite nesting” with structural compilation of the finite written expression and finite orbit iteration over K. Generated nesting depth is not bounded.
5. Preserve separate written-descriptor and value-orbit semantics. A conjunction of term representatives does not replace the descriptor's token pattern.
6. State the transparency convention explicitly before claiming an unconditional model certificate. State that the revised A11 uses X49's adequate notation, not the superseded diagram-only input.

The proposed changes in items 1–5 concern proofs and representation of the decision procedure, not axioms, ranges, or constructors. Item 6 is a semantic clarification only if it matches the intended meaning already adopted.

10. Final certification status

The formerly missing normalized nested extension is supplied relative to the explicit finite kernel. Full nested G* need not be restricted to obtain this result. No change to a name's referent, to the token rules, to C-nv, to N+, or to the merger prohibition is used.

The mathematical conclusion is conditional certification of A11 under the coherent transparency reading and the previously established kernel results. The independent status of those kernel proofs and of the other twelve axioms should remain visible in any consolidated certificate. This report does not assert that a full executable verifier or a formal proof assistant has checked them.

The only source-level semantic qualification retained by this construction is the vacuous-N disposition above. It should not be concealed beneath the word “verified.” The ledger, paper and preceding reports remain unchanged; this is a new report for independent adjudication.



[Section: vacuous-n]
Vacuous value descriptions

TLP — disposition of vacuous N

31 October 2026. Semantic addendum to Nested construction: historical draft [section nested-draft].

Verdict

The retained definition of N determines the coherent reading. Transparency removes a vacuous description of values, not the surrounding truth operation. Consequently, for a meaningful B in which z does not occur,

    V(exists z B,w) = V(B,w),
    V(N_z B,w)      = 1 - V(B,w).

The phrase “likewise for N over z” in X51 must therefore mean the analogous transparency of the value description and sense condition. It cannot consistently repeat the existential truth equation with N_z substituted for the existential.

This resolves which interpretation is compatible with the ledger's retained definitions. It does not establish the author's private intent. If the phrase was intended to impose N_z B=B, that intended rule is contradictory with the retained N definition; it is not a second consistent semantics that the decision procedure must accommodate.

No source is edited, and no thaw or new interpretive selection is performed. The literal identity reading is excluded by the existing definitions; the imprecise sentence needs an editorial correction.

1. Authoritative text

Physical line numbers refer to C:\Users\ogmb\Downloads\TLP Ledger.md, revision 58, SHA-256:

    c64649c2058e6da7dcdd34eb3bed0e3c7db0a63cb517978a72dff894b7033c23

The relevant source statements are:

| Lines | Retained statement | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 131–132 | A vacuous binder is transparent; the existential has its body's sense and truth when its token fits. | The adopted existential equation is explicit. |
| 3601–3606 | The same existential equation is printed, followed by “likewise for N over z.” The exception is assigned to C-nv and the 5.501 tag. | The exception concerns the description/range of values; its prose must be read with the N definition. |
| 5567–5569 | N negates all values; its sense is the intersection of their complements. | N remains joint negation. |
| 8174–8181 | 5.501 describes values; a vacuous binder is transparent, “not a function fx.” | The vacuous abstraction collapses to its constant proposition; it is not ordinary varying-domain enumeration. |
| 8182 | 5.502 defines N as negation of all values. | The truth operation is explicitly defined. |
| 8184 | 5.51 states N(p)=~p. | N on a singleton cannot be identity. |
| 8197–8199 | N over the values of fx is the negation of the existential; the concept “all” is separated from the truth-function. | Dropping a generality description does not drop its enclosing truth operation. |

X51 says that the vacuous rule supersedes X50's range rule (L3620–3622). It does not announce a replacement of 5.502 or the singleton equation at 5.51. The signature continues to state those rules after recording the vacuous exception at L5563–5569.

2. Exact notation and derivation

Write delta_z(B) for the description of values, and distinguish it from the proposition N(delta_z(B)). For non-vacuous z, delta_z(B) describes the named instances admitted under C-nv and N+. For vacuous z, the adopted transparency rule reduces the description to the constant B:

    delta_z(B) = {B}.

This is a singleton description, not the empty description. Nothing varies, but the constant proposition is still present. It also is not a new assertion that an object named z exists as a semantic witness; the vacuous written token is handled by the stipulated fitting condition.

The retained joint-negation definition gives, at every world w,

    V(N(delta_z(B)),w)
      = AND over p in {B} of (1 - V(p,w))
      = 1 - V(B,w).

Existential quantification is its negation, so

    V(exists z B,w)
      = 1 - V(N(delta_z(B)),w)
      = V(B,w).

Thus the explicit existential equation and the retained definition of N agree. The sense condition is the corresponding one: B must have sense and the written vacuous token must be placeable. In the promised Phi fragment the token is placed on an available fresh resource. No name's semantic reference is identified with that token location.

This reasoning is independent of the automaton, profiles, and eventual periodicity. It does not use A11 to settle its own semantic input.

3. Why the alternative identity is inconsistent

Suppose “likewise” instead means

    V(N_z B,w)=V(B,w).

After the same stipulated transparent value-description reduction, 5.502 and 5.51 give

    V(N_z B,w)=1-V(B,w).

Together they require a Boolean truth value to equal its complement. Neither 0 nor 1 satisfies that equation.

This is not rescued by token fitting. For a concrete meaningful body in Phi, use B=R_1(a,b). It denotes a frame state. Choose the atomic token on a fresh R-unit's common pair, with named object tokens a,b; its form token differs from the semantic target form R_1. A fresh leaf object supplies a vacuous object-binder token distinct from those name tokens. The induced fully named token-to-target map is acyclic. Thus the relevant sign can fit under the adopted rules. Worlds with B false and worlds with B true are available under the full world space. The two asserted truth equations disagree in both cases.

The contradiction is between the two semantic equations, not a special counterexample to the finite-state construction. Keeping both equations would destroy the stipulated Boolean semantics before decidability is considered.

4. Precise editorial corrections

These replacements state the interpretation forced by the retained N definition. They are proposals only; the ledger and paper are unchanged.

X51 L3601–3606

Replace the ambiguous “likewise for N over z” passage by:

> If z does not occur in B, the description of values is the singleton B. Its written z-token must fit. The existential has B's sense and truth; joint negation over that description has the same sense condition and the truth of not-B. Transparency removes the vacuous abstraction, not the enclosing truth operation N.

The existing textual grounds and the identification of the exception with C-nv can remain. This does not add a new exception to the truth table of N.

X52 L3743–3754 and L3819–3820

State normalization at the appropriate syntactic level:

    delta_z(B)          -> {B},
    N(delta_z(B))       -> N(B),
    not N(delta_z(B))   -> not N(B), equivalent to B.

Thus a displayed existential can reduce to B. A joint-negation expression cannot reduce directly to B merely because its value variable is vacuous. The implementation must preserve the surrounding operation. The nested-resolution report already uses this convention.

Certificate wording

Use:

> Vacuous value abstractions are transparent. N retains its definition as joint negation, including on singleton value descriptions. The A11 construction uses the corrected all-name bound and the normalized nested compiler, rather than X52's original direct-Mov bound.

Do not say that the original printed X52 proof has thereby been validated unchanged.

5. Effect on the previous report and certification

The semantic qualification in Section 9 of Nested construction: historical draft [section nested-draft] is discharged for the reading compatible with the ledger's retained definitions. There is no need to change N, the quantifier ranges for non-vacuous binders, G*, the token rules, or hereditary A6s to obtain that reading.

The resulting mathematical statement is:

> Under revision 58's effective notation and G*, with vacuous descriptions interpreted as just derived, the repaired finite-state construction in Nested construction: historical draft [section nested-draft], based on its explicitly stated K1–K4 kernel, establishes decidability of tautologyhood on promised meaningful inputs.

This addendum discharges a semantic premise; it is not another independent verification of the entire K1–K4 kernel or of the nested compiler proof. Those proofs remain available for independent adjudication. It does not turn the limited algebraic checks into an executable certification of the complete decision procedure.

The all-thirteen-axiom claim additionally rests on the separate model verifications in the full audit. This addendum neither replaces those verifications nor proves independence or minimality.

If an adjudicator insists that X51's prose expressly stipulates the incompatible identity N_z B=B, the correct disposition is instead a demonstrated semantic contradiction requiring correction—not an unconditional certificate for that literal reading. Nothing here authorizes retaining the identity while declaring the model sound. Because the retained definition of N and the explicit singleton equation settle the compatible reading, the recommended correction is editorial disambiguation. No thaw is performed.



[Section: ordered-audit]
Ordered audit and definedness obstruction

Y audit — ordered certification gates

31 October 2026. Review of the proposed repair, not of an independently verified implementation.

Disposition

The ledger was updated first, with a separate Y register and a preserved revision-58 snapshot. The audit then followed the requested order.

Gate 1: no decisive state-separation counterexample established.

Gate 2: not certified. The proposed total table construction needs an explicit rowwise correctness theorem covering a table with an undefined identity row but defined composite rows. The numerical example below rules out absorbing failure as a substitute for that theorem. The existing full-vector design might support the required behavior; the example does not refute every such design.

Gates 3–4 have not been accepted on the strength of the current construction. This review stops certification at Gate 2 rather than automatically starting another repair cycle. A11 is not refuted. The previous statements that no mathematical lemma remained open, and that only the vacuous-N wording remained, were too strong.

1. What was updated

The working ledger is TLP Ledger.md in the workspace, synchronized to the user's Downloads ledger. The preserved source is the original revision-58 source body retained above, with SHA-256:

    c64649c2058e6da7dcdd34eb3bed0e3c7db0a63cb517978a72dff894b7033c23

Y0–Y7 record provenance, the printed X52 counterexample, the proposed repairs, the limits of their computations, vacuous-N interpretation, empty-expression bookkeeping, and the ordered audit protocol. The opening status notice supersedes historical claims that E32 is closed and Phi certified. X0–X53 and the axioms are preserved as source evidence, not rewritten to hide the earlier claims.

This review is a further self-audit of the submitted arguments. It is not independent confirmation by a second referee.

2. Gate 1 — attempts to separate equal states

The proposed state includes full ambient token relations, all-name substitution rows, own-instance sense/truth tables, and definedness flags. The following previously successful attacks therefore do not immediately separate its full states:

- The four-name chain defeats the original direct-Mov budget, but all-name occurrence accounting distinguishes its successive live interfaces.
- A context introducing a name absent from the filler can affect token fitting; the proposed ambient reservation rows expressly retain that information.
- Shared tokens and repeated atoms require relational boundary assignments rather than independent counts; the proposed acceptance tables retain assignments and equality patterns.
- Name identifications can invalidate inner maps. Full definedness rows could distinguish the resulting outcomes, provided their construction is actually justified.
- A copied inner descriptor need not expose all of its syntax if legal closure transport and a complete table action hold. The closure lemma alone, however, is conditional on the quotient maps being defined.

These observations are not a proof that the full state is a congruence. In particular, putting the answer to every future-legality question into a finite Boolean table proves only finite cardinality of the proposed record format. Computability and correct composition remain Gate 2 obligations.

No pair of legal terms with equal complete proposed states and different legal contextual outcomes was established in this review. The example in the next section deliberately has an illegal intermediate quotient and must not be advertised as such a pair.

3. Gate 2 — undefinedness and direct composite rows

3.1 A concrete map calculation

Use three same-sort words 0,1,2, with

    f(0)=2, f(1)=1, f(2)=2.

Let rho identify 0 and 1 but leave 2 separate:

    rho=(0,0,1).

For f to descend along rho, equal source images must have equal target images. But

    rho(0)=rho(1)=0,
    rho(f(0))=1, while rho(f(1))=0.

The intermediate quotient is therefore undefined.

Now let sigma identify the two image words:

    sigma=(0,0),       sigma after rho=(0,0,0).

Along the direct composite every source and every target has image 0. The quotient is well defined and is the one-point identity map.

Thus

    Defined(f/rho)=false,
    Defined(f/(sigma after rho))=true.

This is an exact finite counterexample to any claim that definedness failure is necessarily preserved by further coarsening of the original declaration. It does not license executing an undefined intermediate G* substitution.

3.2 Its relation to G*

The words can be taken to be form names R1,R2,R3, with object names a,b fixed. Let a legal descriptor have base

    B = R1(a,b) AND R2(a,b) AND R3(a,b)

and operation x[f], where f sends R1 to R3 and fixes R2,R3 (and a,b). The original source map is well defined. The direct map identifying all three form names produces a defined constant-name descriptor. Identifying just R1 and R2 first produces the prohibited inconsistent map.

This example uses the same merger rule as X51, original lines 3584–3588 and 3645–3650. The identities are of one sort and arity; no binder capture, fresh-name generation, or arbitrary syntax inspection is involved. Fitting of the original and directly collapsed named-atom patterns is supplied by fresh R-unit tokens on the common pair, with a further fresh state for the propositional letter. The illegal intermediate is excluded by the grammar, exactly as it should be.

3.3 What it does and does not show about the submitted compiler

Section 3.3 of Nested construction: historical draft [section nested-draft] prescribes composite-row lookup and says “An undefined row remains undefined.” Those statements require a precise scope distinction:

- A failed lookup of a particular row has no truth value and cannot be treated as an admitted term.
- Failure of the identity row of an entire row vector does not justify discarding every other row of that vector. A direct composite row can be defined, as above.

The submitted report does warn against poisoning every row because one fails. Accordingly, the example is not a demonstrated contradiction in every interpretation of its compiler. It does expose the need to specify and prove the stronger rowwise invariant, rather than appealing only to a state of an existing legal intermediate sign.

Let the proposed table of a legal T be k_T, and write its row action as

    A_mu(k_T)[rho] = k_T[rho after mu].

If the mu-row is undefined, A_mu(k_T) can have an undefined identity row and a defined rho-row. Such a vector is not the state of a legal intermediate G* sign mu(T). A correctness proof that quantifies only over legal fillers does not, without another argument, establish its intended interpretation through all the constructors of the claimed total finite algebra.

One could instead give a partial, promise-relative proof and show that these extra vectors are never needed for the claimed observations. Or one could specify a rowwise auxiliary interpretation of direct transformations and prove the total construction correct on it. Neither option is ruled out. The current report must explicitly supply one; the existence of a finite product of Boolean tables is insufficient by itself.

4. The precise remaining obligation

Rowwise extension lemma. For every finite template E and environment of complete substitution tables, give effective constructor rules and an invariant satisfying all of the following:

1. Each defined output row is interpreted by a direct, well-defined transformation under the ledger's rules, without assuming that every intermediate identity row denotes a legal sign.
2. Each undefined output row is justified by the specific transformed descriptor or its future iteration, not by globally discarding a vector whose other rows may be defined.
3. The letter action composes as the specified row lookup, including the example above.
4. For an admitted input and every row used by its own-instance range and truth computation, the observations agree with operational semantics.
5. The nested orbit construction computes future-definedness entries under this invariant, or a weaker promise-relative argument proves those entries unnecessary to the A11 procedure.

Section 5.2 of the submitted report invokes a structural induction over legal fillers. It needs to explain how that induction covers the auxiliary vectors just described, or why the algorithm cannot rely on any uncovered observation. The ordinal rank argument supplies a well-founded reference semantics for legal syntax; it does not by itself interpret a vector with no legal intermediate representative.

This is a missing proof obligation, not a theorem that no such extension exists. A corrected proof might resolve it locally. Under the requested stopping rule, this review does not quietly add that repair and then claim the original proof was complete.

5. Empty-expression check

The initial audit also examined the root/component flags for N(). The source explicitly treats N() as a true component but not a standalone sign (original lines 3591–3592). The ledger additionally defines a fact as a nonempty true situation (original line 7552), uses nonempty picture media (original lines 5608 and 7624), and gives logical operation signs no additional medium image (original line 5550).

These rules support the intended rejection of a standalone string consisting only of iterated N on the empty enumeration: adding logical punctuation does not create a nonempty sign medium. Ordinary embedding as a component must still preserve the stipulated Boolean value. This check is not presented as a new contradiction or the decisive Gate 2 issue. The full constructor proof must nevertheless state the exact modes used at own-instance checks rather than substituting “false” for every non-sign.

6. Reproduction

Run:

    node audit_Y_definedness.js

The output is audit_Y_definedness_results.json. It verifies the intermediate undefined quotient and the defined direct composite. The result is PASS. It is a quotient-map calculation, not a complete G* evaluator and not a legal-context separation test.

The earlier 53,000 closure checks were conditional on the quotient being legal. They do not settle this additional issue about the interpretation and propagation of different definedness rows.
