[Section: promise-proof]
Promise-relative compiler proof

Y10 — Gate 2: promise-relative resolution

31 October 2026. Bounded follow-up to Ordered audit and definedness obstruction [section ordered-audit].

Verdict and limits

The specific Gate 2 objection can be discharged by a promise-relative compiler invariant. An undefined alternative row need not, and must not, be used as the semantic representative of an intermediate sign. On an admitted G* input, the semantic compiler's actual filler environments have map-defined syntactic representatives throughout. Alternative rows are table entries, not recursive compiler inputs.

The repair deliberately abandons the stronger assertion that the procedure decides future map legality or G membership. Remove the proposed infinite-future definedness field from the carrier. No replacement legality oracle is introduced. A11 is already a promise problem, and G already requires all successive applications to be defined.

This resolves the identified Gate 2 definedness obligation, relative to the finite fitting/profile kernel and the stated compiler architecture. It does not re-certify K1–K4 or discharge the remaining Gate 3–4 audit. Nor does it prove a total congruence preserving syntax membership under contexts with illegal intermediate substitutions. Those stronger claims are withdrawn.

1. Source scope and terminology

Physical line numbers refer to the original revision-58 source body retained above, whose SHA-256 is

    c64649c2058e6da7dcdd34eb3bed0e3c7db0a63cb517978a72dff894b7033c23

A11 is expressly a promise problem over possible signs (original lines 160–164). G* forbids a step merging inner closure entries with incompatible images (3584–3588, 3645–3650), and defines successive normalized substitution at 3650–3653. Named-instance commutation is stated at 3625–3631.

Use map-admissible for a sorted, correctly scoped expression whose required series substitutions and nested series substitutions have well-defined maps. This does not mean that the expression has sense. A generated term may fail its own fitting or exposed-atom test and be excluded by C-nv while remaining map-admissible. Empty-value and root/component conventions are also retained separately.

Let Legal(T) denote this syntactic property. It is a mathematical predicate in the proof, not a proposed executable test. Let Obs(T) be the occurrence, token, sense and truth observations specified by the previous kernel when Legal(T) holds, including observations of terms lacking sense.

For an external word map rho, a safe row of T is one for which the direct transformed expression rho(T) is map-admissible. Safe does not mean true, meaningful, or injective. Some permitted operation maps identify names and are nevertheless safe.

For a semantic table entry, first canonicalize the assignment's equality pattern into the corresponding word/name-identification row. Accuracy is required when the resulting named instance is map-admissible. It is not asserted for every arbitrary tuple merely because the uninstantiated open expression is admissible. Equivalently, semantic safety is a property of the complete observation index (word map, equality pattern and parameter assignment). The phrase “correct on safe rows” below includes this qualification. Token and occurrence observations use the syntactic row alone.

The proof distinguishes three matters:

1. Knowing from the input promise that a particular syntactic process is admissible.
2. Computing its sense and truth, which is still required.
3. Deciding admissibility for arbitrary unpromised syntax, which is not required here.

2. The finite carrier and the exact change

Retain the finite row format, all-name parameterization, ambient fitting relations, profile tables, exposed atoms, occurrence data and root/component bookkeeping of the proposed repair. Retain the enlarged bounds Q and b as premises pending their separate audit.

Delete: the field claiming to answer whether every future term of an arbitrary transformed inner series has defined maps. Delete the claim that the compiler computes that predicate for every row.

Call the remaining finite product K_obs. Complete its elementary operations deterministically on all table inputs. Immediate finite failures—such as a locally inconsistent quotient of a displayed finite map or an out-of-budget chart—may receive a fixed error value. Do not propagate one row's error to every other row. No claim is made about the semantic accuracy of entries outside the safe rows of the represented expression.

An unsafe row need not be recognized as unsafe. If no local finite test detects its failure, the finite program can still return some bit pattern. The proof requires accuracy only on safe rows and on the actual observations used for admitted inputs. This is a standard logical use of a promise: it does not add an algorithm that decides the promise.

Every row remains present, so all word maps are represented by finite reindexing:

    A_mu(k)[rho] = k[rho after mu].                         (1)

Never implement (1) by first inspecting k[mu] and discarding the whole vector if that entry fails. The Y9 example remains an explicit prohibition on that implementation.

3. Required compiler architecture

There are two procedures with different purposes.

Semantic compilation

Compile(E,Gamma) walks the original finite expression E. Gamma supplies complete K_obs vectors for its free propositional holes. A mapped hole returns the corresponding reindexed vector (1). Ordinary constructors combine the vectors by finite rowwise operations. Quantifier tables perform their finite assignment loops; they do not recursively call the compiler on each instantiated syntax tree.

For a series [B,x,C], compute

    k0 = Compile(B,Gamma),
    F(k) = Compile(C,Gamma[x:=k]), with term normalization.

Iterate F on complete vectors until a complete vector repeats. The finite truth observations of the admitted term values are combined by joint negation. No future-definedness bit is consulted.

Crucial: the compiler does not re-enter semantic compilation with a single arbitrary row of a vector promoted to a new filler environment. It also does not recompile the whole input under each external map. The vectors already carry the rows; a row request is a lookup or an elementary finite combination.

Written-descriptor calculation

A separate structural calculation handles the tokens and H1 words of the descriptor. Its local x-holes are symbolic word/slot occurrences, not fake propositions with invented truth tables. It computes occurrence sets, exposed atoms, closures, vacuity and fitting relations from finite written data. It never launches a semantic orbit with these display-only placeholders as fillers.

These procedures were informally distinguished in the nested report's two modes. Here their separation is a required condition of the promise-relative argument. An implementation that sends display-only placeholder records into semantic iteration is not covered by this proof.

4. Safe-row invariant

Lemma 1 — safe observations suffice for a legal composite

Assume T_i are map-admissible fillers and E[T_i], after the stipulated normalization, is map-admissible. Fix a safe external row rho of this composite.

Every filler observation needed for the rho-row can be requested as a direct row of some T_i. A request through a hole map mu is indexed by rho after mu, with hygienic local renaming. The requested transformed filler is a component of the legally transformed composite, so its maps are defined. Its observation is therefore a safe row of T_i.

The same claim holds for ordinary binding and finite truth functions. Binding changes token roles and the named-instance checks, not the requirement that the retained nested descriptor maps be well defined. Ht2 removes idle units and vacuous binders, not an arbitrary defective proposition subtree. No claim is made that a syntactically undefined intermediate can be executed and repaired afterwards.

For receiving descriptors, the original filler occurrence sets and the row occurrence sets determine the finite closure calculation. The source filler identity rows are map-admissible by hypothesis. On a safe row the legal closure-transport lemma applies. Thus this calculation does not require inventing a closure for a filler with an undefined identity representative.

Lemma 2 — reindexing preserves the safe-row invariant on admitted copies

Suppose k is correct on every safe row of a map-admissible T, and mu(T) is itself map-admissible. Then A_mu(k) is correct on every safe row of mu(T).

Indeed, if rho(mu(T)) is map-admissible, composition of the two legal transformations and legal normalization gives the same expression as the direct composite transformation. Equation (1) reads the safe row rho after mu of T. This is exactly the observation required.

The hypothesis that mu(T) is map-admissible is essential. The theorem makes no claim that an identity-undefined vector is the state of a legal intermediate G* sign. That is precisely the unproved extension that Gate 2 challenged.

Lemma 3 — promised compilation does not reach illegal filler representatives

For semantic compilation of an admitted G* input, each actual filler environment can be paired with map-admissible syntactic representatives. Every actual orbit vector can be paired with the corresponding generated term, whether or not that term has sense.

Proof. Initially there are no free propositional fillers. At a bracket, its substituted base and every successive term exist with defined maps by the G* promise. At orbit stage m, associate k_m with the actual T_m; the next semantic call is the original finite C with x associated to T_m. All mapped copies retained in the next term are map-admissible, otherwise the promised series would have an undefined step. Thus Lemma 2 applies whenever a mapped-hole result is used as a genuine filled subexpression or as the base of a nested orbit.

The same reasoning applies to each inner bracket reached in B or C: its substituted written descriptor and all of its successive terms are required to have defined maps. The environment receives the actual base or actual generated term of that bracket, not an arbitrary alternative row. Ordinary recursive compiler calls preserve the existing filler representatives. Display-only calculations do not supply semantic environments, by Section 3. This is an induction over the finite compiler call structure, with ordinary induction over each iteration index. QED.

The representatives in this proof are witnesses supplied by the promise. The implementation neither constructs all of them nor tests their future admissibility.

5. Semantic instances do not reintroduce the missing oracle

At a binder, the range still requires N+ and the own-instance sense test. Removing future-definedness flags must not remove those checks.

For the candidate assignments that pass N+, the co-occurring parameter values are distinct and avoid the names in the relevant scope. Replacing those parameters by their names is therefore injective on that interface, off its existing names. The full H1 interface ensures that a relevant series name cannot be hidden from this test merely by writing it in a declaration. This is the commutation situation at original lines 3625–3631.

An injective renaming of these external words cannot identify two distinct sources of an inner map. With binders freshly renamed, it cannot capture an internal binder either. Consequently it preserves map-admissibility and transports the closure and normal form. This gives the independently needed reason that the binder's actual own-instance checks use safe rows. It does not make those instances automatically meaningful: fitting, the atom clause and the truth calculation must still be evaluated.

A finite table may also contain entries for assignments that fail the scope's N+ exclusions. Those entries are not used as admitted values. They need not be supplied with an unproved algorithm for future syntax legality. Scope-local exclusions must be applied before using the candidate's semantic truth entry.

Arbitrary non-injective maps used by series operations are a different case. Their legality is supplied by the G* input promise, not by this injective-renaming argument. The two justifications must not be conflated.

6. Promise-relative compilation theorem

Theorem, relative to the stated finite kernel. Suppose E[T_i] is map-admissible, the fillers T_i are map-admissible, and their supplied vectors are correct on their safe rows. The compiler architecture in Section 3 produces a vector correct on every safe row of the normalized E[T_i]. It terminates without deciding which rows are safe.

Proof. Use structural induction on the finite written E, universally quantified over such fillers and vectors. A hole is Lemma 2; ordinary constructors use the kernel and Lemma 1. A binder's admitted instances use Section 5. These arguments access no unsafe filler row when proving a safe output row.

For a bracket, let T_m be its actual generated terms. They are map-admissible by the hypothesis on the bracket, though their own sense may fail. The smaller-expression induction hypothesis applies to B and to C with the current legal T_m. Hence ordinary induction on m gives correctness of k_m on all safe rows of T_m.

If rho is a safe row of the bracket, legal closure transport and substitution commutation identify its generated terms with rho(T_m). All of these terms are map-admissible. Their own-instance sense and truth observations therefore come from safe rows of k_m. Joint negation over the admitted terms is computed from those observations. The written descriptor's sense is calculated separately.

The entire vector transition F is a deterministic operation on a fixed finite product, including its arbitrarily completed unsafe entries. Therefore it eventually repeats. Accuracy of the actual demanded observations holds at every finite index before any periodicity claim is used. Repetition then permits finite evaluation of the common sequence of demanded observations. Incorrect or uninterpreted entries in unsafe rows do not invalidate repetition of the whole finite code; they can only add distinctions and delay repetition.

Termination of recursive compilation is still induction on the finite written expression: B and C are smaller expressions, the orbit loop has at most |K_obs|+1 states before repetition, and a supplied vector is never expanded into its represented syntax. No safety predicate is called. QED.

What kind of congruence this establishes

The code transition is representative-independent on admitted uses of a fixed context. Equal supplied codes produce equal result codes. When both substitutions are map-admissible, their demanded semantic observations agree by the theorem.

This does not assert that equal codes decide whether an arbitrary new context is map-admissible. It is sufficient for the promised series orbit, whose actual terms are all admitted syntactically by G*. A proof of decidable grammar membership would need additional information and a separate theorem.

7. Disposition of the Y9 example

For f=(2,1,2), mu=(0,0,1), and a further collapse rho, the vector A_mu(k) can have an undefined identity observation and a defined direct-composite observation. Equation (1) retains the latter.

However, using the illegal mu(T) as an actual intermediate filler would violate the input promise. Lemma 3 says that such a filler is not reached by semantic compilation of an admitted input. The compiler is allowed to possess the corresponding alternative entries; possessing an entry is not recursively evaluating an illegal intermediate sign.

Thus the example still refutes globally absorbing failure. It does not refute the promise-relative procedure. The disputed totalization theorem is not required for the latter. This is outcome 2 of the bounded attempt, rather than a claim that every invalid case has acquired a new semantics.

8. Reproducible checks

Run:

    node audit_Y10_suspensions.js

The results are saved in audit_Y10_suspensions_results.json. All assertions passed:

- 19,683 direct-composite row checks on all maps of a three-word alphabet.
- 531,441 associativity checks for the complete row-vector action.
- 1,944 cases with an undefined intermediate quotient and a defined direct composite, all retained by the complete table action.

These tests establish only finite algebraic observations. They do not implement G* normalization, C-nv, token fitting, profile realizability, semantic compiler reachability, or the theorem above. The promise-relative reachability and safe-row proofs, not those counts, discharge the identified objection.

9. Required corrections and next gate

1. Replace the future-definedness field and its purported computation in the nested-resolution report with the observation-only carrier used here.
2. Withdraw the asserted G* membership/total-definedness consequence. No such consequence follows from this proof.
3. Replace “an undefined row remains undefined” by the precise direct-composite lookup rule. Failure is not propagated to unrelated rows.
4. Require semantic compilation of whole vectors and a separate written-descriptor calculation. Do not invoke semantic compilation on display placeholders or arbitrary single-row extracts.
5. State the induction invariant as correctness on safe rows of map-admissible representatives, with sense failure explicitly allowed.

These changes concern the algorithm and its claimed scope, not the frozen axioms, notation, constructors, or interpretation of an illegal merger. A11's promise is used as already stated; it is not strengthened to promise the answer or any semantic truth condition.

Current disposition: the specific Gate 2 obstruction is discharged by this promise-relative argument, subject to independent review. Gate 3, the audit of K1–K4, is next; Gate 4 must assess the combined substitution/profile proof with these corrections incorporated. Phi/A11 is not declared independently certified by this addendum, and no all-thirteen-axiom certificate is issued.



[Section: kernel-audit]
Kernel audit and wrapper counterexample

Y11 — Gate 3 audit of K1–K4

31 October 2026. Further self-audit of the proposed A11 repair.

Verdict

Gate 3 stops on a demonstrated global-budget omission. The published replacement defines v over series bases and operation templates, but the compiler applies the resulting cap to the entire input. Ordinary syntax surrounding the series is not included explicitly. Section 1.1 gives a legal, meaningful, name-free input for which that literal budget is too small for both token fitting and world-profile preservation.

This refutes the stated application of the budget, not A11, the local provenance lemma, or every finite-state construction. If v was intended to include the entire outer ordinary context, that requirement must replace its published definition. The larger bound is a plausible local proof correction; it is not silently substituted for the failed rule in this audit.

The later sections preserve the conditional arguments examined during the review. Their fixed-budget lemmas do not cure a budget that is smaller than the input's actual width. A provisional pass announced during the review is withdrawn. This is a further self-audit, not independent confirmation by another referee. No axiom, interpretation, token rule or name reference is changed.

1. Scope and source references

All physical line citations refer to the original revision-58 source body retained above, SHA-256:

    c64649c2058e6da7dcdd34eb3bed0e3c7db0a63cb517978a72dff894b7033c23

The kernel definitions are in Bounded kernel and flat-series proof [section bounded-kernel]; their use is stated in Nested construction: historical draft [section nested-draft]; Y10 restricts the compiler to the A11 promise and withdraws the claimed future-legality decision procedure.

Relevant ledger rules:

- X47: expand defined signs, preserving binding structure; the definition data are finite and well founded (A8).
- X50, lines 3285–3299: literal exposed-atom clause, whole-sign fitting and own-instance C-nv ranges.
- X50, lines 3310–3327: lexical fitting recursion and ordinary range translation.
- X50, lines 3330–3342: proposed profile data and finite semantic representatives.
- X51, lines 3535–3547: least closure and full interface images H1.
- X51, lines 3562–3588: scope-preserving Ht2 normalization and undefined-merger prohibition.
- X52, lines 3776–3787: the final lexical constraints, ambient names, and independence of copies after their boundary assignments are fixed.

The last point matters for fidelity. The earlier global wording about letters must not be read as requiring every hygienically distinct bound identity in an unfolded syntax tree to have a globally different token. The final recursion expressly permits sharing when lexical constraints permit it. Conversely, it does not permit a binder to share a reserved name token merely because that name is absent from its local body. The audit uses these explicit final rules.

G*'s hygienic labels and no-shadowing convention identify binders and declaration targets. They are not an additional token-inequality relation beyond the final fitting rule. If a stronger physical injectivity condition is imposed instead, K2/K4 would need a different audit; that is not the stated X50/X52 semantics.

1.1 Decisive test: an ordinary wrapper larger than its series

The published definition in Bounded kernel and flat-series proof [section bounded-kernel], line 35, takes v over “all bases and operation templates, outer and inner.” Lines 37 and 93 then prescribe Q=max(1,v+n) and b=4Q+2n+8. It does not explicitly include the outer ordinary context containing the brackets. This test uses that literal definition.

The global use occurs in Nested construction: historical draft [section nested-draft], Section 7: compute Q and b once, enumerate the b-profiles, and compile the whole input e over the resulting carrier. No separate larger cap for the outer ordinary context is specified there. The counterexample targets that application; it does not deny that a separately budgeted ordinary procedure could handle the wrapper.

Let the name-free base be

    B = (Es)(Et)(Ef)(f(s,t) OR not f(s,t)),

and let S=[B,x,x] be the constant series with its empty object/form interface and empty maps. Its base has variable width 3, its operation adds none, and it contains no names. Consequently v=3, n=0, Q=3, and the prescribed b is 20.

Define an ordinary formula outside that series:

    H_m = (Eu)(Ev)(Ep_1)...(Ep_m) AND_{j=1..m} p_j(u,v),
    F_m = H_m AND not N(S),
    m=21.

The bound form variables are binary. N+ makes the p_j values distinct. The root ordinary wrapper has width 23, although the only series base/operation has width 3. All names remain absent. No inner-map merger, capture or new-name rule is involved.

Meaningfulness. H_21 fits Phi by choosing 21 distinct R-form tokens on the common ordered pair (a,b). B also fits; its extra local tokens and the bracket's propositional-letter state can be placed using fresh resources. Actual named instances used below have fitting witnesses relocated beyond their finitely many semantic form indices, so the applicable projection graphs are acyclic. Every series term is B up to bound renaming. This is a legal, meaningful kind-3 input, not a malformed string outside the promise.

The series is a harmless true component after outer negation. B is true in every world: choose any actual frame state for the quantified tuple, and its excluded-middle body is meaningful and true. Therefore N(S) is false and not N(S) is true. F_21 has exactly H_21's truth value.

Token-budget failure. In H_20 there are at most 20 distinct forms on any ordered object pair: 20 R-forms on either common orientation, 20 markers on a marker pair, one R-form on an h-to-leaf pair, and zero elsewhere. H_21 cannot fit H_20, although it fits Phi. Thus the auxiliary fitting equivalence cannot be applied to this input at the prescribed b.

Profile-budget failure. Let W_20 have exactly R_21(a,b),...,R_40(a,b) true. Let W_21 additionally have R_41(a,b) true. All other infinitely many states are false. At cap 20, units below 20 have identical exact marker-count types in both worlds. The true common-edge unit type has false-marker cap 20 and unit supply 20 in both capped profiles (actual supplies 20 and 21). The all-false tail type has infinite supply in both. There are no named exceptions. Thus the two prescribed profiles are identical.

H_21 is false in W_20 and true in W_21. All true states have pair (a,b), so no other object pair supplies an overlooked witness. The 21 distinct true forms give an admitted witness in W_21. Hence F_21 differs between worlds of the same prescribed profile.

This is not a claimed wrong final tautology answer on F_21: it is non-tautological either way. It is a decisive failure of the fitting and semantic-preservation premises used to justify the procedure.

Scope of the correction. Include every ordinary input node, not just nodes inside series bases/operations, when computing the global variable budget. One candidate is w_all, the maximum variable bag of the entire finitely written expanded input with full H1 images, followed by Q_all=max(1,w_all+n). Here w_all=23 and the conservative formula gives b_all=100. This would remove this example, but accepting the complete replacement bound and its use belongs to the next explicit repair, not an unnoticed reinterpretation of the earlier v.

2. K1 — all-name lexical width

Audited statement

After finite definition expansion, let N be every original name in the finite specification, declarations included, and n=|N|. Let v be the largest variable bag among all original template nodes, with full H1 images at holes and the binder included at its body bag. Put

    Q = max(1,v+n).

For a node t use the augmented boundary FV(t) union Names(t), relative to t's own scope. K1 bounds this set and the corresponding binder-body bags by Q throughout legal finite unfolding, including nested unfolding.

Proof audit

Every retained node is either copied from an earlier node or belongs to a receiving template. At a copied node, locally bound identities are freshened bijectively; each external word and name has a single image. The number of distinct augmented boundary words cannot increase. In particular, a name turned into a variable has already been charged once: this is precisely where the old direct-Mov proof failed.

At a receiving node, the external words supplied by a hole are contained in its full declared image. Multiple holes can supply different images of the same source name, but all those images are already present in the template bag used to define v. The bound is not obtained by counting only one occurrence or one hole.

For an existing inner descriptor, a legal map transports its closure: each reachable word is obtained by a finite path of declared map edges, and a well-defined quotient transports those paths in both directions. For a receiving inner descriptor, the enclosing hole's full interface image is already among its generators. Recomputing the least closure can remove idle entries; it cannot create a word outside this declared pool. Ht2 deletes units and binders without moving a retained scope. Thus normalization does not enlarge the tracked bags.

Induction on any finite sequence of legal copy/substitution/normalization steps proves the bound. This proof covers arbitrarily large term size and increasing nesting depth. It does not assert bounded total binder count or decide whether an input is legal.

Adversarial checks

- A chain of n named forms successively moved into variables reaches width n+2; Q=n+2 covers it and is sharp for that family.
- Copying a term into several mapped holes does not multiply the boundary of a node inside one copy; the receiving template's bag accounts for the union outside the copies.
- Private bound identities do not become external names through hygienic copying.
- A hole's source spelling is scope-inert, but its full image is not; dropping identity images would invalidate this proof.

Local disposition: the provenance argument covers the specified series templates. Its use as a bound for the whole input fails without including the outer ordinary context, as Section 1.1 shows. No width claim is made for a different grammar with arbitrary inspection, new-name generation, prefix merging, or an unresolved quotient.

3. K2 — finite token fitting

3.1 Two transfers, not one model substitution

Omega is the uncolored token frame with the four hubs, infinitely many leaf/R units and infinitely many markers in each unit. H_b has b units and b markers per unit. Neither is being substituted for Phi's semantic world.

For a finite positive token-incidence pattern with the lexical inequalities, Phi-fit is equivalent to Omega-fit. One direction embeds Phi in Omega. In the other, a finite witness uses finitely many units and finitely many markers. Send these units injectively to sufficiently large distinct Phi indices. Preserve the four hubs, the R/leaf pairing, marker identities, all required incidences and all inequalities.

This transfer concerns existential whole-sign fitting. It does not preserve a demand that a token be fixed to a particular small Phi unit. Semantic reference to o_i is not such a demand: nu and g are different maps. No negative degree or maximum-capacity token test is introduced by the fitting grammar.

3.2 Exact boundary matching with H_b

For a tuple of at most b selected token identities, retain:

- exact hub identities;
- object/form sort and leaf/R/marker role;
- the partition into touched units, including units touched only by form values;
- equality of markers within each touched unit.

Given fewer than b currently selected identities, a new unit requires a fresh unit on the other side, and fewer than b units are occupied. A new marker in an existing unit requires a fresh marker there, and fewer than b marker identities are occupied. An R-form or leaf in an already matched unit has its uniquely corresponding mate. Repeated values use their existing mates. This gives the b-variable back-and-forth extension property between Omega and H_b for incidence and equality.

The token constraints have a tree decomposition by lexical bags: atom incidences; binder-to-live-letter and binder-to-name inequalities; and globally injective name assignments. Include every ambient reserved name in each relevant bag. Once the boundary is fixed, sibling internal choices are independent under the stipulated rule. Existentially choosing the bound tokens is therefore expressible with b locally reusable variable slots, or equivalently evaluated by finite boundary tables. The extension property proves exact agreement between Omega and H_b, including acceptance with a specified boundary type.

The budget b=4Q+2n+8 is conservative. A checked instance contributes at most Q active parameter names, at most n original names, and at most Q ordinary live words; the remaining slack covers the stated chart/role bookkeeping. Names absent from a component remain reserved if present in the whole sign currently being checked. A subsequent own-instance check starts a different checked sign and recomputes its name set.

3.3 Propositional-letter states and A6s

The finitely many fresh states required for propositional letters are supplied after the relational witness, on unused R-units. Their potentially increasing number is not forced into the fixed H_b. They carry no extra incidence with the hole's object/form words; those words are already included separately by H1. Distinct propositional letters receive distinct fresh states and repeated occurrences of the same letter share its state.

For the applicable finite named projections, relocate the whole token witness beyond all semantic form-unit indices in the checked instance. Token-state forms and named-target forms are then disjoint, so there is no directed cycle. The atom/range rules still determine which named projections are meaningful: relocation does not turn a non-state target into a state. In particular, the argument must not replace the literal exposed-atom clause by a new all-atoms clause.

Conditional disposition: the fixed-budget lemma passes for the stated existential, unanchored token problem when all actual bags fit the budget. A claim about fixed small-unit token anchors, or a globally distinct token for every bound identity, would not follow.

4. K3 — semantic profiles and realizability

Use cap q=b for the compiler. The following proof works for any positive finite q.

4.1 Exact profile definition

Pin every unit containing an original named leaf, R-form, or marker. For each pinned unit i record all three R truth bits; the individual truth bits of its named markers; and the true and false counts of the remaining markers, each capped at q. The four hubs are fixed throughout.

For an unpinned unit record its type

    (three R truth bits, min(q,true markers), min(q,false markers)).

For each type record the number of unpinned units, capped at q. Keep the exact constant interpretations and the identities of pinned units; do not replace the original coordinate names by their anonymous types.

4.2 Effective realizability

This construction is explicit rather than an inference from automorphism invariance.

For each pinned unit i, subtract the number of named marker forms from its known capacity i. The proposed residual true/false caps define two intervals: a cap r<q means exactly r; cap q means at least q. Check whether their sum can equal the remaining capacity. This is finite arithmetic; named marker bits and R bits impose no further capacity constraint.

For unpinned indices i<2q, enumerate their finitely many possible colorings up to the cap: the two actual marker counts sum to i, and the three R bits are arbitrary. A finite search assigns these exceptional units to types.

For every remaining unpinned index i>=2q, the possible capped marker pairs are exactly

    (r,q) for r<q;   (q,s) for s<q;   (q,q),

with any three R bits. These are the tail-allowed types. Both counts below q would have sum below 2q and cannot fill such a unit.

After an exceptional assignment, check each profile quota. An unsaturated quota c<q is exact and must not already be exceeded. A saturated quota q means at least q. A type not allowed in the tail must already meet its quota using exceptional units. A tail-allowed type can receive the finitely many additional units required by its quota.

Finally, at least one tail-allowed type must have saturated quota q. This condition is necessary because infinitely many unpinned tail units remain and there are finitely many types. It is sufficient: satisfy the finite remaining quotas using distinct tail indices, then assign every remaining tail index to one saturated tail-allowed type. Each such index can realize the assigned capped pair: use exactly r true markers for (r,q), exactly s false markers for (q,s), or at least q of each for (q,q). Named indices are skipped. This explicitly constructs an infinite Phi-world realizing the profile.

Thus realizability is a finite search plus arithmetic. It handles exact named exceptions, finite small-capacity exceptions and the infinite tail without assuming independent choices that violate a unit's capacity.

4.3 Finite semantic representative

For a realizable profile, keep each pinned unit and its named markers. Give it exactly the recorded number of residual markers of each color, using q when saturated. For each anonymous type make exactly its recorded capped number of units, each with its recorded capped marker supplies. Keep the hubs and the three R incidences per unit with their recorded truth bits.

This is M_P. It is a finite interpretation of the incidence/truth vocabulary with the original constants. It need not be a literal initial cut of Phi. In particular, an artificial unit representing a named o_i need not contain all i markers: it preserves the observations made by at most q variables, not its full first-order type. The decision procedure may not inspect the spelling i as an extra semantic operation; G*'s no-inspection rule excludes that operation.

4.4 Back-and-forth proof

Maintain an injective matching of all currently touched unpinned units and of the selected marker identities within each unit. Pinned units and named markers are matched exactly. A form value touches its unit even when its leaf has not been selected.

With at most q-1 selected values remaining before a new choice, matching a fresh unpinned unit is possible: supplies are either equal below q or both at least q. Matching a new unnamed marker of a required truth color in a matched unit is possible for the same reason. Named markers, leaves, R-forms and hubs have their stipulated mates. Equalities, unit correlations, E and W atoms are preserved.

Induction on ordinary formulas gives agreement at all quantifier depths for the q-variable fragment. Induction through infinitary Boolean combinations also holds when the actual variable bound is respected. This last qualification is why the original direct-Mov theorem was invalid.

4.5 Contextual sense observations

Under the stipulated semantics, fitting and the exposed-atom test do not depend on the world's truth bits. Their semantic-assignment dependence consists of sorts, equalities/name identifications, frame incidence and the separately computed fitting relation of the current syntactic pattern. These are all preserved by the matching and the role tables. No unknown additional world-dependent sense color is being assumed finite.

This is not permission to forget the syntactic fitting tables. Two signs with the same truth function can have different contextual sense, as the earlier separator demonstrates.

Conditional disposition: the profile lemma passes when the actual variable cap is respected. The finite representative is used for semantic evaluation only; H_b is used for token constraints only.

5. K4 — ordinary compositional kernel

5.1 Token and occurrence composition

At an atom, the row retains its literal incidence constraint and repeated-symbol equalities. At a finite truth-function node, all child token constraints must fit simultaneously; fix the full boundary assignment and ambient name reservations before combining their acceptance bits. Internal child choices can then be combined because all cross-child constraints pass through that boundary or the reserved names.

At a binder z, choose a token of the correct sort, excluding the other same-sort free letters of its body and every reserved same-sort name of the checked sign. Occurrence sets determine whether the binder is vacuous. They also determine which atoms are exposed: selection is by scope, not merely by the spellings occurring in an atom.

A mapped hole composes the external letter map with the current row index. All names—not merely names directly moved to variables—are in the row domain. Locally bound identities are fresh. A moved name takes its resulting role; it does not retain a global name reservation if it has become a variable, unless the current named-instance check promotes it again.

5.2 Own-instance semantic ranges

For a non-vacuous binder over z with body B and current parameter assignment alpha, define

    theta_B(d,alpha) = correct_sort(d)
                      AND Nplus_B(d,alpha)
                      AND S_own(B[d,alpha]).

The last test uses that named instance's own occurrence set, name roles, fitting table and exposed-atom incidences. It does not inherit unrelated ambient reservations from a parent token check. Assignment equalities are canonicalized as the same name before the test. As in Y10, the proof's demanded observations are restricted to map-admissible named instances; future syntax legality is not a new runtime oracle.

Joint negation has value

    not exists d (theta_B(d,alpha) AND V(B[d,alpha])).

The truth entry is consulted only when the own-instance sense test succeeds. For vacuous z, the description reduces to the singleton B; N still negates it. Ordinary finite N uses the component observations, while an own-value admission test uses the standalone sense mode. This retains the explicit N() exception and does not substitute false for every meaningless component.

All these operations are finite on the row tables and M_P. The profile matching justifies the corresponding range steps in infinite Phi. Structural induction on the ordinary context proves composition; it does not inspect a filler or invoke eventual periodicity.

5.3 The ambient-name separator, checked precisely

Let F be one form name and let

    P = (Eu)(Ev)(F(u,v) AND F(v,u)),
    Q = (Eu)(Ev)F(u,v).

Both patterns fit on their own. Use the context

    D[xi] = F(c,d) AND F(d,c) AND xi,

with distinct object names c,d. Its two named orientations force their tokens onto a,b in some order, and F onto an R-form. The whole-sign name reservation then prevents P's binders from using a,b, so D[P] cannot fit. D[Q] can fit by placing Q's bound pair on h,o_m for the same R_m.

Both named orientations are necessary for this argument. A single contextual atom F(c,d) could instead occupy h,o_m and leave a,b available; that would not establish the separator.

The repaired acceptance relations distinguish these contexts because c,d remain reserved even though they are absent from the fillers. Repeated atoms use the same state; two sibling copies of Q may share their internal h,o_m tokens where the lexical rule permits. Distinct names still require distinct token assignments.

For a fully meaningful named context, choose the semantic F,c,d to denote an actual R_i,a,b pair and choose token R_m with m distinct and sufficiently large. This preserves the separation between g and nu and supplies acyclic applicable named projections. The example is about contextual fitting, not a claim that token locations equal those referents.

Conditional disposition: ordinary composition passes under the final scope rules with an adequate common budget. The nested compiler and Y10 reachability remain Gate 4 subjects.

6. Reproducible finite checks

Run:

    node audit_Y11_kernel.js

Output: audit_Y11_kernel_results.json. Built-in Node modules only.

The checker constructs tuple types retaining hubs, roles, touched units, marker equality, truth colors, named units and named markers. For each tuple of length less than q, it compares the complete set of one-value extension types. It checks consistency across all tuples with the same type, not just root truth values.

Results, all assertions passed:

- 3 uniform token-frame pairs, caps q=1,2,3, comparing q units/q markers against q+1 units/q+1 markers.
- 2,072 finite semantic frame/representative pairs: all 512 truth colorings of a two-unit frame at caps 1 and 2, with and without a named-marker exception, plus 24 seeded five-unit cases at cap 3.

- Seed for the additional cases: 20261101.

These tests implement neither infinite profile realizability nor the full C-nv/G* truth evaluator. Realizability is proved in Section 4.2; the general transfer results use the extension proofs, not extrapolation from these counts. Earlier width checks were not rerun: the current K1 audit is the general provenance argument.

The separate executable audit_Y11_wrapper.js reproduces the exact finite counting facts of Section 1.1 and the analytically specified infinite profiles. Its results are in audit_Y11_wrapper_results.json: b=20, wrapper width 23, equal capped profiles, truth values false/true, failure to fit H_20 and a Phi witness. It is a specialized positive-existential counting check, not a full G* interpreter. The general conclusions follow from the proof in Section 1.1.

7. Gate status and consequences

| Kernel | Result of this audit | Essential qualification |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | Local provenance argument retained; global application fails | Outer ordinary syntax omitted from the explicit budget definition |
| K2 | Fixed-budget lemma retained conditionally | The prescribed b does not cover the wrapper witness |
| K3 | Fixed-budget lemma retained conditionally | The actual input exceeds the cap; same-profile worlds separate it |
| K4 | Ordinary structural argument retained conditionally | Cannot certify the whole compiler with undersized tables |

No new axiom or semantic correction is requested. The budget definition needs an explicit proof correction. The detailed profile construction should be included in any consolidated proof rather than referenced merely as “verified.” The auxiliary finite structures must be labeled by purpose, and the ambient separator must use both named orientations.

Gate 3 is not discharged. Gate 4 is deferred. The present bounded audit stops on the global-budget omission and does not automatically start another repair cycle. The likely correction is local to the proof's accounting; the counterexample does not establish that the finite-state route is impossible. A11 and the all-thirteen-axiom model claim remain uncertified. The separate independence/minimality obligations remain unchanged.



[Section: whole-input-budget]
Corrected whole-input budget

Y12 — corrected whole-input budget

31 October 2026. Authorized correction of the Y11 omission.

Disposition

Replace the series-only definition of the variable budget with the whole-input definition below. This includes every ordinary wrapper, all bases and operations, and every nested descriptor after finite definition expansion.

The Y11 budget objection is closed by this correction and its provenance proof. For its witness, Q changes from 3 to 23 and b from 20 to 100. The offending worlds now have different profiles, and the finite token frame admits the required pattern. The correction applies to the entire wrapper family, not just that example.

This is a correction to the proposed decision procedure and its proof bounds, not a change to G*, A11, the frame, quantifier ranges or token rules. Earlier reports remain historical evidence; their series-only budget definitions are superseded by Y12. Gate 4 remains to be audited. No independent all-axiom certification is asserted.

1. Effective definition

Start with the complete closed input e and its finite definition data. Expand the well-founded definitions hygienically under X47. Retain the complete written syntax tree, including ordinary syntax outside every bracket.

Let N be the set of all original names in this expanded input, including declaration names, and n=|N|. Compute the stipulated finite H1 closures and hole images. Sources of declarations remain scope-inert; full target images, including identities, are counted where they occur.

Visit every written syntax node of the resulting input:

- ordinary atomic, Boolean and quantifier nodes outside series;
- each series descriptor and every node in its base and operation;
- recursively, each nested descriptor and its base and operation;
- each hole occurrence with its complete H1 image.

For each node t, form its set FV(t) of object/form variable identities free relative to that node. At a binder z with body B, also include the bag FV(B) union {z}. Local hygienic identities are used, so accidental spelling collisions are not counted as identifications. Propositional letters' additional states are handled separately by the token lemma, not counted as object/form variables.

Define

    w_all = maximum variable-cardinality of all these bags,
    Q_all = max(1, w_all+n),
    b_all = 4 Q_all + 2n + 8.

Use these numbers for the entire computation. In particular, enumerate b_all-profiles once for the complete input and build the token and semantic table formats with this common budget. Do not compute a smaller series-local cap and reuse it for an enclosing ordinary formula.

All these operations are finite syntactic operations on the expanded input. They do not enumerate generated terms, inspect truth, or decide future map admissibility. As in Y10, the latter is supplied only where legitimately covered by A11's existing input promise.

2. Global provenance theorem

Theorem. Under the stipulated legal substitution and Ht2 normalization rules, every augmented live bag of any finitely generated term, and every retained ordinary wrapper bag surrounding it, has size at most Q_all. Augmented live bags count free object/form variables together with the names occurring below that node.

Proof. Initially every node of the entire expanded input—not merely a series template—has at most w_all free variables and at most n names. Its augmented bag therefore has size at most Q_all.

In a copied subtree, internal bound identities are freshened bijectively and each external word has one image. A moved name was already counted in the augmented bag. Identifications decrease, rather than increase, the number of distinct images. Thus copied nodes inherit the bound.

At a receiving context node, a substituted hole contributes no free word or name outside its complete declared image. The receiving node's written bag already contains that image. This applies equally to a series operation, a receiving inner descriptor, and an ordinary input context outside the brackets. Private binders of a filler do not become free at its ancestors.

For existing inner descriptors, legal closure transport maps the old closed declaration to the new one. For receiving descriptors, the original full H1 images cover the contributions of substituted fillers. Recomputing the least closure and deleting idle units cannot introduce a word outside these pools. Ht2 retains scopes of surviving units and removes vacuous binders; it does not move a private variable across its binder.

Induction on any finite sequence of legal unfoldings and normalizations proves the assertion. The ordinary wrapper nodes are now included in the initial case, which was the missing step in the previous application. No bound on total term size or nesting depth is asserted. QED.

Scope of this theorem

The local series proof is retained, with a larger initial set of nodes and hence a possibly larger budget. The theorem still assumes legal transformations; it is not a membership test. It does not authorize resolving an undefined map or inspecting a filler's syntax beyond the stipulated normalization.

3. Instance and table budgets

A named-instance check starts from a body whose free-word bag is bounded by Q_all. At most Q_all active parameter identities can therefore become names in that check. Together with the n original names, this gives at most n+Q_all reserved names for the whole checked instance. A child table retains those reservations even when some names are absent from that child.

The ordinary live bag contributes at most Q_all additional identities. Even allowing another Q_all slots for the stated chart/role bookkeeping gives at most 3Q_all+n identities, below the conservative b_all. Coincident semantic values are canonicalized as the same name and do not increase the count.

This is not a count of every ancestor binder in the unfolded syntax. A variable absent from the currently checked body's free interface does not become an additional name of that body's own-instance check. Ambient names of the current whole token check are retained; unrelated names from a previous parent sense check are not imported into the next own-instance check.

For semantic profiles, original names remain the pinned constants. Active parameter values are handled by the bounded tuple matching, not by pretending that every possible new parameter name was an original pinned constant. The actual variable bound is at most Q_all, and the larger cap b_all is sufficient. Sorts, equality patterns, frame incidence, and the independent fitting tables determine the required ordinary range checks.

Thus the fixed-budget token and profile lemmas reviewed in Y11 now have their width hypotheses satisfied at the outer ordinary context as well as within generated terms. The two finite structures remain separate: H_b_all for token constraints and M_P for semantic evaluation.

4. Y11 regression

Retain the original input:

    B = (Es)(Et)(Ef)(f(s,t) OR not f(s,t)),
    S = [B,x,x],
    H_21 = (Eu)(Ev)(Ep_1)...(Ep_21) AND_j p_j(u,v),
    F = H_21 AND not N(S).

There are no names. The complete written input has variable width 23, so

    w_all=23, n=0, Q_all=23, b_all=100.

H_100 has enough R-forms on (a,b) for H_21. One explicit relational witness uses R_1,...,R_21 there; B can use R_22 and the bracket's separate propositional-letter state can use R_23(a,b). These choices exhibit fitting in the auxiliary frame. They are token assignments, not a change to semantic references.

The worlds W_20 and W_21 in Y11 differ at R_41(a,b). At cap 100, unit 41's marker count is recorded exactly as 41 rather than saturated at 20. Its R truth bits therefore distinguish the profiles. There is no longer a claim that those worlds must agree on F because of an identical profile.

For the full family H_m AND not N(S),

    w_all=max(3,m+2),
    b_all=4 max(3,m+2)+8 > m+2.

Hence every m in the family fits the token capacity, and the profile cap exceeds the number of forms counted. This is an algebraic statement for every finite m, not extrapolation from a finite test list.

[Section: composition-proof]
Nested composition proof

Y13 — Gate 4: composition and nested iteration

31 October 2026. Follow-up to Y10–Y12. Physical ledger line references below are to the original revision-58 source body retained above, SHA-256 c64649c2058e6da7dcdd34eb3bed0e3c7db0a63cb517978a72dff894b7033c23.

Executive verdict

Gate 4 passes at the level of the repaired mathematical argument, subject to the explicit finite-kernel premises below. No new separating counterexample was established. The substitution induction works on the original finite written expression, universally over legal fillers. Its iteration induction is over every finite term index. Neither induction assumes bounded generated nesting depth or uses periodicity to establish compositionality.

The result is an assembly theorem for the proposed procedure, incorporating Y10's promise-relative correction and Y12's whole-input budget. It is not a proof that the original X52 argument was correct. It is not a new independent verification of every kernel lemma or of the other twelve axioms. The repaired argument is ready for independent adjudication; the ledger's model-certificate portion of E32 should remain reopened until that adjudication.

This report concerns revision 58 G* and its effective naming convention. Revision 58 includes changes made after the revision-53 freeze. It must not be cited as certification of the old diagram-only computational input or as evidence that the intervening revisions were conservative.

1. Exact theorem and premises

Conditional assembly theorem. Let e be a closed possible sign of revision-58 G, supplied with its finite definition data and the effective names adopted in X49. Let S(e) mean its stipulated sense condition, and let V_W(e) be its truth in a world W of Phi. Assume the finite-kernel properties K1–K4 below. There is an effective procedure D, without an oracle for G membership, such that

    e is an admitted G* input and S(e)
        => D(e) halts and
           (D(e)=1 iff for every W subseteq A, V_W(e)=1).

No correctness requirement is imposed on strings outside that promise. In particular, D does not decide whether all future substitutions of an arbitrary descriptor are defined. This is the promise formulation of A11 at source lines 160–164.

The premises are concrete mathematical claims, not experimental assumptions:

* K1: whole-input provenance. After X47 expansion, every required unfolded live interface, including ordinary wrappers, fits Y12's budget Q=max(1,w_all+n), b=4Q+2n+8. The bound covers original names, active parameter names and auxiliary boundary roles. It does not bound total generated syntax size or nesting depth.
* K2: fitting kernel. The ambient-aware relations over the auxiliary token structure H_b compute the stipulated lexical fitting predicates. Original names and parameter-name roles reserve tokens as required; sibling internal choices are independent only with their common boundary fixed. Fresh propositional-letter states are supplied separately. Admissible projections exist by the relocation argument. Token positions are not semantic referents.
* K3: profile kernel. There is an effective finite list of exactly realizable world profiles, with exact named exceptions and capped anonymous supplies, and finite semantic representatives M_P. Its tuple matching preserves equality, unit incidence, truth and the named-instance incidence tests for the required budget. It has the extension property for the permitted parameter quantifiers.
* K4: ordinary composition. Occurrence sets, exposed atoms, root/component status, ambient fitting relations and semantic tables have effective ordinary-constructor operations, including N+, C-nv and vacuous-binder normalization. Own-instance tests use the names of the checked instance, not reservations inherited from an unrelated ambient token check.

K1 is the corrected Y12 proposition. K2–K4 are the fixed-budget claims audited in Y11 and stated in the bounded-repair report; their application must use K1's corrected bound. The theorem here proves their nested assembly, not their validity merely by naming them. An adjudicator finding a defect in one of those premises also defeats this conditional application. The finite tests below cannot discharge any such defect.

The coherent vacuous-value convention remains the one recorded in Y5: a vacuous abstraction supplies the singleton B, so existential abstraction yields B and joint negation yields not-B. No new rule making joint negation itself transparent is introduced.

In particular, legal alpha-renaming cannot identify two private binders, and a nonconfluent inner map cannot be repaired by choosing one image.

3. Finite records and what they do not mean

Fix the expanded input and its budgets. Use bounded sorted interface slots, original-name slots, parameter-name slots, and role/equality patterns. Each record contains the complete finite array of the K2–K4 observations under the external word substitutions and ambient reservations allowed by that budget. Semantic columns are indexed by realizable profiles and their parameter tuples; token columns are indexed by H_b placements. These are separate indices.

Private bound spellings are not indices of the carrier. They are hygienically fresh in syntax and represented through the local boundary roles in a table. Deterministic local port ordering and explicit finite renaming between adjacent boundaries prevent an ever-growing supply of generated identifiers from becoming part of a state. A choice of ordering changes the encoding by finite reindexing, not the represented observation.

Repeated occurrences of an atom use the same tuple under an assignment. Shared units and shared token identities remain in the relation; they are not replaced by independent atom counts. An ambient name absent from the filler still appears among the ambient reservation rows. Adding arbitrary new names outside this fixed specification requires rebuilding the carrier. There is no claim of one finite quotient for all possible enlarged contexts.

Call the finite product of these arrays K_obs. There is no infinite-future legality bit. Complete elementary operations deterministically on all records, including records without a legal syntactic representative. No semantics is claimed for their unsafe entries.

For a mapped hole the whole-array action is

    A_mu(k)[rho] = k[rho composed with mu],

with the finite boundary reindexing understood. A failed identity entry cannot erase a defined direct-composite entry. Y9's example remains a counterexample to that erasure rule. It is not an allowed illegal intermediate in G*.

4. Descriptor calculation is separate from term evaluation

Deduction. The written-descriptor calculation can be performed structurally on the finite receiving expression, given the occurrence/fitting data of its outer fillers. It does not need their unfolded syntax or their semantic orbit.

At each local series, start with words in its written base and operation outside its own holes, together with the images contributed by enclosing holes. Close that finite set under the local declared maps. An own-hole occurrence contributes its full H1 image; it does not contribute the atoms of an arbitrarily chosen term. Inner descriptors are processed before receiving descriptors, as Ht2 requires. Local occurrence sets decide vacuity. Deletion removes the vacuous binding operation with the truth convention prescribed for that operation, rather than simply dropping a negation.

The calculation uses only unions, images, finite least closures, equality checks and ordinary boundary-relation operations. Hence it terminates. A locally inconsistent quotient can be assigned an error record. On a safe observation it does not occur.

For an already existing copied descriptor, naturality follows by induction on the finite closure stages. If rho transports each map f to a well-defined map f_bar with rho f = f_bar rho, the image of the initial generators agrees, and the image of each next closure stage agrees. Taking their finite unions yields the transported least closure. Fresh private identities remain distinct. This statement requires a legal quotient; the arbitrary choice of an image at a collision is excluded.

For a newly receiving descriptor, compute its closure from the substituted generators. Do not reuse an old closure without recomputing it. This distinction accounts for holes in inner bases and in inner operations alike. Descriptor fitting uses the resulting written words and its propositional-letter state slots, not the disjunction of its term fitting results.

5. Safe dependency invariant

Use Y10's precise meaning of safe: the direct transformed syntactic expression, including the assignment equality pattern for semantic observations, is map-admissible. Sense failure is allowed. Safety is a proof predicate, not a computed classification.

Deduction. A safe observation of a legal composite depends only on safe observations of the legal fillers that actually occur in it.

For a mapped hole the required observation is the direct composite row. It is the retained transformed filler in the legal composite. Ordinary binding introduces fresh binder identities. An N+-admitted named instance is injective on its co-occurring parameter interface and off the names of that scope; source 3625–3631 therefore supplies the needed instance/substitution commutation. These instance requests cannot create a merger of distinct exposed sources. Noninjective operation maps are justified instead by the G* promise. The two arguments are not interchangeable.

Ht2 deletes idle declarations and vacuous binders, rather than executing an undefined intermediate and repairing it later. Existing descriptor transport uses the legal closure argument above. Receiving descriptors use actual substituted occurrence data. Consequently none of these safe output calculations requires an arbitrary unsafe semantic entry to have a meaning.

The invariant concerns observations actually demanded in the proof. A compiler may compute extra entries with arbitrary deterministic values. Those entries must not be promoted into new semantic filler representatives. Semantic recursive calls receive complete records of the actual base or term; display-only symbolic holes never enter semantic iteration.

6. Nested compilation theorem

Define Compile(E,Gamma) on the original finite expression E. Gamma assigns complete records to its propositional holes. Ordinary cases use K4. Mapped holes use the array action. For a series with base B and operation C define

    k_0 = Compile(B,Gamma)
    F(k) = Compile(C,Gamma[x:=k]), including stipulated normalization.

Enumerate F until an entire record repeats. The output's written fitting/occurrence part is computed separately by Section 4. Its semantic value at an observation index is the joint negation of the true, own-sense-admitted term entries seen in the preperiod and cycle. Root sense and component truth remain separate fields.

Termination proof. Induct on the size of the original E. B and C are proper subexpressions. Every invocation of their compiler terminates by that induction, for every finite Gamma, including uninterpreted records. F is thus a total deterministic function on the fixed finite carrier. The orbit repeats in at most |K_obs|+1 visited positions. The compiler never recursively expands the syntax represented by k. This proves termination even when generated terms have increasing nesting depth.

Correctness proof. Strengthen the induction hypothesis to every legal choice of fillers for E and every supplied record correct on those fillers' safe observations. The hole case is direct-composite lookup. Ordinary cases are K4 and Section 5. At a series, let T_m be the actual normalized term of index m. The promise supplies map-admissibility of every T_m and of its retained nested descriptors. The smaller-expression hypothesis for B gives correctness of k_0. Applied to C with the arbitrary current legal filler T_m, it gives correctness of k_(m+1). Induction on m therefore establishes demanded observation accuracy for every natural m, before truncation is used.

For a safe transformed series, legal substitution/closure commutation identifies its index-m term with the corresponding direct transformed T_m. Its term admission is the term's own sense, not the descriptor's sense and not the ambient fitting status of a larger sign. The output's written descriptor observations agree by Section 4. All the semantic observations needed to evaluate the series are consequently accurate. Entire-record repetition now implies repetition of those observations; joint negation over their infinite sequence equals joint negation over its preperiod and cycle. This proves the induction step.

This is a contextual congruence on admitted uses, represented by the computed records: equal supplied records give equal compiled results for a fixed context; where the substitutions are legal, their required semantic observations agree. It does not assert that code equality determines legality in every context. Nor does it assert that every arbitrary completion of unsafe entries is a canonical semantic invariant of syntax. The sufficient statement is a deterministic finite code computation with the proved safe-observation simulation.

One can define the reference operational semantics without appealing to compiler repetition: atoms have rank 1, ordinary constructors have maximum child rank plus 1, and a bracket has rank greater than the supremum of the ranks of all its finitely indexed operational terms. Structurally defined ordinal rank functions on hole ranks give this bound by iterating the operation's rank function and taking a countable supremum. They are monotone; hygienic substitution respects the rank bound and deletion does not increase it. Thus the term dependencies are well founded. No effective ordinal calculation is used by D.

7. World profiles and the final decision

Deduction from K3 and Section 6. Tuple-matched observations in W and M_P agree for the entire nested expression.

For ordinary nodes, use K3's extension property and K4. This includes form quantification, correlations between selected units, named exceptions and the own-instance sense colours. For a series, apply structural induction to its written base and operation, then natural-number induction to corresponding generated terms. The admitted index sets agree, and truth agrees at every admitted index. Their joint negations therefore agree. Written descriptor fit agrees independently through K2.

This argument does not assume a finite orbit of worlds or derive profile adequacy from automorphism invariance alone. It uses the effective realizability and extension premises of K3. Infinite-world term agreement is established before computing a finite orbit on the representative side.

The decision procedure is now: expand definitions; compute Y12's whole-input budgets; construct the finite tables and exactly realizable profiles; compile the input with empty hole environment; accept precisely when its closed truth column is true at every profile. On promised inputs Section 6 gives termination/correctness of compilation, and profile adequacy gives exactly the all-world condition in Section 1.

8. Reproducible restricted checks

Run node audit_Y13_nested_fragment.js in this directory. Only Node built-ins are required; results are in audit_Y13_nested_fragment_results.json.

Computational observation: 160 comparisons passed (ten cases, four form-name maps, four worlds). The largest observed compiled orbit had four records. Literal generated nesting depths in one family were 0,1,2,3,4,5,6. These checks implement a two-form-name fixed-object fragment, not G* as a whole. They do not implement object/form quantification, general ambient reservations, hereditary projection checking, the full world-profile kernel, or general illegal mergers.

For this fragment put p=R_1(a,b), q=R_2(a,b), and write S(t,F) for joint negation over the iterates of F starting at t. The compact record stores occurring form names, root presence and the four-world truth table. The comparison evaluator instead unfolds literal syntax for three terms at every series. This finite prefix is justified for these particular cases as follows; it is not an empirical cutoff for arbitrary series.

| Case | Base and operation | Infinite value |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | p; t -> t | not p |
| Negation | p; t -> not t | false |
| Constant q | p; t -> q | not p and not q |
| Nested base | p; t -> S(t,id) | false |
| Nested operation meet | p; t -> S(q,y -> y and t) | not p and q |
| Nested operation nonmonotone | p; t -> S(q,y -> not y and t) | not p and q |
| Mapped outer copy | Previous case with t's form names swapped | not p and q |
| Mapped inner copy | p; t -> S(q,y -> swap(y) and t) | not p and q |
| Hole in base and operation | p; t -> S(t,y -> t and y) | false |
| Empty tail | p; t -> N() | not p, under the component convention |

Proof of the prefix claims: identity and constant sequences stabilize immediately; negation has period two. S(t,id) and S(t,y -> t and y) both equal not-t. For the meet case, the inner disjunction is q, giving the constant outer successor not-q. For the nonmonotone inner case, the first two inner terms have disjunction q or t, so its value is not-q and not-t; from p, the outer disjunction is p or not-q within two terms and cannot grow further. Swapping t gives successor not q and not swap(t); if p is true the outer value is already false, while for p=false the second term distinguishes q=false from q=true and all subsequent terms stay false in the latter world. For the mapped-inner case, the first three inner terms are q, p and t, and q and swap(t) and t. Later terms are subsets of these supports, so its value is not q and not(p and t). The same p=false analysis gives the stated outer value. The empty tail has only its initial meaningful term. Applying any of the four global form-name maps pulls these truth identities back along the corresponding world substitution; it does not invalidate them.

The empty-tail case is explicitly a component-convention regression, not an independent proof that every encoding of N() is a legal standalone G* term. The observed growing-depth family demonstrates why generated-depth bounds are unavailable; it does not establish any general impossibility theorem.

These are proof and algorithm corrections. This audit changes no axiom, constructor, range, projection rule or interpretation of an illegal merger, and performs no thaw. No new contradiction requiring a thaw was demonstrated.

Final A11 adjudication

Y14 — adjudication of the corrected A11 argument

31 October 2026.

Verdict

The corrected revision-58 A11 proof is accepted in this mathematical self-audit. No further unproved mathematical lemma was identified in its stated scope. This accepts the combined argument with Y10 and Y12 incorporated, not X52 as originally printed. It does not claim an independently commissioned referee has approved it, a proof assistant has checked it, or a complete decision-procedure implementation has run.

The distinction matters: Y13's theorem was conditional on four explicit kernel lemmas. Reviewing those lemmas and their corrected application found no additional failure. Accordingly, their status in the combined argument is proved premises, rather than additional assumptions about an unspecified automaton. External scrutiny remains desirable, but the absence of an external review is not itself a missing mathematical lemma.

The conclusion concerns revision 58 and X49's adequate effective notation. It does not establish the revision-53 computational-input claim, which was changed in X49. No new change to the system is made here. The all-thirteen-axiom certificate is not closed by this A11-specific adjudication.

This is the stopping point for the present repair/audit cycle. Another round should require a specific objection, not merely the possibility of further review.

1. The claim accepted

Let Phi have its stipulated frame of objects, forms and states, full world space P(A), revision-58 G* signs, and the injective effective decimal naming adopted in X49. Let Delta be the finite well-founded definition data allowed by A8/X47. For a closed admitted sign e write S_Phi(e) for sense and V_Phi,W(e) for truth in world W under the final C-nv, N+, projection, H1 and Ht2 rules.

Theorem (revised A11). There is an effective procedure D such that, for every finite input (Delta,e) satisfying the admitted-sign and sense promise,

    D(Delta,e) halts,
    D(Delta,e)=1  iff  for every W in P(A), V_Phi,W(e)=true.

The promise includes G's requirement that its stipulated successive maps be defined. D is not required to recognize that promise. The theorem makes no efficiency claim and no claim to decide G membership.

The selected reading of vacuity is the one compatible with the retained joint-negation definition: the vacuous value description is the singleton B, so existential abstraction yields B and N over it yields not-B. This follows from the retained definitions as explained in Vacuous value descriptions [section vacuous-n]; it is not an additional truth-table rule for N. If the ambiguous prose were instead imposed as the incompatible equation N_z B=B, this theorem would not describe that inconsistent specification.

2. Scope and source control
