3. Disposition of the four kernel premises

K1: the whole-input bound

Use Y12's definition, not either earlier series-only budget. After expansion and H1 closure, visit every syntax node, including ordinary wrappers. Let w be the maximum free-variable bag size, including binder-body bags; let n count every original name, declarations included. Set

    Q=max(1,w+n),       b=4Q+2n+8.

The provenance argument has two cases. At a node inside a copied filler, the exposed words have a single letterwise image and private binders are renamed bijectively. A name becoming a variable was already charged. At a receiving node, every word brought by a filler is already in that hole's full H1 image. Multiple holes are accounted for by their union in the receiving bag, not by counting a single copy. Legal closure transport and Ht2 do not enlarge these pools or move retained scopes. Induction over any finite unfolding sequence proves the bound.

The ordinary wrapper is now included in the initial case. Thus the Y11 counterexample defeats the old budget but not this one. Neither total binder count nor nesting depth is bounded or needs to be bounded. Parameter naming adds at most one name per active free identity of the checked body. Ambient reservations of that checked instance persist through its token check; unrelated reservations from an earlier check do not accumulate into an unbounded history.

Disposition: the stated bound and its whole-input application survive adjudication.

K2: token fitting and projections

The transfer is in two stages. Any finite positive token-incidence witness in the infinite uniform auxiliary frame Omega can be moved to sufficiently large, distinct Phi units, with enough markers in each. Conversely, Phi embeds in Omega. This is an existential fitting statement: names' referents do not anchor their tokens to small coordinate units.

Omega and H_b match tuples of at most b identities by hubs, roles, touched-unit incidence and marker equality. With fewer than b occupied identities, a fresh unit or marker has a mate. A leaf or R-form of a matched unit has its uniquely determined mate. Lexical fitting is a bounded-boundary existential constraint recursion, including all reserved names, so induction transfers its acceptance relations. Siblings can share internal tokens only where the stipulated lexical inequalities permit it.

Unconstrained propositional-letter states are chosen separately on fresh units, with repeated occurrences sharing their letter's state. They are not forced into H_b. For the applicable named projections, moving all finitely many token forms beyond the semantic target indices makes the token-to-target graph acyclic. This establishes existence of an admissible placement; it does not say every placement satisfies hereditary A6s.

Disposition: the fitting theorem is valid for the required unanchored existential problem. It would not cover a different problem with fixed small-unit token anchors or global distinctness for every private binder, neither of which is the final fitting recursion.

K3: semantic profiles and realizability

Pin the units touched by original names and record their named markers individually. For each pinned unit, record its three R truth bits and capped residual true/false marker supplies. For each anonymous unit record its three R bits and capped true/false marker supplies; cap the number of units of each type. Parameter tuples retain unit correlations, including a unit touched only by a form value.

Realizability is effective. Pinned capacities are exact arithmetic constraints. There are finitely many unpinned indices below 2b to assign. At every unpinned index at least 2b, the possible capped marker pairs are precisely (r,b), (b,s) with r,s<b, and (b,b). After satisfying finite quotas, infinitely many indices can be assigned exactly when at least one tail-allowed type has a saturated quota. Assign the remaining infinite tail to such a type. This is both necessary and sufficient; mere automorphism invariance would not prove it.

In the finite representative, saturated unit and marker supplies are replaced by b copies. At a move with fewer than b selected values, equality, exact named exceptions, roles, truth colours and unit incidence can be extended in both directions. The resulting bounded-variable induction applies at every quantifier depth. Fitting is still computed in H_b, not in this semantic representative. Parameter names are matched tuple values, not newly pinned original constants with arbitrary unrecorded coordinates.

Disposition: exactly realizable profiles, finite representatives and their extension property survive adjudication at the corrected cap. No independence of marker counts from a unit's capacity was assumed.

K4: ordinary composition and range tests

Fix the complete boundary and ambient name placement before combining child acceptance relations. At a binder, choose its token subject to the lexical exclusions. Occurrence data determine vacuity and which atoms are exposed. A mapped hole reads its direct-composite row, with all original names parameterized, including names moved only after several iterations.

For semantic quantification, first apply the scope's N+ exclusions and canonicalize any relevant equalities as identical names. Then test the body's own-instance sense using its own name set, incidence data and fitting relation. Consult its truth only when that sense test succeeds. This is distinct from testing the instance under unrelated ambient token reservations. Empty-N component truth and standalone admission are distinct fields.

The operations are finite and preserve the recorded observations by ordinary structural induction. The earlier closed-cycle/closed-edge separator defeats standalone acceptance summaries but not the full ambient relations: the contextual names remain in the latter even when absent from the filler.

Disposition: ordinary composition survives with these full records. A table containing truth alone, a standalone fit bit, or only directly moved names would not suffice.

4. The potentially circular step

The critical claim is not simply that the record space is finite. It is that the fixed operation acts effectively on those records and preserves the observations needed by the actual series.

Y10 removes future-definedness from the carrier. On a safe output observation of a legal composite, the demanded filler observation is a direct transformed component of that legal composite. It is therefore safe. Parameter-instance requests admitted by N+ are injective on their co-occurring interface and avoid the local names. Arbitrary noninjective operation maps have a different justification: their legality is part of the G* promise. Neither argument uses a computed safety oracle.

Complete records, including uninterpreted alternative rows, are passed to recursive semantic calls. No individual unsafe row or display-only placeholder is promoted to a semantic filler. The direct-composite rule retains Y9's defined composite even when a different intermediate row fails. It does not license that intermediate as a G* sign.

Written descriptor calculation is separate. Its own holes contribute H1 word images and state slots, not the syntax or truth of a representative term. Receiving closures are recomputed from substituted occurrence data. Existing copied closures commute with a legal map by induction on finite closure paths. Local boundary identities are canonically reindexed; unbounded private binder spellings are not stored as new carrier elements.

Now induct on the original finite expression E, universally over its legal fillers. At a bracket, B and C are proper subexpressions. Apply the smaller-expression theorem to B and to C with each actual finite term T_m as filler. Natural-number induction proves accuracy at every m. Only afterwards use repetition of the entire finite code under the deterministic operation to truncate the admitted truth observations. Recursive compiler calls decrease original syntax size, even when T_m has greater nesting depth than the entire original input.

For profile adequacy, repeat the structural/finite-index argument between a world and its representative. Corresponding term admissions and truths agree at every index; their countable joint negations agree. Periodicity is used only to compute that common result on the finite representative, not to establish agreement in the first place.

Adjudication: these dependencies are non-circular in the corrected proof. The earlier stronger claim that the records decide arbitrary future legality remains withdrawn. The sufficient result is a finite deterministic computation with safe-observation simulation on promised inputs, not a total congruence classifying all syntax legality.

7. Ledger, paper and certification consequences

Record the A11 proof as accepted in this self-audit, using the corrected argument. Retain the original X52 counterexamples and the historical Gate 2–3 stops. Do not relabel the original proof as correct. Its required replacements are:

1. Whole-input/all-name accounting, including ordinary wrappers and full H1 images.
2. Full ambient-aware observation arrays with complete direct-composite substitution lookup.

A paper may state that a corrected proof of revision-58 A11 has been supplied, cite this proof package, and describe its exact input promise. Thus the A11-specific mathematical gap is closed in the current self-audit, but E32's all-axiom certificate is not newly closed here. Independence/minimality and countermodel A11 obligations also remain separate.

No new thaw trigger is established by this adjudication, and no thaw is performed. The proof corrections do not change the stipulated signs or semantics. X49's earlier change of computational input remains an acknowledged historical change.

8. Remaining obligations, precisely

The present conclusion is therefore a substantive acceptance of the repaired A11 proof, with explicit provenance and scope, rather than another conditional pass followed by an unspecified demand to prove the same lemma again.



[Section: model-adjudication]
Final model-existence adjudication

Y15 — remaining axioms and the model-existence certificate

31 October 2026. Mathematical self-audit following Y14.

Executive verdict

The remaining twelve axioms pass this audit. Together with the corrected A11 proof accepted in Y14, they give a model-existence proof for the adopted revision-58 system. E32's model-existence obligation can be closed in the current self-audit.

The conclusion uses the fixed Phi frame and an actual world chosen by the simultaneous construction below. It neither validates original X52 nor certifies the superseded revision-53 input requirement. This is not an external independent referee certificate or machine verification. Independence/minimality, including E33 and countermodel A11 obligations, remains separate.

The main remaining issue was simultaneous satisfaction of A16 and A18. A direct Baire-category construction supplies an actual world with both properties. It avoids assuming the existence of a countable transitive model of all set theory. Where a countable forcing model is already supplied, the construction can also be made generic over it. These are different foundational claims and should not be conflated.

No axiom, permitted sign, range rule, projection rule or truth operation is changed. No thaw is performed. The actual-world construction selects a witness to the existing existence requirement; it does not restrict the full world space required by A4.

1. Statement, sources and proof dependencies

Let the object set be

    O={a,b,h,h'} union {o_i : i>=1}.

The forms and their states are exactly

    R_i(a,b), R_i(b,a), R_i(h,o_i),
    f_(i,j)(h',o_i),  1<=j<=i.

All listed symbols are distinct except where repeated. Let A be this countable state set and let the world space be 2^A. Use revision-58 G*, its chosen effective notation, X47 expansion, own-instance C-nv, N+, the final lexical token rule and hereditary A6s.

Model-existence theorem. In ordinary classical mathematics with the Baire category theorem, there exists an actual world chi* on this frame such that the resulting structure satisfies

    A4, A5, A6a, A6s, A7, A8, A11, A13, A14, A16, A17, A18, A19.

The A11 part is the corrected theorem in Y14, not a new proof here. The other parts are proved below. The argument does not infer A16 from rigidity, infer A17 from automorphism invariance alone, or infer A18 from genericity without specifying the regularity needed.

Physical line references are to the original revision-58 source body retained above, SHA-256 c64649c2058e6da7dcdd34eb3bed0e3c7db0a63cb517978a72dff894b7033c23. The axiom statements are at 147–182; the definition of “singled out” is at 189–190. X53's frame and descriptions are at 3906–3952, its A17–A18 arguments at 3953–3973, its A16 descriptions at 3974–3994, and its copying argument at 3995–4004. Earlier source claims were treated as propositions to check, not independent evidence of their own correctness.

Dependency order: finite frame descriptions and token placements -> A17; countability and well-founded countable Boolean semantics -> Borel truth sets; Baire construction plus A17 -> A18; the same selected world plus the descriptions -> A16. None of these steps needs an A11 decision oracle. A11 is combined only at the final model theorem.

2. Finite descriptions: semantic calculations and fitting

Expand the following abbreviations hygienically:

    St(p,u,v) = p(u,v) or not p(u,v)
    Off(p,u,v) = exists s,t (St(p,s,t) and St(p,u,v))
    M_k(x) = exists y,p_1,...,p_k AND_j St(p_j,y,x)
    U_i(x) = M_i(x) and not M_(i+1)(x)
    Rf(p,w) = exists u (St(p,u,w) and Off(p,u,w))
    Unit_i(w,p) = U_i(w) and Rf(p,w).

All are name-free formulas, with object/form sorts as indicated in source 3914–3924. The indices i and k specify finite formula lengths; they are not hidden object names in the formulas.

St is true on meaningful atomic instances. Off includes its second St conjunct so that u,v occur in the scopes of s,t. N+ then requires a disjoint object pair; omitting that guard changes the formula under this semantics.

Counting lemma. At o_i, M_k holds exactly when k<=i. Into o_i, h supplies one R-form and h' supplies i marker forms. N+ forces the k selected form values to be distinct and their common source to differ from x. Into a and b, infinitely many R-forms are available, so every finite M_k holds. No state ends at h or h'. Thus U_i is true exactly of o_i. Also Rf(p,o_i) holds exactly when p=R_i: R_i has a disjoint common-pair state, whereas a marker has only one state.

These are conclusions about admitted quantifier chains, not just ordinary first-order readings. The fitting witnesses needed to justify those chains are as follows. All fresh token-unit indices can be chosen beyond the finitely many semantic form indices in the instance.

| Checked pattern | Compatible tokens |
|---|---|
| Counting at named x | x at a fresh leaf o_m; source at h'; bound forms at enough distinct markers of unit m |
| Rf at named p,w | p at R_m, w at o_m, u at h; Off's s,t at a,b |
| Unit_i and a cycle test | Same p,w placement; counting uses h' and markers, Rf uses h plus the common pair, cycle test uses a,b in its separate scope |
| Two units with a shared orientation test | Distinct leaf units for w,w' and distinct R-form tokens for p,q; a,b shared in the orientation block |
| Marker-count test with u,w and selected forms named | u,w at a,b; selected form names at distinct R-form tokens; each Off block uses h and that R-form's leaf |

The last row is essential. A semantic marker form need not have a marker-form token. Its negative Off subformula must fit even though its semantic witness range is empty. Using R-form tokens gives both the named (a,b) edge and a separate possible off-edge in the token pattern. At the semantic level the named marker has no disjoint edge, so Off is false. Confusing token roles with referents would break this argument.

For the marker-count formula's outer w-instance, U_i(w) also fits with w at b and its counting source at a using sufficiently many R-form tokens. At that stage u is still bound. When the u-body is subsequently checked as its own named instance, the U_i sibling is no longer in that body. This is exactly the adopted own-instance C-nv rule, not a waiver of ambient reservations within a single check.

Nested binder exclusions and global name reservations are respected in these placements. Separate sibling binders share tokens only where the final lexical rule permits it. Move all used token forms to fresh units disjoint from the named target forms; the applicable projection graph then has no directed cycle. False negative branches need a fitting sign, not a successful semantic witness. Consequently the displayed frame calculations survive C-nv, N+ and hereditary A6s.

3. A17: completely general truths determine the world up to isomorphism

Use the source families at 3944–3952:

* HT_i selects Unit_i(w,p) and a true p-edge into w.
* MC_(i,k) selects U_i(w), a common incoming source, and k distinct true forms whose Off condition is false.
* TT_i, FF_i and MIX_i select Unit_i and respectively two true, two false, or one true/one false orientations of a two-way pair.
* OR_(i,j), i!=j, selects both units and uses the same ordered pair to test that both are mixed in the same direction.

The preceding placements verify sense and the successful named prefixes. Their exact readings at every world are:

    HT_i: truth of R_i(h,o_i);
    MC_(i,k): at least k true marker states in unit i;
    TT_i / FF_i / MIX_i: the unordered pair of orientation bits;
    OR_(i,j): the two mixed units have matching orientation.

For MC, the guarded negative Off condition excludes the R_i edge and keeps the markers. For the orientation families, both directed instances must be frame states, so their pair is {a,b}. OR does not choose separate orientations independently for the two units.

Suppose W and W' agree on all completely general truths. The HT family fixes every h-edge bit. All MC thresholds fix each finite number of true markers. The orientation families fix each unit's orientation type. If there are mixed units, choose one i_0: its two worlds' orientation determines a single global choice of identity or swap(a,b). OR_(i_0,j) forces that same choice to match every other mixed unit. Nonmixed pairs are already invariant. Within each unit choose a marker permutation carrying its true subset to the other true subset, possible because the finite cardinalities agree. These permutations, together with the one global swap, give an isomorphism W -> W'. This proves A17.

For later use, these are all the frame automorphisms. The only two-way object pair is {a,b}; h is the remaining source of R-form states, and h' is the source of one-state marker forms. Leaves have no outgoing states. Leaf o_i is fixed by its distinct finite number i of incoming marker forms. Thus each R_i is fixed, and only marker permutations within each unit and the global swap remain. This is a frame argument, independent of the truth-world invariant families.

4. One actual world for A5, A16 and A18

4.1 Borel semantics, without an A11 oracle

Restrict attention temporarily to the closed subspace X of worlds in which every marker state and every R_i(h,o_i) is true. The two orientation bits per unit vary freely, so X is a Cantor space. This restriction is for choosing chi*, not a restriction of Lambda.

There are countably many finite signs with finite definition data and countably many named parameter tuples. For every meaningful proposition p, its truth set B_p within X is Borel. Atoms are clopen; Boolean operations preserve Borelness; object/form value ranges are countable and world-independent; series ranges are their countably many finite-index operational terms, filtered by world-independent sense. The nested operational dependencies are well founded by the structural ordinal-rank construction used in Y13. Hence transfinite induction builds each truth set using countable Boolean operations. This is a semantic regularity proof, not an inference from the presumed decidability of tautologyhood.

4.2 A simultaneous invariant good set

For each B_p choose an open U_p with B_p symmetric-difference U_p meagre. Borel sets have this property: the sets approximable by open sets modulo meagre sets form a sigma algebra containing the open sets. Include the boundary of U_p in the exceptional set. Let Gamma be the countable group generated by finite flips of orientation coordinates and the global swap of the two orientations.

Remove all Gamma-translates of all these exceptional sets from X. Also remove the worlds for which either S minus T or T minus S is finite, where S,T are the two orientation supports. The latter condition is meagre: beyond any finite coordinate prescription one can prescribe another difference in either direction. Its complement is Gamma-invariant.

The resulting G is comeagre, nonempty by the Baire theorem, and Gamma-invariant. At every z in G, each B_p is constant on some neighborhood of z relative to G: outside the exceptional set membership agrees with U_p, and z is not on its boundary. This does not assert local constancy on all worlds.

Choose chi* in G. This proves A5 and ensures both orientation differences are infinite. The choice satisfies all propositions' regularity requirements simultaneously, not one newly selected actual world per proposition.

4.3 A18: no truth-changing minimal alteration preserves general truths

Let p change truth between chi and W, and suppose W has the same completely general truths as chi. By A17 and the frame automorphism calculation, W is either chi or chi-dagger=swap(a,b)(chi): all markers are true, so marker permutations make no difference. The first possibility cannot change p. The difference D between chi* and chi-dagger is infinite.

Both worlds lie in G. At chi-dagger choose a basic finite-coordinate neighborhood on which p has the same truth value relative to G. Flip chi only on the finitely many coordinates of D needed to enter that neighborhood. The result chi' is in G by invariance, and p at chi' equals p at chi-dagger, differing from p at chi. Its change set is a finite proper subset of D. Therefore chi-dagger was not an inclusion-minimal alteration changing p. This proves A18 in its MC-all sense (source 177–179 and the proper-subset argument at 3969–3972).

The argument does not assume minimal alterations always exist. It proves the required statement for every alteration that is minimal. It also does not infer finite sensitivity of a Borel function at arbitrary points.

4.4 Relation to the source's Cohen-generic wording

Source 3909 specifies a pair Cohen-generic over a countable transitive M coding the signs. If such an M is supplied with the relevant Borel codes, its generic points form a comeagre subset of X. Intersecting that set with G still gives a permissible chi*. Alternatively, the source forcing argument works with its stated coding hypotheses.

The model-existence proof above does not require a countable transitive model of all ZFC to exist. A claim that one exists is a distinct foundational assumption and is not proved here. The Baire construction supplies directly the actual-world property for which genericity was used. No axiom requires a particular forcing presentation of chi*; its two supports were never specified by a fixed concrete bit sequence. Choosing them by this existence construction does not change the frame, world space or truth semantics.

5. A16: descriptions and their uniqueness sentences

For o_i use U_i. For h use

    (exists p,y (St(p,x,y) and Off(p,x,y)))
    and not (exists p,y St(p,y,x)).

For h' use

    (exists p,y St(p,x,y))
    and not (exists p,y (St(p,x,y) and Off(p,x,y))).

The first selects the source of multi-state forms without an incoming edge; the second selects a source of only one-state forms. At a,b the incoming edges defeat the h-description and the available off-states defeat the h'-description. Leaves have no outgoing edge. Thus these descriptions have the asserted unique truth values.

Their named x-instances fit with x tokened at a, outgoing edges on (a,b), off-edges on (h,o_m), and incoming edges on (b,a), with compatible R-form tokens. Inner object binders avoid the named x-token. These are token placements, irrespective of x's semantic referent.

Choose i_0 in S minus T, which exists for the selected chi*. Use precisely the repaired source descriptions at 3985–3988:

    D_a(x) = exists w,p (
        U_i0(w)
        and exists u St(p,u,w)
        and exists y (p(x,y) and not p(y,x))).

For D_b reverse the final two orientations. The two-way pair forces an R-form; U_i0 and the incoming edge then force R_i0. Its actual orientation selects a for D_a and b for D_b. Crucially, there is no Rf conjunct here: reinstating it would reintroduce the earlier token obstruction.

At the named satisfying instance place x at a, w at a fresh o_m, p at R_m, the incoming-edge binder at h, the counting blocks at h' and markers, and the reverse-edge binder at b. The D_b case uses the same fitting pattern. All named successful prefixes can be realized with fresh target-disjoint forms. Thus the descriptions really admit their unique intended objects; they are not merely first-order formulas that become empty under C-nv.

A16 also demands sense of the 5.5321 uniqueness sentence, not just unique truth. For U_i the two copies can use distinct fresh leaf units. For h,h' and D_a,D_b place the two outer argument binders at a and b. Each copy's inner reverse-edge binder can use the other token because the other outer argument is absent from that inner binder's local body. Counting and off-edge blocks use fresh units as above. At this written stage the outer arguments are bound letters, not two global name reservations. Hence the doubled sign fits.

Existence holds by the successful single instance. The doubled existential cannot have an admitted true witness with two distinct object values: each component can be true only of the one selected object, and N+ excludes equal values. Some instantiated doubled ranges can be empty, but that does not invalidate the meaningful written uniqueness sentence or its true negation. This verifies the source's “Both” requirement at 189–190 and 3974–3976. Therefore A16 holds at the same chi* used for A18.

6. The remaining axioms

A4: Lambda is stipulated to be all of 2^A. Selecting chi* inside X does not remove any other worlds.

A6a: Under the adopted formulation at 149–150, M=A: all sign-medium states are frame states by fitting, including written descriptor tokens. This is not replaced by a new requirement that every medium state be true in the selected actual valuation. Logical operation signs have no additional projected state as specified at 5550.

A6s: The picture class excludes any nonempty invariant subset of the finite token medium under its projection. For finite D this is the no-directed-cycle condition. It is enforced in admissibility, rather than deduced for every arbitrary projection. The fresh-copy construction below shows it does not block A7. The finiteness premise is explicit in the picture definition at 5607–5611 and 7624.

A7: Let s be a nonempty finite situation. It uses finitely many units and finitely many markers in each. Choose distinct fresh unit indices large enough to accommodate those markers. Keep a,b,h,h' fixed, transport leaves and R-forms to those units, and transport markers injectively. This gives a token copy of the situation's finite state support, preserving every shared object/form and incidence. Name it and use the conjunction of the literals required by s. Projection from the copy onto the original support is well defined and bijective there; its token forms and target forms are disjoint, so it satisfies hereditary A6s. The literal signs have exactly s as their represented situation. If medium valuation at a witnessing world is required, A4 permits the required finite valuation. No unproved disjoint-copy property for arbitrary frames is assumed.

A8: Choose the stipulated finite, uniform, well-founded definition discipline and hygienic notation; expand definitions under X47. The grammar's future map-legality promise is syntactic and world-independent. A8 does not supply, and this proof does not claim, an algorithm deciding that infinite promise. Definitions do not depend on the truth of the expressions being defined.

A13: a,b occur together; h occurs with each o_i; h' occurs with each o_i through its nonempty marker set; every o_i therefore occurs with another object.

A14: Every displayed state has exactly two distinct object entries.

A19: At the all-false world the global swap(a,b) is an automorphism of both frame and valuation. Name-free formulas are equivariant: atomic incidence and truth, token fitting, N+, own-instance filtering, legal substitutions and normalization all transport under this automorphism. Structural induction and the finite-index series induction preserve sense and truth. Thus a and b have matching sense and truth for every name-free one-object formula. Their difference in the actual world is irrelevant: A19 asks for some world.

A11: Use Y14's corrected theorem for revision 58. It depends on the frame and full world space, not on computing the selected chi*. No actual-world oracle enters the decision procedure.

7. Certification, corrections and limits

| Obligation | Disposition |
|---|---|
| A4, A5, A6a, A6s, A7, A8, A13, A14, A19 | Verified above under their adopted definitions |
| A16 | Explicit unique descriptions plus fitting of the uniqueness sentences |
| A17 | Verified invariant families construct the isomorphism |
| A18 | Simultaneous invariant Baire construction plus A17 |
| A11 | Corrected proof accepted in Y14; original X52 remains defective |
| E32 model existence | Closed in this mathematical self-audit using the combined corrected proof |
| External independent certification | Not supplied by this same-session audit |
| Independence/minimality, E33, countermodel A11 | Not settled by model existence |

The existence of this model establishes semantic consistency of the adopted thirteen-axiom system in the stated metatheory. It does not show that its philosophical interpretations are uniquely forced, that the axioms are independent, or that the pre-X49 computational-input claim was correct.

Necessary editorial corrections to any consolidated ledger/paper account:

1. Cite the corrected A11 proof package, retaining the original X52 failures and the changes required by Y10 and Y12.
2. Replace X53's broad independent-block sentence at 3929–3933 by compatible shared-interface placements; arbitrary independent placements do not suffice.
3. Retain the guarded Off definition and the repaired D_a/D_b without Rf. Their rejected variants are genuinely defective.
4. State the Borelness and simultaneous actual-world construction explicitly. Local constancy is relative to the invariant good set, not to all worlds.
5. Avoid making model existence depend silently on a countable transitive model of all set theory. State the direct Baire proof, or clearly state the forcing presentation's hypotheses.
6. Distinguish revised-system model existence, external review, and independence/minimality.

No finite computation is used to establish the universal description families, Borelness, genericity or model existence in this adjudication. Earlier tests remain debugging evidence only. No new executable verifier was run, and no paper text was edited.

Remaining mathematical obligation for this model-existence argument: none identified in the adopted scope, after combining this report with Y14. The appropriate next scrutiny is a specific adversarial objection or genuinely independent review of the fixed proof package. There is no reason to start another open-ended repair cycle merely because further review is possible.

[BEGIN VERBATIM BLOCK: javascript]
// Run: node audit_R2_checks.js
// Independent, bounded checks for the stated lemmas, NOT a full TLP evaluator.
'use strict';
const fs=require('fs'), crypto=require('crypto'), assert=require('assert/strict');
function frame(m){
  const objects=['a','b','h',"h'"], forms=[], states=[];
  for(let i=1;i<=m;i++){
    objects.push(`o${i}`); forms.push(`R${i}`);

function acyclic(arrows){
  const r=new Map(arrows);
  for(const start of r.keys()){
    let x=start;const seen=new Set();
    while(r.has(x)){if(seen.has(x))return false;seen.add(x);x=r.get(x);}
  }
  return true;
}

function prefixWitness(i,n,y,selected){

    }

  }

// Independent ambient-aware fit search over scoped-variable inequality constraints.
function fit(atoms,conflicts,reserved={object:[],form:[]}){
  const unique=[...new Map(atoms.map(a=>[JSON.stringify(a),a])).values()];
  function rec(k,g){
    if(k===unique.length)return g;
    for(const st of H.states){
      const h={...g};let ok=true;
      for(let j=0;j<3;j++){
        const variable=unique[k][j],value=st[j];
        if(variable in h && h[variable]!==value){ok=false;break;}
        // b-prefixed variables are binders. f/o identifies the sort.
        const sort=variable[1]==='f'?'form':'object';
        if(variable[0]==='b' && reserved[sort].includes(value)){ok=false;break;}
        h[variable]=value;
      }
      if(ok&&conflicts.every(([x,y])=>!(x in h&&y in h)||h[x]!==h[y])){
        const answer=rec(k+1,h);if(answer)return answer;
      }
    }
    return null;
  }
  return rec(0,{});
}

'use strict';
// node audit_X52_repair.js -- built-in modules only; not a full G* interpreter.
const fs = require('fs'), assert = require('assert/strict');
let next = 0;
const V = sort => `v:${sort}:${next++}`;
const atom = (p,x,y) => ({k:'a', p,x,y});
const and = xs => ({k:'and', xs});
const ex = (v,b) => ({k:'ex',v,b});
const isV = s => s.startsWith('v:');
function live(t) {
  if(t.k==='a') return new Set([t.p,t.x,t.y]);
  if(t.k==='hole') return new Set(t.map.values());
  if(t.k==='and') return new Set(t.xs.flatMap(x=>[...live(x)]));
  const s=live(t.b); s.delete(t.v); return s;
}
function measure(t, augmented=false) {
  const size = s => [...s].filter(x=>augmented || isV(x)).length;
  let n=size(live(t));
  if(t.k==='and') for(const x of t.xs) n=Math.max(n,measure(x,augmented));
  if(t.k==='ex') n=Math.max(n,size(new Set([...live(t.b),t.v])),measure(t.b,augmented));
  return n;
}
function mapped(t,m) {
  const f=x=>m.get(x)||x;
  if(t.k==='a') return atom(f(t.p),f(t.x),f(t.y));
  if(t.k==='and') return and(t.xs.map(x=>mapped(x,m)));
  return ex(f(t.v),mapped(t.b,m));
}
function fresh(t) {
  const m=new Map();
  function scan(x){if(x.k==='ex'){m.set(x.v,V(x.v.split(':')[1]));scan(x.b);}else if(x.k==='and')x.xs.forEach(scan);}
  scan(t); return mapped(t,m);
}
function norm(t) {
  if(t.k==='a')return t;
  if(t.k==='and')return and(t.xs.map(norm));
  const b=norm(t.b); return live(b).has(t.v)?ex(t.v,b):b;
}
function fill(c,t) {
  if(c.k==='hole')return mapped(fresh(t),c.map);
  if(c.k==='a')return c;
  if(c.k==='and')return and(c.xs.map(x=>fill(x,t)));
  return ex(c.v,fill(c.b,t));
}
function base(names){const x=V('O'),y=V('O');return ex(x,ex(y,and(names.map(p=>atom(p,x,y)))));}

  }

audit_Y13_nested_fragment.js

'use strict';
// node audit_Y13_nested_fragment.js. Named R0(a,b), R1(a,b) fragment only.
// State evaluation is compared with literal syntactic unfolding on analytically
// justified short-prefix cases. This is not the full Phi/G* compiler.
const fs=require('fs'),assert=require('assert/strict');
const ALL=15, ID=[0,1], SWAP=[1,0], MAPS=[[0,0],[0,1],[1,0],[1,1]];
let serial=0,compilerCalls=0,rawNodes=0,maxOrbit=0;
const A=i=>({k:'atom',i}),N=(...xs)=>({k:'N',xs});
const Not=x=>N(x),And=(x,y)=>N(Not(x),Not(y));
const H=(id,map=ID)=>({k:'hole',id,map:[...map]});
function S(base,makeC){const id=++serial;return {k:'series',id,B:base,C:makeC(id)};}
function mapWords(words,map){let out=0;for(let i=0;i<2;i++)if(words&(1<<i))out|=1<<map[i];return out;}
function truthAtom(i){let bits=0;for(let w=0;w<4;w++)if(w&(1<<i))bits|=1<<w;return bits;}
function pullTruth(bits,map){let out=0;for(let w=0;w<4;w++){let old=0;for(let i=0;i<2;i++)if(w&(1<<map[i]))old|=1<<i;if(bits&(1<<old))out|=1<<w;}return out;}
function words(t,env=new Map()){
 if(t.k==='atom')return 1<<t.i;
 if(t.k==='hole'){assert(env.has(t.id));return mapWords(env.get(t.id),t.map);}
 if(t.k==='N')return t.xs.reduce((a,x)=>a|words(x,env),0);
 return closure(t,env);
}
function closure(t,env){let L=0;for(let i=0;i<5;i++){const inner=new Map(env);inner.set(t.id,L);const next=words(t.B,env)|words(t.C,inner);assert((next|L)===next);if(next===L)return L;L=next;}throw Error('Closure did not stabilize');}
const encode=s=>`${s.words}:${Number(s.present)}:${s.truth}`;
function compile(t,env=new Map()){
 compilerCalls++;
 if(t.k==='atom')return {words:1<<t.i,present:true,truth:truthAtom(t.i)};
 if(t.k==='hole'){const x=env.get(t.id);assert(x);return {words:mapWords(x.words,t.map),present:x.present,truth:pullTruth(x.truth,t.map)};}
 if(t.k==='N'){const xs=t.xs.map(x=>compile(x,env));return {words:xs.reduce((a,x)=>a|x.words,0),present:xs.some(x=>x.present),truth:ALL^xs.reduce((a,x)=>a|x.truth,0)};}
 const wordEnv=new Map([...env].map(([id,s])=>[id,s.words]));
 const declared=closure(t,wordEnv),seen=new Set();let k=compile(t.B,env),any=0;
 while(!seen.has(encode(k))){seen.add(encode(k));assert(seen.size<=128);if(k.present)any|=k.truth;const inner=new Map(env);inner.set(t.id,k);k=compile(t.C,inner);}
 maxOrbit=Math.max(maxOrbit,seen.size);
 return {words:declared,present:true,truth:ALL^any};
}
function fresh(t,ren=new Map()){
 if(t.k==='atom')return {...t};
 if(t.k==='hole')return {...t,id:ren.get(t.id)||t.id,map:[...t.map]};
 if(t.k==='N')return N(...t.xs.map(x=>fresh(x,ren)));
 const id=++serial,inner=new Map(ren);inner.set(t.id,id);return {k:'series',id,B:fresh(t.B,ren),C:fresh(t.C,inner)};
}
// Transport a local map only on its actual declared closure. All identifications
// in this two-form-name fragment are confluent; object names remain fixed.
function rename(t,rho,env=new Map()){
 if(t.k==='atom')return A(rho[t.i]);
 if(t.k==='N')return N(...t.xs.map(x=>rename(x,rho,env)));
 if(t.k==='hole'){
  assert(env.has(t.id));const domain=env.get(t.id),out=[0,1],set=new Set();
  for(let i=0;i<2;i++)if(domain&(1<<i)){const a=rho[i],b=rho[t.map[i]];if(set.has(a))assert.equal(out[a],b);out[a]=b;set.add(a);}
  return H(t.id,out);
 }
 const L=closure(t,env),inner=new Map(env);inner.set(t.id,L);return {k:'series',id:t.id,B:rename(t.B,rho,env),C:rename(t.C,rho,inner)};
}
function substitute(t,id,value){
 if(t.k==='atom')return t;
 if(t.k==='hole')return t.id===id?rename(fresh(value),t.map):t;
 if(t.k==='N')return N(...t.xs.map(x=>substitute(x,id,value)));
 assert(t.id!==id);return {...t,B:substitute(t.B,id,value),C:substitute(t.C,id,value)};
}
function present(t){if(t.k==='atom'||t.k==='series')return true;if(t.k==='N')return t.xs.some(present);throw Error('Free propositional hole');}
function literal(t,w,prefix){
 rawNodes++;
 if(t.k==='atom')return !!(w&(1<<t.i));
 if(t.k==='N')return !t.xs.some(x=>literal(x,w,prefix));
 if(t.k==='hole')throw Error('Free hole during literal evaluation');
 let term=t.B;
 for(let i=0;i<prefix;i++){if(present(term)&&literal(term,w,prefix))return false;term=substitute(t.C,t.id,term);}
 return true;
}
function depth(t){if(t.k==='atom'||t.k==='hole')return 0;if(t.k==='N')return Math.max(0,...t.xs.map(depth));return 1+Math.max(depth(t.B),depth(t.C));}
const p=A(0),q=A(1),pTruth=truthAtom(0),qTruth=truthAtom(1);
const cases=[
 ['identity',S(p,x=>H(x)),ALL^pTruth],
 ['negation',S(p,x=>Not(H(x))),0],
 ['constant_q',S(p,()=>q),ALL^(pTruth|qTruth)],
 ['nested_base',S(p,x=>S(H(x),y=>H(y))),0],
 ['nested_operation_meet',S(p,x=>S(q,y=>And(H(y),H(x)))),(ALL^pTruth)&qTruth],
 ['nested_operation_nonmonotone',S(p,x=>S(q,y=>And(Not(H(y)),H(x)))),(ALL^pTruth)&qTruth],
 ['nested_mapped_outer_copy',S(p,x=>S(q,y=>And(Not(H(y)),H(x,SWAP)))),(ALL^pTruth)&qTruth],
 ['nested_mapped_inner_copy',S(p,x=>S(q,y=>And(H(y,SWAP),H(x)))),(ALL^pTruth)&qTruth],
 ['hole_in_base_and_operation',S(p,x=>S(H(x),y=>And(H(x),H(y)))),0],
 ['empty_tail_component_convention',S(p,()=>N()),ALL^pTruth]
];
let comparisons=0;const summaries=[];
for(const [name,t,expected]of cases){const compiled=compile(t);assert.equal(compiled.truth,expected,name);assert(compiled.present);
 for(const rho of MAPS){const transformed=rename(fresh(t),rho),k=compile(transformed),expectedMapped=pullTruth(expected,rho);assert.equal(k.truth,expectedMapped,name);assert.equal(k.words,mapWords(compiled.words,rho));
  for(let w=0;w<4;w++){assert.equal(literal(transformed,w,3),!!(k.truth&(1<<w)),`${name}/${rho}/${w}`);comparisons++;}
 }
 summaries.push({name,truth_bits:compiled.truth,form_name_mask:compiled.words});
}
const growing=cases.find(x=>x[0]==='nested_base')[1];let term=growing.B;const depths=[];
for(let i=0;i<7;i++){depths.push(depth(term));term=substitute(growing.C,growing.id,term);}

/* Run: node audit_checks.js
   Finite token CSP checks, not an implementation of the entire TLP semantics. */
const fs = require('fs');
const crypto = require('crypto');
const assert = require('assert/strict');
function frame(n) {
  const states = [];
  for (let i=1;i<=n;i++) {
    states.push([`R${i}`,'a','b'],[`R${i}`,'b','a'],[`R${i}`,'h',`o${i}`]);
    for(let j=1;j<=i;j++) states.push([`f${i}_${j}`,"h'",`o${i}`]);
  }
  return states;
}
// Atom identifiers are sort-prefixed. Inequalities encode lexical conflicts,
// including every binder versus every ambient name of its sort.
function fit(states, atoms, neq) {
  atoms = [...new Map(atoms.map(a=>[a.join('|'),a])).values()];
  function go(k,m) {
    if(k===atoms.length) return m;
    for(const state of states) {
      const next = {...m}; let ok=true;
      for(let j=0;j<3;j++) {
        const v=atoms[k][j];
        if(v in next && next[v]!==state[j]) {ok=false;break;}
        next[v]=state[j];
      }
      if(ok && neq.every(([x,y])=>!(x in next && y in next) || next[x]!==next[y])) {
        const answer=go(k+1,next); if(answer) return answer;
      }
    }
    return null;
  }
  return go(0,{});
}

X54 — Independence, tier A: A5, A6a, A6s, A8, A16, A18

Proved (refereed, one round; four wording edits applied): each of these six axioms fails in a countermodel that satisfies the other twelve, to the standard of Appendices C and D. The countermodels are those of Appendix B; the proofs are new. Independence of A4, A7, A13, A14, A19 (tier B: A11 on a changed frame) and of A17 (E33) stays open.

Standard. A countermodel for Ak is a structure (frame F, world space Lambda, actual world chi* where it has one, medium, admissible pictures Pi, notation with its definitions) in which every axiom other than Ak holds by a proof, and Ak fails.

Lemma T (transfer). The following proofs use only the frame, Lambda = 2^A, the notation with its definitions, and the fitting and sense rules; none uses chi*: Appendix C (A11; "it depends on the frame and full world space, not on computing the selected chi*", D.5), D.1's counting lemma (semantic, but true at every world), D.2 (A17 and the automorphism calculation), the fitting witnesses of D.1 and D.4 (sense of the descriptions and of their 5.5321 sentences), and D.5 for A4, A6a, A6s, A7, A8, A13, A14, A19. A structure that agrees with Phi in these respects satisfies those axioms by the same proofs. Only D.3 (A5, A18) and, in D.4, the descriptions D_a and D_b (through the choice of i_0 and the actual orientation) use chi*; the descriptions of o_i, h and h' are true at every world.

1. A5. Countermodel: Phi's frame, Lambda = 2^A and notation, with no actual world.
   - A5 fails by construction.
   - A16, A18 (and D12, D15) are stated as conditionals, "If chi* is the actual world, ...": vacuously true.
   - Every other axiom by Lemma T.

2. A16. Countermodel: Phi with chi*_= : every marker state and every R_i(h, o_i) true, and S = T (for definiteness S = T = {}).
   - A16 fails. swap(a, b) is an automorphism of the frame and fixes chi*_= (S = T). Name-free formulas are equivariant under such an automorphism (D.5, A19: atomic incidence and truth, fitting, N+, own-instance filtering, substitution and normalization all transport). So every completely general phi true of a at chi*_= is true of b: no description singles out a.
   - A18 holds. Let W have chi*_='s completely general truths. By A17, W = sigma(chi*_=) for some sigma in Aut(F) = <swap(a, b)> x Prod_i Sym(f_{i,1..i}) (D.2). Marker permutations fix chi*_= (all markers true), and swap fixes it (S = T). So W = chi*_=, which changes no proposition. No genericity is needed.
   - A5: chi*_= exists. Every other axiom by Lemma T.

3. A18. Countermodel: Phi with chi*_-> : every marker state and every R_i(h, o_i) true, S = N_{>0}, T = {}.
   - A16 holds: D.4's descriptions need only some i_0 in S \ T; take i_0 = 1. Sense of the descriptions and of their 5.5321 sentences is by Lemma T; their unique truth at chi*_-> is D.4's calculation with this i_0.
   - A5 holds. Every other axiom except A18 by Lemma T.
   - A18 fails. Let q := (p)(p(b, a) . ~p(a, b)), that is ~(Ep)~(p(b, a) . ~p(a, b)).
     - Sense: the named atoms stand under the non-vacuous form binder p, so the atom clause does not apply to the written sign; tokens p at R_m, a at a, b at b fit, and p's token avoids the name tokens (different sort).
     - Range: at every world, p ranges over the forms f for which the instance f(b, a) . ~f(a, b) has sense, i.e. both (b, a) and (a, b) are f-states: exactly the R_i (D.2: the only two-way object pair is {a, b}, and markers have one state).
     - So q is true at W iff W(R_i(b, a)) = 1 and W(R_i(a, b)) = 0 for every i.
     - Let chi-dagger := swap(a, b)(chi*_->). q is false at chi*_->, true at chi-dagger. Delta(chi-dagger) is the set of all orientation atoms R_i(a, b), R_i(b, a).
     - Minimality (by inclusion, D.3.3): if Delta(W) is a proper subset of Delta(chi-dagger), some orientation atom keeps its chi*_-> value, so some R_j(a, b) is true or some R_j(b, a) false at W, and q(W) = q(chi*_->) = false. So no proper sub-alteration changes q: chi-dagger is a minimal q-changing alteration.
     - chi-dagger has chi*_->'s completely general truths (swap is an automorphism of the frame mapping chi*_-> to chi-dagger; equivariance).
     - So a minimal alteration changes q without changing the completely general truths: A18 fails.

4. A6s. Countermodel: Phi, with its actual world chi* (D.3), and every projection admissible (Pi unrestricted).
   - A6s fails: the elementary sign R_1(a, b), its token on the state R_1(a, b) itself, has r(D) = D.
   - Senses are unchanged: whenever a sign fits and meets the atom clause, an A6s-respecting placement exists (fresh-unit relocation; X50 Lemma 1; first audit, 3.1, "A6s elimination for existential fitting in Phi"). So the propositions, their senses and their truth values at every world are Phi's.
   - Hence A11 (the same procedure), A16-A18 and the rest hold by the proofs for Phi; A7 a fortiori (more pictures).

5. A6a. Countermodel: Phi, with its actual world chi* (D.3), and an external medium: M is a disjoint copy F' of Phi's frame, outside O and A (its objects are not objects of the world, carry no names and fall under no quantifier; otherwise A13, A16 and A11's naming would be affected); every sign's tokens are states of F'; projections map F'-tokens to A.
   - A6a fails: M n A = {}.
   - Fitting in F' coincides with fitting in Phi: an isomorphism F -> F' carries token placements both ways, preserving incidence, (St), N+ and name injectivity. The atom clause concerns the referents of names (objects of F), not tokens. So propositions, senses and truth values are Phi's, and Appendix C's procedure (its token structures are computed from the frame's fitting relations) applies unchanged.
   - A6s holds: r maps tokens in F' into A, so no nonempty D' with r(D') = D'.
   - A7: D.5's fresh-copy construction, carried out in F'.
   - Every other axiom by the proofs for Phi.

6. A8. Countermodel: Phi, with its actual world chi* (D.3), its notation and definitions, plus one circular definition d := ~d (d a propositional sign).
   - A8 fails: the definition is not well-founded.
   - A sign containing d has no finite translation, so it is no proposition (X47: a sign with defined signs has sense iff its translation fits). The propositions, senses and truth values are Phi's.
   - A11: the naming is Phi's. Given a sign and its definitions, first check syntactically whether d occurs (finite expansion graph); if it does, the sign is outside the promise; if not, its reachable definitions are well-founded and Appendix C decides tautologyhood.
   - A5, A16 and A18 by D.3 and D.4 (chi* and the propositions are Phi's); every other axiom by Lemma T.

Status: A5, A6a, A6s, A8, A16, A18 independent. Evidence: the proofs above; the referee's checks on the 3-unit cut (q's sense, range and values; all 63 proper sub-alterations of the 6-atom difference; the six descriptions and their 5.5321 sentences in the A18 countermodel), ref57/y19check.py and y19check.out. This is a same-session audit, not an external certificate. Open: A4, A7, A13, A14, A19 (tier B), A17 (E33).

X55 — Independence, tier B: A11 on unit frames; A13, A14, A19 proved; A4, A7 open

Refereed (one round, fresh referee; edits applied). Lemma G holds for unit frames with no world-space constraint. A13, A14 and A19 are independent. A4 and A7 are not proved; their gaps are recorded below.

Lemma G (A11 on unit frames).
- A unit frame has finitely many hub objects and hub forms (each hub form with finitely many states on hubs), and units i >= 1 of one template: a leaf o_i, finitely many template forms (one copy per unit), each with a fixed finite set of states on hubs and o_i, and marker forms f_{i,j}, 1 <= j <= i, each with the one state f_{i,j}(s, o_i) for a fixed hub s. Lambda = {0,1}^A.
- Appendix C proves A11 on such a frame by the same procedure, with names extended to its hubs and forms. The frame enters only C.1 (names; arities), C.2 (its closing sentence on A6s relocation), C.4 (fitting tables) and C.5 (profiles); C.3 and C.6-C.8 do not depend on the frame.
  - Arities: atoms of any arity are incidence tests; C.3 counts letters, not arity.
  - C.4: Omega_F has the hubs and infinitely many units with infinitely many markers; H_b has b units with b markers each, hubs exact. Units are interchangeable and the marker supply is unbounded, so finite incidence-and-inequality witnesses transport to fresh units, and the back-and-forth property holds.
  - A6s: template forms relocate to fresh units as in Phi. Hub forms do not relocate, so hereditary A6s is checked in every own-instance check, as part of the acceptance relation with the hub-name tokens pinned: finitely many cases, kept exactly in H_b.
  - C.5: an anonymous unit's type is its template bits and capped marker counts; hub bits are exact. Realizability is C.5's arithmetic.
- Not covered: a constrained world space with co-possible tokens. Tracking used states per live form token is insufficient: a bound form letter can be forced into a boundary unit (by Rf), and sibling subtrees can then use both orientation states of it. The record would have to hold, per boundary-touched unit, its template states used, plus the hub states used.
- Actual world: in each countermodel below, chi* is chosen by D.3 over that structure's own propositions (D.3 applies verbatim).

1. A13. Phi plus one idle object z (a hub in no state).
   - A13 fails: z occurs in no state. A11: Lemma G.
   - A16: Phi's descriptions keep their unique objects (each requires an edge at x). z: Z(x) := ~((Ep)(Ey)St(p, x, y) v (Ep)(Ey)St(p, y, x)), true of z only (at z the y-ranges are empty; the p-ranges are not). Z fits with x at a; its doubled 5.5321 sentence fits with the copies at a and b.
   - A17: z is fixed by every automorphism and carries no state; D.2 applies. A18: D.3. A19, A7, A14, A4, A5, A6a, A6s, A8: as for Phi.

2. A19. zeta: objects h and o_n (n >= 1); forms f_{n,j} (1 <= j <= n), each with the one state f_{n,j}(h, o_n); chi* all true.
   - A19 fails: U_n has sense at every object and is true of o_n only (D.1's counting lemma, h the only source), at every world.
   - A11: Lemma G. A16: U_n; h by H(x) := ~(Ep)(Ey)St(p, y, x) (fits with x at a leaf; true of h only); doubled sentences fit on distinct units, H's at two leaves.
   - A17: MC'_{i,k} := (Ew)(U_i(w) . (Eu)(Ep_1 .. p_k) AND_j (St(p_j, u, w) . p_j(u, w))); Aut(zeta) = Prod_i Sym(f_{i,1..i}); equal counts give an automorphism.
   - A18: marker permutations fix chi* (all true); the only world with chi*'s general truths is chi*.
   - A13, A14, A4, A5, A6a, A6s (relocation), A7 (unit shift), A8: as for Phi.

3. A14. Phi plus, in each unit, a unary form V_k with the one state V_k(o_k); chi* by D.3 on the subspace with every V-bit true.
   - A14 fails: V_k(o_k) combines one object. A11: Lemma G.
   - A16: D.1 counts binary forms only; U_i and D.4's descriptions keep their objects.
   - A17: add UT_i := (Ew)(U_i(w) . (Eq)(q(w) . (q(w) v ~q(w)))) (fits with w at o_m, q at V_m; reads V_i(o_i)); with D.2's families, complete.
   - A18: D.3. A7: unit shift moves V_k with its unit; A6s as for Phi. A13, A19, A4, A5, A6a, A8: as for Phi.

Open.
- A7. Countermodel: Phi plus hubs z, z2 and ternary hub forms Q, Q2 with the one states Q(h, h', z), Q2(h', h, z2). A7's failure is confirmed: only Q's and Q2's states are ternary, so a picture of {Q -> 1, Q2 -> 1} has D' = {Q-state, Q2-state} with r(D') = D' (identity placement or swap), which hereditary A6s forbids. Gap: A16 for z and z2. A test on the ternary state's first object must fit at both h and h' (the uniqueness sentence's two copies sit on both ternary states), yet distinguish them; the h-description does not fit there (no binary in-edge at h or h').
- A4. Countermodel: Phi with Lambda_C, C_u := ~(R_i(a, b) . R_i(b, a)) on every unit. Gaps: A7 fails (the possible situation {R_1(a, b) -> 0, R_1(b, a) -> 0} needs both orientation states of one form as tokens, forbidden by co-possibility); D_a, D_b, MX, SO as drafted do not fit; Lemma G's co-possibility clause is unproved. Suggested repair (unchecked): impose C_u on finitely many units only.

Status: with X54 and Appendix B's A11 entry, ten of thirteen axioms are independent: A5, A6a, A6s, A8, A11, A13, A14, A16, A18, A19. Open: A4, A7, A17 (E33).

X56 — Independence of A4 and A7 (November 2026; refereed with one edit, applied)

Claimed and refereed: A4 and A7 are independent. With X54, X55 and Appendix B's A11 entry, twelve of thirteen axioms are independent; A17 (E33) stays open.

1. A4. Countermodel: Φ with Λ_1 := {W : not (W(R_1(a, b)) = W(R_1(b, a)) = 1)} (the constraint on unit 1 only); "situation" read as possible (2.202); a sign's tokens must be co-possible (jointly true in some world of Λ_1). χ*: unit 1 FF; every other unit, every marker and every R_i(h, o_i) as in D.3, chosen by D.3 over this structure's propositions on the subspace X_1 with unit 1 FF (a Cantor space).
   - A4 fails: Λ_1 is a proper subset of {0,1}^A.
   - Fit is Φ's. Co-possibility can bind only on unit 1's two orientation states. Tokens are never pinned (C.4), units are interchangeable and unit 1 has the fewest markers (c(1) = 1), so every fitting placement relocates to fresh units of index >= 2 (C.2, X50 Lemma 1), with hereditary A6s by the same move. Co-possibility never binds; fit and sense are Φ's.
   - A11: Appendix C with unit 1 pinned in every profile, its realizable types FF, AB, BA; C.5's arithmetic and matching are unchanged.
   - A7: a possible finite situation is copied by unit shift onto fresh units >= 2 (D.5). X55's obstruction {R_1(a, b) -> 0, R_1(b, a) -> 0} takes tokens on R_m(a, b), R_m(b, a), m >= 2; the witnessing world values units >= 2 freely.
   - A16: D.4, with i_0 in S \ T and i_0 >= 2. A17: D.2 (TT_1 false at every world; swap(a, b) preserves Λ_1; Aut is Φ's).
   - A18: Γ, generated by finite flips on units >= 2 and the swap, preserves X_1; the isomorphs of χ* are χ* and χ†; D.3.3's variant χ' lies in X_1 ⊆ Λ_1.
   - A19: the all-false world lies in Λ_1; swap as in D.5. A5, A6a, A6s, A8, A13, A14: as for Φ.

2. A7. Countermodel: Φ plus hubs z, z2 and ternary hub forms Q, Q2 with the one states Q(h, h', z), Q2(h', h, z2). χ*: Q and Q2 true, f_{1,1}(h', o_1) false, everything else by D.3 over this structure's propositions on the subspace with these values fixed (all other markers and every R_i(h, o_i) true).
   - A7 fails: only Q's and Q2's states are ternary, so a picture of {Q -> 1, Q2 -> 1} has projection the identity or the swap on them; hereditary A6s forbids both (fixed points and the 2-cycle).
   - A11: Lemma G (X55), hub A6s checked in every own-instance check. A6s swap: a fully named Q-atom takes Q2's state as token and conversely, which puts name h's token at h' and name h''s token at h.
   - A16 for z, z2 (through the actual world; frame tests cannot fit at both h and h'):
     - F(u) := (Ep)(Ey)(St(p, u, y) . ~p(u, y)) ("u has a false out-edge"): fits at h and at h'; at χ* true of h' (f_{1,1} false), false of h.
     - D_z2(x) := (Eq)(Eu, v)(St3(q, u, v, x) . F(u)); D_z(x) := (Eq)(Eu, v)(St3(q, u, v, x) . ~F(u)); St3(q, u, v, x) := q(u, v, x) v ~q(u, v, x). Only z, z2 are third objects of ternary states, with first objects h, h'. D_z is true of z only, D_z2 of z2 only; both have sense at every stage, including the fully named one (F fits at either hub). Their 5.5321 sentences fit with the copies on Q's and Q2's states.
     - Φ's descriptions keep their objects (z, z2 have no binary states).
   - A17: D.2's families plus
     - QT := (Eq)(Eu, v, x)(q(u, v, x) . S(u)), S(u) := ~(Ep)(Ey)(St(p, u, y) . (Eq')(St(q', u, y) . St(p, u, y))) ("u has no two out-forms into one object"). S fits only with u's token at h' (f_{2,1}, f_{2,2} into o_2); true of h, false of h'. At the fully named stage for (Q, h) the A6s swap puts h's token at h', where S fits; the Q2-branch puts h''s token at h, where S does not fit. QT reads Q(h, h', z) at every world.
     - Q2T := (Eq)(Eu, v, x)(q(u, v, x) . T'(u)), T(u) := (Ep)(Ey)(St(p, u, y) . Off(p, u, y)), T'(u) := (Ep)(Ey)St(p, u, y) . ~T(u). At Q2T's fully named stage h''s token is at h, where T' fits; it reads Q2's bit; its Q-branch has no sense.
     - Q, Q2, z, z2 are fixed by every automorphism; complete.
   - A18: D.3 on the fixed subspace; marker permutations fix χ* (unit 1's single marker is false, all others true), so the isomorphs are χ* and swap(a, b)(χ*), and D.3.3 applies.
   - A19: swap(a, b) at the all-false world fixes the hub part. A13 (z, z2 occur with h, h'), A14 (three distinct objects), A4, A5, A6a, A6s (enforced), A8: as for Φ.

Referee: A4 proved; A7 proved after replacing QT's T by S (applied above). X55's QT with T is false at every world: at its fully named stage h's token sits at h', where T cannot fit.

Status: with X54-X56 and Appendix B's A11 entry, twelve of thirteen axioms are independent: A4, A5, A6a, A6s, A7, A8, A11, A13, A14, A16, A18, A19. Open: A17 (E33).

X57 — Independence of A17 (E33): a countable column frame (November 2026; refereed, three wording edits applied)

Claimed and refereed: A17 fails in a countable countermodel Ξ that satisfies the other twelve axioms, to the standard of Appendices C, D and X54-X56. With X54-X56, all thirteen axioms are independent: TLP is minimal under the countermodel standard. By-product: D12 holds at Ξ's χ*, so A17 is strictly stronger than D12 relative to the other axioms (X36's by-product, withdrawn in X49, restored).

Why a new frame class. In every Lemma G unit frame, A17 holds: units are described, their finite types are read, and a finite hub symmetry is fixed by compactness over finite joint types (D.2's OR argument). Frames whose identical units each carry infinitely many unordered markers fail A17, but they fail A18 as well: describable types differ by finitely many markers, so a finite alteration can swap two units. Failing A17 needs infinitely many interchangeable units whose types differ at infinitely many rigid positions. A11 needs those positions to be told apart only by counting, never by an incidence chain: a chain with series descriptors allows lockstep comparison, which makes tautology undecidable. Ξ therefore has two levels. Columns are interchangeable; within a column, levels are fixed by marker count.

1. Frame Ξ.
   - Objects: hub g; column objects c_u (u >= 1); sub-leaves o_{u,j} (u, j >= 1).
   - Forms: B_{u,j} with the one state B_{u,j}(c_u, o_{u,j}); markers f_{u,j,k} (1 <= k <= j) with the one state f_{u,j,k}(g, o_{u,j}).
   - Aut(Ξ) = Sym(columns) ⋉ Prod Sym(markers of each sub-unit) (wreath type):
     - g is the only object with two out-forms into one object;
     - a sub-leaf's level is its marker count;
     - B_{u,j} ties o_{u,j} to c_u.
   - World space {0,1}^A. A world gives each column the sequence β_u(j) := W(B_{u,j}), plus the marker bits.

2. A11 (Lemma G2: Appendix C on column frames). Each column is a Lemma G unit frame with hubs g and c_u, template form B, and markers from g; Ξ glues countably many copies at g. C.1 (the names g, c_u, o_{u,j}, B_{u,j}, f_{u,j,k}, all binary), C.3 and C.6-C.8 are frame-independent. C.2, C.4 and C.5 nest one level.
   - C.2: move every used token column to a fresh column index, keeping levels. Incidences, inequalities and marker capacities survive, and token and target states are disjoint, so hereditary A6s never binds. g has no forms.
   - C.4: Ω_Ξ has infinitely many columns, sub-units per column and markers per sub-unit; H_b has b of each. With fewer than b identities, a new column, a new sub-unit in a touched column, or a new marker in a touched sub-unit always has a mate. Finite witnesses move to fresh columns at large, distinct levels.
   - C.5, profiles:
     - pin every column and every sub-unit that contains a named item;
     - a pinned sub-unit records its B bit, its named markers' truth, and its residual true and false marker counts (capacity j minus named), capped at b;
     - a column records its pinned sub-units and the capped counts of its anonymous sub-unit types (B bit, capped true/false marker counts);
     - an anonymous column's type is that record;
     - the profile is the pinned data plus the capped counts of anonymous column types.
     Realizability is C.5's arithmetic at both levels: per column over levels of capacity j, each column needing a saturated sub-unit type; across columns, infinitely many columns need a saturated realizable column type. The profile set is finite. M_P truncates saturated supplies to b copies at both levels.
   - Matching invariant (a b-pebble strategy):
     - g is matched with g, pinned items with themselves;
     - each touched column with a column of the same capped type;
     - each touched sub-unit with a sub-unit of the same (bit, t, f) type in the matched column;
     - each marker with a marker of the same truth in the matched sub-unit.
     A B-form or marker touches its sub-unit and its column. Atoms hold exactly on (B_{u,j}, c_u, o_{u,j}) and (marker of (u,j), g, o_{u,j}). Incidence, truth, equality, N+ and the atom clause on fully named atoms are preserved. Levels are not atomic: only counting tells them apart, and counting past the cap would need more live variables than the bag bound Q < b allows, so capped counts always leave a mate.
   - Same profile, same truth: two worlds with profile P both match M_P (C.5). C.8's world-profile adequacy carries every series term and each countable joint negation, at one cap b (series generate no names).

3. Profiles with all markers true. Sub-units of level j < b have type (bit, j, 0), one per level; levels >= b have type (bit, b, 0). A column's unpinned type at cap b is therefore (β|_{b-1}, capped counts of 1s and of 0s at levels >= b). If β has infinitely many 0s and 1s, the type is β|_{b-1} with tail (b, b).

4. A17 fails. Let D be the set of sequences w(01)^ω (w a finite word), and let γ := 1 0 1 00 1 000 1 ... . γ is not eventually periodic, so γ ∉ D.
   - W_1: all markers true, columns carrying D bijectively. W_2: the same with D ∪ {γ}.
   - Every finite word is a prefix of infinitely many members of D. So at every cap b both worlds have every prefix type saturated, with tail (b, b), and no other type. Their profiles agree, so every name-free sentence with sense has the same truth at W_1 and W_2.
   - An isomorphism of worlds is a frame automorphism, hence a column permutation that keeps levels. It would have to biject columns preserving sequences, but γ ∉ D. So W_1 and W_2 are not isomorphic.

5. χ*: all markers true; β_u := 1^u 0 τ_u with τ_u := (0^u 1)^ω. The minimal eventual periods u+1 are distinct, so |β_u Δ β_v| is infinite for u != v. Every β_u has infinitely many 0s and 1s.

6. Tests (name-free; the abbreviations are D.1's).
   - Counting: M_k(o_{u,j}) iff k <= j (the sources are g, with j forms, and c_u, with one). g and c_u have no in-edges. So U_j is true exactly of the level-j sub-leaves. It fits with y at a fresh o_{m,J}, J > j. Name reservation forces the counting source to g.
   - Bit_n(x) := (Ey)(U_n(y) . (Ep)p(x,y)); NBit_n(x) := (Ey)(U_n(y) . (Ep)(St(p,x,y) . ~p(x,y))). Both fit with x at c_m (p at B_{m,J}) or at g (p at a marker). At a named c_u they read β_u(n): the atom clause admits only p = B_{u,n}.
   - DS(x) := (Ep,q)(Ey)(St(p,x,y) . St(q,x,y)) fits only at g and is true only of g.

7. A16 at χ*.
   - g: D_g(x) := (Ep)(Ey)St(p,x,y) . ~(Ep)(Ey)(St(p,x,y) . ~p(x,y)) ("an out-edge and no false out-edge").
   - c_u: D_u(x) := AND_{j<=u} Bit_j(x) . NBit_{u+1}(x). The prefix 1^u 0 is unique to β_u; g has no false out-edge; leaves have no out-edge.
   - o_{u,j}: D_{u,j}(y) := U_j(y) . (Ex)(D_u(x) . (Ep)St(p,x,y)).
   - Sense at every stage:
     - x tokens sit at fresh column objects;
     - the inner y-binders avoid the name tokens by taking other levels of the token column;
     - counting sources sit at g;
     - at the fully named stage of D_{u,j}, St(B_{u,j}, c_u, o_{u,j}) is a state.
   - Doubled 5.5321 sentences: D_g's copies sit at g and c_m; D_u's at c_m and c_m'; D_{u,j}'s at sub-leaves of two fresh columns. DS is not a description: its doubled sentence cannot fit, since only g has double out-forms.

8. D12 at χ*. Suppose CGT(W) = CGT(χ*). The following sentences have sense and hold at χ*, hence at W:
   - "no false marker", ~(Ex)(DS(x) . (Ep)(Ey)(St(p,x,y) . ~p(x,y))), with x at g;
   - ~(Ex)NBit_1(x);
   - the 5.5321 sentences of D_g and of each D_u;
   - for each u and n, (Ex)(D_u(x) . Bit_n(x)) or its NBit counterpart, according to β_u(n).
   In order, at W:
   - all markers are true;
   - so g satisfies D_g, and by uniqueness every column has a 0;
   - since no column has a 0 at level 1, every column has prefix 1^u 0 for exactly one u >= 1;
   - each D_u has exactly one realizer, which bijects columns with u;
   - the Bit_n sentences fix every bit.
   Hence W = π(χ*) for a permutation π of columns.

9. A18 at χ* (profile replacement; no genericity needed). Let p change truth between χ* and W, with CGT(W) = CGT(χ*). By 8, W = π(χ*). If π = id, W = χ*. Otherwise:
   - Let b be p's cap. Let J be the pinned columns, the columns v < b-1, and their π-preimages. J is finite.
   - W'' := on each v in J, β_v reset to β_{π(v)} at levels < b and at named levels; χ* off J; all markers true.
   - P(W'') = P(W): on J, the first b-1 bits and the named levels are W's, and both tails are (b, b). Off J, both worlds have only the type (1^{b-1}, (b, b)), infinitely often.
   - So p(W'') = p(W).
   - Δ(W'') is finite and contained in Δ(W), since every changed coordinate takes W's value. Δ(W) is infinite, because some v has π(v) != v and |β_v Δ β_{π(v)}| is infinite. So the inclusion is proper.
   - Hence W is not a minimal p-changing alteration, and A18 holds. Every proposition is covered, series included (2).

10. The remaining axioms.
   - A7: a finite situation is copied onto fresh columns at the same levels; the name g keeps its token at g. Token and target states are disjoint (hereditary A6s), and ρ is injective.
   - A19: swapping columns 1 and 2 is an automorphism fixing the all-false world, so c_1 and c_2 are indiscernible.
   - A13: g and c_u each occur with o_{u,j}.
   - A14: every state is binary on distinct objects.
   - A6s: by relocation (2).
   - A4, A5, A6a, A8: as for Φ.

Referee: Lemma G2 proved, with the matching invariant and "same profile, same truth" stated as in 2. A17's failure proved, with Aut written as a semidirect product. A16, D12 at χ*, A18 and the remaining axioms proved.

Status: with X54-X57 and Appendix B's A11 entry, all thirteen axioms are independent: A4, A5, A6a, A6s, A7, A8, A11, A13, A14, A16, A17, A18, A19. TLP is minimal under the countermodel standard. E33 is closed.

X62 — The user's four items (6 November 2026; the user's decisions)

- A6a's argument (note 16): membership in 𝔸, not obtaining. By 2.06 a non-obtaining state is a negative fact; a picture's sense reads the depicted values from its tokens' values, so obtaining tokens would leave A7 without pictures of situations with a non-obtaining state.
- LI comparison (note 1) stated as a lexicographic pair (V, R) of mark counts per key (kind, level), V first; a mark counts once per proposition at the kind of the heaviest unit narrowed and at the proposition's level (PRINCIPLE).
- D-S4 renamed D20s, with a note: the free number 20 (D20 withdrawn, X42).
- [Witt1973] dropped from the bibliography (cited nowhere).
